api/Egami.Analysis.AlphaCompare.html.title: Enum AlphaCompare | Egami
api/Egami.Analysis.AlphaCompare.html.summary: Enum AlphaCompare Namespace Egami.Analysis Assembly Egami.dll How Compare(Raster, Raster, CompareOptions?) and Difference(Raster, Raster, DifferenceStyle, DifferenceOptions?) treat alpha. public enum AlphaCompare Fields Premultiplied = 0 Colors are multiplied by their alpha before they are compared, so two fully transparent pixels are equal whatever color is stored under them: what a viewer sees. ImageMagick 7's compare works this way too. Straight = 1 The stored channels are compared as they are, so a different color under a transparent pixel counts. Examples // Every cheap metric in one pass, per channel and overall, on the 0 to 1 scale; SSIM on request. CompareResult result = Raster.Compare(expected, actual, new CompareOptions { Ssim = true, Fuzz = 0.02f }); Console.WriteLine($"PSNR {result.Overall.Psnr:F1} dB, SSIM {result.Overall.Ssim:F4}, {result.DifferentPixels} pixels off by more than 2%"); bool sameLook = result.Overall.Psnr >= 40;

api/Egami.Analysis.PerceptualHash.html.title: Class PerceptualHash | Egami
api/Egami.Analysis.PerceptualHash.html.summary: Class PerceptualHash Namespace Egami.Analysis Assembly Egami.dll 64-bit perceptual hashes: images that look alike get hashes a few bits apart, however they were compressed or resized, so the Distance(ulong, ulong) between two hashes says how alike two pictures are. Store the hashes as keys to find near-duplicates. public static class PerceptualHash Inheritance object PerceptualHash Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // Find near-duplicate photos: hash each once, store the 64-bit keys, and call a pair a duplicate within about 10 bits. ulong a = PerceptualHash.Dct(original), b = PerceptualHash.Dct(copy), c = PerceptualHash.Dct(other); bool duplicate = PerceptualHash.Distance(a, b) <= 10; bool unrelated = PerceptualHash.Distance(a, c) > 10; string key = a.ToString("x16", System.Globalization.CultureInfo.InvariantCulture); Remarks Both hashes look at the first frame's brightness only, after flattening it onto white. The bits are in reading order, the first in the most significant bit, so hash.ToString("x16") matches the hex string of Python's imagehash. Methods Dct(Raster) Returns the DCT hash (pHash style; Zauner 2010): the image's brightness reduced to 32 × 32, a 2D DCT-II, and one bit per coefficient of the top-left 8 × 8, set when it is above the median of those coefficients without the DC term. It survives recompression, resizing and small brightness changes; pairs of unrelated photos are about 32 bits apart. public static ulong Dct(Raster image) Parameters image Raster The image. Returns ulong The hash. Exceptions ArgumentNullException image is null. ObjectDisposedException The image has been disposed. Difference(Raster) Returns the difference hash (dHash; Krawetz 2013): the image's brightness reduced to 9 × 8, and one bit per pair of horizontal neighbours, set when the right one is brighter. Faster than Dct(Raster) and a little less robust. public static ulong Difference(Raster image) Parameters image Raster The image. Returns ulong The hash. Exceptions ArgumentNullException image is null. ObjectDisposedException The image has been disposed. Distance(ulong, ulong) Returns the number of bits in which two hashes differ (their Hamming distance), 0 to 64. public static int Distance(ulong a, ulong b) Parameters a ulong One hash. b ulong The other. Returns int The distance: 0 to about 10 for the same picture, around 32 for unrelated ones.

api/Egami.ChromaDownsampling.html.summary: Enum ChromaDownsampling Namespace Egami Assembly Egami.dll How chroma is reduced to the chroma resolution when a raster converts to a subsampled YuvRaster. public enum ChromaDownsampling Fields Average = 0 Averages with the filter that matches the siting: a 2 × 2 box for centered chroma, a [1, 2, 1] filter across co-sited columns or rows. Edges repeat the last sample. Fast = 1 Takes the chroma of the top-left pixel of each block, with no filter. Examples using Raster photo = Raster.Load("duck.png"); // The defaults filter chroma by its siting both ways; Nearest and Fast trade edge quality for speed. YuvConvertOptions fast = new() { Upsampling = ChromaUpsampling.Nearest, Downsampling = ChromaDownsampling.Fast }; using YuvRaster<byte> yuv = YuvRaster.FromRaster(photo, ChromaFormat.Yuv420, YuvColor.Bt601Limited, options: fast); using Raster<Rgba8> back = yuv.ToRaster<Rgba8>(fast);

api/Egami.ChromaUpsampling.html.summary: Enum ChromaUpsampling Namespace Egami Assembly Egami.dll How chroma is brought up to luma resolution when a YuvRaster converts to RGB. public enum ChromaUpsampling Fields Bilinear = 0 Interpolates between neighboring chroma samples, honoring the siting: the 3:1 triangle filter JPEG and WebP decoders use for centered chroma, and the average of the two neighbors between co-sited samples. GetTransferFunction() Returns TransferFunction The transfer function, or null. TryGetYuvColor(ChromaSiting, out YuvColor) Gets how YUV samples tagged with these code points turn into RGB: the matrix MatrixCoefficients names and the range FullRange gives, with the chroma siting the container states separately. See TryFromH273(int, bool, ChromaSiting, out YuvColor). public bool TryGetYuvColor(ChromaSiting siting, out YuvColor color) Parameters siting ChromaSiting Where chroma sits, which the code points do not carry. color YuvColor The color, or the default when the matrix code is not one Egami knows. Returns bool true if the matrix code is known: 0, 1, 5, 6 or 9. Examples // How samples turn into RGB is always stated: a preset, or the codes a video container carries (ITU-T H.273). YuvColor jpeg = YuvColor.Jpeg; // BT.601, full range, chroma centered YuvColor custom = new(YuvMatrix.Bt709, YuvRange.Full, ChromaSiting.Left); if (YuvColor.TryFromH273(matrixCoefficients: 9, fullRange: false, ChromaSiting.TopLeft, out YuvColor fromStream)) { Console.WriteLine($"{fromStream.Matrix}, {fromStream.Range}; back to code {fromStream.ToH273()}"); } // Or straight from the code points an AVIF or PNG cICP box carries. Egami.Colors.ColorCodePoints hdr10 = new(Primaries: 9, TransferCharacteristics: 16, MatrixCoefficients: 9, FullRange: false); hdr10.TryGetYuvColor(ChromaSiting.TopLeft, out YuvColor fromBox);

api/Egami.Colors.ColorModel.html.title: Enum ColorModel | Egami
api/Egami.Colors.ColorModel.html.summary: Enum ColorModel Namespace Egami.Colors Assembly Egami.dll Whether a color encoding has three RGB channels, one gray channel, four CMYK inks, or the inks of an n-colour press. public enum ColorModel Fields Cmyk = 2 Cyan, magenta, yellow and black inks. Gray = 1 One gray channel. NColor = 3 Two to fifteen inks of an n-colour output profile (ICC's 2CLR to FCLR), such as a hexachrome or seven-colour press: ChannelCount says how many, and ColorantNames names them. No pixel type holds them: convert with Apply(ReadOnlySpan<float>, Span<float>) or draw into an InkRaster. Rgb = 0 Red, green and blue. Examples // A ColorProfile says what a raster's numbers mean. The built-ins cover the common encodings... ColorProfile web = ColorProfile.Srgb; ColorProfile wide = ColorProfile.DisplayP3; ColorProfile hdr = ColorProfile.Rec2100Pq; // ...and Create makes any other RGB encoding from primaries and a transfer function. ColorProfile camera = ColorProfile.Create(ColorPrimaries.AdobeRgb, TransferFunction.Gamma(2.2), "Camera RGB"); Console.WriteLine($"{camera.Name}: {camera.Model}, HDR {camera.IsHdr}, same as Adobe RGB: {camera.IsEquivalentTo(ColorProfile.AdobeRgb)}");

api/Egami.Colors.ColorTransform.html.summary: Class ColorTransform Namespace Egami.Colors Assembly Egami.dll A conversion from one color encoding to another, compiled once and then applied to spans of pixels of any type. Reusable and safe to share between threads. Transforms are cached per EgamiContext, so creating the same one again is cheap. public sealed class ColorTransform Inheritance object ColorTransform Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // A transform is compiled once (and cached), then applied to spans of any pixel type, in place or into another type. ColorTransform transform = ColorTransform.Create(ColorProfile.DisplayP3, ColorProfile.Srgb, new ColorTransformOptions { Intent = RenderingIntent.Perceptual }); Rgba8[] pixels = [new(255, 0, 0, 255), new(0, 128, 255, 128)]; transform.Apply<Rgba8>(pixels); RgbaF32[] wide = new RgbaF32[pixels.Length]; transform.Apply<Rgba8, RgbaF32>(pixels, wide); // float types keep values outside 0..1 Remarks Pixels are read in the source encoding's model and written in the target's: RGB pixel types give and take red, green and blue; gray types their gray value; CMYK types (Cmyk8, Cmyk16) their inks. A pixel type of another model is converted to the encoding's model numerically first, as PixelConvert would (an RGB pixel's gray is its luma), and results land in it the same way. Alpha is carried over unchanged, and is opaque when the source has none. 8-bit RGB, BGR, RGBA, BGRA, gray, gray-alpha and CMYK pixels take a fast path; other types go through floats, so float and half types keep values outside 0..1 (as wide-gamut and HDR conversions produce) and integer types are clamped. Properties InputChannels Gets the channels of each color converted from: the source's ChannelCount. public int InputChannels { get; } Property Value int IsIdentity Gets a value indicating whether the two encodings mean the same colors, so applying the transform changes nothing. public bool IsIdentity { get; } Property Value bool Options Gets the intent and black point compensation. public ColorTransformOptions Options { get; } Property Value ColorTransformOptions OutputChannels Gets the channels of each color converted to: the target's ChannelCount. public int OutputChannels { get; } Property Value int Source Gets the encoding converted from. public ColorProfile Source { get; } Property Value ColorProfile Target Gets the encoding converted to. public ColorProfile Target { get; } Property Value ColorProfile Methods Apply(ReadOnlySpan<float>, Span<float>) Converts colors stored as floats, InputChannels per color in and OutputChannels out, each 0 to 1 (inks as tints): the way to convert from or to an n-colour profile, which no pixel type holds, and for any other values that are not pixels. Inputs are clamped to 0 to 1; outputs keep any value the conversion gives. public void Apply(ReadOnlySpan<float> source, Span<float> destination) Parameters source ReadOnlySpan<float> The colors, a whole number of InputChannels values each. destination Span<float> Where to write them: OutputChannels values for each color in source. Exceptions ArgumentException source is not a whole number of colors, or destination is too short. Apply<TPixel>(Span<TPixel>) Converts pixels in place. public void Apply<TPixel>(Span<TPixel> pixels) where TPixel : unmanaged, IPixelType<TPixel> Parameters pixels Span<TPixel> The pixels. Type Parameters TPixel The pixel type. Apply<TFrom, TTo>(ReadOnlySpan<TFrom>, Span<TTo>) Converts pixels from one type to another; the spans may be the same memory when the types are the same. public void Apply<TFrom, TTo>(ReadOnlySpan<TFrom> source, Span<TTo> destination) where TFrom : unmanaged, IPixelType<TFrom> where TTo : unmanaged, IPixelType<TTo> Parameters source ReadOnlySpan<TFrom> The pixels to convert. destination Span<TTo> Where to write them, at least as long as source. Create(ColorProfile, ColorProfile, ColorTransformOptions?, EgamiContext?) Returns ColorTransform The transform. Examples // A transform is compiled once (and cached), then applied to spans of any pixel type, in place or into another type. ColorTransform transform = ColorTransform.Create(ColorProfile.DisplayP3, ColorProfile.Srgb, new ColorTransformOptions { Intent = RenderingIntent.Perceptual }); Rgba8[] pixels = [new(255, 0, 0, 255), new(0, 128, 255, 128)]; transform.Apply<Rgba8>(pixels); RgbaF32[] wide = new RgbaF32[pixels.Length]; transform.Apply<Rgba8, RgbaF32>(pixels, wide); // float types keep values outside 0..1 Exceptions ArgumentNullException source or target is null. api/Egami.Colors.GainMap.html.summary: Class GainMap Namespace Egami.Colors Assembly Egami.dll An HDR gain map: a small image that, with GainMapInfo, turns an SDR base image into its HDR rendition (or the reverse). Read from Ultra HDR, ISO 21496-1 and Apple JPEG files into GainMap; written back by the JPEG writer. Immutable, so rasters can share it. public sealed class GainMap Inheritance object GainMap Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // As stored: the SDR base image, with the gain map in the metadata. using Raster sdr = Raster.Load("ultrahdr.jpg"); GainMap? map = sdr.Metadata.GainMap; // null for a plain JPEG // The HDR rendition for a display 4x as bright as SDR white: linear half floats, 1.0 = SDR white. using Raster<RgbaF16> hdr = Raster.Load<RgbaF16>("ultrahdr.jpg", options: new ReaderOptions { Hdr = new HdrDecode { Headroom = 4 } }); // The same from a raster in hand, at the map's full capacity. using Raster<RgbaF16> full = map!.Apply(sdr); Constructors GainMap(GainMapInfo, Raster) Initializes a gain map from its metadata and image, whose pixels are copied. public GainMap(GainMapInfo info, Raster image) Parameters info GainMapInfo How the map applies. image Raster The map: gray for one channel, anything else as three (red, green, blue), 8 bits a sample. Exceptions ArgumentNullException An argument is null. Properties Channels Gets 1 for a gray map that boosts red, green and blue alike, or 3 for one boost each. public int Channels { get; } Property Value int Height Gets the map's height. public int Height { get; } Property Value int Info Gets how the map applies. public GainMapInfo Info { get; } Property Value GainMapInfo Width Gets the map's width, often a fraction of the base image's. public int Width { get; } Property Value int Methods Apply(Raster, double?) Returns the rendition of baseImage for a display with headroom (its peak over SDR white, linear; null for the map's full HDR capacity): linear RgbaF16 with 1.0 as SDR white (203 cd/m²), in the base image's primaries, with MaxContentLightLevel set from the map's largest boost. The map is upsampled bilinearly row by row, so no full-size copy of it is made. public Raster<RgbaF16> Apply(Raster baseImage, double? headroom = null) Parameters baseImage Raster The base image, in its own encoding (usually sRGB), the size the map was made for (it may differ by scale). headroom double? The display headroom, 1 or more, or null for full HDR. Returns Raster<RgbaF16> The rendition. The caller disposes it. Examples // As stored: the SDR base image, with the gain map in the metadata. using Raster sdr = Raster.Load("ultrahdr.jpg"); GainMap? map = sdr.Metadata.GainMap; // null for a plain JPEG // The HDR rendition for a display 4x as bright as SDR white: linear half floats, 1.0 = SDR white. using Raster<RgbaF16> hdr = Raster.Load<RgbaF16>("ultrahdr.jpg", options: new ReaderOptions { Hdr = new HdrDecode { Headroom = 4 } }); // The same from a raster in hand, at the map's full capacity. using Raster<RgbaF16> full = map!.Apply(sdr); Exceptions ArgumentNullException baseImage is null. ArgumentOutOfRangeException headroom is below 1. Create(Raster, Raster?, GainMapOptions?) Computes the gain map that turns sdr into hdr: for each map pixel, the log2 ratio of the HDR light to the SDR light, averaged over the pixels it covers, stored in 8 bits between the smallest and largest gain. public static GainMap Create(Raster hdr, Raster? sdr = null, GainMapOptions? options = null) Parameters hdr Raster The HDR rendition: linear light with 1.0 as SDR white (as Radiance, OpenEXR and HDR decodes give), or PQ or HLG with its color profile. sdr Raster The SDR rendition to show on SDR displays, the same size; or null to make one with Bt2390, as GainMap does. options GainMapOptions How to make the map, or null for the defaults. Returns GainMap The gain map, for GainMap of the SDR rendition. Examples // An HDR raster as Ultra HDR: the SDR base, tone mapped with BT.2390, and a gain map that brings the HDR raster back. using Raster<RgbaF32> hdr = Raster.Load<RgbaF32>("render.exr"); hdr.Save("render.jpg", new JpegWriterOptions { Quality = 90, GainMap = new GainMapOptions() }); // Or choose the SDR rendition: the map goes in its metadata, and saving as JPEG writes both. using Raster<Rgb8> sdr = hdr.Derive(ops => ops.ToneMap(ToneMapping.Reinhard)).As<Rgb8>(); sdr.Metadata.GainMap = GainMap.Create(hdr, sdr, new GainMapOptions { Scale = 4 }); sdr.Save("graded.jpg", new JpegWriterOptions { Quality = 90 }); Exceptions ArgumentNullException hdr is null. The caller disposes it. public Raster ToRaster(EgamiContext? context = null) Parameters context EgamiContext The context for the raster, or null for Default. Returns Raster The map's image. WithInfo(GainMapInfo) Returns the same map with other metadata. public GainMap WithInfo(GainMapInfo info) Parameters info GainMapInfo The new metadata. Returns GainMap The map.

api/Egami.Colors.RenderingIntent.html.title: Enum RenderingIntent | Egami
api/Egami.Colors.RenderingIntent.html.summary: Enum RenderingIntent Namespace Egami.Colors Assembly Egami.dll How a color conversion handles colors the target cannot show, with the ICC numbering (0 to 3). public enum RenderingIntent Fields AbsoluteColorimetric = 3 Keep in-gamut colors exact, without adapting the white point (paper white shows as it measures). Perceptual = 0 Compress the whole gamut to fit, keeping relations between colors; uses the profile's perceptual tables. RelativeColorimetric = 1 Keep in-gamut colors exact relative to each white point and clip the rest. Saturation = 2 Keep colors vivid rather than exact; uses the profile's saturation tables. Examples // IccData reads a profile's header and tags; it never throws, and says what was wrong with a damaged one. IccData icc = IccData.Parse(bytes); Console.WriteLine($"{icc.Description}: version {icc.Version}, {icc.ProfileClass}, {icc.DataSpace} to {icc.ConnectionSpace}, damaged: {icc.IsDamaged}"); foreach (IccTag tag in icc.Tags) { Console.WriteLine($" {tag.Signature} ({tag.Type}), {tag.Data.Length} bytes"); } // ColorProfile.FromIcc makes an encoding from it: a matrix profile gets its primaries and curve, so an ICC profile written // for Display P3 is equivalent to the built-in. ColorProfile profile = ColorProfile.FromIcc(icc); bool isP3 = profile.IsEquivalentTo(ColorProfile.DisplayP3);

api/Egami.Colors.ToneMapping.html.title: Enum ToneMapping | Egami
api/Egami.Colors.ToneMapping.html.summary: Enum ToneMapping Namespace Egami.Colors Assembly Egami.dll How HDR light above reference white is brought into the 0..1 range of an SDR encoding. public enum ToneMapping Fields Bt2390 = 0 The EETF of ITU-R BT.2390: a Hermite knee in PQ space, applied to max(R, G, B) so hue holds, that leaves darker tones alone and rolls highlights off smoothly to reference white. For photos and video frames. Clip = 2 Clamps to 1. For tests, and for callers doing their own mapping. Reinhard = 1 Extended Reinhard on max(R, G, B), with its white point at the source peak: simple and predictable. Examples // HDR to SDR tone maps by default (BT.2390, source peak from the file's mDCV/cLLI, else 1,000 cd/m²). using Raster<Rgb8> web = hdr.ConvertColor<Rgb8>(ColorProfile.Srgb); // Or choose the curve and peak; Clip turns tone mapping off. using Raster<Rgb8> soft = hdr.ConvertColor<Rgb8>(ColorProfile.Srgb, new ColorTransformOptions { ToneMapping = ToneMapping.Reinhard, SourcePeakNits = 4000 }); // Linear HDR pixels (1.0 = reference white, 203 cd/m²) can be tone mapped in place. using Raster<RgbaF32> linear = hdr.ConvertColor<RgbaF32>(ColorProfile.LinearSrgb, new ColorTransformOptions { ToneMapping = ToneMapping.Clip }); linear.Apply(ops => ops.ToneMap(ToneMapping.Bt2390, sourcePeakNits: 1000));

api/Egami.Colors.TransferFunction.html.summary: Class TransferFunction Namespace Egami.Colors Assembly Egami.dll How a color space encodes light: the curve from stored values to linear light and back. Single values use exact double arithmetic; rows of floats use a vectorized form within 1e-5 of it (PQ rows use the double form), the same on every CPU with or without SIMD. public sealed class TransferFunction : IEquatable<TransferFunction> Inheritance object TransferFunction Implements IEquatable<TransferFunction> Inherited Members object.Equals(object, object) object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Examples // A transfer function decodes stored values to linear light and back; HDR curves put reference white at 1.0. double linear = TransferFunction.Srgb.ToLinear(0.5); // 0.214 double nits = TransferFunction.Pq.ToLinear(0.75) * 203; // a 75% PQ signal is about 983 cd/m² float[] row = [0f, 0.25f, 0.5f, 1f]; TransferFunction.Srgb.ToLinear(row, row); // a whole row at once, in place Remarks Linear 1.0 is the encoding's reference white. For PQ and HLG that is 203 cd/m² (ITU-R BT.2408), so HDR highlights are values above 1. PQ covers 0 to 10,000 cd/m², about 0 to 49.3. HLG decodes for a 1,000 cd/m² display with system gamma 1.2, which puts its reference white (a 75% signal) at 1.0; single values and rows apply its OOTF to each value as for a gray color, and the full OOTF, which depends on the color's luminance, is applied by color conversion. The SDR curves are extended to negative values by mirroring (f(−x) = −f(x)), as CSS Color 4 does, and to values above 1 by their own formula. PQ and HLG treat negative values as 0. api/Egami.Colors.html.title: Namespace Egami.Colors | Egami
api/Egami.Colors.html.summary: Namespace Egami.Colors Classes ColorConvert Converts between color values (IColorValue<TSelf>), through XYZ D65, and between rows of pixels and color values. ColorPrimaries The chromaticities of an RGB color space's red, green and blue primaries and of its white. With a transfer function they make a ColorProfile. ColorProfile What a raster's numbers mean: the color model, the primaries and white point, and the transfer function. Immutable; the built-ins cover the common encodings, and Create(ColorPrimaries, TransferFunction, string?) makes any other RGB encoding. ColorTransform A conversion from one color encoding to another, compiled once and then applied to spans of pixels of any type. Reusable and safe to share between threads. Transforms are cached per EgamiContext, so creating the same one again is cheap. ColorTransformOptions How a color conversion maps colors: the rendering intent, black point compensation, and for HDR sources, tone mapping, the source peak and reference white. Colorant A named ink: a process ink, a spot colour or a technical ink, with how it looks for backends that cannot print it. Names are matched exactly (ordinal, case-sensitive), as PDF matches them; the names Cyan, Magenta, Yellow and Black always mean the process inks, as in PDF's DeviceN. Two colorants are equal when their names are. GainMap An HDR gain map: a small image that, with GainMapInfo, turns an SDR base image into its HDR rendition (or the reverse). Read from Ultra HDR, ISO 21496-1 and Apple JPEG files into GainMap; written back by the JPEG writer. Immutable, so rasters can share it. GainMapInfo How a gain map turns its base image into another rendition, in ISO 21496-1's terms: for a gain map sample g (0 to 1) after gamma, the log2 boost is lerp(GainMapMin, GainMapMax, g), applied as (base + OffsetSdr) × 2^(boost × weight) − OffsetHdr, where the weight rises from 0 at a display headroom of HdrCapacityMin to 1 at HdrCapacityMax. Boosts and capacities are log2 values. GainMapOptions How Create(Raster, Raster?, GainMapOptions?) and GainMap make a gain map (HDR Design question 10). The defaults are libultrahdr's: a full-size map with a gain for each of red, green and blue, gamma 1, encoded at quality 95. HdrMetadata What an HDR file says about the display it was mastered on and the light levels in it (SMPTE ST 2086 and CTA-861.3, as PNG's mDCV and cLLI chunks store them). Tone mapping takes its source peak from here. Luminances are in cd/m². IccData A parsed ICC profile (ICC.1, versions 2 and 4): the header fields, the description and copyright text, and every tag with its bytes. Read-only; FromIcc(IccData) turns it into an encoding that conversion can use. InkColor A colour given as inks: named colorants with tints, as PDF's Separation and DeviceN colours, plus the appearance other backends draw. An ink canvas paints each named ink's plate; an RGB canvas, SVG or a raster without the ink draws Appearance. Immutable. InkSet The inks a printed page uses, fixed when an ink raster is made: the process inks of an output profile, then named spot and technical inks, at most MaxInks in all. Colours naming an ink the set lacks are drawn through their appearance into the process inks, as PDF does for a device without that colorant. Immutable: WithSpot(string, InkAppearance?, ColorantKind) and WithDisabled(string) return a new set. TransferFunction How a color space encodes light: the curve from stored values to linear light and back. Single values use exact double arithmetic; rows of floats use a vectorized form within 1e-5 of it (PQ rows use the double form), the same on every CPU with or without SIMD. Structs Chromaticity A CIE 1931 chromaticity: the x and y coordinates of a color with its brightness left out. CmykColor A CMYK color: ink amounts 0 to 1, 0 being no ink, by the plain formula (K = 1 − max(R, G, B), C = (1 − R − K) / (1 − K)) on encoded sRGB. Real inks need a print profile: From(Rgba8, ColorProfile, ColorTransformOptions?) converts through one. ColorCodePoints The ITU-T H.273 code points that PNG's cICP chunk, AVIF and JPEG XL use to name a color encoding: colour primaries, transfer characteristics, matrix coefficients and the full-range flag, kept exactly as stored so codes Egami does not know round-trip. GainMapValues A value for each of red, green and blue; a one-channel gain map has the same three. HslColor An HSL color: hue, saturation and lightness of encoded sRGB, as CSS hsl() defines them. HsvColor An HSV (HSB) color: hue, saturation and value of encoded sRGB, as color pickers use them. IccTag One tag of an ICC profile: its signature, the type signature its data starts with, and the data. InkAppearance How an ink looks at full tint where it cannot be printed: on an RGB canvas, in SVG, in a proof of a raster without its plate, or drawn into the process inks of a raster that lacks it. A process CMYK colour, an sRGB colour or a Lab colour, as PDF's alternate colour spaces allow. InkTint One ink of an InkColor and its tint. LabColor A CIE Lab* color relative to D50, as ICC and CSS Color 4 define Lab. LchColor A CIE LCh color: the polar form of LabColor (D50), with chroma and hue instead of a and b. OklabColor An Oklab color (Björn Ottosson, 2020): a perceptual space built on linear sRGB, where equal distances look about equally different and hues stay put when lightness or chroma changes. CSS Color 4's oklab(). OklchColor An Oklch color: the polar form of OklabColor, CSS Color 4's oklch(). XyzColor A CIE 1931 XYZ color relative to D65 white (Y = 1 for white), CSS Color 4's XYZ; ToD50() adapts it. YCbCrColor A Y'CbCr color: luma and two chroma differences of encoded sRGB, scaled as 8-bit codes / 255: at full range chroma is centered on 128 / 255, as JPEG and H.273 store it, so a byte reads as value × 255. The members without options use BT.601 at full range, as JPEG does; overloads take a YuvMatrix and YuvRange, from the coefficient table planar YUV images share. Interfaces IColorValue<TSelf> A color value in one color model, convertible to and from CIE XYZ (D65) and sRGB pixels, so ColorConvert can convert between any two models and between pixels and values. Enums ColorModel Whether a color encoding has three RGB channels, one gray channel, four CMYK inks, or the inks of an n-colour press. ColorantKind What a colorant is for, as PDF and ICC name inks. GainMapFormat Where a gain map's metadata came from. IccProfileClass What an ICC profile describes, from its header's class field. InkAppearanceKind The colour model an InkAppearance is given in. RenderingIntent How a color conversion handles colors the target cannot show, with the ICC numbering (0 to 3). ToneMapping How HDR light above reference white is brought into the 0..1 range of an SDR encoding.

api/Egami.Css.html.summary: Namespace Egami.Css Classes CssCalc A length, percentage or number that may be a math function: calc() with + - * / and parentheses, and min(), max() and clamp() (CSS Values 4), nested freely. api/Egami.DecodeStatus.html.summary: Enum DecodeStatus Namespace Egami Assembly Egami.dll Where a RasterDecoder stands, as Status reports it. public enum DecodeStatus Fields Completed = 3 Every frame has been read. FrameEnded = 2 Every row of the current frame has been read; NextFrame() moves to the next. NeedsInput = 1 An incremental decode needs more bytes to go on: the header, or the next rows or frame. Append them. RowsAvailable = 0 Rows of the current frame can be read. Examples // Decode while the bytes arrive, a chunk at a time, as from a download. using RasterDecoder decoder = RasterDecoder.OpenIncremental(); Raster<Rgb8>? band = null; foreach (ReadOnlyMemory<byte> chunk in file.Chunk(4096).Select(c => new ReadOnlyMemory<byte>(c))) { decoder.Append(chunk.Span); if (decoder.HeaderRead) { band ??= Raster.Create<Rgb8>(decoder.Info.Width, 16); int rows; while ((rows = decoder.ReadRows(band)) > 0) { rowsSoFar += rows; // the rows finished so far; an interlaced file shows RenderPreview instead } } } decoder.EndOfInput(); while (decoder.ReadRows(band!) is int rest and > 0) { rowsSoFar += rest; } band?.Dispose();

api/Egami.DiagnosticLevel.html.title: Enum DiagnosticLevel | Egami
api/Egami.DiagnosticLevel.html.summary: Enum DiagnosticLevel Namespace Egami Assembly Egami.dll How much an EgamiDiagnostic matters. Maps one to one onto the Debug, Information and Warning log levels. public enum DiagnosticLevel Fields Debug = 0 Detail for someone chasing a problem, such as a safety limit about to throw or the band count of a parallel decode. Info = 1 A notable decision Egami made for the caller, such as the format detected or the factor picked for a scaled decode. Warning = 2 A problem Egami recovered from, or something lost on purpose, such as a bad checksum read leniently or alpha dropped when saving JPEG. Every Warning raised by a load is also in Warnings. Examples // Info and Debug events are off unless asked for; below the level they are never even formatted. EgamiContext verbose = EgamiContext.Default with { Diagnostics = d => seen.Add(d), DiagnosticLevel = DiagnosticLevel.Debug, }; using Raster image = Raster.Load("duck.jpg", verbose, new ReaderOptions { MinimumSize = new Size(100, 100) }); foreach (EgamiDiagnostic d in seen) { Console.WriteLine($"{d.Level,-7} {d.Id}: {d.Message}"); }

api/Egami.DiagnosticReporter.html.summary: Class DiagnosticReporter Namespace Egami Assembly Egami.dll One call's link to Diagnostics, with the same level filter and per-id cap Egami's own readers and writers use. Get one from StartDiagnostics() at the start of a call (format plug-ins use Diagnostics) and dispose it when the call ends. When the context has no handler it is a shared instance that does nothing, so reporting costs one check. public sealed class DiagnosticReporter : IDisposable Inheritance object DiagnosticReporter Implements IDisposable Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // A decoder outside Egami (a video demuxer, a format plug-in's own entry point) reports through the same handler, with the // same level filter and the same cap of 10 per id per call. Dispose the reporter when the call ends. using (DiagnosticReporter diagnostics = context.StartDiagnostics()) { if (diagnostics.IsEnabled(DiagnosticLevel.Warning)) { diagnostics.Report(DiagnosticLevel.Warning, "Avi.IndexRebuilt", "The index was missing; it was rebuilt from the frames.", offset: 4096); } diagnostics.Report(DiagnosticLevel.Info, "Mjpeg.DhtInserted", "Frames have no Huffman tables; the standard ones were used."); } Remarks Each id is delivered at most 10 times per reporter; disposing sends one more event per capped id that counts the rest. Report(DiagnosticLevel, string, string, long?, int?) may be called from several threads at once. api/Egami.Drawing.Canvas.html.summary: Class Canvas Namespace Egami.Drawing Assembly Egami.Drawing.dll A surface to draw paths, shapes, strokes and images on, through a current transform and clip. The canvas itself is abstract: RasterCanvas<TPixel> draws into pixels, and other backends (a PDF page, a recorder) keep the calls as vectors. Every public call is checked and tracked here (the transform, the clip bounds, the save stack) and then ends in exactly one protected On hook, which is all a backend overrides; hooks added in later versions get default bodies, so adding them never breaks a backend. Coordinates are float pixels, y down; the pixel at (0, 0) covers the square from 0 to 1. Calls draw when they are made. A canvas is for one thread at a time; one large call may still spread its rows over several cores. public abstract class Canvas : IDisposable Inheritance object Canvas Implements IDisposable Derived InkCanvas PictureRecorder RasterCanvas<TPixel> SvgCanvas Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // A canvas draws onto a raster. Calls draw when they are made; dispose the canvas when done. using Raster<Rgba8> raster = Raster.Create(400, 300, Rgba8.White); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = raster.CreateCanvas()) { canvas.FillRect(new RectF(20, 20, 160, 100), new Rgba8(30, 90, 200, 255)); // Save and Restore bracket transform and clip changes. canvas.Save(); canvas.Translate(260, 150); canvas.Rotate(30); canvas.FillRect(new RectF(-50, -30, 100, 60), new Rgba8(200, 60, 30, 200)); canvas.Restore(); canvas.FillCircle(new Vector2(100, 220), 50, Rgba8.Black); } // Blend edges in linear light, which keeps thin lines and translucent colors from darkening. using RasterCanvas<Rgba8> linear = raster.CreateCanvas(new CanvasOptions { ColorSpace = ColorSpace.Linear }); Constructors Canvas(float, float) Initializes a new instance of the Canvas class. protected Canvas(float width, float height) Parameters width float The drawing surface's width in device units. height float The drawing surface's height in device units. DrawAtlas(Raster, ReadOnlySpan<SpriteTransform>, ReadOnlySpan<RectF>, ReadOnlySpan<RgbaF32>, BlendMode, SamplingOptions?, RectF?, Paint?) Draws many sprites from one image in one call, as Skia's drawAtlas: sprite i is sources[i] of the image, placed by transforms[i], and, when there are colors, combined with colors[i] by colorBlend, the color as the destination and the sprite as the source. Each sprite blends with what lies below on its own, so overlapping particles add up. Samples near a sprite's edge may read the image just outside its source rectangle, as in Skia; leave a pixel of space between sprites when that matters. public void DrawAtlas(Raster image, ReadOnlySpan<SpriteTransform> transforms, ReadOnlySpan<RectF> sources, ReadOnlySpan<RgbaF32> colors = default, BlendMode colorBlend = BlendMode.Modulate, SamplingOptions? sampling = null, RectF? cull = null, Paint? paint = null) Parameters image Raster The sprite sheet. transforms ReadOnlySpan<SpriteTransform> Where each sprite goes. sources ReadOnlySpan<RectF> Each sprite's part of the image, in its pixels. colors ReadOnlySpan<RgbaF32> One straight-alpha color per sprite, or empty for none. colorBlend BlendMode How a sprite combines with its color. sampling SamplingOptions How the image is sampled; Egami's default sampling when null. cull RectF? Simplex = 2 Simplex noise: smoother than the SVG kinds, with no grid-aligned artifacts; Egami's own, with no reference library. Turbulence = 1 SVG's turbulence: the sum of the octaves' absolute noise, with sharp creases where it crosses zero. Examples using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = raster.CreateCanvas()) { // SVG's feTurbulence fractal noise, stitched so a 128-pixel tile repeats without a seam, made gray by a color matrix. Paint stone = NoisePaint.Fractal(0.03f, 0.03f, octaves: 5, seed: 7, tileSize: new Size(128, 128)) .WithColorMatrix(new ColorMatrix([0.3f, 0.6f, 0.1f, 0, 0, 0.3f, 0.6f, 0.1f, 0, 0, 0.3f, 0.6f, 0.1f, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1])); canvas.DrawPaint(stone); // Smooth simplex noise as a soft overlay. canvas.DrawPaint(NoisePaint.Simplex(0.01f, octaves: 3) with { BlendMode = BlendMode.Overlay, Opacity = 0.5f }); }

api/Egami.Drawing.Overprint.html.title: Enum Overprint | Egami
api/Egami.Drawing.Overprint.html.summary: Enum Overprint Namespace Egami.Drawing Assembly Egami.Drawing.dll Which plates a paint prints on an ink canvas, as PDF's overprint; see Overprint. public enum Overprint Fields NonZero = 2 As On, but a CMYK colour's zero components leave their plates alone (PDF's overprint mode 1). Off = 0 Every plate is painted: inks the colour does not name get 0, knocking out what is below. On = 1 Only the plates of the inks the colour names are painted; the rest keep what is below. Examples // A spot colour, overprinting what is below. An ink canvas prints its plate; this RGB canvas draws its appearance. var logo = Colors.InkColor.Spot("PANTONE 186 C", 1, Colors.InkAppearance.Cmyk(0, 1, 0.81f, 0.04f)); canvas.FillRect(new RectF(10, 10, 80, 40), new SolidPaint(logo) { Overprint = Overprint.On });

api/Egami.Drawing.Paint.html.title: Class Paint | Egami
api/Egami.Drawing.Paint.html.summary: Class Paint Namespace Egami.Drawing Assembly Egami.Drawing.dll What a drawing call puts on the canvas, and how it combines with what is there: the colors (from the subclass), the BlendMode, an Opacity, whether edges are antialiased, and for shapes an optional Blur. The kinds are SolidPaint, the gradients (LinearGradient, RadialGradient, ConicalGradient, SweepGradient), ImagePaint, NoisePaint, BlendPaint, ColorMatrixPaint and CustomPaint. A color converts to a solid paint where a paint is expected. A paint is an ITextPaint, so a paragraph's text style can carry it. A paint other than a solid one has its own coordinates: LocalMatrix maps them into the canvas's local coordinates, so a gradient or an image turns and scales with the canvas transform, and further with its own matrix. public abstract record Paint : ITextPaint, IEquatable<Paint> Inheritance object Paint Implements ITextPaint IEquatable<Paint> Derived BlendPaint ColorMatrixPaint CustomPaint Gradient ImagePaint NoisePaint PicturePaint SolidPaint Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // A color converts to a SolidPaint. A paint also carries a blend mode, an opacity and whether edges are antialiased. canvas.FillRect(new RectF(0, 0, 200, 100), Rgba8.White); SolidPaint glaze = new(new RgbaF32(0.9f, 0.2f, 0.1f, 1)) { BlendMode = BlendMode.Multiply, Opacity = 0.6f }; canvas.FillCircle(new Vector2(60, 50), 40, glaze); // Pixel art: no antialiasing, so every pixel is fully drawn or not at all. canvas.FillCircle(new Vector2(150, 50), 30, new SolidPaint(Rgba8.Black) { Antialias = false }); Properties Antialias Gets a value indicating whether edges are antialiased: each pixel gets its exact covered area. When false, a pixel is drawn fully when its center is inside and not at all otherwise, for pixel art and masks that must stay binary. Defaults to true. public bool Antialias { get; init; } Property Value bool BlendMode Gets how the paint combines with the pixels under it. Defaults to SourceOver. public BlendMode BlendMode { get; init; } Property Value BlendMode Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The value is not defined. Blur Gets a blur of the shape's coverage, applied before the paint is: a soft-edged shape, or with Outer a glow around it. It applies to shapes, paths and text, not to images. null (the default) draws sharp edges. public MaskBlur? Blur { get; init; } Property Value MaskBlur? Dither Gets a value indicating whether colors are dithered when they are rounded to 8 bits: a 4×4 ordered pattern of less than half a level is added before rounding, which hides the banding of large soft gradients and never changes a flat area of an exact level. Only shaded paints on 8-bit targets dither; solid paints and deeper targets do not. Defaults to false, as in Skia. public bool Dither { get; init; } Property Value bool LocalMatrix Gets the transform from the paint's own coordinates to the canvas's local coordinates, applied before the canvas transform. A gradient's points, an image's pixels and noise's lattice are in paint coordinates, so this stretches a radial gradient into an ellipse or turns a pattern. A matrix that cannot be inverted draws nothing. A solid paint ignores it. Defaults to the identity. public Matrix3x2 LocalMatrix { get; init; } Property Value Matrix3x2 Exceptions ArgumentException An element is not finite. Opacity Gets the paint's opacity, 0 to 1, which multiplies its alpha. Defaults to 1. public float Opacity { get; init; } Property Value float Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The value is outside 0 to 1. Overprint Gets which plates the paint prints on an ink canvas, as PDF's overprint: Off (the default) paints every plate, knocking out what is below; On only the inks the colour names; NonZero as On, leaving the plates of a CMYK colour's zero components alone (PDF's overprint mode 1). RGB canvases ignore it, as PDF viewers do by default. public Overprint Overprint { get; init; } Property Value Overprint Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The value is not defined. Methods WithColorMatrix(ColorMatrix) Returns a paint that runs a color matrix on this paint's colors, as Skia's color-filtered shader: each color, with straight alpha, goes through the matrix and is clamped to 0 to 1. A solid paint gives a solid paint of the transformed color. public Paint WithColorMatrix(ColorMatrix matrix) Parameters matrix ColorMatrix The matrix, as Egami's ColorMatrix operation uses it. Returns Paint The new paint, with this paint's blend mode, opacity, antialiasing, dithering and blur. Operators implicit operator Paint(Rgba8) Converts a color to a SolidPaint. public static implicit operator Paint(Rgba8 color) Parameters color Rgba8 The color. Returns Paint implicit operator Paint(RgbaF32) Converts a float color to a SolidPaint. public static implicit operator Paint(RgbaF32 color) Parameters color RgbaF32 The color. Returns Paint

api/Egami.Drawing.Patch.html.title: Class Patch | Egami
api/Egami.Drawing.Patch.html.summary: Class Patch Namespace Egami.Drawing Assembly Egami.Drawing.dll A curved four-sided surface with a color, value or texture coordinate at each corner, for DrawPatch(Patch, Paint?, BlendMode, ReadOnlySpan<GradientStop>): PDF's Coons and tensor-product patch shadings (types 6 and 7) and Skia's drawPatch. The surface's parameters u (left to right) and v (top to bottom) run from 0 to 1; corner data is interpolated bilinearly in them. Immutable. Corners are in the order top-left (u 0, v 0), top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left. A Coons patch's 12 points go clockwise from the top-left corner, as Skia's: the top curve left to right (points 0 to 3), the right curve down (3 to 6), the bottom curve right to left (6 to 9) and the left curve up (9, 10, 11, 0). A tensor patch's 16 points are its net row by row, top row first, each row left to right. public sealed class Patch Inheritance object Patch Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // A Coons patch: four cubic edges, clockwise from the top-left corner, and a color at each corner. Vector2[] edges = [ new(20, 20), new(80, 0), new(150, 40), new(220, 20), // top, left to right new(200, 80), new(240, 140), new(220, 180), // right, down new(150, 160), new(80, 200), new(20, 180), // bottom, right to left new(40, 120), new(0, 60), // left, up ]; Patch patch = Patch.Coons(edges, [new RgbaF32(1, 0, 0, 1), new RgbaF32(1, 1, 0, 1), new RgbaF32(0, 0, 1, 1), new RgbaF32(0, 1, 0, 1)]); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = raster.CreateCanvas()) { canvas.DrawPatch(patch); // PDF's function-based shadings give each corner a value instead, mapped through a gradient's stops. Patch shaded = Patch.Tensor(patch.ToTensorNet().Span, cornerValues: [0, 0.3f, 1, 0.6f]); canvas.Translate(10, 10); canvas.Scale(0.3f); canvas.DrawPatch(shaded, valueStops: [new GradientStop(0, Rgba8.Black), new GradientStop(1, Rgba8.White)]); } Properties Bounds Gets the bounds of the control points, which hold the whole surface. public RectF Bounds { get; } Property Value RectF CornerColors Gets the corner colors, or empty when there are none: for a patch with inks, their appearances in sRGB. public ReadOnlyMemory<RgbaF32> CornerColors { get; } Property Value ReadOnlyMemory<RgbaF32> CornerInks Gets the corner colours as inks, or empty when the patch has none (see WithInks(ReadOnlySpan<InkColor>)). public ReadOnlyMemory<InkColor> CornerInks { get; } Property Value ReadOnlyMemory<InkColor> CornerTexCoords Gets the corner texture coordinates, or empty when there are none. public ReadOnlyMemory<Vector2> CornerTexCoords { get; } Property Value ReadOnlyMemory<Vector2> CornerValues Gets the corner values, or empty when there are none. public ReadOnlyMemory<float> CornerValues { get; } Property Value ReadOnlyMemory<float> Kind Gets which surface the patch is. public PatchKind Kind { get; } Property Value PatchKind Points Gets the control points: 12 for a Coons patch, 16 for a tensor patch, in the orders the class describes. public ReadOnlyMemory<Vector2> Points { get; } Property Value ReadOnlyMemory<Vector2> Methods Coons(ReadOnlySpan<Vector2>, ReadOnlySpan<RgbaF32>, ReadOnlySpan<Vector2>, ReadOnlySpan<float>) Creates a Coons patch from its four boundary curves. public static Patch Coons(ReadOnlySpan<Vector2> points, ReadOnlySpan<RgbaF32> cornerColors = default, ReadOnlySpan<Vector2> cornerTexCoords = default, ReadOnlySpan<float> cornerValues = default) Parameters points ReadOnlySpan<Vector2> The 12 boundary points, clockwise from the top-left corner. cornerColors ReadOnlySpan<RgbaF32> Four straight-alpha corner colors, or empty. cornerTexCoords ReadOnlySpan<Vector2> Four corner points in the paint's coordinates, or empty. cornerValues ReadOnlySpan<float> Four corner values, mapped through the stops given to DrawPatch(Patch, Paint?, BlendMode, ReadOnlySpan<GradientStop>), or empty. Returns Patch The patch. Examples // A Coons patch: four cubic edges, clockwise from the top-left corner, and a color at each corner. Vector2[] edges = [ new(20, 20), new(80, 0), new(150, 40), new(220, 20), // top, left to right new(200, 80), new(240, 140), new(220, 180), // right, down new(150, 160), new(80, 200), new(20, 180), // bottom, right to left new(40, 120), new(0, 60), // left, up ]; Patch patch = Patch.Coons(edges, [new RgbaF32(1, 0, 0, 1), new RgbaF32(1, 1, 0, 1), new RgbaF32(0, 0, 1, 1), new RgbaF32(0, 1, 0, 1)]); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = raster.CreateCanvas()) { canvas.DrawPatch(patch); // PDF's function-based shadings give each corner a value instead, mapped through a gradient's stops. Patch shaded = Patch.Tensor(patch.ToTensorNet().Span, cornerValues: [0, 0.3f, 1, 0.6f]); canvas.Translate(10, 10); canvas.Scale(0.3f); canvas.DrawPatch(shaded, valueStops: [new GradientStop(0, Rgba8.Black), new GradientStop(1, Rgba8.White)]); } Exceptions ArgumentException There are not 12 points or four of each corner list, both colors and values are given, or a number is not finite. Evaluate(float, float) Returns the point of the surface at parameters (u, v). public Vector2 Evaluate(float u, float v) Parameters u float The horizontal parameter, 0 to 1. v float The vertical parameter, 0 to 1. Returns Vector2 The point, in the canvas's local coordinates. Tensor(ReadOnlySpan<Vector2>, ReadOnlySpan<RgbaF32>, ReadOnlySpan<Vector2>, ReadOnlySpan<float>) Creates a tensor-product patch from its 4×4 net. public static Patch Tensor(ReadOnlySpan<Vector2> points, ReadOnlySpan<RgbaF32> cornerColors = default, ReadOnlySpan<Vector2> cornerTexCoords = default, ReadOnlySpan<float> cornerValues = default) Parameters points ReadOnlySpan<Vector2> The 16 points, row by row from the top, each row left to right. cornerColors ReadOnlySpan<RgbaF32> Four straight-alpha corner colors, or empty. cornerTexCoords ReadOnlySpan<Vector2> Four corner points in the paint's coordinates, or empty. cornerValues ReadOnlySpan<float> Four corner values, or empty. Returns Patch The patch. Exceptions ArgumentException There are not 16 points or four of each corner list, both colors and values are given, or a number is not finite. ToTensorNet() Returns the patch's 4×4 tensor net. A Coons patch's inner points come from its boundary as PDF section 8.7.4.5.8 gives them, so the tensor patch of that net is the same surface. public ReadOnlyMemory<Vector2> ToTensorNet() Returns ReadOnlyMemory<Vector2> The 16 points, row by row from the top. WithInks(ReadOnlySpan<InkColor>) Returns this patch with its four corner colours given as inks: an ink canvas blends their tints across the surface (an ink a corner does not name counts as 0 there); other canvases use the appearances in sRGB, which become CornerColors. public Patch WithInks(ReadOnlySpan<InkColor> cornerInks) Parameters cornerInks ReadOnlySpan<InkColor> Four corner colours, in the order of CornerColors. Returns Patch The new patch. Exceptions ArgumentException There are not four, or the patch has corner values. ArgumentNullException A colour is null.

api/Egami.Drawing.Path.html.title: Class Path | Egami
api/Egami.Drawing.Path.html.summary: Class Path Namespace Egami.Drawing Assembly Egami.Drawing.dll An outline of contours made of lines, quadratic and cubic Bézier curves, with the FillRule that says which points it covers when filled. A path never changes after it is built, so one path can be drawn from many threads and kept by any canvas backend. Coordinates are float pixels, y down. Build one with PathBuilder or a shape helper such as Circle(Vector2, float). public sealed class Path Inheritance object Path Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Examples // A path is built once and never changes, so it can be drawn many times and from many threads. Path heart = new PathBuilder() .MoveTo(150, 60) .CubicTo(150, 30, 100, 20, 90, 60) .CubicTo(80, 100, 130, 130, 150, 160) .CubicTo(170, 130, 220, 100, 210, 60) .CubicTo(200, 20, 150, 30, 150, 60) .Close() .ToPath(); canvas.FillPath(heart, Rgba8.Red); // SVG's arc command, and the even-odd rule: an inner contour becomes a hole. Path frame = new PathBuilder() .AddRect(new RectF(10, 10, 60, 60)) .AddCircle(new Vector2(40, 40), 20) .MoveTo(10, 120) .ArcTo(radii: new Vector2(30, 20), rotationDegrees: 0, largeArc: false, clockwise: true, end: new Vector2(70, 120)) .Close() .ToPath(FillRule.EvenOdd); canvas.FillPath(frame, Rgba8.Black); bool hit = heart.Contains(new Vector2(150, 100)); // hit testing on the curves themselves RectF box = heart.TightBounds; // curves measured at their extremes Properties Bounds Gets the bounds of every point, control points included: cheap, and never smaller than the outline. public RectF Bounds { get; } Property Value RectF Contours Gets the contours, each as a path of its own with this path's fill rule. public IReadOnlyList<Path> Contours { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<Path> Empty Gets a path with no contours. public static Path Empty { get; } Property Value Path FillRule Gets which points the path covers when filled. public FillRule FillRule { get; } Property Value FillRule IsConvex Gets a value indicating whether the path is one convex contour: every turn goes the same way and it winds around once. A path that is a line, a point or empty counts as convex. public bool IsConvex { get; } Property Value bool IsEmpty Gets a value indicating whether the path draws nothing: it has no line or curve. public bool IsEmpty { get; } Property Value bool Points Gets the points, in order: one for each move and line, two for each quadratic and three for each cubic. public ReadOnlySpan<Vector2> Points { get; } Property Value ReadOnlySpan<Vector2> TightBounds Gets the exact bounds of the outline: curves are measured at their extremes, not their control points. public RectF TightBounds { get; } Property Value RectF Verbs Gets the commands, in order. public ReadOnlySpan<PathVerb> Verbs { get; } Property Value ReadOnlySpan<PathVerb> Methods Apply(PathEffect) Returns the path an effect makes of this one, such as its dashes or its corners rounded. public Path Apply(PathEffect effect) Parameters effect PathEffect The effect. Returns Path The new path. Examples // A hand-drawn chart line: jittered the same way on every run, then its corners rounded. Path data = Path.Polygon([new(10, 80), new(50, 30), new(90, 60), new(130, 20), new(170, 50)], close: false); PathEffect sketchy = PathEffect.Jitter(segmentLength: 6, deviation: 1.5f, seed: 7).Then(PathEffect.Corner(3)); using Raster<Rgba8> chart = Raster.Create(180, 100, Rgba8.White); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = chart.CreateCanvas()) { canvas.StrokePath(data, new Stroke(2) { Effect = sketchy }, new Rgba8(40, 40, 40, 255)); // Dots along the line, and hatching inside a circle. canvas.FillPath(data.Apply(PathEffect.Stamp(Path.Circle(Vector2.Zero, 2), advance: 12, style: StampStyle.Translate)), Rgba8.Black); canvas.FillPath(Path.Circle(new Vector2(150, 75), 20).Apply(PathEffect.Hatch(Matrix3x2.CreateScale(1, 5) * Matrix3x2.CreateRotation(0.6f), width: 1)), Rgba8.Black); } // A line that draws itself: trim it to a growing fraction of its length, frame by frame. Path frame30 = data.Apply(PathEffect.Trim(0, 0.3f)); Arc(RectF, float, float) Creates the open arc of an ellipse; 0 degrees is the right end of the horizontal axis and positive angles turn clockwise. public static Path Arc(RectF oval, float startDegrees, float sweepDegrees) Parameters oval RectF The rectangle the ellipse fills. startDegrees float Where the arc starts. sweepDegrees float How far it turns, at most a full turn either way. Returns Path The path. Circle(Vector2, float) Creates a circle, clockwise. public static Path Circle(Vector2 center, float radius) Parameters center Vector2 The center. radius float The radius. Returns Path The path. Combine(IEnumerable<Path>, PathOp, float) Combines any number of paths with one operation in a single pass, as if it were applied in order, left to right: ((a op b) op c) and so on. Far faster than chaining Op(Path, PathOp, float) for many paths, since every outline is cut and sorted once. The result is as Op(Path, PathOp, float) describes. public static Path Combine(IEnumerable<Path> paths, PathOp op, float tolerance = 0.05) Parameters paths IEnumerable<Path> The paths; each keeps its own fill rule. op PathOp The operation. tolerance float How close, in path units, points must be to count as the same, as Op(Path, PathOp, float) describes. Returns Path The combined path; empty when there are no paths. Examples // A frame: one round rectangle cut out of another, kept as curves, so a PDF or SVG backend writes it exactly. Path frame = Path.RoundRect(new RoundRect(new RectF(0, 0, 200, 140), 24)) .Difference(Path.RoundRect(new RoundRect(new RectF(20, 20, 160, 100), 12))); // Many shapes in one pass, applied left to right; overlaps and self-intersections removed; an area grown by 4 units. Path dots = Path.Combine([Path.Circle(new Vector2(40, 40), 30), Path.Circle(new Vector2(80, 40), 30), Path.Circle(new Vector2(60, 75), 30)], PathOp.Union); Path clean = Path.Star(new Vector2(50, 50), 45, 20, 5).Simplify(); Path halo = dots.Inflate(4, LineJoin.Round); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException op is not defined, or tolerance is not positive and finite. Contains(Vector2) Returns whether the filled path covers a point, by the winding number of the outline itself, curves included, and the fill rule. Open contours count as closed. A point exactly on the outline counts as inside, as in Skia. public bool Contains(Vector2 point) Parameters point Vector2 The point. Returns bool true if the point is covered. Difference(Path, float) Returns the area of this path without the other, as Op(Path, PathOp, float) describes. public Path Difference(Path other, float tolerance = 0.05) Parameters other Path The path to cut away. tolerance float How close points must be to count as the same. Returns Path The difference. Inflate(float, LineJoin, float) Returns the area grown outwards by a distance, or for a negative distance shrunk inwards: the union of the path and the outline of a pen twice the distance wide, or the difference. Corners grow by the join: round keeps the distance everywhere, miter keeps them sharp up to the miter limit. Open contours count as closed, as fills close them. The grown or cut parts are straight pieces within a hundredth of the distance (at most a tenth of a unit); the rest keeps its curves. public Path Inflate(float distance, LineJoin join = LineJoin.Round, float miterLimit = 4) Parameters distance float How far to grow; negative to shrink. join LineJoin How grown corners look. miterLimit float The longest miter, in multiples of twice the distance, as MiterLimit defines it. Returns Path The offset path, simplified; empty when it shrinks away. Examples // A frame: one round rectangle cut out of another, kept as curves, so a PDF or SVG backend writes it exactly. Path frame = Path.RoundRect(new RoundRect(new RectF(0, 0, 200, 140), 24)) .Difference(Path.RoundRect(new RoundRect(new RectF(20, 20, 160, 100), 12))); // Many shapes in one pass, applied left to right; overlaps and self-intersections removed; an area grown by 4 units. Path dots = Path.Combine([Path.Circle(new Vector2(40, 40), 30), Path.Circle(new Vector2(80, 40), 30), Path.Circle(new Vector2(60, 75), 30)], PathOp.Union); Path clean = Path.Star(new Vector2(50, 50), 45, 20, 5).Simplify(); Path halo = dots.Inflate(4, LineJoin.Round); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException A value is not finite, join is not defined, or miterLimit is below 1. Intersect(Path, float) Returns the area of both this path and the other, as Op(Path, PathOp, float) describes. public Path Intersect(Path other, float tolerance = 0.05) Parameters other Path The other path. tolerance float How close points must be to count as the same. Returns Path The intersection. Line(Vector2, Vector2) Creates a straight line, for stroking. public static Path Line(Vector2 start, Vector2 end) Parameters start Vector2 Where it starts. end Vector2 Where it ends. Returns Path The path. Op(Path, PathOp, float) Combines this path's area with another's. Each keeps its own fill rule; open contours count as closed, as fills close them. The result keeps the inputs' lines, quadratics and cubics, split exactly where outlines cross, so it is exact for PDF and SVG output; its outer contours run clockwise on screen and its holes counterclockwise, with the nonzero fill rule, and none of them cross. public Path Op(Path other, PathOp op, float tolerance = 0.05) Parameters other Path The other path. op PathOp The operation. tolerance float How close, in path units, points must be to count as the same: crossings are found to well within it, and ends, crossings and curves closer than it merge, which keeps nearly touching or overlapping outlines from making slivers. A caller who will draw the result ten times larger passes a tenth of it. Returns Path The combined path. Examples // A frame: one round rectangle cut out of another, kept as curves, so a PDF or SVG backend writes it exactly. Path frame = Path.RoundRect(new RoundRect(new RectF(0, 0, 200, 140), 24)) .Difference(Path.RoundRect(new RoundRect(new RectF(20, 20, 160, 100), 12))); // Many shapes in one pass, applied left to right; overlaps and self-intersections removed; an area grown by 4 units. Path dots = Path.Combine([Path.Circle(new Vector2(40, 40), 30), Path.Circle(new Vector2(80, 40), 30), Path.Circle(new Vector2(60, 75), 30)], PathOp.Union); Path clean = Path.Star(new Vector2(50, 50), 45, 20, 5).Simplify(); Path halo = dots.Inflate(4, LineJoin.Round); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException op is not defined, or tolerance is not positive and finite. Oval(RectF) Creates the ellipse that fills a rectangle, clockwise. public static Path Oval(RectF bounds) Parameters bounds RectF The rectangle. Returns Path The path. ParseSvg(ReadOnlySpan<char>, FillRule, bool) Reads SVG path data, the grammar of an SVG d attribute (SVG 1.1 and SVG 2): every command (M, L, H, V, C, S, Q, T, A, Z and their relative forms), implicit repeats, compact numbers such as 0.5.5 and arc flags without separators. Arcs become cubic curves, as ArcTo(Vector2, float, bool, bool, Vector2) makes them. Empty or blank data is an empty path. public static Path ParseSvg(ReadOnlySpan<char> data, FillRule fillRule = FillRule.NonZero, bool lenient = false) Parameters data ReadOnlySpan<char> The path data. fillRule FillRule The fill rule of the path; SVG's fill-rule is not part of the data. lenient bool Whether to keep every complete command before the first error instead of throwing, as SVG tells renderers to draw a path with an error in it. Returns Path The path. Examples // An icon from SVG path data, drawn four times larger, and written back as compact relative data. Path heart = Path.ParseSvg("M12 21.35l-1.45-1.32C5.4 15.36 2 12.28 2 8.5 2 5.42 4.42 3 7.5 3c1.74 0 3.41.81 4.5 2.09" + "C13.09 3.81 14.76 3 16.5 3 19.58 3 22 5.42 22 8.5c0 3.78-3.4 6.86-8.55 11.54L12 21.35z"); string d = heart.Transform(Matrix3x2.CreateScale(4)).ToSvg(new SvgPathFormat { Relative = true, Compact = true }); // Untrusted data: TryParseSvg says whether it is valid; lenient keeps what comes before an error, as browsers draw it. bool valid = Path.TryParseSvg("M0 0 L10 10 L20", out Path? strict); Path drawn = Path.ParseSvg("M0 0 L10 10 L20", lenient: true); try { Path.ParseSvg("M0 0 X"); } catch (SvgPathException e) { Console.WriteLine($"{e.Problem} at character {e.Position}"); } Exceptions SvgPathException The data breaks the grammar and lenient is false. ArgumentOutOfRangeException fillRule is not defined. api/Egami.Drawing.PathBuilder.html.summary: Class PathBuilder Namespace Egami.Drawing Assembly Egami.Drawing.dll Builds a Path one command at a time. Arcs, ovals and round corners become cubic curves as they are added, so a path holds only lines, quadratics and cubics. A line or curve with no contour open starts one at the last contour's start (or the origin), as SVG and Skia do. Building takes time in proportion to the points added; ToPath(FillRule) copies them, so the builder can go on or be reused. public sealed class PathBuilder Inheritance object PathBuilder Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // A path is built once and never changes, so it can be drawn many times and from many threads. Path heart = new PathBuilder() .MoveTo(150, 60) .CubicTo(150, 30, 100, 20, 90, 60) .CubicTo(80, 100, 130, 130, 150, 160) .CubicTo(170, 130, 220, 100, 210, 60) .CubicTo(200, 20, 150, 30, 150, 60) .Close() .ToPath(); canvas.FillPath(heart, Rgba8.Red); // SVG's arc command, and the even-odd rule: an inner contour becomes a hole. Path frame = new PathBuilder() .AddRect(new RectF(10, 10, 60, 60)) .AddCircle(new Vector2(40, 40), 20) .MoveTo(10, 120) .ArcTo(radii: new Vector2(30, 20), rotationDegrees: 0, largeArc: false, clockwise: true, end: new Vector2(70, 120)) .Close() .ToPath(FillRule.EvenOdd); canvas.FillPath(frame, Rgba8.Black); bool hit = heart.Contains(new Vector2(150, 100)); // hit testing on the curves themselves RectF box = heart.TightBounds; // curves measured at their extremes Constructors PathBuilder() Initializes a new instance of the PathBuilder class, empty. public PathBuilder() Properties CurrentPoint Gets the point the next command starts from: the last point added, or the contour's start after Close(). public Vector2 CurrentPoint { get; } Property Value Vector2 IsEmpty Gets a value indicating whether nothing has been added. public bool IsEmpty { get; } Property Value bool Methods AddArc(RectF, float, float) Adds the arc of an ellipse as a new open contour: from startDegrees through sweepDegrees, where 0 is the right end of the horizontal axis and positive angles turn clockwise on screen. A sweep beyond ±360 degrees draws the whole ellipse once. public PathBuilder AddArc(RectF oval, float startDegrees, float sweepDegrees) Parameters oval RectF The rectangle the ellipse fills. startDegrees float Where the arc starts. sweepDegrees float How far it turns. api/Egami.Drawing.PathEffect.html.summary: Class PathEffect Namespace Egami.Drawing Assembly Egami.Drawing.dll Turns one path into another before it is filled or stroked: dashes, rounded corners, trimming, jitter, shapes stamped along the path, hatching. Effects are immutable, so one can be shared and reused; Then(PathEffect) and Plus(PathEffect) combine them. Apply one with Apply(PathEffect), or set it on Effect to have the canvas apply it before stroking. The set is Skia's: dash, corner, trim, discrete, 1D path, 2D line and 2D path effects, composed and summed. public abstract record PathEffect : IEquatable<PathEffect> Inheritance object PathEffect Implements IEquatable<PathEffect> Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // A hand-drawn chart line: jittered the same way on every run, then its corners rounded. Path data = Path.Polygon([new(10, 80), new(50, 30), new(90, 60), new(130, 20), new(170, 50)], close: false); PathEffect sketchy = PathEffect.Jitter(segmentLength: 6, deviation: 1.5f, seed: 7).Then(PathEffect.Corner(3)); using Raster<Rgba8> chart = Raster.Create(180, 100, Rgba8.White); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = chart.CreateCanvas()) { canvas.StrokePath(data, new Stroke(2) { Effect = sketchy }, new Rgba8(40, 40, 40, 255)); // Dots along the line, and hatching inside a circle. canvas.FillPath(data.Apply(PathEffect.Stamp(Path.Circle(Vector2.Zero, 2), advance: 12, style: StampStyle.Translate)), Rgba8.Black); canvas.FillPath(Path.Circle(new Vector2(150, 75), 20).Apply(PathEffect.Hatch(Matrix3x2.CreateScale(1, 5) * Matrix3x2.CreateRotation(0.6f), width: 1)), Rgba8.Black); } // A line that draws itself: trim it to a growing fraction of its length, frame by frame. Path frame30 = data.Apply(PathEffect.Trim(0, 0.3f)); Methods Corner(float) Returns an effect that rounds every corner between two straight lines with a quadratic curve that starts and ends radius from the corner (less on lines shorter than twice that), as Skia's corner effect does. Corners next to curves stay sharp. public static PathEffect Corner(float radius) Parameters radius float How far from each corner the rounding starts; 0 leaves the path as it is. Returns PathEffect The effect. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException radius is negative or not finite. Dash(DashPattern) Returns an effect that cuts a path into dashes, for paths that are filled or shapes that are not stroked; a stroke's own Dash is better for strokes, since vector backends keep it as data. public static PathEffect Dash(DashPattern pattern) Parameters pattern DashPattern The dashes. Returns PathEffect The effect. Hatch(Matrix3x2, float) Returns an effect that hatches the area a path covers with parallel lines, as Skia's 2D line effect does: the lines are the rows through the centers of a lattice's cells (y = ½, 1½ and so on, and below), mapped into the path's space by lattice, cut where they leave the area by its fill rule. With a width, each line is outlined to it, so the result is filled; with width 0 the lines are left open, for a stroke to draw. public static PathEffect Hatch(Matrix3x2 lattice, float width = 0) Parameters lattice Matrix3x2 The transform from lattice space, where rows are a unit apart, into the path's space: a scale sets the spacing, a rotation the angle. width float The width of the lines, or 0 for open lines. Returns PathEffect The effect. Exceptions ArgumentException lattice cannot be inverted. ArgumentOutOfRangeException width is negative or not finite. HatchPath(Matrix3x2, Path) Returns an effect that stamps a shape at every point of a lattice inside the area a path covers, as Skia's 2D path effect does. The result is the shapes, filled by the shape's fill rule. public static PathEffect HatchPath(Matrix3x2 lattice, Path shape) Parameters lattice Matrix3x2 The transform from lattice space, where the points are the centers of the unit cells (x and y at a half), into the path's space. shape Path The shape, around its own origin, placed at each point. Returns PathEffect The effect. Exceptions ArgumentException lattice cannot be inverted. Jitter(float, float, ulong) Returns an effect that cuts each contour into straight pieces about segmentLength long and moves their ends across the path by up to deviation, for a hand-drawn look, as Skia's discrete effect does. The moves are a hash of the seed, the contour and the point, so the same path gives the same result on every thread and machine. public static PathEffect Jitter(float segmentLength, float deviation, ulong seed = 0) Parameters segmentLength float The length of the pieces. deviation float The largest move, either way. seed ulong The seed; another seed gives other moves. Returns PathEffect The effect. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException segmentLength is not positive, or a value is not finite. Plus(PathEffect) Returns an effect that draws the results of this one and of other together, as Skia's sum effect does. public PathEffect Plus(PathEffect other) Parameters other PathEffect The other effect. Returns PathEffect The combined effect. Stamp(Path, float, float, StampStyle) Returns an effect that repeats a shape along each contour, every advance units, as Skia's 1D path effect does. The result is the shapes, filled by the shape's fill rule. public static PathEffect Stamp(Path shape, float advance, float phase = 0, StampStyle style = StampStyle.Translate) Parameters shape Path The shape, around its own origin, which goes on the path. advance float The distance between copies. phase float How far into the repeat each contour starts, as a dash pattern's phase is (and as Skia and PostScript read it): the first copy goes at the advance less the phase, modulo the advance. style StampStyle How each copy is placed. Returns PathEffect The effect. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException advance is not positive, or a value is not finite or defined. Then(PathEffect) Returns an effect that applies this one and then next to its result, as Skia's compose effect does. public PathEffect Then(PathEffect next) Parameters next PathEffect The effect applied second. Returns PathEffect The combined effect. Trim(float, float, bool) Returns an effect that keeps the part of a path between two fractions of its total length, all contours counted in order, as Skia's trim effect does: animate the end from 0 to 1 and the path draws itself. public static PathEffect Trim(float start, float end, bool inverted = false) Parameters start float Where the kept part starts, from 0 to 1. end float Where it ends, from 0 to 1; nothing is kept when it is not after start. inverted bool Whether to keep the rest instead. Returns PathEffect The effect. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException start or end is outside 0 to 1.
