api/Egami.Drawing.PathMeasure.html.summary: Class PathMeasure Namespace Egami.Drawing Assembly Egami.Drawing.dll Measures a path: the length of each contour, and the point, direction and pieces at any distance along it. Lengths are exact to about 1e-4 units, curves included: each curve's length is integrated by adaptive Gauss–Legendre quadrature, and a distance is turned back into a point on the curve by Newton steps, so long curves do not gather the errors of a flattened outline. Contours of zero length are left out, as Skia's SkContourMeasureIter leaves them. Measuring is done once, here; the queries are cheap and safe from many threads. public sealed class PathMeasure Inheritance object PathMeasure Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // Measure a path: its length, and a point and direction at any distance, curves included. Path route = new PathBuilder().MoveTo(10, 90).CubicTo(60, 0, 140, 160, 190, 60).ToPath(); PathMeasure measure = new(route); ContourMeasure contour = measure.Contours[0]; Vector2 halfway = contour.GetPosition(contour.Length / 2); Vector2 heading = contour.GetTangent(contour.Length / 2); // An arrowhead placed at the end, turned along the path, and the middle third as a path of its own (still a cubic). Path arrow = Path.Polygon([new(-6, -4), new(0, 0), new(-6, 4)]).Transform(contour.GetMatrix(contour.Length)); Path middle = contour.GetSegment(contour.Length / 3, 2 * contour.Length / 3); Constructors PathMeasure(Path, bool) Initializes a new instance of the PathMeasure class. public PathMeasure(Path path, bool forceClosed = false) Parameters path Path The path. forceClosed bool Whether to measure open contours as if closed, with the line back to their start. Properties Contours Gets the contours that have a length, in the path's order. public IReadOnlyList<ContourMeasure> Contours { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<ContourMeasure> TotalLength Gets the length of all the contours together. public float TotalLength { get; } Property Value float

api/Egami.Drawing.PathOp.html.title: Enum PathOp | Egami
api/Egami.Drawing.PathOp.html.summary: Enum PathOp Namespace Egami.Drawing Assembly Egami.Drawing.dll How Op(Path, PathOp, float) and Combine(IEnumerable<Path>, PathOp, float) combine the areas of two paths: Skia's five operations. public enum PathOp Fields Difference = 0 The first area without the second. Intersect = 1 Where both areas are. ReverseDifference = 4 The second area without the first. Union = 2 Where either area is. Xor = 3 Where exactly one of the areas is. Examples // A frame: one round rectangle cut out of another, kept as curves, so a PDF or SVG backend writes it exactly. Path frame = Path.RoundRect(new RoundRect(new RectF(0, 0, 200, 140), 24)) .Difference(Path.RoundRect(new RoundRect(new RectF(20, 20, 160, 100), 12))); // Many shapes in one pass, applied left to right; overlaps and self-intersections removed; an area grown by 4 units. Path dots = Path.Combine([Path.Circle(new Vector2(40, 40), 30), Path.Circle(new Vector2(80, 40), 30), Path.Circle(new Vector2(60, 75), 30)], PathOp.Union); Path clean = Path.Star(new Vector2(50, 50), 45, 20, 5).Simplify(); Path halo = dots.Inflate(4, LineJoin.Round);

api/Egami.Drawing.PathVerb.html.title: Enum PathVerb | Egami
api/Egami.Drawing.PathVerb.html.summary: Enum PathVerb Namespace Egami.Drawing Assembly Egami.Drawing.dll One drawing command of a Path; the comment on each says how many points it takes. public enum PathVerb : byte Fields Close = 4 Closes the contour with a line back to its start; takes no point. Cubic = 3 A cubic Bézier curve: two control points and the end point. Line = 1 A straight line to one point. Move = 0 Starts a contour at one point. Quad = 2 A quadratic Bézier curve: one control point and the end point. Examples // A path is built once and never changes, so it can be drawn many times and from many threads. Path heart = new PathBuilder() .MoveTo(150, 60) .CubicTo(150, 30, 100, 20, 90, 60) .CubicTo(80, 100, 130, 130, 150, 160) .CubicTo(170, 130, 220, 100, 210, 60) .CubicTo(200, 20, 150, 30, 150, 60) .Close() .ToPath(); canvas.FillPath(heart, Rgba8.Red); // SVG's arc command, and the even-odd rule: an inner contour becomes a hole. Path frame = new PathBuilder() .AddRect(new RectF(10, 10, 60, 60)) .AddCircle(new Vector2(40, 40), 20) .MoveTo(10, 120) .ArcTo(radii: new Vector2(30, 20), rotationDegrees: 0, largeArc: false, clockwise: true, end: new Vector2(70, 120)) .Close() .ToPath(FillRule.EvenOdd); canvas.FillPath(frame, Rgba8.Black); bool hit = heart.Contains(new Vector2(150, 100)); // hit testing on the curves themselves RectF box = heart.TightBounds; // curves measured at their extremes

api/Egami.Drawing.Picture.html.title: Class Picture | Egami
api/Egami.Drawing.Picture.html.summary: Class Picture Namespace Egami.Drawing Assembly Egami.Drawing.dll Recorded canvas calls, from a PictureRecorder or Load(Stream, EgamiContext?): replay them on any canvas with DrawPicture(Picture, Matrix3x2?, Paint?, bool) or Playback(Canvas), fill shapes with them through a PicturePaint, render them with ToRaster<TPixel>(float, CanvasOptions?, EgamiContext?), or keep them in an .egdr file with Save(Stream). Replay is always vector, so a picture stays sharp at any scale. Immutable, and safe to replay on several threads and canvases at once. public sealed class Picture Inheritance object Picture Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // Record any picture code once... PictureRecorder recorder = new(new RectF(0, 0, 40, 40)); DrawLogo(recorder); Picture logo = recorder.Finish(); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = raster.CreateCanvas()) { // ...and replay it anywhere, at any scale, still sharp: replay is vector. canvas.DrawPicture(logo, Matrix3x2.CreateTranslation(10, 10)); canvas.DrawPicture(logo, Matrix3x2.CreateScale(4) * Matrix3x2.CreateTranslation(60, 10)); // A paint with an opacity merges the whole picture as one layer. canvas.DrawPicture(logo, Matrix3x2.CreateTranslation(240, 10), new SolidPaint(Rgba8.White) { Opacity = 0.4f }); // Drawn many times at one scale, a cached image is cheaper than replaying. for (int i = 0; i < 6; i++) { canvas.DrawPicture(logo, Matrix3x2.CreateTranslation(230 + (i * 25), 150), cacheAsImage: true); } } using Raster<Rgba8> icon = logo.ToRaster<Rgba8>(scale: 2); Properties Bounds Gets the picture's bounds in its own coordinates, as the recorder was given them. public RectF Bounds { get; } Property Value RectF CallCount Gets the number of recorded calls, saves and transforms included; nested pictures count as one. public int CallCount { get; } Property Value int Methods Load(Stream, EgamiContext?) Reads an Egami picture file. The file is untrusted input: its images go through the PNG reader with the context's SafetyLimits, what it decodes counts toward MaxTotalBytes, and pictures may nest 64 deep and replay at most 50 million calls with nested pictures expanded. public static Picture Load(Stream stream, EgamiContext? context = null) Parameters stream Stream The stream to read from, to its end. context EgamiContext The context whose limits apply, or null for the default. Returns Picture The picture. Examples // Keep a picture in Egami's own documented format, and load it later; a loaded file is untrusted, so the context's // safety limits apply. using (FileStream file = File.Create("logo.egdr")) { logo.Save(file); } Picture loaded; using (FileStream file = File.OpenRead("logo.egdr")) { loaded = Picture.Load(file); } Exceptions UnsupportedFormatException The data is not an .egdr file, or is a major version this reader does not know. CorruptDataException The file is damaged. LimitExceededException The file is larger, or nests deeper, than the limits allow. Playback(Canvas) Replays the calls on a canvas through its public calls, between a Save() and a Restore(); recorded transforms apply after the canvas's transform at the start. public void Playback(Canvas canvas) Parameters canvas Canvas The canvas. Examples // Record any picture code once... PictureRecorder recorder = new(new RectF(0, 0, 40, 40)); DrawLogo(recorder); Picture logo = recorder.Finish(); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = raster.CreateCanvas()) { // ...and replay it anywhere, at any scale, still sharp: replay is vector. canvas.DrawPicture(logo, Matrix3x2.CreateTranslation(10, 10)); canvas.DrawPicture(logo, Matrix3x2.CreateScale(4) * Matrix3x2.CreateTranslation(60, 10)); // A paint with an opacity merges the whole picture as one layer. canvas.DrawPicture(logo, Matrix3x2.CreateTranslation(240, 10), new SolidPaint(Rgba8.White) { Opacity = 0.4f }); // Drawn many times at one scale, a cached image is cheaper than replaying. for (int i = 0; i < 6; i++) { canvas.DrawPicture(logo, Matrix3x2.CreateTranslation(230 + (i * 25), 150), cacheAsImage: true); } } using Raster<Rgba8> icon = logo.ToRaster<Rgba8>(scale: 2); Save(Stream) Writes the picture as an Egami picture file (.egdr), Egami's own documented binary format: a signature and version, then chunks that a reader skips when it does not know them. Images are kept as PNG (so a float image is kept at 16 bits), paths and numbers as 32-bit floats, nested pictures once however often they are used, and text as its outlines, since a file holds no fonts. A picture that loads back replays the same calls and draws the same pixels, except that text comes back as outline fills, which the raster backend draws as paths rather than from its glyph cache. public void Save(Stream stream) Parameters stream Stream The stream to write to. Examples // Keep a picture in Egami's own documented format, and load it later; a loaded file is untrusted, so the context's // safety limits apply. using (FileStream file = File.Create("logo.egdr")) { logo.Save(file); } Picture loaded; using (FileStream file = File.OpenRead("logo.egdr")) { loaded = Picture.Load(file); } Exceptions NotSupportedException A call holds C# code a file cannot: a CustomPaint, or a layer's filter, backdrop or soft mask. The message gives the call's index. Nothing is written in that case. ToRaster<TPixel>(float, CanvasOptions?, EgamiContext?) Renders the picture's Bounds into a new raster, over transparency. public Raster<TPixel> ToRaster<TPixel>(float scale = 1, CanvasOptions? options = null, EgamiContext? context = null) where TPixel : unmanaged, IPixelType<TPixel> Parameters scale float Raster pixels per picture unit. options CanvasOptions The canvas settings, or null for the defaults. context EgamiContext The context the raster is made in, or null for the default. Returns Raster<TPixel> A raster of the bounds' size times the scale, rounded up. Type Parameters TPixel The raster's pixel type. Examples // Record any picture code once... PictureRecorder recorder = new(new RectF(0, 0, 40, 40)); DrawLogo(recorder); Picture logo = recorder.Finish(); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = raster.CreateCanvas()) { // ...and replay it anywhere, at any scale, still sharp: replay is vector. canvas.DrawPicture(logo, Matrix3x2.CreateTranslation(10, 10)); canvas.DrawPicture(logo, Matrix3x2.CreateScale(4) * Matrix3x2.CreateTranslation(60, 10)); // A paint with an opacity merges the whole picture as one layer. canvas.DrawPicture(logo, Matrix3x2.CreateTranslation(240, 10), new SolidPaint(Rgba8.White) { Opacity = 0.4f }); // Drawn many times at one scale, a cached image is cheaper than replaying. for (int i = 0; i < 6; i++) { canvas.DrawPicture(logo, Matrix3x2.CreateTranslation(230 + (i * 25), 150), cacheAsImage: true); } } using Raster<Rgba8> icon = logo.ToRaster<Rgba8>(scale: 2); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException scale is not positive and finite, or the raster would be too large.

api/Egami.Drawing.PicturePaint.html.summary: Class PicturePaint Namespace Egami.Drawing Assembly Egami.Drawing.dll A Picture as a paint: a tiling pattern, the shape of PDF's and SVG's tiling patterns and Skia's picture shader. The Tile rectangle of the picture, in its own coordinates, is repeated by TileX and TileY under LocalMatrix and the canvas transform. The raster backend renders one tile at the device scale the paint is drawn at and keeps it with the picture, so a pattern stays sharp when zoomed and is rendered once for repeated fills at one scale. A tile is at most 4096 pixels a side. public sealed record PicturePaint : Paint, ITextPaint, IEquatable<Paint>, IEquatable<PicturePaint> Inheritance object Paint PicturePaint Implements ITextPaint IEquatable<Paint> IEquatable<PicturePaint> Inherited Members Paint.BlendMode Paint.Opacity Paint.Antialias Paint.LocalMatrix Paint.Dither Paint.Overprint Paint.Blur Paint.WithColorMatrix(ColorMatrix) object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // A tile drawn once as vectors fills any shape, repeated, and stays sharp when the canvas is zoomed. api/Egami.Drawing.PixelGeometry.html.summary: Enum PixelGeometry Namespace Egami.Drawing Assembly Egami.Drawing.dll The order of a display's color subpixels, which LCD text edging needs to know. public enum PixelGeometry Fields BgrHorizontal = 2 Blue, green and red stripes from left to right. BgrVertical = 4 Blue, green and red stripes from top to bottom. RgbHorizontal = 1 Red, green and blue stripes from left to right, the common LCD layout. RgbVertical = 3 Red, green and blue stripes from top to bottom, as on a rotated display. Unknown = 0 Not known: LCD edging falls back to grayscale. Examples ParagraphStyle style = new() { DefaultStyle = new TextStyle { FontFamilies = [family], Size = 18, Color = new Rgba8(30, 30, 60, 255), Shadows = [new TextShadow(new System.Numerics.Vector2(1, 1), 2, new Rgba8(0, 0, 0, 80))], }, Align = TextAlign.Justify, }; // One call: wrap into a box, centred across the lines. TextLayout layout = Paragraph.Create("Laid out once, drawn many times.", style).Layout(300); canvas.DrawTextLayout(layout, new System.Numerics.Vector2(10, 110), visibleRect: new RectF(0, 0, 320, 200)); // Inline placeholders (an icon, a badge) are drawn by a painter called with each one's box. canvas.DrawTextLayout(layout, new System.Numerics.Vector2(10, 130), placeholderPainter: (c, index, box) => c.FillRoundRect(new RoundRect(box, 3), new Rgba8(200, 60, 40, 255))); // The same text as one path: glyphs and decorations. Examples using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = raster.CreateCanvas()) { // Group opacity: the overlapping circles fade as one shape, with no darker overlap. canvas.SaveLayer(0.5f); canvas.FillCircle(new Vector2(80, 100), 60, new Rgba8(200, 30, 30, 255)); canvas.FillCircle(new Vector2(140, 100), 60, new Rgba8(200, 30, 30, 255)); canvas.Restore(); // A group blended with Multiply and blurred as a whole; the layer grows by the blur's reach, so nothing is cut. canvas.SaveLayer(new LayerOptions { BlendMode = BlendMode.Multiply, Filter = ops => ops.Blur(4) }); canvas.FillRect(new RectF(180, 40, 90, 120), new Rgba8(40, 120, 220, 255)); canvas.FillCircle(new Vector2(225, 100), 30, Rgba8.White); canvas.Restore(); } Remarks Allocates the layer over the options' bounds inside the clip, grown by the filter's reach (the whole bounds, or the raster, when the reach is unknown), and starts it transparent, as a copy of the backdrop, or as the filtered backdrop. api/Egami.Drawing.html.title: Namespace Egami.Drawing | Egami
api/Egami.Drawing.html.summary: Namespace Egami.Drawing Classes Annotation A link or a destination for DrawAnnotation(RectF, Annotation): what a document backend writes, and pixels never show. BlendPaint Two paints combined pixel by pixel with a blend mode, as Skia's blend shader: Source is blended onto Destination, and the result is what this paint draws. Each part keeps its own LocalMatrix and Opacity (its blend mode, blur and dithering are not used), inside this paint's own local matrix. Canvas A surface to draw paths, shapes, strokes and images on, through a current transform and clip. The canvas itself is abstract: RasterCanvas<TPixel> draws into pixels, and other backends (a PDF page, a recorder) keep the calls as vectors. Every public call is checked and tracked here (the transform, the clip bounds, the save stack) and then ends in exactly one protected On hook, which is all a backend overrides; hooks added in later versions get default bodies, so adding them never breaks a backend. Coordinates are float pixels, y down; the pixel at (0, 0) covers the square from 0 to 1. Calls draw when they are made. A canvas is for one thread at a time; one large call may still spread its rows over several cores. CanvasOptions Settings for a raster canvas. ColorMatrixPaint Another paint with a color matrix run on its colors, as Skia's color-filtered shader: each color, unpremultiplied, goes through the matrix, is clamped to 0 to 1 and is premultiplied again. WithColorMatrix(ColorMatrix) makes one. ConicalGradient A gradient between two circles, as the HTML canvas's createRadialGradient, Skia's two-point conical gradient and a PDF type 3 shading define it: for each t, the circle whose center and radius are t of the way from the start circle to the end one; a pixel takes the largest t whose circle passes through it with a radius of at least 0. It covers a focal point inside a circle (a start radius of 0), one circle inside the other, and cones drawn on one side only. ContourMeasure One measured contour of a PathMeasure. Distances run from 0 at the contour's start to Length at its end; distances outside are clamped to them, as in Skia. CustomPaint A paint whose colors come from C# code: override Shade(int, int, Span<PremulRgbaF32>, in Matrix3x2) to fill a row of premultiplied float colors. Rows are shaded in parallel bands, so Shade(int, int, Span<PremulRgbaF32>, in Matrix3x2) must be thread-safe and must give a pixel the same color whichever band or thread asks; then the result is the same at any core count. A backend that keeps vectors, such as a PDF page, cannot run C# and draws the call through its raster fallback instead. Derive a record class from it. DashPattern The dashes of a stroke: lengths of drawn and skipped stretches in turn, in path units, and where in the pattern each contour starts, as PDF's d, SVG's stroke-dasharray and stroke-dashoffset, and Skia's dash effect define them. An odd number of lengths repeats once to make an even one, as SVG says, and a pattern whose lengths add up to 0 draws a solid line. Each dash is an open piece of the path that follows its curves and gets the stroke's caps; the pattern starts afresh on each contour. DrawingExtensions Ways into a canvas from Egami's rasters and operation chains. EncodedImage An image kept as its file's bytes, such as a JPEG, for DrawImage(EncodedImage, RectF, SamplingOptions?, Paint?): a backend that can store the bytes as they are, as a PDF page stores a JPEG as DCTDecode, gets them through OnDrawEncodedImage without decoding and encoding again; every other backend draws the decoded pixels. The bytes are probed when the image is made and decoded at most once, on first need. Immutable and thread-safe. FallbackImage A drawing call rendered into pixels by Canvas.RasterizeFallback, for a backend to place as an image. FontExtensions Glyphs and text as Paths in canvas units, y down, for clipping, stroking or measuring them as shapes. GlyphCache The process-wide cache of glyph coverage masks the raster canvas draws small text from: one mask per typeface (each variation position its own), glyph, device em size, axis scales, subpixel phase, edging, hinting and synthesis, for glyphs up to 256 device pixels per em under a scale-and-translate transform. Masks hold one byte per pixel, or three for LCD edging. Bigger, rotated or skewed glyphs fill as paths and are not cached. Masks are rendered by the same rasterizer as paths and drawn at the same rounded positions either way, so the cache changes speed, never pixels. Shared by every canvas on every thread; least recently used masks go first when the budget is spent. Gradient A paint whose color changes along a line, around a center or between two circles by its stops. Each pixel center maps back through the canvas transform and LocalMatrix to a position t along the gradient, which Tile brings into 0 to 1 and the stops turn into a color. On 8-bit targets t picks one of 1024 colors made once per paint; float and 16-bit targets mix the stops exactly. GradientInterpolation How a gradient mixes its stops: the color space, as CSS Color 4 defines them, and for Oklch the way around the hue circle. ImagePaint An image as a paint: shapes are filled with the image's pixels, pixel (0, 0) covering the paint-space square from 0 to 1, under LocalMatrix and the canvas transform. TileX and TileY say what lies past its edges, so it tiles as a pattern, and Decal leaves the outside transparent, as image masks and stencils need. When the paint shrinks the image, sampling reads the nearest smaller level of a MipChain. InkCanvas A canvas that draws into an InkRaster's plates: printing inks instead of RGB. It shares RasterCanvas<TPixel>'s rasterizer, clips and layers, so shapes, strokes and text cover exactly the same pixels; where the RGB canvas blends colours, this one sets each plate. A paint's Ink prints its inks by name (inks the raster lacks through their appearance into the process inks); RGB colours, gradients and images convert into the process inks through RgbSource and the ink set's profile. InkCanvasOptions How an InkCanvas turns colours that are not inks into its process inks. Lattice A grid over an image for DrawImageLattice(Raster, Lattice, RectF, SamplingOptions?, Paint?), as Skia's lattice: the x and y divisions cut the image into columns and rows that alternate fixed and stretchable, starting with fixed, so a division at the image's left or top edge makes the first column or row stretchable. Fixed columns and rows keep their size when the destination is large enough and shrink in proportion when it is not; stretchable ones share what is left. A nine-patch is the lattice with two divisions each way. LayerOptions How a layer started by SaveLayer(LayerOptions?) is merged at the matching Restore(): filtered, masked, faded by Opacity and blended into what lies below with BlendMode, through the clip. A layer is what PDF calls a transparency group. LinearGradient A gradient along a line: t is 0 on the line through Start square to it, and 1 through End. MarkedContent A tag that brackets a run of drawing for a document backend, as PDF's marked content (BMC, BDC and EMC): a structure element of tagged PDF (a paragraph, a heading, a figure), an artifact such as a page number, or a span with replacement text. Mesh Triangles with an optional color, texture coordinate or value at each vertex, for DrawMesh(Mesh, Paint?, BlendMode, ReadOnlySpan<GradientStop>): Gouraud-shaded triangles, textured triangles (a paint mapped through the texture coordinates) and PDF's free-form and lattice-form shadings (one value per vertex, mapped through gradient stops). Immutable: the constructor copies what it is given. NinePatch An image with its Lattice, as Android's nine-patch (.9.png) files hold them. NoisePaint Procedural noise as a paint. Fractal(float, float, int, int, Size?) and Turbulence(float, float, int, int, Size?) follow SVG 1.1's feTurbulence step by step (its random table, lattice and gradients), so the pixels match Skia's noise shaders and browsers within rounding; Simplex(float, int, int, Size?) is smoother and can tile. Each of the four channels is its own noise, straight alpha included. The noise lives in paint coordinates: it scales and turns with the canvas transform and LocalMatrix. Paint What a drawing call puts on the canvas, and how it combines with what is there: the colors (from the subclass), the BlendMode, an Opacity, whether edges are antialiased, and for shapes an optional Blur. The kinds are SolidPaint, the gradients (LinearGradient, RadialGradient, ConicalGradient, SweepGradient), ImagePaint, NoisePaint, BlendPaint, ColorMatrixPaint and CustomPaint. A color converts to a solid paint where a paint is expected. A paint is an ITextPaint, so a paragraph's text style can carry it. A paint other than a solid one has its own coordinates: LocalMatrix maps them into the canvas's local coordinates, so a gradient or an image turns and scales with the canvas transform, and further with its own matrix. Patch A curved four-sided surface with a color, value or texture coordinate at each corner, for DrawPatch(Patch, Paint?, BlendMode, ReadOnlySpan<GradientStop>): PDF's Coons and tensor-product patch shadings (types 6 and 7) and Skia's drawPatch. The surface's parameters u (left to right) and v (top to bottom) run from 0 to 1; corner data is interpolated bilinearly in them. Immutable. Corners are in the order top-left (u 0, v 0), top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left. A Coons patch's 12 points go clockwise from the top-left corner, as Skia's: the top curve left to right (points 0 to 3), the right curve down (3 to 6), the bottom curve right to left (6 to 9) and the left curve up (9, 10, 11, 0). A tensor patch's 16 points are its net row by row, top row first, each row left to right. Path An outline of contours made of lines, quadratic and cubic Bézier curves, with the FillRule that says which points it covers when filled. A path never changes after it is built, so one path can be drawn from many threads and kept by any canvas backend. Coordinates are float pixels, y down. Build one with PathBuilder or a shape helper such as Circle(Vector2, float). PathBuilder Builds a Path one command at a time. Arcs, ovals and round corners become cubic curves as they are added, so a path holds only lines, quadratics and cubics. A line or curve with no contour open starts one at the last contour's start (or the origin), as SVG and Skia do. Building takes time in proportion to the points added; ToPath(FillRule) copies them, so the builder can go on or be reused. PathEffect Turns one path into another before it is filled or stroked: dashes, rounded corners, trimming, jitter, shapes stamped along the path, hatching. Effects are immutable, so one can be shared and reused; Then(PathEffect) and Plus(PathEffect) combine them. Apply one with Apply(PathEffect), or set it on Effect to have the canvas apply it before stroking. The set is Skia's: dash, corner, trim, discrete, 1D path, 2D line and 2D path effects, composed and summed. PathMeasure Measures a path: the length of each contour, and the point, direction and pieces at any distance along it. Lengths are exact to about 1e-4 units, curves included: each curve's length is integrated by adaptive Gauss–Legendre quadrature, and a distance is turned back into a point on the curve by Newton steps, so long curves do not gather the errors of a flattened outline. Contours of zero length are left out, as Skia's SkContourMeasureIter leaves them. Measuring is done once, here; the queries are cheap and safe from many threads. Picture Recorded canvas calls, from a PictureRecorder or Load(Stream, EgamiContext?): replay them on any canvas with DrawPicture(Picture, Matrix3x2?, Paint?, bool) or Playback(Canvas), fill shapes with them through a PicturePaint, render them with ToRaster<TPixel>(float, CanvasOptions?, EgamiContext?), or keep them in an .egdr file with Save(Stream). Replay is always vector, so a picture stays sharp at any scale. Immutable, and safe to replay on several threads and canvases at once. PicturePaint A Picture as a paint: a tiling pattern, the shape of PDF's and SVG's tiling patterns and Skia's picture shader. The Tile rectangle of the picture, in its own coordinates, is repeated by TileX and TileY under LocalMatrix and the canvas transform. The raster backend renders one tile at the device scale the paint is drawn at and keeps it with the picture, so a pattern stays sharp when zoomed and is rendered once for repeated fills at one scale. A tile is at most 4096 pixels a side. PictureRecorder A canvas that records instead of picture: every hook call is kept with its arguments, and Finish() returns them as an immutable Picture to replay on any canvas, at any scale, as often as needed, as Skia's SkPictureRecorder. Any code that draws on a Canvas can draw into it. Paths, paints, images and nested pictures are kept by reference: images must not change while the picture is in use. RadialGradient A gradient in circles around a center: t is the distance from Center divided by Radius. RasterCanvas<TPixel> The raster backend: a canvas that draws into a raster's pixels, with exact-area antialiasing, blended through Egami's Compositor in the pixel type's own precision. A clip that is a pixel-aligned rectangle stays a rectangle; any other clip becomes a coverage mask over the clip's bounds. A call whose area exceeds 256 KiB of destination rows spreads its rows over up to MaxParallelism cores, with the same pixels at any core count. A layer from SaveLayer(LayerOptions?) is premultiplied in the raster's class (PremulRgba8 for 8-bit rasters, PremulRgbaF32 for deeper ones) and covers only its bounds inside the clip, grown by its filter's reach; its memory comes from the raster's EgamiContext and is released at Restore(). ShadowOptions The light and colors of DrawShadow(Path, ShadowOptions?), after Skia's shadow model (the Material Design one): a shape lifted Elevation above the canvas casts an ambient shadow, blurred by its height, and a spot shadow from a round light at LightPosition, moved away from the light and blurred by the light's size. SoftMask A mask made by drawing, as a PDF soft mask: Draw runs on a canvas of its own with the layer's transform and clip, and its alpha, or its luminosity over Backdrop, through the optional Transfer curve, multiplies the layer. A luminosity mask of a white shape on black shows the layer only inside the shape. SolidPaint One color everywhere, with straight alpha. The color keeps float precision, so float and 16-bit targets get it in full; values outside 0 to 1 are kept on the paint, and the blend clamps them as Egami's Compositor does. Stroke How a path is outlined: the pen's width, caps, joins and miter limit. The settings travel with the drawing call as data, so a vector backend can write them as they are (PDF's w, J, j and M). The pen is applied in the canvas's local space and then transformed, so a non-uniform scale gives an elliptical pen, as in PDF, SVG and Skia. SvgPathException Thrown by ParseSvg(ReadOnlySpan<char>, FillRule, bool) when SVG path data breaks the grammar. SvgPathFormat How ToSvg(SvgPathFormat?) writes SVG path data. SweepGradient A gradient around a center, as Skia's sweep gradient and CSS's conic-gradient: t goes from 0 at StartAngle to 1 at EndAngle, in degrees clockwise (on a y-down screen) from the positive x axis. TextOnPathOptions How ShapeOnPath(Font, string, Path, TextOnPathOptions?) lays text along a path. Structs CornerRadii The x and y radius of each corner of a RoundRect, clockwise from the top-left. A radius below 0 counts as 0, and a corner with either radius 0 is square. GradientStop One color of a gradient at a position along it, from 0 (the start) to 1 (the end). Two stops at the same offset make a hard edge: the later one applies from that offset on. A gradient whose first stop is after 0 or whose last is before 1 repeats the nearest stop's color to the end, as CSS does. MaskBlur A Gaussian blur of a shape's coverage before the paint is applied, as Skia's blur mask filter: Sigma is in device pixels, so it does not scale with the canvas transform. Set it as Blur. Egami blurs with its fast blur; an axis-aligned rectangle with Normal is computed exactly from the error function, which is faster still. RectF A rectangle in float pixels, y down: the left edge at X, the top at Y. A width or height of 0 or less makes it empty. Pixel (0, 0) covers the square from (0, 0) to (1, 1), so a rectangle with whole-number edges covers whole pixels. RoundRect A rectangle with an x and y radius per corner. Radii that would overlap are scaled down together, as CSS and Skia do: every radius is multiplied by the smallest ratio of a side's length to the sum of the two radii along it, when that ratio is below 1. A radius below 0 counts as 0, and a corner with either radius 0 is square. SpriteTransform A sprite's placement in DrawAtlas(Raster, ReadOnlySpan<SpriteTransform>, ReadOnlySpan<RectF>, ReadOnlySpan<RgbaF32>, BlendMode, SamplingOptions?, RectF?, Paint?), as Skia's RSXform: a rotation with a uniform scale, then a move. A point (x, y) of the sprite, measured from its source rectangle's top-left corner, goes to (ScaleCos·x − ScaleSin·y + Tx, ScaleSin·x + ScaleCos·y + Ty). Interfaces IColorGlyphRenderer Draws color glyphs of a format Egami.Drawing does not draw itself, such as the SVG documents of an OpenType SVG table (Egami.Svg's SvgGlyphRenderer). Set on ColorGlyphRenderer, it is asked first for every glyph whose font has that format, except where the font has a COLR version 1 glyph, so the order is COLR v1, the renderer, COLR v0, sbix, CBDT, then the outline. Contexts are immutable and safe to share. Change one with a with expression. public sealed record EgamiContext : IEquatable<EgamiContext> Inheritance object EgamiContext Implements IEquatable<EgamiContext> Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples var context = EgamiContext.Default with { Limits = SafetyLimits.Default with { MaxPixels = 100_000_000 }, MaxParallelism = 4, }; Properties Default Gets the context used when a call passes none. The first read fixes it: SetDefault(EgamiContext) works only before that. public static EgamiContext Default { get; } Property Value EgamiContext DiagnosticLevel Gets the lowest level Diagnostics receives. Defaults to Warning; events below it are never built. public DiagnosticLevel DiagnosticLevel { get; init; } Property Value DiagnosticLevel Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The value set is not a defined level. Diagnostics Gets the handler that receives Egami's warnings and notable decisions, or null (the default) for none, which costs nothing. It runs inline, possibly on several decode threads at once, so it must be quick and thread-safe. An exception it throws fails the call, which turns warnings into errors. Warnings a load raises arrive in Warnings order as the call ends; Info and Debug events arrive as they happen. One id is delivered at most 10 times per call, then once more as a count of the rest. public Action<EgamiDiagnostic>? Diagnostics { get; init; } Property Value Action<EgamiDiagnostic> Examples // With Microsoft.Extensions.Logging: one line at startup sends every call's warnings to the app's log, with the id as // a property to filter and count on. Egami itself has no logging dependency. Defaults to PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, BMP, QOI, PNM, TIFF, JBIG2, JPEG 2000 and TGA. public IReadOnlyList<FormatInfo> Formats { get; init; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<FormatInfo> Limits Gets the safety limits applied when reading. Defaults to Default. public SafetyLimits Limits { get; init; } Property Value SafetyLimits Exceptions ArgumentNullException The value set is null. MaxParallelism Gets the most threads one operation may use. 1 means fully sequential. Defaults to the processor count. public int MaxParallelism { get; init; } Property Value int Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The value set is less than 1. Memory Gets the source of all pixel memory. Defaults to Shared. public IPixelMemorySource Memory { get; init; } Property Value IPixelMemorySource Exceptions ArgumentNullException The value set is null. Methods SetDefault(EgamiContext) Replaces Default, once, at startup, so that format plugins, memory sources and limits apply to every call that passes no context. public static void SetDefault(EgamiContext context) Parameters context EgamiContext The context to use as the default. Exceptions InvalidOperationException Default was already read or set. StartDiagnostics() Starts reporting for one call outside Egami's own loads and saves, such as a video decode or a plug-in's own entry point, with the same DiagnosticLevel filter and per-id cap. Dispose it when the call ends. public DiagnosticReporter StartDiagnostics() Returns DiagnosticReporter A reporter for the call; a shared one that does nothing when Diagnostics is null. Examples // A decoder outside Egami (a video demuxer, a format plug-in's own entry point) reports through the same handler, with the // same level filter and the same cap of 10 per id per call. Dispose the reporter when the call ends. using (DiagnosticReporter diagnostics = context.StartDiagnostics()) { if (diagnostics.IsEnabled(DiagnosticLevel.Warning)) { diagnostics.Report(DiagnosticLevel.Warning, "Avi.IndexRebuilt", "The index was missing; it was rebuilt from the frames.", offset: 4096); } diagnostics.Report(DiagnosticLevel.Info, "Mjpeg.DhtInserted", "Frames have no Huffman tables; the standard ones were used."); } WithFormat(FormatInfo) Returns a copy of this context with format registered. Examples // A caption on a photo: white text with a dark shadow, its baseline 24 pixels above the bottom. using Raster<Rgba8> photo = Raster.Create(640, 360, new Rgba8(90, 120, 160, 255)); var font = new Font(Typeface.FromFile(FontFile), 28); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = photo.CreateCanvas()) { var origin = new Vector2(24, photo.Height - 24); canvas.DrawText("Lofoten, March", origin + new Vector2(2, 2), font, new Rgba8(0, 0, 0, 160)); canvas.DrawText("Lofoten, March", origin, font, Rgba8.White); } Remarks There is no DPI: a 12-unit font on a raster is 12 pixels per em, and the canvas transform scales it like any other drawing. Use FromPoints(Typeface, float, float) to size from points at a resolution. default(Font) has no typeface: its Typeface is null, its Scale 0, and the members that need the face (metrics, advances, shaping and measuring) throw InvalidOperationException. Create fonts with the constructor or FromPoints(Typeface, float, float). Measures text as Shape(string, ShapingOptions?) lays it out, as MeasureText(string, ShapingOptions?) does, without making a string of it: a slice of a larger text or a buffer you reuse. public TextMeasure MeasureText(ReadOnlySpan<char> text, ShapingOptions? options = null) Parameters text ReadOnlySpan<char> The text. options ShapingOptions The shaping options, as for Shape(string, ShapingOptions?); span ranges index text. Returns TextMeasure The widest line's advance, the exact ink bounds, the line count and the vertical metrics. Examples // Measure each word of a longer text in place: a span is measured without making a string of it. ReadOnlySpan<char> text = "Measure every word of this sentence"; float widest = 0; foreach (Range word in text.Split(' ')) { widest = Math.Max(widest, font.MeasureText(text[word]).Advance); } Exceptions ArgumentException options asks for fallback or a span in another font. InvalidOperationException The font is default(Font), which has no typeface. MeasureText(string, ShapingOptions?) Measures text as Shape(string, ShapingOptions?) lays it out, so a measured width always equals the drawn advance. public TextMeasure MeasureText(string text, ShapingOptions? options = null) Parameters text string The text. options ShapingOptions The shaping options, as for Shape(string, ShapingOptions?). Returns TextMeasure The widest line's advance, the exact ink bounds, the line count and the vertical metrics. Examples // A label shrunk until it fits a 200-pixel button, then centred on it. const string label = "Download the full report"; var box = new RectF(20, 20, 200, 40); var font = new Font(face, 24); while (font.MeasureText(label).Advance > box.Width - 16 && font.Size > 8) { font = new Font(face, font.Size - 1); } TextMeasure size = font.MeasureText(label); var origin = new Vector2( box.X + ((box.Width - size.Advance) / 2), box.Y + ((box.Height - size.Height) / 2) + size.Ascent); using Raster<Rgba8> image = Raster.Create(240, 80, Rgba8.White); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = image.CreateCanvas()) { canvas.FillRoundRect(new RoundRect(box, 8), new Rgba8(30, 90, 200, 255)); canvas.DrawText(label, origin, font, Rgba8.White); } Exceptions ArgumentNullException text is null. ArgumentException options asks for fallback or a span in another font. InvalidOperationException The font is default(Font), which has no typeface. Shape(string, ShapingOptions?) Turns text into a glyph run with the full shaper (Shape(string, Font, ShapingOptions?)): ligatures, kerning, marks and the script rules of the font's GSUB and GPOS, bidi order, one glyph run for every line. \n, \r\n, \r, U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029 start a new line one LineHeight lower at x = 0 (a vertical line one LineHeight to the left); other control characters give no glyph; characters the face lacks give .notdef. public GlyphRun Shape(string text, ShapingOptions? options = null) Parameters text string The text. options ShapingOptions The direction, language, script, features and spans, or null for Default. Returns GlyphRun The run, with the text and a cluster per glyph; positions are relative to the first baseline's left end, y down. api/Egami.Fonts.FontCollection.html.summary: Class FontCollection Namespace Egami.Fonts Assembly Egami.Fonts.dll A set of faces grouped into families: the caller's own, or System for the fonts installed on the machine. Finds families by name and faces by style with the CSS Fonts Level 4 matching steps. public sealed class FontCollection : IReadOnlyCollection<FontFamily>, IEnumerable<FontFamily>, IEnumerable Inheritance object FontCollection Implements IReadOnlyCollection<FontFamily> IEnumerable<FontFamily> IEnumerable Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // Installed fonts, found without native calls and indexed on first use; a style is matched by the CSS rules. FontMatch? match = FontCollection.System.Match(GenericFamily.SansSerif, FontStyle.Bold); // Your own fonts work the same way; System is read-only, so add the installed fonts to your collection to have both. var fonts = new FontCollection(); fonts.AddFile(FontFile); fonts.AddSystemFonts(); FontMatch noto = fonts.Match("Noto Sans", FontStyle.BoldItalic)!.Value; Font font = noto.ToFont(16); Remarks Faces group under their typographic family (name ID 16, else 1). A name lookup tries, in order, the typographic family, the legacy family (ID 1), the full name (ID 4) and the PostScript name (ID 6), comparing case-insensitively in every language the fonts hold. A name not found returns null or false: nothing is swapped in silently. Files added by path are indexed from their name and OS/2 tables only and loaded when a face is matched. Adding is thread-safe; lookups see the faces added before they started. Constructors FontCollection(FontLoadOptions?) Initializes an empty collection. public FontCollection(FontLoadOptions? options = null) Parameters options FontLoadOptions How faces are loaded when matched, or null for Default. Examples // Installed fonts, found without native calls and indexed on first use; a style is matched by the CSS rules. FontMatch? match = FontCollection.System.Match(GenericFamily.SansSerif, FontStyle.Bold); // Your own fonts work the same way; System is read-only, so add the installed fonts to your collection to have both. var fonts = new FontCollection(); fonts.AddFile(FontFile); fonts.AddSystemFonts(); FontMatch noto = fonts.Match("Noto Sans", FontStyle.BoldItalic)!.Value; Font font = noto.ToFont(16); Properties Count Gets the number of families. public int Count { get; } Property Value int Families Gets the families, sorted by name. public IReadOnlyList<FontFamily> Families { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<FontFamily> Options Gets the options faces are loaded with. public FontLoadOptions Options { get; } Property Value FontLoadOptions System Gets the fonts installed on this machine, found without native calls by scanning the platform's font directories (Windows: the Windows and per-user Fonts folders; macOS: the System, Library and user Fonts folders; Linux: the fontconfig dir entries and the usual share/fonts folders). Indexed on first use; Refresh() rescans. It is read-only: to match your own fonts beside the installed ones, call AddSystemFonts() on a collection of your own. public static FontCollection System { get; } Property Value FontCollection Methods Add(Typeface) Adds a loaded face. public void Add(Typeface typeface) Parameters typeface Typeface The face. Exceptions InvalidOperationException The collection is System, which is read-only. Returns int The number of faces added. Exceptions DirectoryNotFoundException The directory does not exist. InvalidOperationException The collection is System, which is read-only. AddFile(string) Adds every face of a font file, indexed from its names and loaded when matched. public int AddFile(string path) Parameters path string A .ttf, .otf, .ttc, .otc, .woff or .woff2 file; a web font is decompressed and loaded at once. Returns int The number of faces added. Exceptions UnsupportedFormatException The file is not a TrueType or OpenType font or collection. CorruptDataException The file's headers cannot be read. InvalidOperationException The collection is System, which is read-only. AddSystemFonts() Adds the installed fonts, as System has indexed them (indexing them first if it has not yet), so they can be matched beside your own. The faces load with this collection's Options; Refresh() on System later does not change them. public int AddSystemFonts() Returns int The number of faces added. api/Egami.Fonts.FontEdging.html.summary: Enum FontEdging Namespace Egami.Fonts Assembly Egami.Fonts.dll How a glyph's edges are turned into pixels. public enum FontEdging Fields Alias = 1 One bit per pixel: a pixel is covered when its centre is inside the outline (nonzero rule). Antialias = 0 Grayscale antialiasing: each pixel covered by the share of its area inside the outline. api/Egami.Fonts.Layout.WordBreak.html.summary: Enum WordBreak Namespace Egami.Fonts.Layout Assembly Egami.Fonts.dll Where breaks may fall inside words (CSS word-break). public enum WordBreak Fields BreakAll = 1 Letters and digits of any script break like ideographs, between any two. Normal = 0 Unicode's rules: words break at spaces and punctuation, ideographs between any two. Examples // Where lines may end: after spaces and hyphens, and always at the end; a line must end after a newline. api/Egami.Fonts.Layout.WritingMode.html.summary: Enum WritingMode Namespace Egami.Fonts.Layout Assembly Egami.Fonts.dll Whether lines run horizontally or vertically (CSS writing-mode). public enum WritingMode Fields HorizontalTb = 0 Horizontal lines stacked downwards. VerticalLr = 2 Vertical lines stacked left to right, as Mongolian. VerticalRl = 1 Vertical lines stacked right to left, as Chinese and Japanese books. Examples // Font families come from a collection; later families cover what the first lacks. FontCollection fonts = new(); fonts.AddFile(System.IO.Path.Combine(folder, "NotoSans-Regular.ttf")); fonts.AddFile(System.IO.Path.Combine(folder, "NotoSansArabic-Regular.ttf")); fonts.TryGetFamily("Noto Sans", out FontFamily latin); fonts.TryGetFamily("Noto Sans Arabic", out FontFamily arabic); // Styles nest: the inner span keeps the outer one's size and adds a color and an underline. RichText text = new RichTextBuilder() .Append("Peace is ") .Push(new TextStyle { Size = 20 }) .Append("\u0633\u0644\u0627\u0645 ") .Push(new TextStyle { Color = new Rgba8(200, 30, 30, 255), Decoration = new TextDecoration() }) .Append("in Arabic") .Pop() .Pop() .AddPlaceholder(new Placeholder(16, 16, PlaceholderAlignment.Middle)) .ToRichText(); ParagraphStyle style = new() { DefaultStyle = new TextStyle { FontFamilies = [latin, arabic], Size = 16, LineHeight = LineHeight.Multiple(1.4f) }, Align = TextAlign.Justify, LineBreaking = new LineBreakOptions(WordBreak: WordBreak.Normal), }; // Shaped once: lay it out at any width later. api/Egami.Fonts.Layout.html.title: Namespace Egami.Fonts.Layout | Egami
api/Egami.Fonts.Layout.html.summary: Namespace Egami.Fonts.Layout Classes DecorationShape One decoration line over a decorated stretch of one text line: an underline, overline or line-through at one position and thickness for the whole stretch (the lowest underline and thickest line among its fonts, as CSS), cut where glyphs cross an underline or overline when SkipInk is Auto. LayoutRun A piece of a line: glyphs of one font and bidi level, or a placeholder, tab or break. LineBreaks Finds where lines may break: Unicode's line breaking algorithm (UAX #14, Unicode 17.0) from Egami's own tables, with CSS Text 3's word-break and line-break switches. No shaping is involved, and there are no dictionaries: Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar break only at spaces and zero width spaces. LineFlow Lays a paragraph out one line at a time, each at its own width, so text can flow across columns and pages or around images; Layout(float) is built on it. Not thread-safe; make one per flow. Paragraph A paragraph of styled text, prepared once to be laid out at any width: styles resolved, bidi levels and break opportunities found, text itemized into runs and each run shaped. Immutable and safe to share between threads. ParagraphStyle How a paragraph is laid out: its default text style, direction, alignment, line breaking, line filling, hyphens, ellipsis and line limits, line box rules, tabs and writing mode. The defaults follow CSS: start-aligned, greedy filling, normal line height, tab stops every 8 spaces, horizontal lines. RichText Text with styles: a string, the StyleSpans over it (sorted, never overlapping) and the Placeholders for its object replacement characters, in order. Immutable; build one with RichTextBuilder. RichTextBuilder Builds a RichText: Push(TextStyle) a style, Append(string) text, Pop() back to the enclosing style. Styles nest: a pushed style's unset fields come from the one it is pushed on, and the result has one flat span per stretch of equal style. Strut A minimum line box every line has, from a font and a line height (CSS's strut), or with Force the exact line box, for line grids in forms and columns. TextDecoration Lines drawn with text (CSS Text Decoration 4). TextLayout A paragraph laid out at a width: its lines of glyph runs and the size of its layout box. Positions are in canvas units relative to the box's top-left corner, y down; nothing is rounded to pixels. Immutable and safe to share between threads. TextLine One line of a laid-out paragraph: the text it holds, its line box and its runs in visual order. Coordinates are the layout box's, or for a line from a LineFlow, the line's own box with its top at 0. TextStyle How a stretch of text looks. Every field is optional: an unset field takes the enclosing builder style's, then the paragraph's DefaultStyle, then Egami's default (16 pixels, black, normal line height, no decoration). Fields that change shaping (fonts, size, style, variations, language, features, letter spacing) split a paragraph into separately shaped runs; the others (colors, paints, background, decoration, shadows) never do, so a color change inside a ligature keeps the ligature. Structs Caret Where a caret is drawn: the primary segment, and at a bidi boundary, where the position touches text of both directions, a secondary segment at the other text's edge. CaretLine A caret segment across the line: vertical in horizontal layouts, horizontal in vertical ones. DecorationSegment A piece of a decoration line along a text line: its left and right x. LineBreak A place where a line may or must end. LineBreakEnumerator Enumerates line break opportunities; get one from Enumerate(ReadOnlySpan<char>, LineBreakOptions). LineBreakOptions How text may break into lines, as CSS Text 3 sets it: word-break, overflow-wrap, line-break and the content language. The default is CSS's default: Unicode's line breaking algorithm (UAX #14) with breaks before small kana, as browsers break. LineHeight The height a run asks of its line box (CSS line-height): Normal from the font's metrics, a Multiple(float) of the font size or an Absolute(float) height. The extra over the font's ascent and descent is split half above and half below. Placeholder An inline box laid out with the text, such as an icon or an image, which the caller draws: it stands for an object replacement character (U+FFFC) in the text, so bidi, line breaking and indexes treat it as one character. StyleSpan A text style over a stretch of a RichText, in UTF-16 units. TabStop An explicit tab stop. TextPosition A caret position: a UTF-16 index at a grapheme cluster boundary and the side it belongs to. TextShadow A shadow under text: the glyphs and decorations again, moved and blurred (CSS text-shadow). Interfaces ITextPaint A paint that Egami.Fonts carries for text but never reads: Egami.Drawing's Paint implements it, so gradients, images and blend modes reach text drawn from a layout without Egami.Fonts depending on the drawing package. Enums CaretMove How MoveCaret(TextPosition, CaretMove, float) moves a caret. LayoutRunKind What a LayoutRun holds. LineBreakStrictness How strictly line breaks follow Chinese and Japanese rules (CSS line-break): breaks before small kana, hyphens, iteration marks and some punctuation. LineFill How lines are filled. LineHeightKind How a LineHeight is given. OverflowWrap Whether a piece wider than its line may break anywhere (CSS overflow-wrap). PlaceholderAlignment How a Placeholder sits on its line. SelectionHeight How tall selection rectangles are. TabAlignment How text aligns on a tab stop. TextAffinity Which side of a position a caret belongs to where one index has two places: at a line wrap or a bidi boundary. TextAlign How lines align in their width (CSS text-align). TextAlignLast How the last line, and lines before a hard break, align (CSS text-align-last). TextDecorationLines Which decoration lines are drawn. TextDecorationSkipInk Whether underlines and overlines skip glyph ink. TextDecorationStyle How decoration lines are drawn. TextJustify How justified lines stretch (CSS text-justify). TextOrientation How characters stand in vertical lines (CSS text-orientation). WordBreak Where breaks may fall inside words (CSS word-break). WritingMode Whether lines run horizontally or vertically (CSS writing-mode).

api/Egami.Fonts.Shaping.OpenTypeLayout.h.summary: Class OpenTypeLayout Namespace Egami.Fonts.Shaping Assembly Egami.Fonts.dll What a face's OpenType layout tables (GSUB and GPOS) offer: the scripts, language systems and features they list, and the glyphs GSUB can produce from a set of glyphs. A table whose structure is damaged is left out whole, as the shaper leaves it out. public sealed class OpenTypeLayout Inheritance object OpenTypeLayout Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // What the font's layout tables list. OpenTypeLayout layout = face.Layout; IReadOnlyList<FontTag> scripts = layout.Scripts; // DFLT, cyrl, grek, latn IReadOnlyList<FontTag> languages = layout.GetLanguageSystems(new FontTag("latn")); IReadOnlyList<FontTag> features = layout.GetFeatures(new FontTag("latn")); // liga, kern, ... Properties DefaultClosureFeatures Gets the layout features hb-subset keeps by default, which GetClosure(IEnumerable<ushort>, IEnumerable<FontTag>?) follows when no features are given: the common ones (such as ccmp, liga, locl, calt and kern), fractions, vertical forms, East Asian spacing, and those the Arabic, Hangul, Tibetan and Indic shapers apply; not discretionary ones such as smcp, dlig or ss01. public static IReadOnlyList<FontTag> DefaultClosureFeatures { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<FontTag> Features Gets every feature tag GSUB and GPOS list, in tag order. public IReadOnlyList<FontTag> Features { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<FontTag> HasGlyphClasses Gets whether the face has a usable GDEF table with glyph classes. public bool HasGlyphClasses { get; } Property Value bool HasGpos Gets whether the face has a usable GPOS table (positioning such as kerning and mark placement). public bool HasGpos { get; } Property Value bool HasGsub Gets whether the face has a usable GSUB table (substitutions such as ligatures and contextual forms). public bool HasGsub { get; } Property Value bool Scripts Gets the script tags GSUB and GPOS list, such as latn, arab or DFLT, in tag order. public IReadOnlyList<FontTag> Scripts { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<FontTag> Methods GetClosure(IEnumerable<ushort>, IEnumerable<FontTag>?) Gets the glyphs the face's GSUB substitutions can produce from glyphs: the glyphs themselves and every glyph a lookup of the given features (in any script and language system, with the lookups their contextual rules call and their feature variations) can substitute for them, repeated until nothing is added. This is the layout closure hb-subset computes, so a subset that keeps these glyphs can be shaped again as the full face would be. public IReadOnlySet<ushort> GetClosure(IEnumerable<ushort> glyphs, IEnumerable<FontTag>? features = null) Parameters glyphs IEnumerable<ushort> The glyph ids to start from, such as those of the characters a page uses; ids the face does not have are ignored. features IEnumerable<FontTag> The feature tags whose lookups are followed, or null for DefaultClosureFeatures; pass Features to follow every feature and an empty list to follow none. Returns IReadOnlySet<ushort> The glyph ids, ascending when enumerated. Examples // The glyphs a web font subset needs so that it shapes "office" as the full font does: the characters' glyphs and every // glyph GSUB can turn them into (the "ffi" ligature, for one). ushort[] used = [0, .. "office".Select(c => face.GetGlyph(c))]; IReadOnlySet<ushort> keep = face.Layout.GetClosure(used); // hb-subset's default features IReadOnlySet<ushort> all = face.Layout.GetClosure(used, face.Layout.Features); // every feature, small caps too GetFeatures(FontTag, FontTag?) Gets the feature tags a language system lists, including its required feature, in tag order. public IReadOnlyList<FontTag> GetFeatures(FontTag script, FontTag? language = null) Parameters script FontTag The script tag. language FontTag? The language system tag, or null for the script's default system. Returns IReadOnlyList<FontTag> The tags; empty when no table lists the script. GetLanguageSystems(FontTag) Gets the language system tags a script lists, such as URD or SRB; the default system is not listed. public IReadOnlyList<FontTag> GetLanguageSystems(FontTag script) Parameters script FontTag The script tag. Returns IReadOnlyList<FontTag> The tags, in tag order; empty when no table lists the script.

api/Egami.Fonts.Shaping.TextShaper.html.summary: Class TextShaper Namespace Egami.Fonts.Shaping Assembly Egami.Fonts.dll OpenType text shaping in managed code: a run of text in one font becomes positioned glyphs with GSUB substitutions, GPOS positioning and the script rules HarfBuzz applies. public static class TextShaper Inheritance object TextShaper Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // One run, one font, as HarfBuzz's hb_shape: ligatures, kerning and marks from the font's GSUB and GPOS. var font = new Font(face, 24); var glyphs = new GlyphBuffer(); string text = "office"; TextShaper.ShapeRun(text, 0, text.Length, font, new RunProperties { Script = Script.Latin }, glyphs); for (int i = 0; i < glyphs.Count; i++) { ushort id = glyphs.GlyphIds[i]; int cluster = glyphs.Clusters[i]; // index in text the glyph came from GlyphPosition position = glyphs.Positions[i]; // in the font's units (pixels here) bool breakable = (glyphs.Flags[i] & GlyphFlags.UnsafeToBreak) == 0; } float width = glyphs.Advance; Remarks Stateless and thread-safe; each call needs its own GlyphBuffer. Methods Shape(string, Font, ShapingOptions?) Shapes text: splits it into lines at hard breaks, resolves each line's bidi levels, splits it into runs of one level, script, span and font (falling back per grapheme cluster as Fallback says), shapes each run as ShapeRun(ReadOnlySpan<char>, int, int, Font, RunProperties, GlyphBuffer) does and orders the runs for display. Control characters other than the breaks (a tab, for one) give no glyph. Nothing wraps. public static ShapedText Shape(string text, Font font, ShapingOptions? options = null) Parameters text string The text. font Font The font and size. options ShapingOptions The direction, language, script, features, fallback, cluster level and spans; null for Default. Returns ShapedText The shaped lines; an empty text gives one empty line. Examples // Whole text: lines at hard breaks, bidi levels, script runs, fallback fonts, runs in display order. var font = new Font(face, 24); var options = new ShapingOptions { Fallback = new FontFallback(fonts.Families) }; ShapedText shaped = TextShaper.Shape("Shalom: \u05E9\u05DC\u05D5\u05DD!", font, options); float x = 0; foreach (ShapedRun run in shaped.Lines[0].Runs) { GlyphRun glyphs = run.ToGlyphRun(new System.Numerics.Vector2(x, 0), shaped.Text); // what a canvas draws x += run.Advance; } Exceptions ArgumentNullException text is null, or font has no typeface. ArgumentOutOfRangeException A span is not inside the text, or two spans overlap. ShapeRun(ReadOnlySpan<char>, int, int, Font, RunProperties, GlyphBuffer) Shapes one run, as HarfBuzz's hb_shape: no bidi, script or font splitting; the run is one script in one direction. Clusters are UTF-16 indexes into text; the characters around the run are context for joining scripts. public static void ShapeRun(ReadOnlySpan<char> text, int start, int length, Font font, RunProperties properties, GlyphBuffer buffer) Parameters text ReadOnlySpan<char> The text the run is part of. start int The index of the run's first UTF-16 unit. length int The number of UTF-16 units in the run. font Font The font and size; positions are in its units. properties RunProperties The run's script, language, direction, features and cluster level. buffer GlyphBuffer Receives the glyphs in visual order. Exceptions ArgumentNullException buffer is null, or font has no typeface. ArgumentOutOfRangeException The run is not inside text.

Without fallback (None, the default) shaping depends only on the fonts passed, never on the machine. GlyphBuffer A reusable buffer of shaped glyphs: glyph ids, the UTF-16 index of the text each came from, glyph flags and positions, in visual order. ShapeRun(ReadOnlySpan<char>, int, int, Font, RunProperties, GlyphBuffer) fills it; reuse one buffer for many runs to avoid allocations. OpenTypeLayout What a face's OpenType layout tables (GSUB and GPOS) offer: the scripts, language systems and features they list, and the glyphs GSUB can produce from a set of glyphs. A table whose structure is damaged is left out whole, as the shaper leaves it out. ShapedLine One line of ShapedText: its range and its runs in visual order. ShapedRun A run of a ShapedLine: one font, one bidi level, one script, one language, and its glyphs. ShapedText Text shaped by Shape(string, Font, ShapingOptions?): one ShapedLine per line between hard breaks, each with its runs in visual order. Nothing wraps. ShapingOptions How Shape(string, Font, ShapingOptions?) shapes text: the paragraph direction, the language, script and features of the whole text, the fonts that take characters the font lacks, the cluster level, and styled spans. SystemFontFallback The installed-font resolver of System: fixed families for each script on Windows, macOS and Linux (Segoe UI Emoji, Apple Color Emoji or Noto Color Emoji for emoji; the language picks Japanese, Chinese or Korean faces for Han), then any installed face that maps the cluster, found once and remembered for the process. TextShaper OpenType text shaping in managed code: a run of text in one font becomes positioned glyphs with GSUB substitutions, GPOS positioning and the script rules HarfBuzz applies. Structs FontFeature An OpenType feature setting: a feature tag, a value and the range of UTF-16 units it applies to, in HarfBuzz's model. A value of 0 turns a feature off (such as default ligatures), 1 turns it on, and higher values pick an alternate. GlyphPosition How a shaped glyph moves the pen and sits relative to it, in the units of the Font it was shaped with. RunProperties What one run of text is shaped as: its script, language, direction, features and cluster level. TextSpan A range of text with its own font, language or features, for Spans. BareCff = 3 A bare CID-keyed CFF stream with an identity charset (CID = new glyph id), as PDF embeds for CIDFontType0C. Needs CFF outlines. api/Egami.Fonts.Unicode.TextDirection.ht.title: Enum TextDirection | Egami
api/Egami.Fonts.Unicode.TextDirection.ht.summary: Enum TextDirection Namespace Egami.Fonts.Unicode Assembly Egami.Fonts.dll The direction of a paragraph or a run of text. public enum TextDirection Fields Auto = 0 The paragraph direction follows the first strong character (UAX #9 rules P2 and P3), left to right when there is none. LeftToRight = 1 Left to right. RightToLeft = 2 Right to left. TopToBottom = 3 Top to bottom, for vertical runs; bidi treats it as left to right. Examples // A Hebrew word inside English text: three runs, the middle one drawn right to left. string text = "abc \u05D0\u05D1\u05D2 def"; using BidiResult result = Bidi.Resolve(text, TextDirection.Auto); int paragraph = result.ParagraphLevel; // 0: the first strong character is Latin foreach (BidiRun run in result.Reorder(0, result.Length)) { Console.WriteLine($"{run.Start}+{run.Length} {(run.IsRightToLeft ? "right to left" : "left to right")}"); }

api/Egami.Fonts.html.summary: Namespace Egami.Fonts Classes BitmapColorGlyph An sbix or CBDT glyph: its image, the strike's size and where the image goes, in font units with y up, so it scales with the font; the drawing code decodes and resamples it. CffOptions What a bare CFF stream lacks and an sfnt would supply, for FromCff(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, CffOptions?). CffStandardStrings The Compact Font Format's predefined data (Adobe Technical Note #5176, appendices A and B): the 391 standard strings that string ids (SIDs) below 391 name, and the Standard and Expert encodings as glyph names by code. CharacterMap One character map of a face, as stored: a cmap subtable for one (platform, encoding) pair, or a CFF font's own encoding as FreeType presents it (platform 7). Codes are the subtable's own: bytes for a Macintosh (1,0) map or a symbol font's (3,0) map, never translated to Unicode. CidSystemInfo The character collection a CID-keyed font's CIDs belong to (its CFF ROS operator), such as Adobe-Japan1-7; PDF's CIDSystemInfo dictionary carries the same three values. ColorCompositePaint Two paints composited: the source onto the backdrop with a blend or Porter-Duff mode. ColorGlyph A glyph's color description from TryGetColorGlyph(ushort, FontPalette?, out ColorGlyph?, float): a PaintColorGlyph (COLR) or a BitmapColorGlyph (sbix, CBDT). ColorGlyphPaint A paint clipped to a glyph's outline. ColorGlyphReferencePaint Another color glyph's paint graph drawn here, as COLR's PaintColrGlyph reuses it. ColorLayersPaint Paints drawn one over another, in order. ColorLine The stops of a color gradient and what happens past them. ColorLinearGradientPaint A linear gradient filling the clip: the color line runs from P0 toward P1, with lines of equal color parallel to P0–P2, as COLR defines it. ColorPaint One node of a color glyph's paint graph, in font units with y up: COLR version 1 as OpenType 1.9.1 defines it (version 0 glyphs become layers of solid glyph fills), with variable values already taken at the face's position and palette colors resolved. ColorRadialGradientPaint A gradient between two circles filling the clip. ColorSolidPaint One color filling the clip. ColorSweepGradientPaint A gradient around a center filling the clip, angles in degrees counter-clockwise from the x axis (y up). ColorTransformPaint A paint under an affine transform in font units: COLR's transform, translate, scale, rotate and skew paints, each as its matrix (row vectors, y up). FontCollection A set of faces grouped into families: the caller's own, or System for the fonts installed on the machine. Finds families by name and faces by style with the CSS Fonts Level 4 matching steps. FontFamily The faces of one family in a FontCollection, matched by style. FontLoadOptions How a font file is read: leniently with diagnostics (the default), or strictly. FontLoader Tells what font data holds and loads every face of a collection. FontPalette The palette a color font draws with: a CPAL palette by index or by the background it suits, with entries overridden, as CSS's font-palette and @font-palette-values. FontPaletteInfo One CPAL palette of a face. FontSubset A font holding only some glyphs of another, from FontSubsetter. FontSubsetter Writes fonts that hold only the glyphs a document uses, as PDF embedding and SVG export want: TrueType, OpenType CFF or bare CFF, with composite glyphs and seac accents closed over and unused CFF subroutines dropped. GlyphRun Positioned glyphs of one font, ready to draw: glyph ids, one position per glyph relative to the run's origin (the first baseline's left end, y down, in canvas units), and optionally the source text with the UTF-16 index each glyph came from, which lets a PDF writer keep text searchable. NamedInstance A named instance of a variable font, such as "Bold Condensed", from its fvar table. PaintColorGlyph A COLR glyph: its paint graph and, for version 1, the clip box the font gives. SubsetOptions How Subset(Typeface, IEnumerable<ushort>, SubsetOptions?) writes a subset. Typeface One font face: its names, style, metrics, character map, glyph outlines and kerning, read from a TrueType or OpenType font, a collection, or a bare CFF stream. Immutable and safe to share across threads, canvases and backends. VariationAxis One axis of a variable font, from its fvar table. Structs CharacterMapping A code and the glyph a CharacterMap gives it. ColorStop A stop of a color line. Font A typeface at a size: the em in canvas units (pixels on a raster, points on a PDF page). Scales the face's font-unit metrics and turns text into a positioned GlyphRun. FontExtents A face's vertical metrics and decoration positions, with y up: in font units from Extents, or in canvas units from Extents. FontMatch A matched face and the styling it lacks, from Match(FontStyle). FontNameRecord One decoded string of a font's naming table, such as the family name in one language. FontPaletteEntry One palette entry replaced, as CSS's override-colors. FontProbe The result of Probe(ReadOnlySpan<byte>). FontStyle A face's style, or the style asked for when matching: weight from 1 to 1000 (400 normal, 700 bold), width from 1 to 9 (5 normal, as OS/2 usWidthClass), and slant. FontTag A four-byte OpenType tag, such as the table tag glyf or the feature tag kern. FontVariation A position on one axis of a variable font, in the axis's own units, such as weight 650. GlyphColor A color in a color glyph: a resolved palette color, or the foreground (palette entry 0xFFFF), which takes the paint's color and keeps only this color's alpha as a factor. GlyphExtents A box around ink, such as a glyph's outline, with y up in font units or in a Font's size. GlyphTransform A glyph's placement in a transformed GlyphRun: a rotation and uniform scale, then its origin, as Skia's RSXform. A point (x, y) of the glyph, y down, goes to (ScaleCos x - ScaleSin y + Tx, ScaleSin x + ScaleCos y + Ty). TextBounds A box in canvas units with y down, such as the ink of a GlyphRun relative to its origin. TextMeasure The size of text as MeasureText(string, ShapingOptions?) lays it out, in canvas units. VerticalMetrics One set of a face's ascent, descent and line gap as stored in a table, in font units with y up. To load the data as an image instead, use CcittFormat. public static class CcittFax Inheritance object CcittFax Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // A PDF image with /Filter /CCITTFaxDecode: its DecodeParms become the parameters, and the result is the filter's // output, packed rows with black 0 and white 1, ready for the image's /Decode array and color space. CcittFaxParameters parameters = new() { K = -1, EncodedByteAlign = true, Columns = 301, Rows = 48 }; byte[] rows = CcittFax.Decode(stream, parameters, out int rowCount); Methods Decode(ReadOnlySpan<byte>, CcittFaxParameters, out int, EgamiContext?) Decodes CCITT fax data to packed rows, as PDF's CCITTFaxDecode filter gives them: one bit a pixel, most significant bit first, each row padded to whole bytes with 0 bits, black 0 and white 1 unless BlackIs1. public static byte[] Decode(ReadOnlySpan<byte> data, CcittFaxParameters parameters, out int rows, EgamiContext? context = null) Parameters data ReadOnlySpan<byte> The coded data, as the stream holds it after the filters before CCITTFaxDecode. parameters CcittFaxParameters The stream's DecodeParms. rows int The number of rows returned: Rows when it is above 0, else the rows decoded. context EgamiContext The context whose safety limits and diagnostics apply, or null for Default. Returns byte[] The rows, (Columns + 7) / 8 bytes each. Examples // A PDF image with /Filter /CCITTFaxDecode: its DecodeParms become the parameters, and the result is the filter's // output, packed rows with black 0 and white 1, ready for the image's /Decode array and color space. CcittFaxParameters parameters = new() { K = -1, EncodedByteAlign = true, Columns = 301, Rows = 48 }; byte[] rows = CcittFax.Decode(stream, parameters, out int rowCount); Remarks A damaged row ends decoding (after DamagedRowsBeforeError skipped rows, when it applies): the rows before it are kept, the rest are white, and a warning goes to the context's Diagnostics. Data that ends before Rows rows also warns. Exceptions ArgumentNullException parameters is null. ArgumentOutOfRangeException A parameter is outside what it can mean, such as Columns below 1. CorruptDataException Not one row decodes. LimitExceededException The image breaks a safety limit. Encode(ReadOnlySpan<byte>, CcittFaxParameters) Encodes packed rows as CCITT fax data, the inverse of Decode(ReadOnlySpan<byte>, CcittFaxParameters, out int, EgamiContext?): one bit a pixel, most significant bit first, each row padded to whole bytes, black 0 and white 1 unless BlackIs1. The parameters that describe the result are the ones a PDF's DecodeParms then carries. public static byte[] Encode(ReadOnlySpan<byte> rows, CcittFaxParameters parameters) Parameters rows ReadOnlySpan<byte> The packed rows, (Columns + 7) / 8 bytes each; padding bits are ignored. parameters CcittFaxParameters The coding to write: K, EndOfLine, EndOfBlock, Columns, Rows and BlackIs1 are used. Returns byte[] The coded data. Examples // A bi-level scan as a PDF image with /Filter /CCITTFaxDecode: pack its rows (0 black, 1 white), then write Group 4. int rowBytes = (scan.Width + 7) / 8; byte[] rows = new byte[rowBytes * scan.Height]; for (int y = 0; y < scan.Height; y++) { Span<Gray8> row = scan.Row(y); for (int x = 0; x < scan.Width; x++) { if (row[x].L >= 128) { rows[(y * rowBytes) + (x >> 3)] |= (byte)(0x80 >> (x & 7)); } } } // These parameters are the image's DecodeParms: << /K -1 /Columns 301 /Rows 48 >>. CcittFaxParameters parameters = new() { K = -1, Columns = scan.Width, Rows = scan.Height }; byte[] g4 = CcittFax.Encode(rows, parameters); Remarks K below 0 writes Group 4 (ITU-T T.6), the smallest coding for scanned text; 0 writes one-dimensional Group 3 (modified Huffman rows). EndOfLine puts an EOL before each Group 3 row, and EndOfBlock ends the data with RTC or EOFB. The row count is Rows when it is above 0, else every whole row of rows. Exceptions ArgumentNullException parameters is null. ArgumentOutOfRangeException A parameter is outside what it can mean, or rows holds fewer rows than Rows. NotSupportedException K above 0 (mixed Group 3) or EncodedByteAlign is asked for: neither is written.

Raster<TPixel> raster = input.CreateRaster<TPixel>(width, height); using IMemoryOwner<byte> row = input.RentScratch(width * 4); for (int y = 0; y < height; y++) { input.ReadExactly(row.Memory.Span[..(width * 4)]); PixelConvert.Convert<Rgba8, TPixel>(MemoryMarshal.Cast<byte, Rgba8>(row.Memory.Span[..(width * 4)]), raster.Row(y)); } return raster; } public Raster Read(EgamiInput input, ReaderOptions options) => Read<Rgba8>(input, options); private static (int Width, int Height) Header(EgamiInput input) { input.Skip(4); return ((int)input.ReadUInt32BigEndian(), (int)input.ReadUInt32BigEndian()); } } private sealed class Writer : IFormatWriter { public void Write<TPixel>(Raster<TPixel> raster, Stream output, WriterOptions options) where TPixel : unmanaged, IPixelType<TPixel> { Span<byte> header = stackalloc byte[12]; "RAW8"u8.CopyTo(header); BinaryPrimitives.WriteUInt32BigEndian(header[4..], (uint)raster.Width); BinaryPrimitives.WriteUInt32BigEndian(header[8..], (uint)raster.Height); output.Write(header); Rgba8[] row = new Rgba8[raster.Width]; for (int y = 0; y < raster.Height; y++) { PixelConvert.Convert<TPixel, Rgba8>(raster.Row(y), row); output.Write(MemoryMarshal.AsBytes(row.AsSpan())); } } } } Remarks Readers never call the stream directly. api/Egami.Formats.Exr.ExrCompression.htm.title: Enum ExrCompression | Egami
api/Egami.Formats.Exr.ExrCompression.htm.summary: Enum ExrCompression Namespace Egami.Formats.Exr Assembly Egami.dll How an OpenEXR part's pixel data is compressed. public enum ExrCompression Fields B44 = 6 Half samples in fixed 4 × 4 blocks of 14 bytes, 32 scanlines a block. Lossy. B44A = 7 B44, with flat blocks stored in 3 bytes. Lossy. Dwaa = 8 DreamWorks' DCT compression, 32 scanlines a block. Lossy. Dwab = 9 DreamWorks' DCT compression, 256 scanlines a block. Lossy. Htj2k256 = 11 High-throughput JPEG 2000 at 256 scanlines a block, new in OpenEXR 3.4. Egami reads the header but not the pixels. Htj2k32 = 12 High-throughput JPEG 2000 at 32 scanlines a block, new in OpenEXR 3.4. Egami reads the header but not the pixels. None = 0 Not compressed. Piz = 4 A Haar wavelet and Huffman coding, 32 scanlines a block. Lossless; good on grainy photographs. Pxr24 = 5 Float samples rounded to 24 bits, then deflated, 16 scanlines a block. Lossy for float, lossless for half and uint. Rle = 1 Run-length encoding of byte differences, one scanline a block. Lossless. Zip = 3 Deflate of byte differences, 16 scanlines a block. Lossless. Zips = 2 Deflate of byte differences, one scanline a block. Lossless. Zstd = 10 Zstandard, new in OpenEXR 3.4. Egami reads the header but not the pixels. Examples // Half-float RGBA, ZIP-compressed, by default; a sRGB or other non-linear raster is linearized first. beauty.Save("copy.exr"); beauty.Save("float.exr", new ExrWriterOptions { Compression = ExrCompression.Piz, PixelType = ExrPixelType.Float });
