api/Egami.Formats.Ico.IcoEntryEncoding.h.summary: Enum IcoEntryEncoding Namespace Egami.Formats.Ico Assembly Egami.dll How an icon entry's pixels are stored. public enum IcoEntryEncoding Fields Bmp = 1 A BMP without its file header: the color rows, then a 1-bit AND mask that marks transparent pixels. Png = 0 A whole PNG file. Examples // A favicon: 16, 32 and 48 resized from one raster. A raster that is not square is centred on transparency. logo.Save("favicon.ico", new IcoWriterOptions { Sizes = IcoWriterOptions.FaviconSizes }); // Windows' set: 16 to 256, the 256 entry as PNG and the rest as 32-bit BMP, as Microsoft's guidance asks. logo.Save("app.ico", new IcoWriterOptions { Sizes = IcoWriterOptions.WindowsSizes, Filter = Egami.Operations.ResampleFilter.Lanczos3 }); // Hand-drawn small sizes: each raster is written at its own size; the 48 comes from the largest raster. using Raster<Rgba8> drawn16 = logo.Derive(ops => ops.Fit(16, 16)); Raster.SaveAll([logo, drawn16], "drawn.ico", new IcoWriterOptions { Sizes = [16, 48] });

api/Egami.Formats.Jpeg.JpegColorSpace.ht.summary: Enum JpegColorSpace Namespace Egami.Formats.Jpeg Assembly Egami.dll The color model a JPEG's components are stored in. public enum JpegColorSpace Fields Cmyk = 3 Four components of cyan, magenta, yellow and black (Adobe transform 0). Converted to RGB when decoded. Gray = 0 One component of luma. Rgb = 2 Three components of red, green and blue, as an Adobe segment with transform 0 says. YCbCr = 1 Three components of luma and chroma: the usual JFIF case. Ycck = 4 Four components, YCbCr plus black (Adobe transform 2). Converted to RGB when decoded. Examples using Raster photo = Raster.Load("duck.jpg", options: new JpegReaderOptions { FastUpsampling = true }); JpegDetails details = (JpegDetails)photo.Metadata.FormatDetails!; Console.WriteLine($"{details.ColorSpace}, progressive: {details.Progressive}, quality about {details.EstimatedQuality}"); foreach (JpegComponent component in details.Components) { Console.WriteLine($"Component {component.Id}: sampled {component.HorizontalSampling} × {component.VerticalSampling}"); } // Gray output, and 4:4:4 (no chroma subsampling) for sharp colored edges. photo.Save("gray.jpg", new JpegWriterOptions { ColorType = JpegColorType.Gray }); photo.Save("sharp.jpg", new JpegWriterOptions { Quality = 90, Subsampling = ChromaSubsampling.Subsample444 });

api/Egami.Formats.Jpeg.JpegColorType.htm.title: Enum JpegColorType | Egami
api/Egami.Formats.Jpeg.JpegColorType.htm.summary: Enum JpegColorType Namespace Egami.Formats.Jpeg Assembly Egami.dll Which components a JPEG is written with. public enum JpegColorType Fields Auto = 0 Gray for gray pixel types, CMYK for CMYK pixel types, YCbCr for everything else. Cmyk = 2 Four CMYK components with an Adobe marker (transform 0), the values inverted as Photoshop writes them and every reader expects. Other pixel types are converted to ink with the plain formula. Auto picks this for CMYK pixel types. Gray = 1 One gray component, whatever the pixel type; color is converted to luma. Ycck = 3 Four YCCK components with an Adobe marker (transform 2): cyan, magenta and yellow converted to YCbCr as libjpeg converts Adobe CMYK, chroma subsampled as Subsampling says, and the inverted black at full size. Usually smaller than Cmyk. api/Egami.Formats.Jpeg.JpegTransformEdge.summary: Enum JpegTransformEdges Namespace Egami.Formats.Jpeg Assembly Egami.dll What a lossless transform does with the blocks at the right or bottom edge when the image is not a whole number of MCUs (8 or 16 pixels) across or down, so those blocks cannot move to the other side intact. public enum JpegTransformEdges Fields Keep = 2 Leaves partial MCUs where they are, unmirrored, as jpegtran does by default: every pixel is kept, but a strip up to 15 pixels wide at the edge is not turned with the rest. Strict = 1 Throws InvalidOperationException when a partial MCU would have to move, as jpegtran -perfect does, so the result is always exact and full size. Trim = 0 Drops the partial MCU from an edge that is mirrored, so the image loses up to 15 pixels there (up to 7 for gray), as jpegtran -trim does. Edges that stay in place keep every pixel. Examples // Turns the photo upright by its EXIF orientation without re-encoding: no quality is lost, and the tag is reset. JpegTransform.Apply("sideways.jpg", "upright.jpg", new JpegTransformOptions { Operation = JpegTransformOperation.AutoOrient }); // Rotates, crops and drops the color in one pass; a file can be transformed in place. JpegTransformResult result = JpegTransform.Apply("upright.jpg", "upright.jpg", new JpegTransformOptions { Operation = JpegTransformOperation.Rotate90, Crop = new Rect(0, 0, 200, 120), Grayscale = true, }); Console.WriteLine($"{result.Width} × {result.Height}");

api/Egami.Formats.Jpeg.JpegTransformOper.summary: Enum JpegTransformOperation Namespace Egami.Formats.Jpeg Assembly Egami.dll The rotation or flip a lossless JPEG transform applies, in the terms of jpegtran. public enum JpegTransformOperation Fields AutoOrient = 8 Whatever the EXIF orientation needs to show the image upright, after which the orientation is set to Normal: the lossless version of AutoOrient(). A file with no orientation, or an upright one, is copied. FlipHorizontal = 1 Mirrored left to right. FlipVertical = 2 Mirrored top to bottom. None = 0 No rotation or flip; with Crop or Grayscale only those apply. Rotate180 = 4 Turned 180°. Rotate270 = 5 Turned 270° clockwise (90° counterclockwise). Rotate90 = 3 Turned 90° clockwise. Transpose = 6 Mirrored along the top-left to bottom-right diagonal: rows become columns. Transverse = 7 Mirrored along the top-right to bottom-left diagonal. Examples // Turns the photo upright by its EXIF orientation without re-encoding: no quality is lost, and the tag is reset. JpegTransform.Apply("sideways.jpg", "upright.jpg", new JpegTransformOptions { Operation = JpegTransformOperation.AutoOrient }); // Rotates, crops and drops the color in one pass; a file can be transformed in place. JpegTransformResult result = JpegTransform.Apply("upright.jpg", "upright.jpg", new JpegTransformOptions { Operation = JpegTransformOperation.Rotate90, Crop = new Rect(0, 0, 200, 120), Grayscale = true, }); Console.WriteLine($"{result.Width} × {result.Height}");

api/Egami.Formats.Jpeg.JpegWriterOptions.summary: Class JpegWriterOptions Namespace Egami.Formats.Jpeg Assembly Egami.dll Options for writing JPEG. The defaults are libjpeg-turbo's cjpeg defaults: quality 75, 4:2:0 and the standard Huffman tables of T.81 Annex K, so files compare one to one. public sealed class JpegWriterOptions : WriterOptions Inheritance object WriterOptions JpegWriterOptions Inherited Members WriterOptions.StripMetadata WriterOptions.OmitSrgbProfile object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples using Raster photo = Raster.Load("duck.jpg", options: new JpegReaderOptions { FastUpsampling = true }); JpegDetails details = (JpegDetails)photo.Metadata.FormatDetails!; Console.WriteLine($"{details.ColorSpace}, progressive: {details.Progressive}, quality about {details.EstimatedQuality}"); foreach (JpegComponent component in details.Components) { Console.WriteLine($"Component {component.Id}: sampled {component.HorizontalSampling} × {component.VerticalSampling}"); } // Gray output, and 4:4:4 (no chroma subsampling) for sharp colored edges. photo.Save("gray.jpg", new JpegWriterOptions { ColorType = JpegColorType.Gray }); photo.Save("sharp.jpg", new JpegWriterOptions { Quality = 90, Subsampling = ChromaSubsampling.Subsample444 }); Properties Background Gets the color that transparent pixels are composited onto before writing, since JPEG has no alpha, or null to ignore alpha (every pixel written as if opaque). Its own alpha is ignored. Defaults to null. public Rgba8? Background { get; init; } Property Value Rgba8? ColorType Gets which components to write. Defaults to Auto. public JpegColorType ColorType { get; init; } Property Value JpegColorType Default Gets the default options. public static JpegWriterOptions Default { get; } Property Value JpegWriterOptions GainMap Gets how to write an HDR raster as an Ultra HDR JPEG (HDR Design question 10), or null (the default) to write its pixels as they are. Set, the raster is tone mapped with Bt2390 to the SDR base image, written at Quality, and Create(Raster, Raster?, GainMapOptions?) makes the map that brings the HDR raster back, written after it as KeepGainMap says. To choose the SDR rendition yourself, set GainMap of the SDR raster to Create(Raster, Raster?, GainMapOptions?)'s map and save that. Needs the whole raster, so a streamed encode throws NotSupportedException. public GainMapOptions? GainMap { get; init; } Property Value GainMapOptions Examples // An HDR raster as Ultra HDR: the SDR base, tone mapped with BT.2390, and a gain map that brings the HDR raster back. using Raster<RgbaF32> hdr = Raster.Load<RgbaF32>("render.exr"); hdr.Save("render.jpg", new JpegWriterOptions { Quality = 90, GainMap = new GainMapOptions() }); // Or choose the SDR rendition: the map goes in its metadata, and saving as JPEG writes both. using Raster<Rgb8> sdr = hdr.Derive(ops => ops.ToneMap(ToneMapping.Reinhard)).As<Rgb8>(); sdr.Metadata.GainMap = GainMap.Create(hdr, sdr, new GainMapOptions { Scale = 4 }); sdr.Save("graded.jpg", new JpegWriterOptions { Quality = 90 }); KeepGainMap Gets a value indicating whether a gain map the raster carries (GainMap, from an Ultra HDR, ISO 21496-1 or Apple file) is written back: the gain map JPEG after the image, an MPF index, ISO 21496-1 metadata and Adobe's hdrgm XMP with a GContainer directory, so HDR displays show the HDR rendition. A map read from the file is copied as it was stored; one an operation moved is encoded again. StripMetadata leaves it out too. Defaults to true. public bool KeepGainMap { get; init; } Property Value bool Examples // Crops, turns, flips and resizes move the gain map with the picture; saving as JPEG writes it back. using Raster photo = Raster.Load("ultrahdr.jpg"); using Raster cropped = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Crop(16, 16, 200, 150).Rotate(90)); cropped.Save("cropped.jpg"); // still Ultra HDR // Operations that change pixel values drop it (Operation.GainMapDropped), and so do formats other than JPEG // (Save.GainMapDropped); KeepGainMap = false leaves it out on purpose. cropped.Save("sdr-only.jpg", new JpegWriterOptions { KeepGainMap = false }); OptimizeHuffman Gets a value indicating whether to build Huffman tables for this image in a second pass instead of using the standard ones: usually 5 to 10% smaller files, and slower. Defaults to false. public bool OptimizeHuffman { get; init; } Property Value bool Precision Gets the bits per sample, 8 or 12. 12 keeps the detail of 16-bit and float images (written as SOF1, or SOF2 when progressive, with Huffman tables always optimized), but no browser shows 12-bit JPEG; 8-bit pixel types gain nothing from it. Defaults to 8. public int Precision { get; init; } Property Value int Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The value is not 8 or 12. Progressive Gets a value indicating whether to write a progressive file: libjpeg's standard scan script (ten scans for color, six for gray) with Huffman tables optimized for each scan, as cjpeg -progressive writes. Readers show a coarse image first and refine it; files are usually a few percent smaller than baseline, and decode to the same pixels. The encoder holds every quantized coefficient until the last scan, about 2 bytes per sample, counted against MaxTotalBytes; a streamed encode buffers. Re-saving a progressive file writes baseline unless this is set. Defaults to false. public bool Progressive { get; init; } Property Value bool Quality Gets the quality, 1 (smallest) to 100 (best). It scales the example quantization tables of T.81 Annex K with the IJG formula, so the same number gives about the same file as other libjpeg-based encoders. Defaults to 75. public int Quality { get; init; } Property Value int Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The value is outside 1 to 100. RestartInterval Gets the number of MCUs between restart markers, or 0 for none. Restart markers let a reader resynchronize after damaged data, at 2 bytes each. Defaults to 0. public int RestartInterval { get; init; } Property Value int Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The value is outside 0 to 65,535. Subsampling Gets the chroma subsampling. Defaults to Subsample420 (4:2:0). Ignored for gray output. public ChromaSubsampling Subsampling { get; init; } Property Value ChromaSubsampling

api/Egami.Formats.Jxl.JxlWriterOptions.h.summary: Class JxlWriterOptions Namespace Egami.Formats.Jxl Assembly Egami.dll Options for writing JPEG XL. public sealed class JxlWriterOptions : WriterOptions Inheritance object WriterOptions JxlWriterOptions Inherited Members WriterOptions.StripMetadata WriterOptions.OmitSrgbProfile object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // Lossless JPEG XL, about the size cjxl -d 0 makes at the same effort (1 fastest to 7 smallest, 5 by default). using Raster photo = Raster.Load("duck.png"); photo.Save("duck-lossless.jxl", new JxlWriterOptions { Lossless = true, Effort = 7 }); Properties AlphaDistance Gets the distance alpha is written at in lossy files, on Distance's scale: 0 (the default) keeps alpha exact, larger values (up to 25) code it lossy through Modular's squeeze, smaller but with softer edges. From a distance of 10 the whole image, alpha included, is coded at half size as cjxl codes it, so alpha is exact only below that. Lossless files keep alpha exact. public float AlphaDistance { get; init; } Property Value float Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The value is outside 0 to 25. Default Gets the default options. public static JxlWriterOptions Default { get; } Property Value JxlWriterOptions Distance Gets the Butteraugli-style distance lossy files are written at, as cjxl -d takes it: 1.0 is visually lossless, larger values give smaller files with more visible loss, 0.1 to 25. Defaults to null, which takes the distance from Quality. public float? Distance { get; init; } Property Value float? Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The value is outside 0.1 to 25. Effort Gets how hard the encoder works, 1 (fastest) to 7 (smallest files), on libjxl's effort scale for both kinds, so the same number gives about the same file as cjxl -e. Lossless: 1 is libjxl's fast lossless path, 2 and 3 use fixed trees, 4 and up learn the tree, and 5 and up also try local palettes and color transforms. Lossy: 1 to 3 use 8×8 DCTs and one quantization value, 4 adds finer LF and context modeling, 5 adaptive quantization, chroma from luma, Gaborish and simple block sizes, 6 the full block-size search, and 7 patches for repeated shapes such as text. Defaults to 5. public int Effort { get; init; } Property Value int Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The value is outside 1 to 7. KeepTransparentColors Gets whether lossy files keep the color of fully transparent pixels. false lets the encoder replace it by that of the visible neighbours, which makes files smaller (libjxl does that by default); true, the default as for WebP, keeps it as well as lossy coding does. Lossless files always keep it. public bool KeepTransparentColors { get; init; } Property Value bool Lossless Gets whether to write lossless (Modular, every sample exact) or lossy (VarDCT in XYB) data, or null (the default) to keep the kind of the JPEG XL file the raster was read from (lossless for a Modular file without XYB), and write lossy otherwise, as cjxl does for PNG input. Quality 100 with no Distance also writes lossless unless this is false. public bool? Lossless { get; init; } Property Value bool? PhotonNoiseIso Gets the ISO speed of film-like photon noise the decoder adds to lossy images, as cjxl --photon_noise_iso takes it (for example 3200 for a grainy look); the noise depends on the image size like a 35 mm sensor's. Defaults to null, no noise. Lossless files ignore it. public float? PhotonNoiseIso { get; init; } Property Value float? Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The value is not a positive number up to 10⁷. Progressive Gets whether lossy files are progressive as cjxl -p makes them: the LF image in a frame of its own (squeezed, so a 1:8 and smaller preview comes first) and the HF coefficients in three passes by frequency, so a partial file shows a coarse image that sharpens. Files grow slightly. Defaults to false. Lossless files ignore it. public bool Progressive { get; init; } Property Value bool Quality Gets the lossy quality, 0 (smallest) to 100 (best), on cjxl's -q scale, so the same number gives about the same file: 90 is distance 1.0 (visually lossless), each step below 100 adds 0.09 down to 30, and the distance grows faster below. 100 is lossless. Distance, when set, takes its place. Defaults to 90. public int Quality { get; init; } Property Value int Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The value is outside 0 to 100.

Save counts the raster's frames and ignores this. public int? FrameCount { get; init; } Property Value int? Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The value is less than 1. api/Egami.Formats.Pnm.PnmKind.html.summary: Enum PnmKind Namespace Egami.Formats.Pnm Assembly Egami.dll Which Netpbm variant a file is, or which one to write. public enum PnmKind Fields Auto = 0 When writing: PFM for float types without alpha, PGM for other gray types, PPM for other types without alpha, PAM for types with alpha. Bitmap = 1 PBM (P1 or P4): one bit a pixel, 1 for black. FloatMap = 5 PFM (PF or Pf): 32-bit float RGB or gray in linear light, loaded as RgbF32 or GrayF32. Gray pixel types are written as Pf, the rest as PF; alpha is dropped. Graymap = 2 PGM (P2 or P5): gray. Pam = 4 PAM (P7): gray, RGB, or either with alpha. Pixmap = 3 PPM (P3 or P6): RGB. Examples // Auto: P5 (PGM) for gray, P6 (PPM) for color, P7 (PAM) when the pixel type has alpha. image.Save("duck.ppm"); // The plain-text forms, for tools that read them; lines are at most 70 characters. image.Save("duck-plain.ppm", new PnmWriterOptions { PlainText = true }); // A 1-bit bitmap, thresholded at 50% gray. image.Save("duck.pbm", new PnmWriterOptions { Kind = PnmKind.Bitmap });

Raster<TPixel> raster = input.CreateRaster<TPixel>(width, height); using IMemoryOwner<byte> row = input.RentScratch(width * 4); for (int y = 0; y < height; y++) { input.ReadExactly(row.Memory.Span[..(width * 4)]); PixelConvert.Convert<Rgba8, TPixel>(MemoryMarshal.Cast<byte, Rgba8>(row.Memory.Span[..(width * 4)]), raster.Row(y)); } return raster; } public Raster Read(EgamiInput input, ReaderOptions options) => Read<Rgba8>(input, options); private static (int Width, int Height) Header(EgamiInput input) { input.Skip(4); return ((int)input.ReadUInt32BigEndian(), (int)input.ReadUInt32BigEndian()); } } private sealed class Writer : IFormatWriter { public void Write<TPixel>(Raster<TPixel> raster, Stream output, WriterOptions options) where TPixel : unmanaged, IPixelType<TPixel> { Span<byte> header = stackalloc byte[12]; "RAW8"u8.CopyTo(header); BinaryPrimitives.WriteUInt32BigEndian(header[4..], (uint)raster.Width); BinaryPrimitives.WriteUInt32BigEndian(header[8..], (uint)raster.Height); output.Write(header); Rgba8[] row = new Rgba8[raster.Width]; for (int y = 0; y < raster.Height; y++) { PixelConvert.Convert<TPixel, Rgba8>(raster.Row(y), row); output.Write(MemoryMarshal.AsBytes(row.AsSpan())); } } } } Properties Access Gets whether a RasterDecoder streams this image's rows or decodes it into a buffer first. api/Egami.Formats.RecoveryMode.html.summary: Enum RecoveryMode Namespace Egami.Formats Assembly Egami.dll How a reader handles damaged data. public enum RecoveryMode Fields Lenient = 0 Return what was decoded when the data ends early or a checksum fails after valid pixels, and note the problem in Warnings. Data that would need guessing, such as an invalid header, still throws. Strict = 1 Throw CorruptDataException on any problem. Examples EgamiContext strict = EgamiContext.Default with { Limits = SafetyLimits.Default with { MaxPixels = 25_000_000, MaxTotalBytes = 256L * 1024 * 1024 }, }; try { // Read the header first: cheap, and it rejects what you do not want before any pixel memory is used. RasterInfo info = Raster.Probe(upload, strict); if (info.Width > 8000 || info.Height > 8000) { throw new InvalidDataException("Too large."); } using Raster image = Raster.Load(upload, strict, new ReaderOptions { Recovery = RecoveryMode.Strict }); Console.WriteLine($"{info.Format.Name} {image.Width} × {image.Height}"); } catch (UnsupportedFormatException) { Console.WriteLine("Not an image format we accept."); } catch (LimitExceededException e) { Console.WriteLine($"Over the {e.LimitName} limit."); } catch (CorruptDataException e) { Console.WriteLine($"Damaged at byte {e.Offset}."); }

api/Egami.Formats.SignatureMatcher.html.title: Delegate SignatureMatcher | Egami
api/Egami.Formats.SignatureMatcher.html.summary: Delegate SignatureMatcher Namespace Egami.Formats Assembly Egami.dll Returns whether the first bytes of a file belong to a format. public delegate bool SignatureMatcher(ReadOnlySpan<byte> header) Parameters header ReadOnlySpan<byte> The first bytes of the data, up to the longest SignatureLength of all registered formats. It is shorter only if the data itself is shorter. Returns bool true if the data looks like this format. Examples // Every built-in format, with its name, extensions and MIME types; Raster.Save picks one by extension. foreach (FormatInfo format in new[] { PngFormat.Info, JpegFormat.Info, GifFormat.Info, BmpFormat.Info, TgaFormat.Info, QoiFormat.Info, PnmFormat.Info }) { Console.WriteLine($"{format.Name}: {string.Join(", ", format.Extensions)} ({string.Join(", ", format.MimeTypes)})"); } // A SignatureMatcher decides from the first SignatureLength bytes whether a file is in the format. SignatureMatcher isPng = PngFormat.Info.Matches; bool png = isPng(File.ReadAllBytes("duck.png").AsSpan(0, PngFormat.Info.SignatureLength));

api/Egami.Formats.Tga.TgaAlphaType.html.summary: Enum TgaAlphaType Namespace Egami.Formats.Tga Assembly Egami.dll The TGA 2.0 alpha type from the extension area. public enum TgaAlphaType Fields None = 0 No alpha data. Premultiplied = 4 Premultiplied alpha. Egami un-premultiplies it on load. Straight = 3 Straight alpha. UndefinedIgnore = 1 Undefined data in the alpha bits, to be ignored. api/Egami.Formats.Tga.TgaPixelFormat.htm.summary: Enum TgaPixelFormat Namespace Egami.Formats.Tga Assembly Egami.dll The pixel layout a TGA is written with. public enum TgaPixelFormat Fields Auto = 0 8-bit gray for gray types without alpha, 24-bit when every pixel is opaque, else 32-bit with alpha. Bgr24 = 3 24-bit blue, green and red. Alpha is dropped, not blended onto a background. Bgra32 = 4 32-bit blue, green, red and alpha. Gray8 = 1 8-bit gray (image type 3). Indexed8 = 2 8-bit indices into a color map of up to 256 colors, with alpha in the map when the image has any. Examples image.Save("duck-gray.tga", new TgaWriterOptions { PixelFormat = TgaPixelFormat.Gray8, Rle = false }); using Raster back = Raster.Load("duck-gray.tga"); TgaDetails details = (TgaDetails)back.Metadata.FormatDetails!; bool upsideDown = details.Origin is TgaOrigin.BottomLeft or TgaOrigin.BottomRight; bool hasAlpha = details.AlphaType is TgaAlphaType.Straight or TgaAlphaType.Premultiplied;

CcittGroup3 = 3 CCITT Group 3 fax, T.4 (3); 1-bit images only. CcittGroup4 = 4 CCITT Group 4 fax, T.6 (4); 1-bit images only. CcittRle = 2 CCITT modified Huffman run lengths (2); read only. CcittRleWord = 32771 CCITT run lengths on 16-bit words (32771); read only. Deflate = 8 Deflate (8), the zlib format. DngJpegXl = 52546 JPEG XL under DNG 1.7's code (52546), for previews and other pages that are not camera RAW; read only. Jpeg = 7 JPEG as Adobe's TIFF Technical Note 2 describes it (7). JpegXl = 50002 JPEG XL (50002), each strip or tile a JPEG XL codestream or file; read only. Lzw = 5 LZW (5). None = 1 No compression (1). Raster<TPixel> raster = input.CreateRaster<TPixel>(width, height); using IMemoryOwner<byte> row = input.RentScratch(width * 4); for (int y = 0; y < height; y++) { input.ReadExactly(row.Memory.Span[..(width * 4)]); PixelConvert.Convert<Rgba8, TPixel>(MemoryMarshal.Cast<byte, Rgba8>(row.Memory.Span[..(width * 4)]), raster.Row(y)); } return raster; } public Raster Read(EgamiInput input, ReaderOptions options) => Read<Rgba8>(input, options); private static (int Width, int Height) Header(EgamiInput input) { input.Skip(4); return ((int)input.ReadUInt32BigEndian(), (int)input.ReadUInt32BigEndian()); } } private sealed class Writer : IFormatWriter { public void Write<TPixel>(Raster<TPixel> raster, Stream output, WriterOptions options) where TPixel : unmanaged, IPixelType<TPixel> { Span<byte> header = stackalloc byte[12]; "RAW8"u8.CopyTo(header); BinaryPrimitives.WriteUInt32BigEndian(header[4..], (uint)raster.Width); BinaryPrimitives.WriteUInt32BigEndian(header[8..], (uint)raster.Height); output.Write(header); Rgba8[] row = new Rgba8[raster.Width]; for (int y = 0; y < raster.Height; y++) { PixelConvert.Convert<TPixel, Rgba8>(raster.Row(y), row); output.Write(MemoryMarshal.AsBytes(row.AsSpan())); } } } } Properties Default Gets the default options. public static WriterOptions Default { get; } Property Value WriterOptions OmitSrgbProfile Gets whether to leave out an embedded ICC profile that means sRGB (IsEquivalentTo(ColorProfile)), which saves about 3 KB on a web image; PNG writes its small sRGB chunk instead. api/Egami.Formats.html.title: Namespace Egami.Formats | Egami
api/Egami.Formats.html.summary: Namespace Egami.Formats Classes EgamiInput The data a reader decodes: the caller's stream behind a pooled 64 KB buffer, with exact-read helpers. It also carries the context, limits and cancellation token for the load, and is the only way a reader allocates pixel memory. EncodeStart<TPixel> What an encode starts from: the size, metadata and options, and the whole image when Save has one. FormatInfo Describes a file format: its names, how to recognize it, and its reader and writer. HdrDecode How to read the HDR rendition of an image with a gain map, for Hdr. RasterInfo What a file's header says, read without decoding pixels. ReaderOptions Options for reading. The defaults read everything leniently. Formats with options of their own derive from it, such as JpegReaderOptions. RowEncoder<TPixel> One encode in progress: a still image's rows top-down with WriteRow(ReadOnlySpan<TPixel>), or whole frames with WriteFrame(Frame<TPixel>), then Complete(). RowReader One open image, as a format reader streams it: frames of rows at the stored size. Derive from RowReader<TNatural>, which names the natural pixel type. RowReader<TNatural> An open image whose natural pixel type is TNatural, as Load(Stream, EgamiContext?, ReaderOptions?) would give it. WriterOptions Options for writing. Each format has a subclass with its own settings; writers given this base class use their defaults. Interfaces IFormatReader Reads one file format. Readers are stateless and safe to share across threads. They read only through EgamiInput and allocate pixel memory only through CreateRaster<TPixel>(long, long, ClearMode), which checks the safety limits first, so no reader can allocate before the size has been checked. IFormatWriter Writes one file format. Writers are stateless, safe to share across threads, and never change the raster they are given. IRowFormatReader An optional interface for a format's reader: an open image that hands out rows as they are asked for, so RasterDecoder streams the format, with Region and MinimumSize applied on the way out. A reader without it still works everywhere: the decoder reads the whole image with Read(EgamiInput, ReaderOptions) and serves rows from it. Load, Probe and an incremental decode keep using IFormatReader. IRowFormatWriter An optional interface for a format's writer: an encoder that takes rows and frames one at a time. A writer that implements it streams through RasterEncoder<TPixel> and Transcode(Stream, Stream, FormatInfo, Action<RasterOps>?, ReaderOptions?, WriterOptions?, EgamiContext?), and Save(Stream, FormatInfo, WriterOptions?) and SaveAsync use it in place of Write<TPixel>(Raster<TPixel>, Stream, WriterOptions), so all of them write the same bytes. A writer without it still works everywhere: the encoder gathers the image and calls Write<TPixel>(Raster<TPixel>, Stream, WriterOptions) at the end. Enums RasterAccess How a decode produces rows, as Access reports it. RecoveryMode How a reader handles damaged data. Delegates SignatureMatcher Returns whether the first bytes of a file belong to a format.

api/Egami.Metadata.html.summary: Namespace Egami.Metadata Classes ExifData A parsed EXIF block (a TIFF structure, CIPA DC-008): the tags of IFD0, the EXIF, GPS and interoperability sub-IFDs and IFD1 with its thumbnail, with typed getters for the common ones. An unedited block writes back byte for byte; after an edit it is laid out again, keeping the maker note at its old offset when it fits, since maker notes often hold offsets of their own. ExifEntry One EXIF value: its tag, TIFF type and raw bytes, with accessors that read them as text, integers or fractions. FormatDetails Format-specific details the reader found, such as the original color type or palette. Each format derives its own. FrameMetadata Metadata that belongs to one frame. IptcData Parsed IPTC-IIM datasets (IPTC-IIM 4.2), as news agencies, stock libraries and Lightroom write them next to XMP, with typed getters for the common ones. Shaped like ExifData: an unedited block writes back byte for byte; after an edit it is rebuilt in record and dataset order, record 1 first, with the coded character set (1:90) set to UTF-8 whenever a value is not plain ASCII. IptcEntry One IPTC-IIM dataset as stored: its key and its bytes. RasterMetadata Metadata that belongs to the whole raster. It is kept apart from the pixels and survives operations unless an operation makes it wrong. Metadata problems never fail a load: broken blocks are kept as bytes and noted in Warnings. TextEntry A text entry, such as a PNG text chunk or a GIF comment. XmpArray An XMP array: items in order, each a simple value (string), an XmpStruct or another XmpArray, with a language for the items of a language alternative. XmpData A parsed XMP packet: its properties by namespace URI and local name, each a simple value, an XmpArray or an XmpStruct, with typed getters and setters for what apps ask for most (Dublin Core, XMP Basic, Photoshop and TIFF properties). An unedited packet writes back byte for byte; an edited one is written as canonical RDF/XML with padding, keeping every property it does not know, qualifiers included. XmpNamespaces The namespace URIs of the XMP schemas apps use most. XmpStruct An XMP structure: named fields, each a simple value (string), an XmpArray or another XmpStruct, such as Iptc4xmpCore:CreatorContactInfo. XmpData holds its top-level properties the same way. Structs ExifFraction A rational EXIF value, such as an exposure time of 1/250 or an aperture of 28/10. ExifKey An EXIF tag: its number and the IFD it lives in. The named keys cover the tags most programs read and write. GeoPosition A position from the GPS tags of an EXIF block. IptcKey An IPTC-IIM dataset: its record and dataset numbers, as "2:25" for keywords. The named keys cover the datasets news, stock and photo software read and write; any other pair works too. Resolution Physical pixel density. XmpName An XMP property name: a namespace URI and a local name, such as dc:title. Prefixes vary between files, so Egami never matches on them; XmpNamespaces holds the URIs of the common schemas. Enums ColorSpaceHint What the raster's pixel values mean, as far as the file said. ExifIfd The image file directories (IFDs) an EXIF block holds its tags in. ExifType The TIFF data types EXIF values are stored as. FrameBlend How a frame is combined with what is already on the canvas. FrameDisposal What happens to a frame's area before the next frame is drawn. ImageOrientation How stored pixels must be turned to show the image upright: the EXIF Orientation tag (274). The value says which way the camera was held; AutoOrient applies it. ResolutionUnit The unit of a Resolution. XmpArrayKind The three kinds of XMP array.

api/Egami.Metafiles.Metafile.html.summary: Class Metafile Namespace Egami.Metafiles Assembly Egami.Metafiles.dll A Windows metafile, WMF, EMF or EMF+ (and their gzip forms WMZ and EMZ), read and checked; its records stay internal (design question 3). The size facts come from the header: an EMF's frame, a placeable WMF's box and units per inch, or a plain WMF's window extent at 96 DPI. A metafile is immutable and safe to read from many threads. public sealed class Metafile Inheritance object Metafile Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // WMF, EMF and EMF+ alike, and the gzip forms WMZ and EMZ. Metafile chart = Metafile.Load(path); Console.WriteLine($"{chart.Kind}, {chart.Size.X} by {chart.Size.Y} points"); // At twice the screen's resolution, over white; text uses the installed fonts. using Raster<Rgba8> image = chart.Rasterize<Rgba8>(new MetafileRenderOptions { Dpi = 192, Background = new RgbaF32(1, 1, 1, 1), }); image.Save(output); Properties Description Gets an EMF's description (the application, then the picture's name, on separate lines), or null. public string? Description { get; } Property Value string Dpi Gets the resolution of the units the picture was recorded in: an EMF's reference device in pixels per inch, a placeable WMF's units per inch, or 96 for a plain WMF. public Vector2 Dpi { get; } Property Value Vector2 Frame Gets the picture's frame in points: an EMF's frame rectangle (its origin may be away from zero), a placeable WMF's box, or a plain WMF's window extent from zero. public RectF Frame { get; } Property Value RectF Kind Gets what the file holds. public MetafileKind Kind { get; } Property Value MetafileKind Size Gets the picture's size in points (1/72 inch), the size Word and PowerPoint give it. public Vector2 Size { get; } Property Value Vector2 Warnings Gets what the load skipped or assumed, such as a record that runs past the end of the file. public IReadOnlyList<EgamiDiagnostic> Warnings { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<EgamiDiagnostic> Methods Draw(Canvas, RectF?, MetafileRenderOptions?) Draws the picture on a canvas: in points from the canvas's origin (the frame's corner there), or with its frame stretched to box exactly, as Word stretches a picture to its frame. Drawing calls only the public canvas API, so a raster canvas, a PDF page, SvgCanvas or a PictureRecorder receive the same calls. It never throws on content: what it cannot draw is skipped and reported to the context's diagnostics. public void Draw(Canvas canvas, RectF? box = null, MetafileRenderOptions? options = null) Parameters canvas Canvas The canvas. box RectF? The rectangle to stretch the frame to, in the canvas's coordinates, or null. options MetafileRenderOptions Fonts, antialiasing and playback, or null for the defaults. Examples Metafile picture = Metafile.Load(path); // The frame is stretched to the box, as Word stretches a picture to its frame. The same calls draw on a PDF page. using Raster<Rgba8> page = Raster.Create<Rgba8>(400, 300); using RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = page.CreateCanvas(); canvas.Clear(new RgbaF32(1, 1, 1, 1)); picture.Draw(canvas, new RectF(50, 50, 300, 200)); Load(Stream, MetafileLoadOptions?) Reads a WMF, EMF, WMZ or EMZ stream from its current position to its end. public static Metafile Load(Stream stream, MetafileLoadOptions? options = null) Parameters stream Stream The stream; it is read to its end and left open. options MetafileLoadOptions How to read it, or null for the defaults. Returns Metafile The metafile. Examples // Untrusted files: the context's limits bound the file size and what EMZ and WMZ inflate to; a record that runs past // the end is skipped with a warning, and what came before it plays. MetafileLoadOptions options = new() { Context = EgamiContext.Default with { Limits = SafetyLimits.Default with { MaxTotalBytes = 16 << 20 } }, }; Metafile picture = Metafile.Load(new MemoryStream(bytes), options); if (picture.Kind is MetafileKind.EmfPlusDual or MetafileKind.EmfPlusOnly) { Console.WriteLine("Drawn by its EMF+ records, as GDI+ draws it."); } Exceptions CorruptDataException The data is no WMF or EMF file, or its header is broken. LimitExceededException The data, or an EMZ or WMZ stream once inflated, is larger than the context's MaxTotalBytes. Load(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>, MetafileLoadOptions?) Reads WMF, EMF, WMZ or EMZ bytes, such as a picture taken out of a Word or PowerPoint file. public static Metafile Load(ReadOnlyMemory<byte> data, MetafileLoadOptions? options = null) Parameters data ReadOnlyMemory<byte> The file's bytes; they are copied, so the memory can be reused once this returns. options MetafileLoadOptions How to read it, or null for the defaults. Returns Metafile The metafile. Examples // A picture taken out of a document, already in memory: no stream needed. Metafile picture = Metafile.Load(bytes); using Raster<Rgba8> page = Raster.Create<Rgba8>(200, 150); using RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = page.CreateCanvas(); picture.Draw(canvas, new RectF(0, 0, 200, 150)); Exceptions CorruptDataException The data is no WMF or EMF file, or its header is broken. LimitExceededException The data, or EMZ or WMZ data once inflated, is larger than the context's MaxTotalBytes. Load(string, MetafileLoadOptions?) Reads a .wmf, .emf, .wmz or .emz file. public static Metafile Load(string path, MetafileLoadOptions? options = null) Parameters path string The file. options MetafileLoadOptions How to read it, or null for the defaults. Returns Metafile The metafile. Examples // WMF, EMF and EMF+ alike, and the gzip forms WMZ and EMZ. Metafile chart = Metafile.Load(path); Console.WriteLine($"{chart.Kind}, {chart.Size.X} by {chart.Size.Y} points"); // At twice the screen's resolution, over white; text uses the installed fonts. using Raster<Rgba8> image = chart.Rasterize<Rgba8>(new MetafileRenderOptions { Dpi = 192, Background = new RgbaF32(1, 1, 1, 1), }); image.Save(output); Exceptions CorruptDataException The file is no WMF or EMF file, or its header is broken. LimitExceededException The file, or an EMZ or WMZ file once inflated, is larger than the context's MaxTotalBytes. Rasterize<TPixel>(MetafileRenderOptions?) Draws the picture into a new raster: at its size at Dpi (96 by default), or at a target width and/or height (the other side keeps the aspect ratio), over Background. public Raster<TPixel> Rasterize<TPixel>(MetafileRenderOptions? options = null) where TPixel : unmanaged, IPixelType<TPixel> Parameters options MetafileRenderOptions The size, background, fonts and playback, or null for the defaults. Returns Raster<TPixel> The raster. Type Parameters TPixel The pixel type of the raster. Examples // WMF, EMF and EMF+ alike, and the gzip forms WMZ and EMZ. Metafile chart = Metafile.Load(path); Console.WriteLine($"{chart.Kind}, {chart.Size.X} by {chart.Size.Y} points"); // At twice the screen's resolution, over white; text uses the installed fonts. using Raster<Rgba8> image = chart.Rasterize<Rgba8>(new MetafileRenderOptions { Dpi = 192, Background = new RgbaF32(1, 1, 1, 1), }); image.Save(output); Exceptions LimitExceededException The raster would break the context's size limits.

api/Egami.MipChain.html.title: Class MipChain | Egami
api/Egami.MipChain.html.summary: Class MipChain Namespace Egami Assembly Egami.dll A chain of ever-halved copies of an image, for making many smaller sizes fast: each resize starts from the smallest level that is still at least twice the target, so a gallery of thumbnail sizes reads each source pixel about once instead of once per size. Level 0 is the source itself; each next level halves the size, rounding up, by averaging 2 × 2 blocks of premultiplied pixels. public sealed class MipChain : IDisposable Inheritance object MipChain Implements IDisposable Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // A responsive image set: one chain, then each width from the smallest level at least twice its size. using MipChain chain = MipChain.Build(photo); foreach (int width in (int[])[320, 240, 160, 120, 80]) { using Raster thumbnail = chain.Fit(width, width, ResampleFilter.Lanczos2); thumbnail.Save($"egret-{width}.png"); } Remarks The levels together take a third more memory than the source. Every frame of an animation gets its levels. The chain does not copy or dispose the source, which must outlive it; disposing the chain frees the levels it made. Properties Levels Gets the levels, from the source (level 0) down to 1 × 1. public IReadOnlyList<Raster> Levels { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<Raster> Exceptions ObjectDisposedException The chain has been disposed. Methods Build(Raster, ColorSpace) Builds the chain for source, down to a 1 × 1 level. public static MipChain Build(Raster source, ColorSpace colorSpace = ColorSpace.Encoded) Parameters source Raster The image; it becomes level 0 as it is, so it must outlive the chain. colorSpace ColorSpace Where the levels and the resizes from them blend: the stored values (the default) or linear light. Returns MipChain The chain. The caller must dispose it. Exceptions ArgumentNullException source is null. ArgumentOutOfRangeException colorSpace is not defined. LimitExceededException The levels would break the context's MaxTotalBytes. Dispose() Frees the levels the chain made; the source is left alone. public void Dispose() Fit(int, int, ResampleFilter, bool) Returns the image fitted inside width × height with its aspect ratio kept, the same size Fit(int, int, ResampleFilter, ColorSpace, bool) gives from the source, resized from the smallest level at least twice that size. public Raster Fit(int width, int height, ResampleFilter filter = ResampleFilter.Bicubic, bool enlarge = true) Parameters width int The box width, at least 1. height int The box height, at least 1. filter ResampleFilter The resampling kernel. enlarge bool Whether an image smaller than the box is scaled up; false returns it at its own size. Returns Raster The new raster. The caller must dispose it. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException A size is less than 1, or the filter is not defined. ObjectDisposedException The chain has been disposed. Resize(int, int, ResampleFilter) Returns the image resized to exactly width × height, from the smallest level at least twice that size in both directions (the source when there is none), as Resize(int, int, ResampleFilter, ColorSpace) would from the source. public Raster Resize(int width, int height, ResampleFilter filter = ResampleFilter.Bicubic) Parameters width int The width, at least 1. height int The height, at least 1. filter ResampleFilter The resampling kernel. Returns Raster The new raster, with the source's pixel type and metadata. The caller must dispose it. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException A size is less than 1, or the filter is not defined. ObjectDisposedException The chain has been disposed.

api/Egami.Operations.BlendMode.html.title: Enum BlendMode | Egami
api/Egami.Operations.BlendMode.html.summary: Enum BlendMode Namespace Egami.Operations Assembly Egami.dll How a source color is combined with the destination under it: the twelve Porter–Duff operators, Plus and Modulate, and the separable and non-separable blend modes of the W3C Compositing and Blending specification, plus Add and Subtract. Blend modes (Multiply to Luminosity) blend the colors where both are present, then composite source-over. The values are fixed: they never change between releases. public enum BlendMode Fields Add = 25 The sum of the colors, clamped: B = min(1, Cs + Cd) (Photoshop's Linear Dodge). Clear = 1 Both are removed: the result is transparent. Color = 29 The source's hue and saturation with the destination's luminosity: tints a gray image. ColorBurn = 20 Darkens the destination to reflect the source: B = 1 − min(1, (1 − Cd) / Cs). ColorDodge = 19 Brightens the destination to reflect the source: B = min(1, Cd / (1 − Cs)). Darken = 17 The darker of the two colors, per channel. Destination = 3 The destination is kept: d. Drawing with it changes nothing. DestinationAtop = 10 The destination on top of the source, only where the source is: s(1 − αd) + d·αs. DestinationIn = 6 The destination where the source is: d·αs. Use it to cut an image to a shape. DestinationOut = 8 The destination where the source is not: d(1 − αs). Use it to punch a shape out of an image. DestinationOver = 4 The destination covers the source: s(1 − αd) + d, drawing behind what is there. Difference = 23 The absolute difference of the colors: B = |Cd − Cs|. Exclusion = 24 Like Difference with lower contrast: B = Cs + Cd − 2·Cs·Cd. HardLight = 21 Multiplies where the source is dark and screens where it is light, as a harsh spotlight would. Hue = 27 The source's hue with the destination's saturation and luminosity. Lighten = 18 The lighter of the two colors, per channel. Luminosity = 30 The source's luminosity with the destination's hue and saturation. Modulate = 13 The product of color and of alpha: s·d. Multiply = 14 Multiplies the colors, which always darkens: B = Cs·Cd. White changes nothing; black gives black. Overlay = 16 Multiplies or screens depending on the destination, raising contrast: HardLight with the layers swapped. Plus = 12 The sum, clamped to 1, of color and of alpha: min(1, s + d) (the W3C "lighter"). Saturation = 28 The source's saturation with the destination's hue and luminosity. Screen = 15 Multiplies the inverted colors, which always lightens: B = Cs + Cd − Cs·Cd. Black changes nothing. SoftLight = 22 Darkens or lightens depending on the source, as a diffused spotlight would (the W3C formula). Source = 2 The source replaces the destination: s. SourceAtop = 9 The source on top of the destination, only where the destination is: s·αd + d(1 − αs). SourceIn = 5 The source where the destination is: s·αd. SourceOut = 7 The source where the destination is not: s(1 − αd). SourceOver = 0 The source covers the destination: s + d(1 − αs). The default, and what every 1.x DrawImage does. Subtract = 26 The source taken from the destination, clamped: B = max(0, Cd − Cs). Xor = 11 Each where the other is not: s(1 − αd) + d(1 − αs). Examples // One enum names every mode. Blend modes (Multiply to Luminosity) blend the colors, then cover what is under them. BlendMode[] darkening = [BlendMode.Multiply, BlendMode.Darken, BlendMode.ColorBurn]; BlendMode[] cutting = [BlendMode.DestinationIn, BlendMode.DestinationOut]; // shape the destination by the image's alpha Remarks Every mode works on premultiplied values; with s the source and d the destination, each with alpha αs and αd. The source's alpha is multiplied by the opacity first, so opacity 0 leaves the destination as it was for every mode except Clear, Source, DestinationAtop, Modulate and the In and Out modes, whose results depend on where the source is.

api/Egami.Operations.BlurMethod.html.title: Enum BlurMethod | Egami
api/Egami.Operations.BlurMethod.html.summary: Enum BlurMethod Namespace Egami.Operations Assembly Egami.dll How Blur(float, ColorSpace, BlurMethod) computes a Gaussian blur. public enum BlurMethod Fields Exact = 0 The exact Gaussian kernel, radius ceil(3σ): what Blur(float, ColorSpace) does. Its cost grows with σ. Fast = 1 Three box passes per axis with fractional end weights, whose variance equals σ² exactly (Gwosdek et al., 2011): the cost per pixel does not grow with σ, and from σ = 3 up the result is within 50 dB PSNR of Exact. Below σ = 2 it runs the exact kernel, which is as cheap there. Examples // A large, soft background blur: Fast costs the same at any sigma and is within 50 dB of the exact Gaussian from sigma 3. using Raster soft = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Blur(40, ColorSpace.Linear, BlurMethod.Fast), Ct);

api/Egami.Operations.ColorFilter.html.summary: Class ColorFilter Namespace Egami.Operations Assembly Egami.dll A function of one pixel's color, as a value: build one from a matrix, curves, a 3D table or a tone step, chain filters with Then(ColorFilter), mix two with Lerp(ColorFilter, ColorFilter, float), run one with ApplyFilter(ColorFilter) or on your own pixels with Apply<TPixel>(Span<TPixel>), and save it as a .cube file through ToLut3D(int). Like Skia's SkColorFilter, a filter sees only the pixel's own straight RGBA: no neighbours, position or image statistics, so any chain of filters runs as one pass. public sealed class ColorFilter Inheritance object ColorFilter Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // A look as a value: build it once, mix it in at 70%, apply it to any image or to your own pixels. Immutable and safe to share between threads. Returns ColorFilter The filter. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException amount is outside 0..1. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException amount is negative or not finite. api/Egami.Operations.ColorSpace.html.title: Enum ColorSpace | Egami
api/Egami.Operations.ColorSpace.html.summary: Enum ColorSpace Namespace Egami.Operations Assembly Egami.dll The color space in which resizing, blurs and grayscale blend colors: the stored sRGB-encoded values, or linear light. public enum ColorSpace Fields Encoded = 0 Blends the stored sRGB-encoded values, as most libraries and browsers do. The default: faster, and what most people expect. Linear = 1 Converts to linear light, blends, and converts back. Physically correct: fine light detail on dark backgrounds keeps its brightness when reduced. Examples // Lanczos3 is sharper than the default Bicubic; Nearest keeps hard pixel edges (pixel art, masks). using Raster sharp = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Resize(200, 0, ResampleFilter.Lanczos3), Ct); // Blending in linear light keeps fine bright detail on dark backgrounds from going dim when reduced. using Raster linear = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Resize(200, 0, ResampleFilter.Mitchell, ColorSpace.Linear), Ct);

api/Egami.Operations.ColorVisionDeficien.title: Enum ColorVisionDeficiency | Egami
api/Egami.Operations.ColorVisionDeficien.summary: Enum ColorVisionDeficiency Namespace Egami.Operations Assembly Egami.dll A color vision deficiency to simulate. public enum ColorVisionDeficiency Fields Achromatopsia = 3 No color vision: only luminance is seen; a severity below 1 mixes toward it. Deuteranopia = 1 Missing or shifted medium-wavelength (green) cones, the most common kind; a severity below 1 is deuteranomaly. Protanopia = 0 Missing or shifted long-wavelength (red) cones; a severity below 1 is protanomaly. Tritanopia = 2 Missing or shifted short-wavelength (blue) cones; a severity below 1 is tritanomaly. Examples // A two-color poster, then a check of how it reads to someone with deuteranopia. raster.Apply(o => o.Duotone(Rgba8.FromHex("#1b2a49"), Rgba8.FromHex("#f2c14e")).Posterize(4, DitherMode.Ordered), Ct); using Raster<Rgba8> preview = raster.Derive(o => o.SimulateColorBlindness(ColorVisionDeficiency.Deuteranopia), Ct); // High contrast for low vision: gray, lightness inverted so dark becomes light, and more contrast. using Raster<Rgba8> readable = raster.Derive(o => o.HighContrast(grayscale: true, ContrastInvert.Lightness, contrast: 0.3f), Ct);

api/Egami.Operations.Compositor.html.summary: Class Compositor Namespace Egami.Operations Assembly Egami.dll Blends rows of pixels with a BlendMode, for code that composites outside an operation chain: a custom IRasterOperation, a rasterizer filling spans, a layer merge. It runs the kernels DrawImage runs, so Blend<TPixel>(BlendMode, ReadOnlySpan<TPixel>, Span<TPixel>, float, ColorSpace) on a row gives the pixels DrawImage gives there. Every method works for every pixel type, allocates nothing once warm, and is safe to call from many threads at once. public static class Compositor Inheritance object Compositor Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // Blend rows in your own code: a source row, a destination row, and coverage from an antialiased edge. Rgba8[] source = new Rgba8[256], destination = new Rgba8[256]; byte[] coverage = new byte[256]; for (int x = 0; x < 256; x++) { source[x] = new Rgba8((byte)x, 80, 200, 255); destination[x] = new Rgba8(250, 250, 240, 255); coverage[x] = (byte)Math.Clamp((x - 100) * 8, 0, 255); // a soft edge from x = 100 to 132 } Compositor.Blend<Rgba8>(BlendMode.Multiply, source, destination, coverage); // One color through coverage, the way a rasterizer fills a shape's spans. api/Egami.Operations.EdgeOperator.html.title: Enum EdgeOperator | Egami
api/Egami.Operations.EdgeOperator.html.summary: Enum EdgeOperator Namespace Egami.Operations Assembly Egami.dll The kernels Edges(EdgeOperator, bool) finds edges with. Every operator is scaled so a full black-to-white step gives 1 at its strongest pixel; stronger responses (corners, single bright pixels) clamp to 1. public enum EdgeOperator Fields Kirsch = 4 Kirsch's eight 3 × 3 compass kernels (5 on one side, −3 on the others); the strongest response is kept. Laplacian3x3 = 6 The 3 × 3 Laplacian (8 in the middle, −1 around it), as an absolute value: edges come out as thin double lines. Laplacian5x5 = 7 The 5 × 5 Laplacian (24 in the middle, −1 around it), as an absolute value. LaplacianOfGaussian = 8 The 5 × 5 Laplacian of Gaussian (16 in the middle, then −2, −1), as an absolute value: smoothed against noise. Prewitt = 2 Prewitt's 3 × 3 pair, weights 1, 1, 1 across the derivative. RobertsCross = 3 Roberts' 2 × 2 cross of diagonal differences, the pixel and the one below and to its right: the sharpest and noisiest. Robinson = 5 Robinson's eight 3 × 3 compass kernels with weights 1, 2, 1 (Sobel's, turned in 45° steps); the strongest response is kept. Scharr = 1 Scharr's 3 × 3 pair (weights 3, 10, 3), whose magnitude depends least on the edge's direction. Sobel = 0 Sobel and Feldman's 3 × 3 pair, weights 1, 2, 1 across the derivative: the usual choice. Examples using Raster edges = photo.Derive(o => o.Edges(), Ct); // Sobel, gray, 0 to 1 using Raster crisp = photo.Derive(o => o.Edges(EdgeOperator.Scharr), Ct); // rotation-steady using Raster colored = photo.Derive(o => o.Edges(EdgeOperator.Sobel, grayscale: false), Ct); // per channel using Raster lines = photo.Derive(o => o.Blur(1).Edges(EdgeOperator.Laplacian3x3), Ct); // second derivative

Built-in operations implement it, and so can callers: add one to a chain with Add(IRasterOperation). public interface IRasterOperation Examples /// <summary>Swaps red and blue, in parallel bands of rows.</summary> public sealed class SwapRedBlue : IRasterOperation { public Size OutputSize(Size input) => input; public void Run<TPixel>(OperationInput<TPixel> input) where TPixel : unmanaged, IPixelType<TPixel> { input.ForEachBand((start, end) => { for (int y = start; y < end; y++) { Span<TPixel> source = input.Source.Row(y); Span<TPixel> destination = input.Destination.Row(y); for (int x = 0; x < source.Length; x++) { Vector4 v = source[x].ToScaled(); destination[x] = TPixel.FromScaled(new Vector4(v.Z, v.Y, v.X, v.W)); } } }); } } Remarks Implementations must be stateless or immutable: one instance runs on every frame and may run on several threads. Methods OutputSize(Size) Returns the frame size after this operation, so the pipeline can plan memory before any pixel changes. Size OutputSize(Size input) Parameters input Size The frame size before it. Returns Size The size after it. Return input for operations that keep the size. Exceptions ArgumentException The operation cannot apply to a frame of this size. Run<TPixel>(OperationInput<TPixel>) Runs the operation on one frame: reads Source and writes every pixel of Destination. The two can be the same plane, so an operation must handle working in place. void Run<TPixel>(OperationInput<TPixel> input) where TPixel : unmanaged, IPixelType<TPixel> Parameters input OperationInput<TPixel> The planes, context and cancellation token. Type Parameters TPixel The pixel type.

api/Egami.Operations.IWarp.html.title: Interface IWarp | Egami
api/Egami.Operations.IWarp.html.summary: Interface IWarp Namespace Egami.Operations Assembly Egami.dll A general warp: a mapping from each output pixel back to the source point it shows. Egami samples the points with the same sampler as Transform(Homography, TransformOptions?), so every warp gets antialiasing where it shrinks the image, and edge modes. Positions are in pixels with the origin at the top-left corner of the top-left pixel, so pixel centers sit at +0.5. public interface IWarp Examples // Any mapping from output points back to source points; the sampler antialiases wherever it shrinks the image. IWarp ripple = Warp.FromFunction(p => new Vector2(p.X + (6 * MathF.Sin(p.Y / 15)), p.Y)); using Raster rippled = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Warp(ripple, new SamplingOptions { Edges = EdgeMode.Mirror }), Ct); // The same as an IWarp, mapping a whole row per call: no per-pixel delegate, so it is faster. using Raster again = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Warp(new Ripple(6, 15), new SamplingOptions { Edges = EdgeMode.Mirror }), Ct); Remarks Map(int, Size, Span<Vector2>) is called for every output row, from several threads at once, so an implementation must be stateless or immutable. The sampler finds each pixel's footprint from the points its neighbours map to, so a warp only maps points, never derivatives. Methods Map(int, Size, Span<Vector2>) Fills source with the source point of every output pixel center in row y: element x is where output point (x + 0.5, y + 0.5) comes from. A NaN coordinate marks a pixel with no source, which shows the background. void Map(int y, Size input, Span<Vector2> source) Parameters y int The output row. input Size The input size. source Span<Vector2> One point per output column. OutputSize(Size) Returns the size of the warped image for an input of input. Size OutputSize(Size input) Parameters input Size The input size. Returns Size The output size; return input for a warp that keeps the size.

Positions are in pixels of the raster, x to the right, y down and z up out of the image; a pixel's center is at (x + 0.5, y + 0.5), as in Skia. public abstract record Light : IEquatable<Light> Inheritance object Light Implements IEquatable<Light> Derived DistantLight PointLight SpotLight Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // Three light sources, as SVG and Skia have them. api/Egami.Operations.Lut3D.html.title: Class Lut3D | Egami
api/Egami.Operations.Lut3D.html.summary: Class Lut3D Namespace Egami.Operations Assembly Egami.dll A 3D color lookup table: an N × N × N grid of output RGB values over the input cube, with red varying fastest, as .cube files and Hald images store it, and an optional 1D shaper per channel read before the grid (DaVinci Resolve's 1D-plus-3D .cube). Read one with Read(string, EgamiContext?) or FromHald(Raster), and apply it with FromLut(Lut3D, LutInterpolation). public sealed class Lut3D Inheritance object Lut3D Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // Export a grade for DaVinci Resolve or Premiere, then load a .cube file and apply it at 70%. ColorFilter grade = ColorFilter.Curves(ToneCurve.FromPoints([(0, 0), (0.25f, 0.2f), (0.75f, 0.82f), (1, 1)])) .Then(ColorFilter.Saturation(1.1f)); CubeFile.Write("my-grade.cube", grade.ToLut3D(size: 33), title: "My grade"); Lut3D lut = CubeFile.Read("my-grade.cube"); raster.Apply(o => o.ApplyFilter(ColorFilter.Lerp(ColorFilter.Identity, ColorFilter.FromLut(lut), 0.7f)), Ct); // Tables can also be built from a function, and read at any color. Lut3D warm = Lut3D.FromFunction(c => new Vector3(c.X, c.Y * 0.97f, c.Z * 0.9f), size: 17); Vector3 gray = warm.Evaluate(new Vector3(0.5f), LutInterpolation.Tetrahedral); Remarks Values are 32-bit floats and may lie outside 0..1; a filter clamps what it reads. Immutable and safe to share between threads. Properties DomainMax Gets the input that maps to the last grid point on each axis (DOMAIN_MAX in a .cube file). Defaults to 1. public Vector3 DomainMax { get; } Property Value Vector3 DomainMin Gets the input that maps to the first grid point on each axis (DOMAIN_MIN in a .cube file). Defaults to 0. public Vector3 DomainMin { get; } Property Value Vector3 this[int, int, int] Gets one grid point's output. public Vector3 this[int red, int green, int blue] { get; } Parameters red int The red index, 0 to Size − 1. green int The green index. blue int The blue index. Property Value Vector3 The output color. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException An index is out of range. ShaperSize Gets the number of entries in the 1D shaper read before the grid, or 0 when there is none. public int ShaperSize { get; } Property Value int Size Gets the number of grid points along each axis. public int Size { get; } Property Value int Methods Evaluate(Vector3, LutInterpolation) Returns the table's output for one color. public Vector3 Evaluate(Vector3 color, LutInterpolation interpolation = LutInterpolation.Tetrahedral) Parameters color Vector3 The input; each channel is clamped to the shaper's range, then to the domain. interpolation LutInterpolation How to read between grid points. Defaults to Tetrahedral. Returns Vector3 The output, unclamped. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException interpolation is not defined. FromFunction(Func<Vector3, Vector3>, int) Creates a table by sampling function at every grid point over 0..1. public static Lut3D FromFunction(Func<Vector3, Vector3> function, int size = 33) Parameters function Func<Vector3, Vector3> The color function; it is called only here. size int The points per axis, from 2 to 256. Defaults to 33. Returns Lut3D The table. Exceptions ArgumentNullException function is null. ArgumentOutOfRangeException size is outside 2 to 256. ArgumentException The function returned a value that is not finite. FromHald(Raster) Reads a Hald CLUT image, as ImageMagick, G'MIC and RawTherapee write them: a level-L image is L³ × L³ pixels holding an L² table, red fastest, row by row. The image's own color profile is ignored, since it is a table rather than a picture. public static Lut3D FromHald(Raster hald) Parameters hald Raster The image; its first frame is read. Returns Lut3D The table. Exceptions ArgumentNullException hald is null. ArgumentException The image is not square with a side that is a cube from 8 to 4096. FromValues(int, ReadOnlySpan<Vector3>, Vector3?, Vector3?) Creates a table from its grid values, red varying fastest, then green, then blue. public static Lut3D FromValues(int size, ReadOnlySpan<Vector3> values, Vector3? domainMin = null, Vector3? domainMax = null) Parameters size int The points per axis, from 2 to 256. values ReadOnlySpan<Vector3> Exactly size³ finite colors. domainMin Vector3? The input at the first grid point, or null for 0. domainMax Vector3? The input at the last grid point, or null for 1; above domainMin on every axis. Returns Lut3D The table. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException size is outside 2 to 256. ArgumentException The value count is wrong, a value is not finite, or the domain is empty. ToHald(int) Writes the table as a Hald image of level: (level²)³ grid points in a level³ × level³ 16-bit image, for grading in an editor and loading back with FromHald(Raster). public Raster<Rgba16> ToHald(int level = 8) Parameters level int The Hald level, from 2 to 16. Defaults to 8 (a 512 × 512 image holding a 64³ table). Returns Raster<Rgba16> The image; the caller disposes it. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException level is outside 2 to 16. WithShaper(ReadOnlySpan<Vector3>, float, float) Returns this table with a 1D shaper read before it, as the first table of a 1D-plus-3D .cube file. public Lut3D WithShaper(ReadOnlySpan<Vector3> shaper, float inputMin = 0, float inputMax = 1) Parameters shaper ReadOnlySpan<Vector3> From 2 to 65,536 finite RGB entries, the first for inputMin and the last for inputMax. inputMin float The input at the shaper's first entry. Defaults to 0. inputMax float The input at its last entry, above inputMin. Defaults to 1. Returns Lut3D The table with the shaper, replacing any it had. Exceptions ArgumentException The shaper's length or values are out of range, or the range is empty.

api/Egami.Operations.MorphologyOp.html.title: Enum MorphologyOp | Egami
api/Egami.Operations.MorphologyOp.html.summary: Enum MorphologyOp Namespace Egami.Operations Assembly Egami.dll The operations of Morphology(MorphologyOp, StructuringElement, int), all flat (gray-level) and per channel. public enum MorphologyOp Fields BottomHat = 6 The Close minus the image: the dark details smaller than the shape. Alpha is kept. Close = 3 Dilate, then erode: fills dark gaps and holes smaller than the shape. Never darkens a pixel. Dilate = 0 The maximum over the shape: light areas grow, dark specks vanish. Erode = 1 The minimum over the shape: light areas shrink, light specks vanish. Gradient = 4 Dilate minus erode: the outlines of shapes, as wide as the shape. Alpha is kept. Open = 2 Erode, then dilate: removes light details smaller than the shape and keeps the rest. Never brightens a pixel. TopHat = 5 The image minus its Open: the light details smaller than the shape. Alpha is kept. Examples // Close removes dark specks smaller than the shape (dust and toner dots on the paper) and keeps strokes wider than it; // Open does the opposite, for light pinholes in dark areas. using Raster<Gray8> scan = Raster.Load<Gray8>("scan.tif"); scan.Apply(o => o.Morphology(MorphologyOp.Close, StructuringElement.Disk(1)), Ct); // The outlines of shapes, and the light details smaller than a disk. using Raster outlines = scan.Derive(o => o.Morphology(MorphologyOp.Gradient, StructuringElement.Square(1)), Ct); using Raster details = scan.Derive(o => o.Morphology(MorphologyOp.TopHat, StructuringElement.Disk(5)), Ct);

api/Egami.Operations.NoiseKind.html.title: Enum NoiseKind | Egami
api/Egami.Operations.NoiseKind.html.summary: Enum NoiseKind Namespace Egami.Operations Assembly Egami.dll The noise AddNoise(NoiseKind, float, bool, ulong) adds: ImageMagick's +noise kinds, with values on 0..1 and the amount as ImageMagick's -attenuate. At amount 1 the formulas are ImageMagick's Q16 ones. public enum NoiseKind Fields Gaussian = 0 Normal noise of standard deviation 5/64 × amount (about 20 of 255 levels at amount 1), plus a small part that grows with the value. Impulse = 2 Salt and pepper: each value becomes 0 or 1, each with probability amount / 20. Laplacian = 3 Laplacian (two-sided exponential) noise of scale 5/128 × amount: sharper peaked and heavier tailed than Gaussian. Multiplicative = 4 Normal noise proportional to the value: v × (1 + amount / 4 × N(0, 1)), so dark areas stay clean. Poisson = 5 Photon (shot) noise: a Poisson count of mean 12.5 × amount × v, scaled back, so the variance is v / (12.5 × amount). Uniform = 1 Uniform noise, ±amount / 128. Examples // Film grain: gray Gaussian noise at a third of ImageMagick's default strength; the same seed gives the same grain. photo.Apply(ops => ops.AddNoise(NoiseKind.Gaussian, 0.3f, monochrome: true, seed: 42), Ct);

api/Egami.Operations.OperationReach.html.summary: Struct OperationReach Namespace Egami.Operations Assembly Egami.dll How far an operation chain reads past each output pixel, in whole pixels across and down: a pixel of the result can depend on input pixels up to X columns and Y rows away. A blur of σ reaches about 3σ; a color matrix reaches nothing. Reach(Action<RasterOps>) measures a chain, so code that runs one on part of a larger picture, such as a canvas layer, can include the pixels around it that the chain will read. public readonly record struct OperationReach : IEquatable<OperationReach> Implements IEquatable<OperationReach> Inherited Members ValueType.Equals(object) ValueType.GetHashCode() ValueType.ToString() object.Equals(object, object) object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Examples // How far a chain reads around each pixel: run it on a part of a picture padded by this much, and the part comes out as it // would in the whole picture. OperationReach? reach = RasterOps.Reach(ops => ops.Blur(3).Glow(4, Rgba8.White)); if (reach is OperationReach r) { Console.WriteLine($"pad by {r.X} × {r.Y}"); } // A resize reads the whole image: its reach is unknown. Assert.Null(RasterOps.Reach(ops => ops.Resize(100, 100))); Constructors OperationReach(int, int) How far an operation chain reads past each output pixel, in whole pixels across and down: a pixel of the result can depend on input pixels up to X columns and Y rows away. api/Egami.Operations.PixelMath.html.title: Enum PixelMath | Egami
api/Egami.Operations.PixelMath.html.summary: Enum PixelMath Namespace Egami.Operations Assembly Egami.dll An arithmetic operation with a constant, for Arithmetic(PixelMath, float, ColorChannels): ImageMagick's -evaluate operators. public enum PixelMath Fields Add = 0 v + value. Divide = 3 v / value; dividing by 0 divides by the smallest positive number instead. Log = 5 log(value · v + 1) / log(value + 1): brightens shadows, more strongly as value grows. Max = 7 The larger of v and value. Min = 6 The smaller of v and value. Multiply = 2 v · value. Pow = 4 v raised to the power value. Set = 8 value, whatever v is. Subtract = 1 v − value. Examples // Lift the shadows with a log curve, then cap the highlights; values are on a 0 to 1 scale, as ImageMagick's -evaluate. photo.Apply(ops => ops .Arithmetic(PixelMath.Log, 3) .Arithmetic(PixelMath.Min, 0.95f), Ct);
