api/Egami.Operations.RasterOps.html.title: Class RasterOps | Egami
api/Egami.Operations.RasterOps.html.summary: Class RasterOps Namespace Egami.Operations Assembly Egami.dll Animation steps: they work on the frames of the whole animation rather than on each frame, so they run in Apply, Derive and Transcode (which then decodes the whole animation first) but not inside Within. Frames in memory are already full pictures of what is on screen, so there is no Coalesce, and the writers find each frame's changed area themselves, so there is no Optimize. public sealed class RasterOps Inheritance object RasterOps Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Extension Methods DrawingExtensions.Draw(RasterOps, Action<Canvas, int>, CanvasOptions?) DrawingExtensions.Draw(RasterOps, Action<Canvas>, CanvasOptions?) Examples raster.Apply(ops => ops.Add(new MyOperation())); Methods AdaptiveThreshold(float, int?, Rgba8?, Rgba8?) Thresholds each pixel against the mean of the window around it (Bradley and Roth, 2007): a pixel is dark when its luminance is more than limit below its window's mean, so uneven lighting on a scanned page does not swallow text. Alpha is kept. public RasterOps AdaptiveThreshold(float limit = 0.15, int? window = null, Rgba8? below = null, Rgba8? above = null) Parameters limit float How far below the local mean a pixel must be to count as dark, from 0 to 1. Defaults to 0.15. window int? The window's side in pixels, at least 1, or null (the default) for an eighth of the width. below Rgba8? The dark color, or null for black. above Rgba8? The light color, or null for white. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Threshold a scanned page for OCR: Otsu's level for an evenly lit page, or Bradley's local threshold for uneven light. float level = page.FindThreshold(ThresholdMethod.Otsu); using Raster<Gray8> even = page.Derive(o => o.AutoThreshold(ThresholdMethod.Otsu), Ct); using Raster<Gray8> uneven = page.Derive(o => o.AdaptiveThreshold(limit: 0.15f), Ct); Remarks A luminance plane, 4 bytes a pixel, counts against MaxTotalBytes. Inside a rectangle or mask, the scope is its image. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException An argument is out of range. Add(IRasterOperation) Adds a step, such as a custom IRasterOperation. public RasterOps Add(IRasterOperation operation) Parameters operation IRasterOperation The operation. Returns RasterOps This builder. Exceptions ArgumentNullException operation is null. AddNoise(NoiseKind, float, bool, ulong) Adds noise to red, green and blue (or a CMYK raster's inks), as ImageMagick's +noise with -attenuate does: film grain, sensor noise, or salt and pepper for testing filters. Alpha is never touched. The same seed gives the same pixels on any machine and at any thread count, and inside a scope an area gets the noise the whole image would get there. public RasterOps AddNoise(NoiseKind kind, float amount = 1, bool monochrome = false, ulong seed = 0) Parameters kind NoiseKind The kind of noise. amount float The strength, as ImageMagick's -attenuate, from 0 (changes nothing) to 10; 1 gives ImageMagick's default. monochrome bool Whether red, green and blue get the same noise, so it has no color. seed ulong The seed: change it for different noise. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Film grain: gray Gaussian noise at a third of ImageMagick's default strength; the same seed gives the same grain. photo.Apply(ops => ops.AddNoise(NoiseKind.Gaussian, 0.3f, monochrome: true, seed: 42), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException kind is not defined, or amount is outside 0..10. AlphaToGray() Makes the image a gray picture of its alpha: red, green and blue become the alpha value and alpha becomes opaque, as ImageMagick's -alpha extract does. A color matrix, so it fuses with neighbouring color steps. public RasterOps AlphaToGray() Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples using Raster alpha = photo.Derive(ops => ops.AlphaToGray(), Ct); // see the transparency as gray using Raster cutout = photo.Derive(ops => ops.CopyAlpha(new Mask(matte)), Ct); // a gray image becomes the alpha using Raster onWhite = cutout.Derive(ops => ops.Flatten(Rgba8.White), Ct); // composite onto white, opaque using Raster luma = photo.Derive(ops => ops.LuminanceToAlpha(), Ct); // brightness becomes alpha ApplyFilter(ColorFilter) Runs a ColorFilter on every pixel. Adjacent filters, tone steps and color matrices run as one pass over the image, clamping between steps as running them one by one would. public RasterOps ApplyFilter(ColorFilter filter) Parameters filter ColorFilter The filter. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // A look as a value: build it once, mix it in at 70%, apply it to any image or to your own pixels. ColorFilter look = ColorFilter.Level(0.03f, 0.97f).Then(ColorFilter.Saturation(1.2f)).Then(ColorFilter.Tint(new Rgba8(255, 190, 140, 255), 0.2f)); ColorFilter subtle = ColorFilter.Lerp(ColorFilter.Identity, look, 0.7f); raster.Apply(o => o.ApplyFilter(subtle), Ct); Span<Rgba8> swatch = [new Rgba8(200, 120, 80, 255), new Rgba8(40, 60, 90, 255)]; subtle.Apply(swatch); Exceptions ArgumentNullException filter is null. Arithmetic(PixelMath, float, ColorChannels) Applies op with value to every value of channels, on values scaled 0 to 1 and clamped back to 0..1, as ImageMagick's -evaluate defines each operator. 8-bit and 16-bit pixels are evaluated as 16-bit samples and rounded as ImageMagick's Q16 build rounds them, through a table per call, so results are identical to -evaluate. public RasterOps Arithmetic(PixelMath op, float value, ColorChannels channels = ColorChannels.Color) Parameters op PixelMath The operator. value float The constant, on the same 0 to 1 scale for Add, Subtract, Min, Max and Set. channels ColorChannels The channels to change. Defaults to Color; alpha changes only when included. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Lift the shadows with a log curve, then cap the highlights; values are on a 0 to 1 scale, as ImageMagick's -evaluate. photo.Apply(ops => ops .Arithmetic(PixelMath.Log, 3) .Arithmetic(PixelMath.Min, 0.95f), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException op is not defined, value is not finite, or channels holds values that are not channels. AutoGamma(bool, bool) Applies the Gamma(float) that moves the image's mean to 0.5, as ImageMagick's -auto-gamma; an image whose mean is 0 or 1 is left alone. Measured like AutoLevel(bool, bool). public RasterOps AutoGamma(bool linked = true, bool perFrame = false) Parameters linked bool Whether the channels share one gamma from their joint mean (the default) or each gets its own. perFrame bool Whether each frame is measured alone. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Fix a dull scan: stretch it to the full range, clipping the darkest 2% and lightest 1%, then set the midtones. raster.Apply(o => o.Normalize().AutoGamma(), Ct); // Or stretch each channel on its own, which also removes a cast. raster.Apply(o => o.AutoLevel(linked: false), Ct); // Measured steps measure only their scope: here the sky alone is stretched. raster.Apply(o => o.Within(new Rect(0, 0, raster.Width, raster.Height / 3), sky => sky.AutoLevel()), Ct); AutoLevel(bool, bool) Stretches the darkest value to 0 and the lightest to 1, as ImageMagick's -auto-level. The chain runs up to this step, the result is measured, and the step becomes a Level(float, float, float, float, float); inside Within(Rect, Action<RasterOps>), Within(Mask, Action<RasterOps>) or OnChannels(ColorChannels, Action<RasterOps>) only that scope is measured. Transparent pixels do not count. public RasterOps AutoLevel(bool linked = true, bool perFrame = false) Parameters linked bool Whether red, green and blue share one black and one white point (the default, which keeps colors), or each gets its own, which also removes a cast. perFrame bool Whether each frame is measured alone, as ImageMagick does, instead of all frames together so an animation does not flicker. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Fix a dull scan: stretch it to the full range, clipping the darkest 2% and lightest 1%, then set the midtones. raster.Apply(o => o.Normalize().AutoGamma(), Ct); // Or stretch each channel on its own, which also removes a cast. raster.Apply(o => o.AutoLevel(linked: false), Ct); // Measured steps measure only their scope: here the sky alone is stretched. raster.Apply(o => o.Within(new Rect(0, 0, raster.Width, raster.Height / 3), sky => sky.AutoLevel()), Ct); AutoOrient() Turns the image the way its EXIF orientation says, so it looks as the camera meant, and sets the orientation to Normal. Each orientation is one exact pass (a flip, a quarter turn or a transpose); an image without EXIF, or already upright, is left alone. Followed by Resize(int, int, ResampleFilter, ColorSpace), Fit(int, int, ResampleFilter, ColorSpace, bool) or Cover(int, int, Anchor, ResampleFilter, ColorSpace), the resize runs first on the stored image and the small result is turned, which matches the other order to within rounding. public RasterOps AutoOrient() Returns RasterOps This builder. AutoThreshold(ThresholdMethod, ThresholdMode, Rgba8?, Rgba8?, bool) Thresholds at the level method finds in the histogram, as ImageMagick's -auto-threshold; see FindThreshold(ThresholdMethod, ThresholdMode). Measured like AutoLevel(bool, bool). public RasterOps AutoThreshold(ThresholdMethod method = ThresholdMethod.Otsu, ThresholdMode mode = ThresholdMode.Luminance, Rgba8? below = null, Rgba8? above = null, bool perFrame = false) Parameters method ThresholdMethod How the level is found. Defaults to Otsu. mode ThresholdMode What is measured. Defaults to Luminance. below Rgba8? The lower color, or null for black. above Rgba8? The upper color, or null for white. perFrame bool Whether each frame is measured alone. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Threshold a scanned page for OCR: Otsu's level for an evenly lit page, or Bradley's local threshold for uneven light. float level = page.FindThreshold(ThresholdMethod.Otsu); using Raster<Gray8> even = page.Derive(o => o.AutoThreshold(ThresholdMethod.Otsu), Ct); using Raster<Gray8> uneven = page.Derive(o => o.AdaptiveThreshold(limit: 0.15f), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException An enum value is not defined. AutoWhiteBalance(WhiteBalanceMethod, bool) Removes a color cast it measures, by method. Measured like AutoLevel(bool, bool). public RasterOps AutoWhiteBalance(WhiteBalanceMethod method = WhiteBalanceMethod.GrayWorld, bool perFrame = false) Parameters method WhiteBalanceMethod How the cast is found. Defaults to GrayWorld, ImageMagick's -white-balance. perFrame bool Whether each frame is measured alone. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Correct a tungsten-lit photo, as a raw editor's temperature slider does. raster.Apply(o => o.WhiteBalance(temperature: 3200), Ct); // Or pick a gray card's color and make it neutral. raster.Apply(o => o.WhiteBalance(new Rgba8(182, 170, 151, 255)), Ct); // Or let the image tell: ImageMagick's gray world, or the brightest pixels as white. raster.Apply(o => o.AutoWhiteBalance(WhiteBalanceMethod.GrayWorld), Ct); raster.Apply(o => o.AutoWhiteBalance(WhiteBalanceMethod.WhitePatch), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException method is not defined. BilateralBlur(float, float, int?) Smooths while keeping edges (Tomasi and Manduchi's bilateral filter): each neighbour counts by its distance, through a Gaussian of spatialSigma, and by how much its color differs, through a Gaussian of rangeSigma, so noise flattens and edges stay. The color difference is the root-mean-square difference of red, green and blue on 0..1, so on a gray image the sigmas mean what ImageMagick's -bilateral-blur WxW+(255·rangeSigma)+spatialSigma means. Alpha is averaged with the same weights; edges repeat the edge pixel. public RasterOps BilateralBlur(float spatialSigma, float rangeSigma, int? radius = null) Parameters spatialSigma float The reach in pixels, above 0 and at most 50. rangeSigma float How different a color may be and still count, above 0, on the 0..1 scale: 0.1 keeps most edges. radius int? The window's radius, or null for ⌈2 · spatialSigma⌉ as ImageMagick's width; at most 100. Above 8 the taps are taken every ⌈radius / 8⌉ pixels, so the cost stays bounded. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Smooth skin or sky while keeping edges: neighbours count less the more their color differs (0.1 on the 0..1 scale). using Raster smooth = photo.Derive(ops => ops.BilateralBlur(spatialSigma: 4, rangeSigma: 0.1f), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException A sigma is not positive and finite or above its limit, or radius is negative or above 100. BlendColor(Rgba8, BlendMode, float, ColorSpace) Blends one color over every pixel by mode: Multiply tints, Screen washes out, Color colorizes. The color's own alpha and opacity set how strongly. public RasterOps BlendColor(Rgba8 color, BlendMode mode, float opacity = 1, ColorSpace colorSpace = ColorSpace.Encoded) Parameters color Rgba8 The color, with straight alpha. mode BlendMode How the color combines with each pixel. opacity float Multiplies the color's alpha before the mode: 1 uses it as it is. colorSpace ColorSpace Where pixels are blended. Defaults to Encoded. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Warm the photo with an orange tint, and give it a gray-blue color grade. photo.Apply(ops => ops .BlendColor(new Rgba8(255, 200, 150, 255), BlendMode.Multiply) .BlendColor(new Rgba8(60, 80, 110, 255), BlendMode.Color, opacity: 0.3f), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException opacity is outside 0..1, or an enum value is not defined. Bloom(float, float, float) Makes bright areas glow, as a camera's bloom: the parts of each channel above threshold, stretched to 0..1 and scaled by intensity, blurred in linear light with Fast and screened onto the image in linear light. It is exactly the chain written by hand: a layer made with one ColorMatrix(ColorMatrix) (red, green and blue times k = intensity / (1 − threshold), minus threshold × k, clamped) and Blur(float, ColorSpace, BlurMethod) in linear light, then drawn with DrawImage, Screen, in linear light. public RasterOps Bloom(float threshold = 0.8, float sigma = 10, float intensity = 1) Parameters threshold float The stored value above which a channel blooms, from 0 to under 1. sigma float The bloom's blur in pixels, from 0 to 1000. intensity float How strongly the bloom is added, from 0 (nothing) to 100; values are clamped to 1 before the blur. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Highlights above 80% bleed light into their surroundings, added in linear light as a lens does. photo.Apply(ops => ops.Bloom(threshold: 0.8f, sigma: 12, intensity: 1.5f), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException threshold is outside 0 to under 1, sigma is outside 0..1000, or intensity is outside 0..100. Blur(float, ColorSpace) Blurs with a Gaussian of standard deviation sigma pixels (radius ceil(3σ), weights normalized). Edges repeat the edge pixel. Above σ = 100, where a true Gaussian needs over 600 taps a pass, it runs as three box blurs of matched width, whose variance is within 3% of the Gaussian's. public RasterOps Blur(float sigma, ColorSpace colorSpace = ColorSpace.Encoded) Parameters sigma float The standard deviation in pixels; 0 changes nothing. colorSpace ColorSpace Where pixels are blended. Defaults to Encoded. Returns RasterOps This builder. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException sigma is negative or not finite. Blur(float, ColorSpace, BlurMethod) Blurs with a Gaussian of standard deviation sigma pixels, computed by method. Exact is Blur(float, ColorSpace); Fast costs the same at any σ, for shadows, glows and other large blurs. Edges repeat the edge pixel. public RasterOps Blur(float sigma, ColorSpace colorSpace, BlurMethod method) Parameters sigma float The standard deviation in pixels; 0 changes nothing. colorSpace ColorSpace Where pixels are blended. method BlurMethod How the blur is computed. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // A large, soft background blur: Fast costs the same at any sigma and is within 50 dB of the exact Gaussian from sigma 3. using Raster soft = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Blur(40, ColorSpace.Linear, BlurMethod.Fast), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException sigma is negative, not finite or above 1000, or an enum value is not defined. BoxBlur(int) Replaces each pixel with the mean of the (2r + 1) square around it. Edges repeat the edge pixel. public RasterOps BoxBlur(int radius) Parameters radius int The radius in pixels; 0 changes nothing. Returns RasterOps This builder. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException radius is negative or above 1000. Brightness(float) Multiplies red, green and blue by amount: 1 changes nothing, 0 gives black. See Brightness(float). public RasterOps Brightness(float amount) Parameters amount float The factor, 0 or more. Returns RasterOps This builder. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException amount is negative or not finite. CannyEdges(float, float, float) Finds thin edges with Canny's detector, as ImageMagick's -canny 0x{sigma}+{low × 100}%+{high × 100}% does: the luma is smoothed by a Gaussian, Canny's first differences give the gradient, pixels that are not the strongest across their edge are dropped, and hysteresis keeps pixels whose magnitude reaches high times the largest, plus those 8-connected to them that reach low times it. Writes white edges on black, one pixel wide, with alpha kept: a gray result works as a Mask as it is, a color one with Luminance. Reads the whole image, so inside a scope it sees all of it. public RasterOps CannyEdges(float sigma = 1, float low = 0.1, float high = 0.3) Parameters sigma float The Gaussian's standard deviation in pixels, 0 (no smoothing) to 100. low float The low threshold, as a fraction 0 to 1 of the largest gradient; at most high. high float The high threshold, as a fraction 0 to 1 of the largest gradient. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Thin white edges on black. A gray raster works as a Mask as it is; an RGBA one needs MaskChannel.Luminance, // because a Mask of a raster with alpha reads its alpha. using Raster<Gray8> edges = Raster.Load<Gray8>("duck.png"); edges.Apply(o => o.CannyEdges(sigma: 1.4f).Dilate(1), Ct); // thin edges, thickened photo.Apply(o => o.Within(new Mask(edges), s => s.FillColor(Rgba8.Red)), Ct); // paint over them Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException sigma is negative, not finite or above 100; a threshold is outside 0 to 1, or low is above high. ChangeSpeed(double) Plays the animation factor times as fast: every delay is divided by it, rounded to whole milliseconds. public RasterOps ChangeSpeed(double factor) Parameters factor double The speed-up, more than 0: 2 plays twice as fast, 0.5 at half speed. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Twice as fast, then backwards: a boomerang clip is the clip followed by its reverse. using Raster fast = clip.Derive(ops => ops.ChangeSpeed(2), Ct); using Raster backwards = fast.Derive(ops => ops.Reverse(), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException factor is not finite or not positive. Clahe(int, int, float, int) Contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization (Zuiderveld, 1994) on L*, as ImageMagick's -clahe: each of tilesX × tilesY tiles gets its own clipped, equalized curve, blended smoothly between tile centers, so local detail comes up without the noise of plain equalization. a* and b* are kept. Each frame is its own. public RasterOps Clahe(int tilesX = 8, int tilesY = 8, float clipLimit = 2, int bins = 256) Parameters tilesX int Tiles across, from 1 to 256. Defaults to 8. tilesY int Tiles down, from 1 to 256. Defaults to 8. clipLimit float How far a tile's histogram may rise, as a multiple of its mean bin (2 is mild, 4 strong); 0 does not clip. bins int The histogram bins, from 2 to 4,096. Defaults to 256. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Bring out detail in a flat, foggy landscape: CLAHE on 8 × 8 tiles, then ImageMagick's local contrast. raster.Apply(o => o.Clahe(tilesX: 8, tilesY: 8, clipLimit: 2).LocalContrast(radius: 0.1f, strength: 0.15f), Ct); Remarks The lightness plane, 4 bytes a pixel, counts against MaxTotalBytes. Inside a rectangle or mask, the scope is its image. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException An argument is out of range. ColorMatrix(ColorMatrix) Applies a color matrix to straight RGBA and clamps the result. Adjacent color steps are multiplied into one matrix before anything runs, so the chain clamps once, at its end. public RasterOps ColorMatrix(ColorMatrix matrix) Parameters matrix ColorMatrix The matrix. Returns RasterOps This builder. Colorize(Rgba8, float) Blends red, green and blue toward color, as ImageMagick's -colorize. See Colorize(Rgba8, float). public RasterOps Colorize(Rgba8 color, float amount) Parameters color Rgba8 The color. amount float The blend, from 0 to 1. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // A two-color poster, then a check of how it reads to someone with deuteranopia. raster.Apply(o => o.Duotone(Rgba8.FromHex("#1b2a49"), Rgba8.FromHex("#f2c14e")).Posterize(4, DitherMode.Ordered), Ct); using Raster<Rgba8> preview = raster.Derive(o => o.SimulateColorBlindness(ColorVisionDeficiency.Deuteranopia), Ct); // High contrast for low vision: gray, lightness inverted so dark becomes light, and more contrast. using Raster<Rgba8> readable = raster.Derive(o => o.HighContrast(grayscale: true, ContrastInvert.Lightness, contrast: 0.3f), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException amount is outside 0..1. Contrast(float) Scales red, green and blue around mid-gray: 1 changes nothing, 0 gives flat gray. See Contrast(float). public RasterOps Contrast(float amount) Parameters amount float The factor, 0 or more. Returns RasterOps This builder. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException amount is negative or not finite. Examples // Fill the region around (10, 10) whose colors are close to its own, as a paint bucket does. photo.Apply(ops => ops.FloodFill(new Point(10, 10), Rgba8.White, tolerance: 0.1f), Ct); Remarks The fill keeps a visited set of one bit a pixel, which counts against MaxTotalBytes. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException tolerance is outside 0..1, connectivity is not defined, or the seed lies outside the image when the chain runs. Gamma(float) Raises red, green and blue to 1/gamma, as ImageMagick's -gamma: 2.2 brightens. See Gamma(float). public RasterOps Gamma(float gamma) Parameters gamma float The gamma, above 0. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // A basic tone panel: levels with a midtone lift, a gentle S-curve, and a warm tint in the midtones. The three steps run as // one pass over the pixels. raster.Apply(o => o .Level(black: 0.04f, white: 0.96f, gamma: 1.1f) .SigmoidalContrast(4, midpoint: 0.5f) .Tint(new Rgba8(255, 200, 150, 255), 0.15f), Ct); raster.Save("duck-toned.jpg"); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException gamma is not a positive finite number. Glow(float, Rgba8, float, bool) Adds a glow around the image's alpha shape, as an editor's outer glow layer style: the alpha, blurred with Fast, spread, and filled with color, drawn behind the image. With inner the glow comes in from the shape's edges instead and is drawn on the image, inside the shape only. It is exactly the chain written by hand: a layer made with a ColorMatrix(ColorMatrix) (the color, and alpha or 1 − alpha), Blur(float, ColorSpace, BlurMethod), Arithmetic(PixelMath, float, ColorChannels) multiplying alpha by 1 / (1 − spread) and Opacity(float) for the color's alpha, then drawn with DrawImage (the image over the layer, or the layer over the image with SourceAtop). Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // A soft yellow glow around the badge, behind it; spread hardens it before it fades. using Raster outer = logo.Derive(ops => ops.Glow(8, new Rgba8(255, 210, 0, 230), spread: 0.3f), Ct); // A white glow coming in from the badge's edges, inside it only. using Raster inner = logo.Derive(ops => ops.Glow(5, Rgba8.White, inner: true), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException sigma is outside 0..1000, or spread is outside 0 to under 1. Grayscale(LumaWeights, float, ColorSpace) Converts toward gray. By default the luma is taken from the stored, gamma-encoded values, as CSS filters do; pass Linear to weigh the colors in linear light, which keeps perceived brightness better. public RasterOps Grayscale(LumaWeights mode = LumaWeights.Rec709, float amount = 1, ColorSpace colorSpace = ColorSpace.Encoded) Parameters mode LumaWeights The luma weights. Defaults to Rec709. amount float 0 changes nothing, 1 gives full gray. colorSpace ColorSpace Where the luma is taken. Defaults to Encoded. Returns RasterOps This builder. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException An argument is out of range. HighContrast(bool, ContrastInvert, float) Skia's high-contrast accessibility filter. See HighContrast(bool, ContrastInvert, float). public RasterOps HighContrast(bool grayscale = false, ContrastInvert invert = ContrastInvert.None, float contrast = 0) Parameters grayscale bool Whether colors become gray first. invert ContrastInvert How to invert. Defaults to None. contrast float The contrast, from −1 to 1. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // A two-color poster, then a check of how it reads to someone with deuteranopia. raster.Apply(o => o.Duotone(Rgba8.FromHex("#1b2a49"), Rgba8.FromHex("#f2c14e")).Posterize(4, DitherMode.Ordered), Ct); using Raster<Rgba8> preview = raster.Derive(o => o.SimulateColorBlindness(ColorVisionDeficiency.Deuteranopia), Ct); // High contrast for low vision: gray, lightness inverted so dark becomes light, and more contrast. using Raster<Rgba8> readable = raster.Derive(o => o.HighContrast(grayscale: true, ContrastInvert.Lightness, contrast: 0.3f), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException An argument is out of range. HueRotate(float) Rotates hue around the luma axis. See HueRotate(float). public RasterOps HueRotate(float degrees) Parameters degrees float The angle; 0 changes nothing. Returns RasterOps This builder. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException degrees is not finite. InnerShadow(float, float, float, Rgba8) Adds a shadow inside the image's alpha shape, as an editor's inner shadow layer style: everything outside the shape, moved by (dx, dy) rounded to whole pixels, blurred with Fast and filled with color, drawn on the image inside the shape only. Past the image's edges counts as outside, so a shape that touches an edge is shadowed from there too. It is exactly the chain written by hand: a layer made with a ColorMatrix(ColorMatrix) (the color, and 1 − alpha), Offset(int, int, EdgeMode, Rgba8) with the uncovered strips filled with the opaque color, Blur(float, ColorSpace, BlurMethod) and Opacity(float) for the color's alpha, then drawn over the image with SourceAtop. public RasterOps InnerShadow(float dx, float dy, float sigma, Rgba8 color) Parameters dx float How far the shadow moves right, in pixels (negative moves it left), at most 10000 either way. dy float How far the shadow moves down, in pixels, at most 10000 either way. sigma float The shadow's blur in pixels, from 0 (a hard shadow) to 1000. color Rgba8 The shadow's color, with its alpha as the shadow's opacity. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // A shadow inside the badge, cast from up and left, as a pressed button looks. using Raster pressed = logo.Derive(ops => ops.InnerShadow(2, 3, 3, new Rgba8(0, 0, 0, 140)), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException An offset is not finite or beyond 10000 either way, or sigma is outside 0..1000. Invert(float) Replaces red, green and blue with 1 − value, blended by amount. See Invert(float). public RasterOps Invert(float amount = 1) Parameters amount float 0 changes nothing, 1 inverts fully. Returns RasterOps This builder. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException amount is outside 0..1. Kuwahara(int, float) Smooths while keeping edges, with the Kuwahara filter as ImageMagick's -kuwahara defines it: of the four (r + 1) squares that have the pixel as a corner, the one whose luma varies least gives the pixel its value, sampled at that square's middle. With sigma above 0 the image is blurred first with ImageMagick's kernel for radius x sigma (a Gaussian of σ out to the radius). The variances come from summed-area tables, so the cost does not grow with the radius. public RasterOps Kuwahara(int radius = 3, float sigma = 0) Parameters radius int The radius in pixels, from 1 to 100. sigma float The blur before, in pixels, from 0 (none) to 100. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Flattens texture into patches while keeping edges; a small blur first, as ImageMagick's -kuwahara 4x1. using Raster smooth = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Kuwahara(4, sigma: 1), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException radius is outside 1..100, or sigma is outside 0..100. LensBlur(float, LensBlurOptions?) Blurs as an out-of-focus lens does: each point spreads into the aperture's shape, a disc or a polygon of 5 to 12 blades, so small lights become discs, unlike a Gaussian's soft spots. Works in linear light by default, since a lens adds light; HighlightGain makes bright lights bloom. The cost does not grow with the radius: the blur runs by FFT on tiles. Edges repeat the edge pixel. public RasterOps LensBlur(float radius, LensBlurOptions? options = null) Parameters radius float The aperture's radius in pixels, from 0 (changes nothing) to 128. options LensBlurOptions The aperture and highlights, or null for a round aperture in linear light. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Blur the background like a wide-open lens with a six-blade aperture: bright points become hexagons. LensBlurOptions lens = new() { Blades = 6, Rotation = 15, HighlightGain = 4, HighlightThreshold = 0.8f }; photo.Apply(ops => ops.Within(new Rect(0, 0, photo.Width, photo.Height / 3), o => o.LensBlur(12, lens)), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException radius is negative, not finite or above 128, or an option is out of range: blades other than 0 or 5 to 12, a rotation that is not finite, a gain below 1 or not finite, a threshold outside 0..1, or an undefined color space. Level(float, float, float, float, float) Stretches black..white to outputBlack..outputWhite with a midtone gamma, as ImageMagick's -level and +level. See Level(float, float, float, float, float). public RasterOps Level(float black = 0, float white = 1, float gamma = 1, float outputBlack = 0, float outputWhite = 1) Parameters black float The input that becomes outputBlack, from 0 to 1. white float The input that becomes outputWhite, from 0 to 1. gamma float The midtone gamma, above 0: above 1 brightens. outputBlack float The output for black, from 0 to 1. outputWhite float The output for white, from 0 to 1. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // A basic tone panel: levels with a midtone lift, a gentle S-curve, and a warm tint in the midtones. The three steps run as // one pass over the pixels. raster.Apply(o => o .Level(black: 0.04f, white: 0.96f, gamma: 1.1f) .SigmoidalContrast(4, midpoint: 0.5f) .Tint(new Rgba8(255, 200, 150, 255), 0.15f), Ct); raster.Save("duck-toned.jpg"); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException A value is out of range, or black equals white. Lighting(Light, LightingModel, LightingOptions?) Lights the image as a height field with the SVG 1.1 lighting filters (feDiffuseLighting and feSpecularLighting), with Skia's parameters: the height channel (alpha by default) times SurfaceScale is a surface, its normal comes from SVG's Sobel stencils (with SVG's own stencils on the edges and corners), and the light's color is scaled by N·L (Diffuse(float)) or (N·H)^shininess (Specular(float, float)). The result is the light map (opaque for diffuse; for specular, alpha is the largest color channel), or, with Blend, the light map blended onto the image, which keeps its alpha. Light is computed on stored values, as Skia does in its working space; SVG's default of linear light is not applied. public RasterOps Lighting(Light light, LightingModel model, LightingOptions? options = null) Parameters light Light The light: DistantLight, PointLight or SpotLight, in pixel coordinates. model LightingModel How the surface reflects: Diffuse(float) or Specular(float, float); the default value is a diffuse model with kd 0, which is black. options LightingOptions The surface scale, height channel and blend; null for the defaults. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // A photo's luminance as the height: light areas stand up. SurfaceScale is the height of white, in pixels. LightingOptions relief = new() { Height = HeightSource.Luminance, SurfaceScale = 6 }; using Raster lit = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Lighting(new DistantLight(300, 50), LightingModel.Diffuse(), relief), Ct); // The same light blended onto the photo instead of replacing it. using Raster shaded = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Lighting(new DistantLight(300, 50), LightingModel.Diffuse(1.3f), relief with { Blend = BlendMode.Overlay }), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentNullException light is null. LocalContrast(float, float) Brings out local detail, as ImageMagick's -local-contrast: L* is pushed away from a wide blur of itself by strength, so large-scale light changes less than detail. a* and b* are kept. public RasterOps LocalContrast(float radius = 0.1, float strength = 0.125) Parameters radius float The blur radius as a fraction of 20% of the longer side, above 0 and at most 1; the default 0.1 blurs over 2%. strength float How strongly detail is raised, 0 or more; the default 0.125 is ImageMagick's 12.5%. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Bring out detail in a flat, foggy landscape: CLAHE on 8 × 8 tiles, then ImageMagick's local contrast. raster.Apply(o => o.Clahe(tilesX: 8, tilesY: 8, clipLimit: 2).LocalContrast(radius: 0.1f, strength: 0.15f), Ct); Remarks Two lightness planes, 4 bytes a pixel each, count against MaxTotalBytes. Inside a rectangle or mask, the scope is its image. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException An argument is out of range. LuminanceToAlpha() Sets alpha to the luminance of the stored values, 0.212656 R + 0.715158 G + 0.072186 B (the Rec. 709 weights as ImageMagick derives them from the sRGB primaries), and keeps the color, exactly as ImageMagick's -alpha copy does; on a gray raster this turns the gray into alpha. A color matrix, so it fuses with neighbouring color steps. To also black out the color, as Skia's luma filter does, follow it with OnChannels(ColorChannels.Color, o => o.FillColor(Rgba8.Black)). public RasterOps LuminanceToAlpha() Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples using Raster alpha = photo.Derive(ops => ops.AlphaToGray(), Ct); // see the transparency as gray using Raster cutout = photo.Derive(ops => ops.CopyAlpha(new Mask(matte)), Ct); // a gray image becomes the alpha using Raster onWhite = cutout.Derive(ops => ops.Flatten(Rgba8.White), Ct); // composite onto white, opaque using Raster luma = photo.Derive(ops => ops.LuminanceToAlpha(), Ct); // brightness becomes alpha MakeTransparent(Rgba8, float, float) Makes pixels within tolerance of color transparent, keeping their color, by ImageMagick's -fuzz distance, so with no softness the result equals ImageMagick's -fuzz with -transparent. softness ramps alpha up over the next band of distance, for antialiased edges and green screens. public RasterOps MakeTransparent(Rgba8 color, float tolerance = 0, float softness = 0) Parameters color Rgba8 The color to remove, with its alpha (opaque for most keys). tolerance float The color distance that becomes fully transparent, from 0 (the exact color) to 1 (every color). softness float The band of distance beyond the tolerance over which alpha returns to full; 0 for a hard edge. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Remove a green screen: within 0.15 of pure green becomes transparent, and alpha ramps back over the next 0.1 for soft edges. photo.Apply(ops => ops.MakeTransparent(new Rgba8(0, 177, 64, 255), tolerance: 0.15f, softness: 0.1f), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException tolerance is outside 0..1, or softness is negative or not finite. Median(int, bool) Replaces each channel with its median over the (2r + 1) square around the pixel, as ImageMagick's -statistic Median does: removes salt-and-pepper noise while keeping edges. Works on stored values, so 8 and 16-bit results are exact; edges repeat the edge pixel. The cost per pixel does not grow with the radius on byte types. public RasterOps Median(int radius, bool includeAlpha = false) Parameters radius int The radius in pixels, from 0 (changes nothing) to 100. includeAlpha bool Whether alpha gets its own median too; by default it is kept. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Salt-and-pepper noise disappears and edges stay sharp; radius 2 is a 5 × 5 window. photo.Apply(ops => ops.Median(2), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException radius is negative or above 100. MergeDuplicates(float) Removes each frame equal to the one before it and adds its delay to the frame that stays, as ImageMagick's -layers RemoveDups: a screen recording that sat still for seconds becomes one long frame. What is on screen at every moment is unchanged. Removed frames take their metadata with them. public RasterOps MergeDuplicates(float tolerance = 0) Parameters tolerance float How far a pixel may differ and still count as equal, by ImageMagick's -fuzz distance, from 0 (the default, exact) to 1. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Shrink a screen recording: merge frames that barely change, drop frames no viewer shows, then resample to 25 fps. recording.Apply(ops => ops.MergeDuplicates(tolerance: 0.01f).DropZeroDelay().Retime(25), Ct); recording.Save("recording.gif"); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException tolerance is outside 0 to 1. Morphology(MorphologyOp, StructuringElement, int) Flat morphology: each channel's maximum (dilate) or minimum (erode) over shape around each pixel, or one of their combinations, as ImageMagick's -morphology. Works on stored values, alpha included, so 8 and 16-bit results are exact; Gradient, TopHat and BottomHat keep alpha. Edges repeat the edge pixel. Rectangles cost the same per pixel at any size; other shapes grow with their height. public RasterOps Morphology(MorphologyOp op, StructuringElement shape, int iterations = 1) Parameters op MorphologyOp The operation. shape StructuringElement The structuring element. iterations int How many times each dilation and erosion runs, 1 to 100: Open with 2 erodes twice, then dilates twice. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Close removes dark specks smaller than the shape (dust and toner dots on the paper) and keeps strokes wider than it; // Open does the opposite, for light pinholes in dark areas. using Raster<Gray8> scan = Raster.Load<Gray8>("scan.tif"); scan.Apply(o => o.Morphology(MorphologyOp.Close, StructuringElement.Disk(1)), Ct); // The outlines of shapes, and the light details smaller than a disk. using Raster outlines = scan.Derive(o => o.Morphology(MorphologyOp.Gradient, StructuringElement.Square(1)), Ct); using Raster details = scan.Derive(o => o.Morphology(MorphologyOp.TopHat, StructuringElement.Disk(5)), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException op is not defined, or iterations is outside 1 to 100. MotionBlur(float, float, float, bool) Streaks the image along a direction, as a camera moving during the exposure, with ImageMagick's -motion-blur meaning: each pixel averages 2⌈radius⌉ + 1 samples one pixel apart, from itself toward angle, weighted by a Gaussian of sigma from the pixel. Samples between pixels are read bilinearly; edges repeat the edge pixel. public RasterOps MotionBlur(float radius, float sigma, float angle, bool centered = false) Parameters radius float Half the streak's length in pixels, from 0 (changes nothing) to 127. sigma float How fast the weights fall along the streak, above 0. angle float The direction in degrees, clockwise from the x axis (y points down). centered bool Whether the streak runs both ways from the pixel, instead of only toward angle. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples using Raster moving = photo.Derive(ops => ops.MotionBlur(radius: 12, sigma: 4, angle: 15), Ct); // a streak toward 15° using Raster spinning = photo.Derive(ops => ops.RotationalBlur(8), Ct); // 8° around the center using Raster zooming = photo.Derive(ops => ops.ZoomBlur(0.2f, new System.Numerics.Vector2(320, 200)), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException An argument is not finite or out of range. Normalize(bool, bool) ContrastStretch(float, float, bool, bool) at ImageMagick's -normalize points: the darkest 2% of the pixels become black and the lightest 1% white. public RasterOps Normalize(bool linked = true, bool perFrame = false) Parameters linked bool Whether the channels share one pair of points (the default) or each gets its own. perFrame bool Whether each frame is measured alone. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Fix a dull scan: stretch it to the full range, clipping the darkest 2% and lightest 1%, then set the midtones. raster.Apply(o => o.Normalize().AutoGamma(), Ct); // Or stretch each channel on its own, which also removes a cast. raster.Apply(o => o.AutoLevel(linked: false), Ct); // Measured steps measure only their scope: here the sky alone is stretched. raster.Apply(o => o.Within(new Rect(0, 0, raster.Width, raster.Height / 3), sky => sky.AutoLevel()), Ct); Offset(int, int, EdgeMode, Rgba8) Moves the image by whole pixels, right by dx and down by dy, with no resampling. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Roll the image half way round, so its edges meet in the middle, which shows whether it tiles seamlessly. using Raster rolled = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Offset(photo.Width / 2, photo.Height / 2), Ct); // Fill a 1920 × 1080 wallpaper with copies of the duck's head. using Raster wallpaper = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Tile(1920, 1080, source: new Rect(380, 60, 160, 160)), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException edges is not defined. OilPaint(int, int) Makes the image look painted, as ImageMagick's -paint does: around each pixel, in the (2r + 1) square, pixels are sorted into levels bins by intensity, and the pixel becomes a pixel of the most common bin, unchanged. With 256 levels on 8-bit images the result is ImageMagick's exactly; fewer levels make larger, flatter strokes. Works on stored values; the histogram slides along each row, so a larger radius costs little more per pixel than the window's size. public RasterOps OilPaint(int radius = 3, int levels = 20) Parameters radius int The brush radius in pixels, from 1 to 50. levels int The number of intensity bins, from 2 to 256. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples using Raster painted = photo.Derive(ops => ops.OilPaint(radius: 4, levels: 20), Ct); using Raster magick = photo.Derive(ops => ops.OilPaint(3, levels: 256), Ct); // ImageMagick's -paint 3, pixel for pixel Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException radius is outside 1..50, or levels is outside 2..256. Each must keep the size, as in Within(Rect, Action<RasterOps>). Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Soften only the alpha; invert only the red. photo.Apply(ops => ops .OnChannels(ColorChannels.Alpha, o => o.Blur(2)) .OnChannels(ColorChannels.Red, o => o.Invert()), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException channels holds values that are not channels. ArgumentNullException build is null. ArgumentException An operation inside would change the size or the color encoding; the message names it. Opacity(float) Multiplies alpha by amount. Has no effect on pixel types without alpha. public RasterOps Opacity(float amount) Parameters amount float 0 makes the image transparent, 1 changes nothing. Returns RasterOps This builder. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException amount is outside 0..1. Pad(int, int, Rgba8, Anchor) Enlarges the canvas to width × height, placing the image at anchor and filling the new area with background. public RasterOps Pad(int width, int height, Rgba8 background = default, Anchor anchor = Anchor.Center) Parameters width int The new width, at least the image's width. height int The new height, at least the image's height. background Rgba8 The color of the new area. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException A size is less than 1, or smaller than the image when the chain runs (use Crop(Rect) to shrink), or anchor is not defined. Pixelate(int, Point) Pixelates: the image is cut into square cells, and every pixel of a cell becomes the cell's average, taken on premultiplied values so transparent pixels do not darken it. Examples // 12-pixel cells, each the average of what it covers. using Raster blocks = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Pixelate(12), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException cellSize is outside 1..4096. Posterize(int, DitherMode) Rounds red, green and blue to levels evenly spaced values each, as ImageMagick's -posterize, optionally dithered: ordered dithering adds a fixed 8 × 8 pattern before rounding, Floyd–Steinberg spreads each value's rounding error to its neighbours. Defaults to None. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // A two-color poster, then a check of how it reads to someone with deuteranopia. raster.Apply(o => o.Duotone(Rgba8.FromHex("#1b2a49"), Rgba8.FromHex("#f2c14e")).Posterize(4, DitherMode.Ordered), Ct); using Raster<Rgba8> preview = raster.Derive(o => o.SimulateColorBlindness(ColorVisionDeficiency.Deuteranopia), Ct); // High contrast for low vision: gray, lightness inverted so dark becomes light, and more contrast. using Raster<Rgba8> readable = raster.Derive(o => o.HighContrast(grayscale: true, ContrastInvert.Lightness, contrast: 0.3f), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException levels is outside 2 to 256, or dither is not defined. QuadDistort(Vector2, Vector2, Vector2, Vector2, TransformOptions?) Moves the image's four corners to four points, bending it in perspective: ImageMagick's Perspective distort. Corners are pixel edges, so the top-right corner of a 100-pixel-wide image is (100, 0). public RasterOps QuadDistort(Vector2 topLeft, Vector2 topRight, Vector2 bottomRight, Vector2 bottomLeft, TransformOptions? options = null) Parameters topLeft Vector2 Where the top-left corner goes. topRight Vector2 Where the top-right corner goes. bottomRight Vector2 Where the bottom-right corner goes. bottomLeft Vector2 Where the bottom-left corner goes. options TransformOptions The filter, edges, background and viewport, or null for the defaults. Examples // Pin the image onto a trapezoid, as if it lay on a table: its corners go to these four points (pixel edges, so the // image's own corners are (0, 0) and (640, 480)). using Raster onTable = photo.Derive(ops => ops.QuadDistort(new(200, 0), new(440, 0), new(640, 300), new(0, 300)), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentException A point is not finite, three of them lie on one line, or the viewport is empty. Quantize(PaletteOptions?) Reduces each frame to at most MaxColors colors, as a palette format would, but keeps the pixel type: an Rgba16 image stays Rgba16 with at most that many distinct values. Each frame gets its own palette (its own colors when they fit, Wu's quantizer otherwise) unless FixedPalette fixes one, and is dithered as the options say. Use ToIndexed(PaletteOptions?, int) for the indices themselves. public RasterOps Quantize(PaletteOptions? options = null) Parameters options PaletteOptions The color limit, dithering, refinement and matching, or null for Default. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // A 16-color poster with Atkinson's dither; the pixel type stays as it was. photo.Apply(ops => ops.Quantize(new PaletteOptions { MaxColors = 16, Dither = DitherMode.Atkinson }), Ct); photo.Save("poster.png"); Reach(Action<RasterOps>) Returns how far a chain reads past each output pixel: the sum of its steps' reaches. Pixel-by-pixel steps (color matrices, arithmetic, color filters, blending a color, keying) reach nothing; blurs, convolutions, morphology, glows and drop shadows reach as far as their kernels and offsets. A step whose reach is unbounded or unknown (a resize, a geometric transform, a histogram step, a custom IRasterOperation) makes the whole chain's reach unknown. public static OperationReach? Reach(Action<RasterOps> build) Parameters build Action<RasterOps> Records the chain, as for Apply(Action<RasterOps>, CancellationToken); it is recorded, not run. Returns OperationReach? The reach, or null when some step's reach is unknown. Examples // How far a chain reads around each pixel: run it on a part of a picture padded by this much, and the part comes out as it // would in the whole picture. OperationReach? reach = RasterOps.Reach(ops => ops.Blur(3).Glow(4, Rgba8.White)); if (reach is OperationReach r) { Console.WriteLine($"pad by {r.X} × {r.Y}"); } // A resize reads the whole image: its reach is unknown. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Correct a tungsten-lit photo, as a raw editor's temperature slider does. raster.Apply(o => o.WhiteBalance(temperature: 3200), Ct); // Or pick a gray card's color and make it neutral. raster.Apply(o => o.WhiteBalance(new Rgba8(182, 170, 151, 255)), Ct); // Or let the image tell: ImageMagick's gray world, or the brightest pixels as white. raster.Apply(o => o.AutoWhiteBalance(WhiteBalanceMethod.GrayWorld), Ct); raster.Apply(o => o.AutoWhiteBalance(WhiteBalanceMethod.WhitePatch), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException An argument is out of range. Within(Mask, Action<RasterOps>) Runs the operations build adds, then mixes each pixel with the original by the mask's coverage: none keeps the original, full keeps the result, and values between blend the two on premultiplied pixels, so a soft mask edge gives a soft transition. Only the box around the mask's non-zero coverage is touched. Masks nest by multiplying their coverage, and mix freely with rectangles. public RasterOps Within(Mask mask, Action<RasterOps> build) Parameters mask Mask The coverage: a raster of any size and type, placed at its offset, read by its channel. build Action<RasterOps> Adds the operations. Each must keep the size, as in Within(Rect, Action<RasterOps>). Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Edit only the sky: a gray mask, white where the edit applies fully, black where it does not, soft in between. photo.Apply(ops => ops .Within(new Mask(sky), o => o.Saturation(1.3f).Contrast(1.1f)) // Or take coverage from a logo's alpha, placed on the photo, and invert the area under it. .Within(new Mask(logo, new Point(20, 20), MaskChannel.Alpha), o => o.Invert()), Ct); Remarks The mask raster must stay undisposed until the chain has run. Masking a raster with itself reads from a copy, made when the step runs. Exceptions ArgumentNullException build is null. ArgumentException The mask has no raster, or an operation inside would change the size or the color encoding. ArgumentOutOfRangeException The mask's channel is not defined. Within(Rect, Action<RasterOps>) Runs the operations build adds so that only pixels inside area change, as if the image were edited through a rectangular hole. Filters read the real pixels around the area, so a blurred rectangle has no seam and equals the whole-image blur there; flips and a 180° turn mirror the area itself. Positions inside (DrawImage, FillColor) are the raster's, as outside. Scopes nest: a rectangle inside a rectangle is their intersection. public RasterOps Within(Rect area, Action<RasterOps> build) Parameters area Rect The rectangle, in the raster's coordinates. It is clipped to the raster; one that misses it changes nothing. build Action<RasterOps> Adds the operations. Each must keep the size: a resize, crop, pad, 90° or free turn, AutoOrient, ConvertColor or ToneMap throws. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples // Blur a face: only pixels inside the rectangle change, and the blur reads the real pixels around it, so there is no seam. photo.Apply(ops => ops .Within(new Rect(200, 120, 160, 120), o => o.Blur(6)) .Within(new Rect(0, 0, photo.Width, 60), o => o.Brightness(0.8f).Saturation(0.5f)), Ct); // a darker band on top Exceptions ArgumentNullException build is null. ArgumentOutOfRangeException area has a negative width or height. ArgumentException An operation inside would change the size or the color encoding; the message names it. ZoomBlur(float, Vector2?) Streaks the image along rays from center, as a zoom during the exposure (Photoshop's radial zoom blur): each pixel averages samples on the ray through it, spanning amount of its distance from the center, half inward and half outward, about one per pixel (at most 256). The center does not move, and a flat image stays flat. public RasterOps ZoomBlur(float amount, Vector2? center = null) Parameters amount float The streak's length as a fraction of the distance from the center, from 0 (changes nothing) to 1. center Vector2? The center in pixels, pixel centers at +0.5, or null for the image's center. Returns RasterOps This builder. Examples using Raster moving = photo.Derive(ops => ops.MotionBlur(radius: 12, sigma: 4, angle: 15), Ct); // a streak toward 15° using Raster spinning = photo.Derive(ops => ops.RotationalBlur(8), Ct); // 8° around the center using Raster zooming = photo.Derive(ops => ops.ZoomBlur(0.2f, new System.Numerics.Vector2(320, 200)), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException amount is outside 0..1, or the center is not finite.

api/Egami.Operations.ResampleFilter.html.title: Enum ResampleFilter | Egami
api/Egami.Operations.ResampleFilter.html.summary: Enum ResampleFilter Namespace Egami.Operations Assembly Egami.dll The kernel a resize or rotation uses to blend source pixels. public enum ResampleFilter Fields Bicubic = 0 Keys cubic with a = −0.5 (Catmull-Rom): sharp, with slight ringing at hard edges. The default. Bilinear = 3 A triangle (tent) kernel: smooth and soft, with no ringing. Box = 2 Averages the source pixels each output pixel covers. Good for large reductions of flat artwork. Gaussian = 8 A Gaussian with σ = ½, exp(−2x²), out to 2 pixels, as ImageMagick's Gaussian filter: soft, with no ringing at all. Hermite = 7 The Hermite cubic (B = C = 0), 2|x|³ − 3|x|² + 1 out to 1 pixel: smooth like Bilinear when enlarging, without its corners, and no ringing. Lanczos2 = 6 A two-lobe windowed sinc, sinc(x)·sinc(x / 2) out to 2 pixels, as ImageMagick's Lanczos2: nearly as sharp as Lanczos3 with less ringing, and faster. Lanczos3 = 5 A three-lobe windowed sinc: the sharpest, with the most ringing, and the slowest. Mitchell = 4 Mitchell–Netravali with B = C = 1/3: softer than Bicubic, with less ringing. Nearest = 1 Picks the closest source pixel without blending. Exact and fastest; blocky when enlarging, aliased when shrinking. Spline = 9 The cubic B-spline (B = 1, C = 0) out to 2 pixels: the smoothest cubic, with no ringing and noticeable blur. Examples // Lanczos3 is sharper than the default Bicubic; Nearest keeps hard pixel edges (pixel art, masks). using Raster sharp = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Resize(200, 0, ResampleFilter.Lanczos3), Ct); // Blending in linear light keeps fine bright detail on dark backgrounds from going dim when reduced. using Raster linear = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Resize(200, 0, ResampleFilter.Mitchell, ColorSpace.Linear), Ct);

Examples /// <summary>Black or white per pixel: ForEachBand gives each worker a band of rows from start to end.</summary> private sealed class Threshold(float level) : IRasterOperation { public Size OutputSize(Size input) => input; public void Run<TPixel>(OperationInput<TPixel> input) where TPixel : unmanaged, IPixelType<TPixel> { RowBandAction band = (start, end) => { for (int y = start; y < end; y++) { Span<TPixel> source = input.Source.Row(y), destination = input.Destination.Row(y); for (int x = 0; x < source.Length; x++) { Vector4 v = source[x].ToScaled(); float on = ((0.2126f * v.X) + (0.7152f * v.Y) + (0.0722f * v.Z)) >= level ? 1 : 0; destination[x] = TPixel.FromScaled(new Vector4(on, on, on, v.W)); } } }; input.ForEachBand(band); } }

Corrects (or adds) barrel and pincushion lens distortion with the PanoTools model that ImageMagick's Barrel distort, Hugin and lens databases use: each output point at radius r from the center samples the source at radius r × (a·r³ + b·r² + c·r + d), with r normalized to half the image's smaller side. The size is kept. public static IWarp Barrel(double a, double b, double c, double? d = null, Vector2? center = null) Parameters a double The cubic coefficient. b double The quadratic coefficient. c double The linear coefficient. d double? The constant term, or null (the default) for 1 − a − b − c, which keeps the scale at r = 1. center Vector2? The center of the distortion, or null (the default) for the image's center. Returns IWarp The warp. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException A coefficient or the center is not finite. BarrelInverse(double, double, double, double?, Vector2?) The inverse lens model, ImageMagick's BarrelInverse distort: each output point at radius r samples the source at radius r / (a·r³ + b·r² + c·r + d), r normalized as for Barrel(double, double, double, double?, Vector2?). The size is kept. public static IWarp BarrelInverse(double a, double b, double c, double? d = null, Vector2? center = null) Parameters a double The cubic coefficient. b double The quadratic coefficient. c double The linear coefficient. d double? The constant term, or null (the default) for 1 − a − b − c. center Vector2? The center of the distortion, or null (the default) for the image's center. Returns IWarp The warp. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException A coefficient or the center is not finite. DePolar(float, float, Vector2?, float, float?) Unwraps a circle into a rectangle, ImageMagick's DePolar distort, the inverse of Polar(float, float, Vector2?, float, float?): output columns are angles and rows radii from minRadius to maxRadius around the center. The output is as tall as the radii's difference and as wide as their mean circumference, rounded up. public static IWarp DePolar(float maxRadius = 0, float minRadius = 0, Vector2? center = null, float fromDegrees = -180, float? toDegrees = null) Parameters maxRadius float The outer radius; 0 (the default) for the distance from the center to the nearest edge, −1 for the farthest corner. minRadius float The inner radius, 0 or more and less than the outer. center Vector2? The center, or null (the default) for the image's center. fromDegrees float The angle of the output's left edge. toDegrees float? The angle of its right edge; null (the default) for a full circle. Returns IWarp The warp. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException A radius or angle is not finite, or the radii are out of order. Implode(float) Pulls the image toward its center, ImageMagick's -implode; a negative amount pushes it out (explodes). The size is kept. public static IWarp Implode(float amount) Parameters amount float The strength: 0 changes nothing, 1 is strong. Returns IWarp The warp. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException amount is not finite. Magnifier(Rect, float, float) Magnifies the area lens by zoom, as Skia's magnifier filter does: the middle of the lens shows the zoomed image, and over the last inset pixels to the lens's edge it blends back into the surroundings with rounded corners. Outside the lens nothing moves. The size is kept. public static IWarp Magnifier(Rect lens, float zoom, float inset) Parameters lens Rect The lens, in pixels. zoom float The magnification; 1 or less changes nothing, as in Skia. inset float The width of the blending band, 0 or more; 0 gives a hard edge. Returns IWarp The warp. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The lens is empty, or the zoom or inset is out of range or not finite. Polar(float, float, Vector2?, float, float?) Wraps the image around a circle, ImageMagick's Polar distort: the source's columns become angles (0° pointing down, growing counter-clockwise on screen from fromDegrees to toDegrees) and its rows radii, the top row at minRadius and the bottom at maxRadius. The output is the square around the circle, as ImageMagick's +distort sizes it. public static IWarp Polar(float maxRadius = 0, float minRadius = 0, Vector2? center = null, float fromDegrees = -180, float? toDegrees = null) Parameters maxRadius float The outer radius; 0 (the default) for the distance from the center to the nearest edge, −1 for the farthest corner. minRadius float The inner radius, 0 or more and less than the outer. center Vector2? The center, used for the special radii; null (the default) for the image's center. fromDegrees float The angle of the source's left edge. toDegrees float? The angle of its right edge; null (the default) for a full circle. Returns IWarp The warp. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException A radius or angle is not finite, or the radii are out of order. Swirl(float, Vector2?, float?) Swirls the image about its center, ImageMagick's -swirl: points turn by degrees at the center, falling to 0 at the radius with the square of the distance. The size is kept; points outside the radius stay put. public static IWarp Swirl(float degrees, Vector2? center = null, float? radius = null) Parameters degrees float The turn at the center; positive turns clockwise. center Vector2? The center, or null (the default) for ImageMagick's, the middle of the image. radius float? The radius, or null (the default) for half the image's larger side; the swirl is stretched to the image's aspect ratio. Returns IWarp The warp. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException A value is not finite, or the radius is not more than 0. Wave(float, float) Shifts each column up or down along a sine wave, ImageMagick's -wave: column x moves down by |amplitude| + amplitude × sin(2πx / wavelength). The image grows by twice the amplitude in height. public static IWarp Wave(float amplitude, float wavelength) Parameters amplitude float The wave's height, in pixels. wavelength float The wave's length, in pixels, more than 0. api/Egami.Operations.WhiteBalanceMethod..summary: Enum WhiteBalanceMethod Namespace Egami.Operations Assembly Egami.dll How AutoWhiteBalance(WhiteBalanceMethod, bool) finds the cast to remove. public enum WhiteBalanceMethod Fields GrayWorld = 0 Gray world in Lab, as ImageMagick's -white-balance: the mean a* and b* of the image, weighted by lightness, are taken out of every pixel. The default. WhitePatch = 1 The brightest 1% of the pixels is taken to be white, and the channels are scaled in linear light so it becomes neutral. Examples // Correct a tungsten-lit photo, as a raw editor's temperature slider does. raster.Apply(o => o.WhiteBalance(temperature: 3200), Ct); // Or pick a gray card's color and make it neutral. raster.Apply(o => o.WhiteBalance(new Rgba8(182, 170, 151, 255)), Ct); // Or let the image tell: ImageMagick's gray world, or the brightest pixels as white. raster.Apply(o => o.AutoWhiteBalance(WhiteBalanceMethod.GrayWorld), Ct); raster.Apply(o => o.AutoWhiteBalance(WhiteBalanceMethod.WhitePatch), Ct);

api/Egami.Operations.html.title: Namespace Egami.Operations | Egami
api/Egami.Operations.html.summary: Namespace Egami.Operations Classes AnimationOverlayOptions Options for DrawAnimation(Raster, Point, AnimationOverlayOptions?). ColorFilter A function of one pixel's color, as a value: build one from a matrix, curves, a 3D table or a tone step, chain filters with Then(ColorFilter), mix two with Lerp(ColorFilter, ColorFilter, float), run one with ApplyFilter(ColorFilter) or on your own pixels with Apply<TPixel>(Span<TPixel>), and save it as a .cube file through ToLut3D(int). Like Skia's SkColorFilter, a filter sees only the pixel's own straight RGBA: no neighbours, position or image statistics, so any chain of filters runs as one pass. Compositor Blends rows of pixels with a BlendMode, for code that composites outside an operation chain: a custom IRasterOperation, a rasterizer filling spans, a layer merge. It runs the kernels DrawImage runs, so Blend<TPixel>(BlendMode, ReadOnlySpan<TPixel>, Span<TPixel>, float, ColorSpace) on a row gives the pixels DrawImage gives there. Every method works for every pixel type, allocates nothing once warm, and is safe to call from many threads at once. ConvolutionKernel A convolution kernel: an odd width and height of weights, applied as laid out (the weight at column 0, row 0 multiplies the pixel up and to the left of the center). The sum is divided by Divisor and Offset is added to the color channels. CubeFile Reads and writes .cube LUT files: the Adobe Cube LUT Specification 1.0 (a 1D or a 3D table, with TITLE, DOMAIN_MIN and DOMAIN_MAX), and DaVinci Resolve's variant with a 1D shaper before the 3D table (LUT_1D_INPUT_RANGE and LUT_3D_INPUT_RANGE). DistantLight A light infinitely far away, shining from one direction on every pixel, as SVG's feDistantLight. The direction toward the light is (cos Azimuth · cos Elevation, sin Azimuth · cos Elevation, sin Elevation) in the raster's coordinates (y down), which is the vector Skia's DistantLit factories take. DropShadowOptions The less common settings of DropShadow(float, float, float, Rgba8, DropShadowOptions?): a different vertical blur, whether the canvas grows, whether only the shadow is kept, and how the blur is computed. LensBlurOptions The aperture and highlights of LensBlur(float, LensBlurOptions?). The defaults give a round aperture in linear light with no highlight boost. Light A light for Lighting(Light, LightingModel, LightingOptions?): DistantLight, PointLight or SpotLight, the three light sources of the SVG 1.1 lighting filters (feDistantLight, fePointLight and feSpotLight), with Skia's parameters. Positions are in pixels of the raster, x to the right, y down and z up out of the image; a pixel's center is at (x + 0.5, y + 0.5), as in Skia. LightingOptions The surface and output settings of Lighting(Light, LightingModel, LightingOptions?). Lut3D A 3D color lookup table: an N × N × N grid of output RGB values over the input cube, with red varying fastest, as .cube files and Hald images store it, and an optional 1D shaper per channel read before the grid (DaVinci Resolve's 1D-plus-3D .cube). Read one with Read(string, EgamiContext?) or FromHald(Raster), and apply it with FromLut(Lut3D, LutInterpolation). OperationInput<TPixel> Everything an operation gets for one frame. PointLight A light at one point, shining in every direction, as SVG's fePointLight and Skia's PointLit factories. RasterOps Animation steps: they work on the frames of the whole animation rather than on each frame, so they run in Apply, Derive and Transcode (which then decodes the whole animation first) but not inside Within. Frames in memory are already full pictures of what is on screen, so there is no Coalesce, and the writers find each frame's changed area themselves, so there is no Optimize. SamplingOptions How a transform or warp samples the source: the filter, the color space it blends in, what samples outside the source read, and the background color. SpotLight A light at one point that shines toward a target, as SVG's feSpotLight and Skia's SpotLit factories. Light falls off away from the axis as cos(angle)^Exponent and stops at ConeAngle, with Skia's soft cone edge. ToneCurve A curve from 0..1 to 0..1 for one channel, as a photo editor's curves dialog draws it: inputs outside 0..1 are clamped first and results are clamped to 0..1. Use one in Curves(ToneCurve); the tone steps (Level, Gamma and the rest) are curves too, evaluated exactly. TransformOptions How a transform samples the source and how large its result is: SamplingOptions plus a viewport. Warp Makes warps from functions. Warps The built-in warps for Warp(IWarp, SamplingOptions?): lens correction, polar and depolar, arc, swirl, wave and implode with ImageMagick's parameter meanings, so its documentation describes them and its results are their reference, and Skia's magnifier. Positions are in pixels with pixel centers at +0.5. Structs ColorMatrix A 4 × 5 color matrix applied to straight (not premultiplied) RGBA scaled to 0..1: each output channel is m[row, 0] × R + m[row, 1] × G + m[row, 2] × B + m[row, 3] × A + m[row, 4], rows in R, G, B, A order, and results are clamped to 0..1. The factories follow the W3C Filter Effects definitions. Homography A 3 × 3 projective matrix in double precision, for perspective transforms. It follows Matrix3x2's conventions: points are row vectors, so [x, y, 1] × H = [X, Y, W] and the point lands at (X / W, Y / W); A * B applies A first, then B. Coordinates are in pixels with the origin at the top-left corner of the top-left pixel, so pixel centers sit at +0.5. LightingModel How a surface reflects light in Lighting(Light, LightingModel, LightingOptions?): Diffuse(float) (SVG's feDiffuseLighting, Lambert's N·L) or Specular(float, float) (feSpecularLighting, Phong–Blinn's (N·H)^shininess), with SVG's and Skia's constants. Mask A raster read as coverage, 0 (none) to full, placed on the image being edited: where an operation inside Within(Mask, Action<RasterOps>) applies and how strongly. The raster may have any size and pixel type; outside it coverage is 0, or full when Inverted. Its first frame is used for every frame. It must stay undisposed until the chain has run. OperationReach How far an operation chain reads past each output pixel, in whole pixels across and down: a pixel of the result can depend on input pixels up to X columns and Y rows away. A blur of σ reaches about 3σ; a color matrix reaches nothing. Reach(Action<RasterOps>) measures a chain, so code that runs one on part of a larger picture, such as a canvas layer, can include the pixels around it that the chain will read. StructuringElement The shape Morphology(MorphologyOp, StructuringElement, int) takes its maximum or minimum over: a set of cells around an origin, which sits on the pixel being computed. The factories make the shapes ImageMagick's -morphology kernels of the same names make (its Plus is Cross(int) here). The default value is the origin alone, which changes nothing. Interfaces IRasterOperation One step of an operation chain. Built-in operations implement it, and so can callers: add one to a chain with Add(IRasterOperation). IWarp A general warp: a mapping from each output pixel back to the source point it shows. Egami samples the points with the same sampler as Transform(Homography, TransformOptions?), so every warp gets antialiasing where it shrinks the image, and edge modes. Positions are in pixels with the origin at the top-left corner of the top-left pixel, so pixel centers sit at +0.5. Enums Anchor Where an image sits inside a larger area, or which part of it is kept when it is cut down. AnimationTiming How DrawAnimation(Raster, Point, AnimationOverlayOptions?) pairs the overlay's frames with the base's. BlendMode How a source color is combined with the destination under it: the twelve Porter–Duff operators, Plus and Modulate, and the separable and non-separable blend modes of the W3C Compositing and Blending specification, plus Add and Subtract. Blend modes (Multiply to Luminosity) blend the colors where both are present, then composite source-over. The values are fixed: they never change between releases. BlurMethod How Blur(float, ColorSpace, BlurMethod) computes a Gaussian blur. ChannelSource Where an output channel of ShuffleChannels(ChannelSource, ChannelSource, ChannelSource, ChannelSource) takes its value from. ColorChannel One channel of a raster's working RGBA, or its luminance, for ExtractChannel(ColorChannel). ColorChannels A set of a raster's working RGBA channels, for OnChannels(ColorChannels, Action<RasterOps>). ColorSpace The color space in which resizing, blurs and grayscale blend colors: the stored sRGB-encoded values, or linear light. ColorVisionDeficiency A color vision deficiency to simulate. Connectivity Which neighbours a flood fill spreads to. ContrastInvert How HighContrast(bool, ContrastInvert, float) inverts, as Skia's high-contrast filter does. EdgeMode How a convolution reads taps that fall past the image border. EdgeOperator The kernels Edges(EdgeOperator, bool) finds edges with. Every operator is scaled so a full black-to-white step gives 1 at its strongest pixel; stronger responses (corners, single bright pixels) clamp to 1. EqualizeMode What Equalize(EqualizeMode, bool) equalizes. HeightSource Which channel Lighting(Light, LightingModel, LightingOptions?) reads as the surface's height. LumaWeights The luma weights a grayscale conversion uses. LutInterpolation How a Lut3D reads between its grid points. MaskChannel Which values of a raster a Mask reads as coverage. MorphologyOp The operations of Morphology(MorphologyOp, StructuringElement, int), all flat (gray-level) and per channel. NoiseKind The noise AddNoise(NoiseKind, float, bool, ulong) adds: ImageMagick's +noise kinds, with values on 0..1 and the amount as ImageMagick's -attenuate. At amount 1 the formulas are ImageMagick's Q16 ones. PixelMath An arithmetic operation with a constant, for Arithmetic(PixelMath, float, ColorChannels): ImageMagick's -evaluate operators. ResampleFilter The kernel a resize or rotation uses to blend source pixels. StackMode How Stack(IReadOnlyList<Raster>, StackMode) combines the same channel of the same pixel across rasters. ThresholdMethod How AutoThreshold(ThresholdMethod, ThresholdMode, Rgba8?, Rgba8?, bool) and FindThreshold(ThresholdMethod, ThresholdMode) choose a level from the histogram. ThresholdMode What a threshold compares with its level. WhiteBalanceMethod How AutoWhiteBalance(WhiteBalanceMethod, bool) finds the cast to remove. Delegates RowBandAction Processes a band of rows: rows start (inclusive) to end (exclusive).

api/Egami.PixelMemoryUsage.html.summary: Class PixelMemoryUsage Namespace Egami Assembly Egami.dll What a PooledPixelMemorySource has handed out and not yet had back, and opt-in tracking of blocks that were never disposed. Get it from Usage; most callers want PooledPixelMemorySource.Shared.Usage. public sealed class PixelMemoryUsage Inheritance object PixelMemoryUsage Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples PixelMemoryUsage usage = PooledPixelMemorySource.Shared.Usage; usage.CaptureStackTraces = true; usage.LeakDetected += (_, leak) => Console.WriteLine($"{leak.Bytes} bytes never disposed, allocated at {leak.StackTrace}"); usage.TrackLeaks = true; RunTheCodeUnderSuspicion(); Console.WriteLine($"{usage.LiveBlocks} blocks, {usage.LiveBytes} bytes still out"); Remarks The counts are always kept, at the cost of one atomic addition per allocation and per return. Leak tracking adds a small object with a finalizer to every block allocated while it is on, so turn it on only while looking for a leak. Properties CaptureStackTraces Gets or sets whether tracked blocks record the stack trace of their allocation for LeakDetected. It makes every allocation much slower. Defaults to false. public bool CaptureStackTraces { get; set; } Property Value bool LiveBlocks Gets the number of blocks handed out and not yet disposed. public long LiveBlocks { get; } Property Value long LiveBytes Gets the bytes in blocks handed out and not yet disposed. public long LiveBytes { get; } Property Value long TrackLeaks Gets or sets whether blocks allocated from now on are tracked, so that one collected without being disposed raises LeakDetected and leaves the counts. Defaults to false. public bool TrackLeaks { get; set; } Property Value bool Events LeakDetected Occurs when a block allocated while TrackLeaks was on is collected by the garbage collector without having been disposed. Handlers run on the finalizer thread, so they must be quick, must not throw, and must not touch objects that may already be finalized. Leaks are reported here, not through Diagnostics: they belong to the memory source and are found after any call has ended. public event EventHandler<PixelMemoryLeakEventArgs>? api/Egami.Pixels.AlphaKind.html.title: Enum AlphaKind | Egami
api/Egami.Pixels.AlphaKind.html.summary: Enum AlphaKind Namespace Egami.Pixels Assembly Egami.dll How a pixel type stores alpha. public enum AlphaKind Fields None = 0 The type has no alpha channel. Every pixel is opaque. Premultiplied = 2 Premultiplied alpha: each color channel is stored already multiplied by alpha. The conversions of IPixelType<TSelf> still take and return straight values, so only code that reads the memory directly sees it. Straight = 1 Straight (not premultiplied) alpha. Examples // What a pixel type stores, for code that handles any TPixel. PixelLayoutInfo layout = Rgba16.Layout; Console.WriteLine($"{layout.ChannelOrder} {layout.ChannelType}: {layout.ChannelCount} channels, {layout.BitsPerChannel} bits each, {layout.BytesPerPixel} bytes"); bool needsAlpha = layout.Alpha != AlphaKind.None; bool eightBit = layout.ChannelType == PixelChannelType.Unorm8; bool bgrOrder = Bgr8.Layout.ChannelOrder is PixelChannelOrder.Bgr or PixelChannelOrder.Bgra;

api/Egami.Pixels.ChromaFormat.html.title: Enum ChromaFormat | Egami
api/Egami.Pixels.ChromaFormat.html.summary: Enum ChromaFormat Namespace Egami.Pixels Assembly Egami.dll How a YuvRaster stores chroma: at what resolution against luma, or not at all. public enum ChromaFormat Fields Yuv400 = 3 Luma only, with no chroma planes: a gray picture, such as a gray JPEG or monochrome AV1. Yuv420 = 0 Chroma at half the width and half the height of luma, as most video, lossy WebP and most JPEG files store it. Yuv422 = 1 Chroma at half the width and the full height of luma. Yuv444 = 2 Chroma at the full size of luma. Examples // A 1080p frame as video stores it: full-size luma, chroma at half width and height, BT.709 at limited range. using YuvRaster<byte> frame = YuvRaster.Create(1920, 1080, ChromaFormat.Yuv420, YuvColor.Bt709Limited); // 10-bit HDR planes hold samples 0 to 1023 in ushorts; an alpha plane is optional. using YuvRaster<ushort> hdr = YuvRaster.Create(3840, 2160, ChromaFormat.Yuv420, 10, YuvColor.Bt2020Limited, alpha: true); Console.WriteLine($"Chroma planes are {frame.U!.Width}×{frame.U.Height}");

api/Egami.Pixels.ChromaSiting.html.title: Enum ChromaSiting | Egami
api/Egami.Pixels.ChromaSiting.html.summary: Enum ChromaSiting Namespace Egami.Pixels Assembly Egami.dll Where each chroma sample of a Yuv420 or Yuv422 picture sits against the luma samples it covers. Conversions filter chroma to match, so colors line up with edges. Ignored for 4:4:4 and 4:0:0. public enum ChromaSiting Fields Center = 0 Centered between the luma samples it covers, both ways: JPEG, VP8 and lossy WebP. Left = 1 On the left luma column of each pair and centered vertically: BT.601 and BT.709 video, MPEG-2 and later, and AV1's "vertical" position. TopLeft = 2 On the top-left luma sample of each 2 × 2 block: BT.2020 and AV1's "colocated" position. Examples // How samples turn into RGB is always stated: a preset, or the codes a video container carries (ITU-T H.273). YuvColor jpeg = YuvColor.Jpeg; // BT.601, full range, chroma centered YuvColor custom = new(YuvMatrix.Bt709, YuvRange.Full, ChromaSiting.Left); if (YuvColor.TryFromH273(matrixCoefficients: 9, fullRange: false, ChromaSiting.TopLeft, out YuvColor fromStream)) { Console.WriteLine($"{fromStream.Matrix}, {fromStream.Range}; back to code {fromStream.ToH273()}"); } // Or straight from the code points an AVIF or PNG cICP box carries. Egami.Colors.ColorCodePoints hdr10 = new(Primaries: 9, TransferCharacteristics: 16, MatrixCoefficients: 9, FullRange: false); hdr10.TryGetYuvColor(ChromaSiting.TopLeft, out YuvColor fromBox);
