It must be at least as long as source. Type Parameters TFrom The source pixel type. TTo The destination pixel type. Remarks Conversions between integer types where either side has 8-bit (or narrower packed) channels go through Rgba8, so they are exact: 8 to 16 bits multiplies by 257, and 16 to 8 bits rounds to the nearest value. Conversions between integer types wider than 8 bits go through Rgba16, also exact. All other conversions, including every one with a float or half-float side, go through red, green, blue and alpha scaled to 0..1. Converting to a gray type takes the Rec. 709 luma of the color, weighted in linear light; gray colors keep their value. Converting to a type without alpha drops alpha, and converting from one gives every pixel full alpha. Common pairs use SIMD: channel reordering between the 8-bit RGB layouts, 8 to 16 bits and back, and gray to RGB. Results are identical with and without SIMD. The spans must not overlap unless both are the same type and start at the same address. Exceptions ArgumentException destination is shorter than source.

api/Egami.Pixels.YuvMatrix.html.summary: Enum YuvMatrix Namespace Egami.Pixels Assembly Egami.dll The matrix between RGB and luma-chroma (Y'CbCr) values, as ITU-T H.273 names them. Shared by YCbCrColor and planar YUV images, so their coefficients never disagree. public enum YuvMatrix Fields Bt2020Ncl = 2 ITU-R BT.2020, non-constant luminance: Kr 0.2627, Kb 0.0593. UHD and HDR video. Bt601 = 0 ITU-R BT.601: Kr 0.299, Kb 0.114. JPEG, and standard-definition video. Bt709 = 1 ITU-R BT.709: Kr 0.2126, Kb 0.0722. High-definition video. Identity = 3 No matrix: Y is green, Cb blue and Cr red, as AV1 stores lossless RGB. Examples // Color values in the models apps ask for, from and to pixels, and between each other. Rgba8 orange = new(240, 128, 32, 255); HslColor hsl = HslColor.From(orange); // hue 28°, saturation 0.87, lightness 0.53 LabColor lab = ColorConvert.Convert<HslColor, LabColor>(hsl); // through XYZ OklchColor oklch = OklchColor.From(orange); YCbCrColor jpeg = YCbCrColor.From(orange); // BT.601 full range, as JPEG YCbCrColor video = YCbCrColor.From(orange, YuvMatrix.Bt709, YuvRange.Limited); // Color difference: CIEDE2000 on Lab, distance on Oklab. double deltaE = lab.DeltaE2000(LabColor.From(new Rgba8(235, 130, 40, 255))); // Whole rows at once, from any pixel type and encoding. Rgba8[] pixels = [orange, new(10, 20, 30, 255)]; OklabColor[] row = new OklabColor[pixels.Length]; ColorConvert.FromPixels<Rgba8, OklabColor>(pixels, row); ColorConvert.FromPixels<Rgba8, OklabColor>(pixels, row, ColorProfile.DisplayP3); // the same pixels read as Display P3

api/Egami.Pixels.YuvPackedFormat.html.summary: Enum YuvPackedFormat Namespace Egami.Pixels Assembly Egami.dll The interleaved YUV layouts that operating system decoders, GPUs and webcams hand out, which a YuvRaster copies to and from its planes with CopyFromPacked(YuvPackedFormat, ReadOnlySpan<byte>, int, ReadOnlySpan<byte>, int) and CopyToPacked(YuvPackedFormat, Span<byte>, int, Span<byte>, int). public enum YuvPackedFormat Fields Nv12 = 0 8-bit 4:2:0 in two planes: Y, then U and V interleaved (U first) at half width and height. Nv21 = 1 8-bit 4:2:0 in two planes: Y, then V and U interleaved (V first) at half width and height. P010 = 2 10-bit 4:2:0 in two planes of little-endian 16-bit words, samples in the high 10 bits: Y, then U and V interleaved. P016 = 3 4:2:0 in two planes of little-endian 16-bit words, samples in the high bits (16, or 10 or 12 with zero low bits): Y, then U and V interleaved. Uyvy = 5 8-bit 4:2:2 in one plane, four bytes for two pixels: U, Y0, V, Y1. Yuyv = 4 8-bit 4:2:2 in one plane, four bytes for two pixels: Y0, U, Y1, V (also called YUY2). Examples // An NV12 frame from Media Foundation or MediaCodec: Y rows, then interleaved U, V rows, both at the same stride. int width = 640, height = 360, stride = 704; byte[] nv12 = new byte[stride * height * 3 / 2]; using YuvRaster<byte> frame = YuvRaster.Create(width, height, ChromaFormat.Yuv420, YuvColor.Bt709Limited); frame.CopyFromPacked(YuvPackedFormat.Nv12, nv12, stride); // A webcam's YUYV, 4:2:2 in one plane, the other way. using YuvRaster<byte> webcam = YuvRaster.Create(width, height, ChromaFormat.Yuv422, YuvColor.Bt601Limited); byte[] yuyv = new byte[width * 2 * height]; webcam.CopyToPacked(YuvPackedFormat.Yuyv, yuyv);

api/Egami.Pixels.html.title: Namespace Egami.Pixels | Egami
api/Egami.Pixels.html.summary: Namespace Egami.Pixels Classes PixelConvert Converts spans of pixels from one pixel type to another. Structs Abgr8 A pixel with 8-bit alpha, blue, green and red channels, in that order, with straight alpha. Matches the bytes of a little-endian 32-bit RGBA value read as an integer. Alpha8 A pixel with one 8-bit alpha channel: a mask, or glyph coverage. As a color it is black with that alpha; converting a color to it keeps only the alpha, so a type without alpha gives 255. Argb8 A pixel with 8-bit alpha, red, green and blue channels, in that order, with straight alpha. Matches the byte order of big-endian ARGB buffers, such as Java's and some TIFF and PSD files. Bgr565 A 16-bit packed pixel: blue in bits 0 to 4, green in bits 5 to 10, red in bits 11 to 15, and no alpha. The same memory as Skia's and Android's RGB 565 and the 16-bit BMP 5-6-5 bit field. Widening and narrowing both round to the nearest value, so every 16-bit value survives a round trip through Rgba8. Bgr8 A pixel with 8-bit blue, green and red channels, in that order, and no alpha. Bgra4444 A 16-bit packed pixel: blue in bits 0 to 3, green in 4 to 7, red in 8 to 11 and straight alpha in 12 to 15. The same memory as the DXGI and Vulkan B4G4R4A4 formats. Each level widens to 8 bits by multiplying by 17, and narrowing rounds to nearest. Bgra8 A pixel with 8-bit blue, green, red and straight alpha channels, in that order. Cmyk16 A pixel with 16-bit cyan, magenta, yellow and black ink amounts, in that order, 0 meaning no ink. 16-bit CMYK TIFF and PSD. Cmyk8 A pixel with 8-bit cyan, magenta, yellow and black ink amounts, in that order, 0 meaning no ink. CMYK JPEG, TIFF and PSD. Gray16 A pixel with one 16-bit luminance channel and no alpha. Gray8 A pixel with one 8-bit luminance channel and no alpha. GrayAlpha16 A pixel with 16-bit luminance and straight alpha channels, in that order. GrayAlpha8 A pixel with 8-bit luminance and straight alpha channels, in that order. GrayF32 A pixel with one 32-bit float luminance channel, nominally 0 to 1, and no alpha: PFM gray maps, depth and height maps. PixelLayoutInfo Describes the memory layout of a pixel type. PremulBgra8 A pixel with 8-bit blue, green and red channels premultiplied by the alpha channel, in that order: the layout of Windows and GPU surfaces. PremulRgba8 A pixel with 8-bit red, green and blue channels premultiplied by the alpha channel, in that order: Skia's N32 premultiplied. PremulRgbaF32 A pixel with 32-bit float red, green and blue channels premultiplied by the alpha channel, in that order, for float compositing and blending. The conversions take and return straight colors; values are not clamped, except that a premultiplied pixel with zero alpha has no color. Rgb10A2 A 32-bit packed pixel: red in bits 0 to 9, green in 10 to 19, blue in 20 to 29 and straight alpha in 30 and 31. The same memory as the DXGI R10G10B10A2 and Vulkan A2B10G10R10 formats, used by 10-bit displays. Ten-bit levels round to the nearest 16-bit value and convert through Rgba16 exactly; two-bit alpha widens by multiplying. Rgb16 A pixel with 16-bit red, green and blue channels, in that order, and no alpha. Rgb8 A pixel with 8-bit red, green and blue channels, in that order, and no alpha. RgbF32 A pixel with 32-bit float red, green and blue channels, in that order, nominally 0 to 1, and no alpha. Rgba16 A pixel with 16-bit red, green, blue and straight alpha channels, in that order. Rgba8 A pixel with 8-bit red, green, blue and straight alpha channels, in that order. Egami's default working type. RgbaF16 A pixel with 16-bit float (Half) red, green, blue and straight alpha channels, in that order, nominally 0 to 1. Values outside 0..1 (HDR) are kept until written to an integer type; conversion to and from float rounds as (Half)f does: to nearest even, with values above 65,504 becoming infinity. RgbaF32 A pixel with 32-bit float red, green, blue and straight alpha channels, in that order, nominally 0 to 1. YuvColor How the samples of a YuvRaster turn into RGB: the matrix, the range and where chroma sits. Every load, wrap and conversion states one, so a picture is never read with a guessed matrix. Interfaces IPixelType<TSelf> A pixel type: an unmanaged struct holding one pixel. The conversions (ToScaled, FromScaled, ToRgba8, FromRgba8) always use sRGB-encoded values with straight (not premultiplied) alpha; Layout says how the pixel is stored, so Egami can take faster paths for layouts it knows. Types from outside Egami may use any layout, with Other for ones Egami does not know. Enums AlphaKind How a pixel type stores alpha. ChromaFormat How a YuvRaster stores chroma: at what resolution against luma, or not at all. ChromaSiting Where each chroma sample of a Yuv420 or Yuv422 picture sits against the luma samples it covers. Conversions filter chroma to match, so colors line up with edges. Ignored for 4:4:4 and 4:0:0. PixelChannelOrder The order in which a pixel type stores its channels. PixelChannelType The storage type of every channel in a pixel type. YuvMatrix The matrix between RGB and luma-chroma (Y'CbCr) values, as ITU-T H.273 names them. Shared by YCbCrColor and planar YUV images, so their coefficients never disagree. YuvPackedFormat The interleaved YUV layouts that operating system decoders, GPUs and webcams hand out, which a YuvRaster copies to and from its planes with CopyFromPacked(YuvPackedFormat, ReadOnlySpan<byte>, int, ReadOnlySpan<byte>, int) and CopyToPacked(YuvPackedFormat, Span<byte>, int, Span<byte>, int). YuvRange Whether luma-chroma values use the whole range or the video range.

api/Egami.PooledPixelMemorySource.html.title: Class PooledPixelMemorySource | Egami
api/Egami.PooledPixelMemorySource.html.summary: Class PooledPixelMemorySource Namespace Egami Assembly Egami.dll The default IPixelMemorySource. Small blocks are arrays rented from a shared pool; larger blocks are unmanaged memory aligned to 64 bytes, which stays off the large object heap and suits SIMD. Planes larger than MaxBlockBytes are split into several blocks of whole rows. public sealed class PooledPixelMemorySource : IPixelMemorySource Inheritance object PooledPixelMemorySource Implements IPixelMemorySource Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // Every pixel buffer comes from the context's IPixelMemorySource; wrap the pooled one to count what it hands out. CountingSource counting = new(PooledPixelMemorySource.Shared); EgamiContext context = EgamiContext.Default with { Memory = counting }; using (Raster<Rgba8> image = Raster.Create<Rgba8>(512, 512, context)) { image.Apply(ops => ops.Blur(2)); } Console.WriteLine($"{counting.Blocks} blocks, {counting.Bytes:N0} bytes"); Remarks Unmanaged blocks are kept after use, up to MaxRetainedBytes, and reused by later allocations of a similar size, because memory fresh from the operating system is slow the first time it is written. api/Egami.Quantization.DitherMode.html.title: Enum DitherMode | Egami
api/Egami.Quantization.DitherMode.html.summary: Enum DitherMode Namespace Egami.Quantization Assembly Egami.dll How the error of mapping pixels to a palette is spread: error diffusion (Floyd–Steinberg and eight other published kernels, and Riemersma's Hilbert-curve walk) or an ordered pattern (Bayer 2, 4, 8 and 16, and 3 × 3). The values are fixed. public enum DitherMode Fields Atkinson = 3 Atkinson's error diffusion (Apple, 1984): spreads six eighths of the error, so flat areas keep more contrast. Bayer16x16 = 14 A 16 × 16 ordered (Bayer) pattern: the finest steps, for large palettes. Bayer2x2 = 12 A 2 × 2 ordered (Bayer) pattern: coarse, visible cross-hatching. Bayer4x4 = 13 A 4 × 4 ordered (Bayer) pattern. Burkes = 4 Burkes' error diffusion (1988): two rows, 32nds. FloydSteinberg = 0 Floyd–Steinberg error diffusion: the smoothest gradients; frames of an animation dither one row after another. JarvisJudiceNinke = 5 Jarvis, Judice and Ninke's error diffusion (1976): three rows, 48ths; smooth but slow. None = 2 No dithering: each pixel takes the nearest palette color. Ordered = 1 An 8×8 ordered (Bayer) pattern: stable between animation frames and parallel, at some cost in quality. Ordered3x3 = 15 A 3 × 3 ordered pattern. Riemersma = 11 Riemersma's dithering (1998): error diffusion along a Hilbert curve with a 16-pixel memory, so no direction shows. Sierra2 = 7 Sierra's two-row error diffusion, 16ths. Sierra3 = 6 Sierra's three-row error diffusion (1989), 32nds. SierraLite = 8 Sierra's Filter Lite: three neighbours, quarters; nearly as smooth as Floyd–Steinberg and faster. StevensonArce = 9 Stevenson and Arce's error diffusion (1985), four rows, 200ths. Stucki = 10 Stucki's error diffusion (1981): three rows, 42nds; sharper than Jarvis, Judice and Ninke. Examples using FileStream output = File.Create("duck.gif"); photo.Save(output, GifFormat.Info, new GifWriterOptions { Palette = new PaletteOptions { MaxColors = 128, Dither = DitherMode.Ordered }, // FloydSteinberg (default), Ordered or None PaletteScope = GifPaletteScope.PerFrame, // Auto (default): one table when all frames fit, else one per frame });

api/Egami.Raster.html.summary: Class Raster Namespace Egami Assembly Egami.dll Measuring images: comparison, statistics, histograms, colors and a pixel signature. Nothing here changes a raster. public abstract class Raster : IDisposable Inheritance object Raster Implements IDisposable Derived Raster<TPixel> Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // Load in the pixel type that best fits the file (here Rgba8: this PNG stores alpha). using Raster image = Raster.Load("duck.png"); Console.WriteLine($"{image.Width} × {image.Height}, {image.Layout.ChannelOrder}"); // Make a thumbnail that fits 200 × 200, keeping the aspect ratio, and save it as JPEG. image.Apply(ops => ops.Fit(200, 200)); image.Save("duck-small.jpg"); Remarks A raster is not thread-safe. Several threads may read it at once, but nothing may read while another thread writes. Methods that return a new raster say so in their name (Copy, As); everything else works in place. Properties Context Gets the context the raster allocates from: its memory source, limits and MaxParallelism, for code outside Egami that works on the raster's pixels, such as a canvas drawing onto it. public EgamiContext Context { get; } Property Value EgamiContext FrameCount Gets the number of frames. Always at least 1. public abstract int FrameCount { get; } Property Value int Height Gets the height in pixels. public int Height { get; } Property Value int Layout Gets the memory layout of the pixel type. public abstract PixelLayoutInfo Layout { get; } Property Value PixelLayoutInfo Metadata Gets the raster's metadata. public RasterMetadata Metadata { get; } Property Value RasterMetadata Width Gets the width in pixels. public int Width { get; } Property Value int Methods Append(IReadOnlyList<Raster>, Axis, int, Rgba8, Alignment) Returns the images side by side or stacked, as ImageMagick's +append and -append do with -gravity: each image's first frame in order, with spacing pixels between them, aligned across the strip and with background around the smaller ones. public static Raster Append(IReadOnlyList<Raster> images, Axis axis = Axis.Horizontal, int spacing = 0, Rgba8 background = default, Alignment alignment = Alignment.Start) Parameters images IReadOnlyList<Raster> At least one raster, of any sizes and pixel types. axis Axis Side by side (the default) or stacked. spacing int The gap between neighbours, in pixels, 0 or more. background Rgba8 The color of gaps and of the space around smaller images; transparent black by default. alignment Alignment Where smaller images sit across the strip. Returns Raster The strip, with the first raster's pixel type, metadata and color profile; other images are converted to them. The caller must dispose it. Examples // Side by side with a 10-pixel white gap, the shorter image centered vertically (ImageMagick's +append). using Raster strip = Raster.Append([duck, egret], Axis.Horizontal, spacing: 10, background: Rgba8.White, alignment: Alignment.Center); // Stacked, as -append does. using Raster column = Raster.Append([duck, egret], Axis.Vertical); Exceptions ArgumentNullException images or one of them is null. ArgumentException images is empty. ArgumentOutOfRangeException The spacing is negative or an enum is not defined. LimitExceededException The result would break MaxTotalBytes. Apply(Action<RasterOps>, CancellationToken) Runs a chain of operations on every frame, changing this raster in place. See Apply(Action<RasterOps>, CancellationToken). public void Apply(Action<RasterOps> build, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters build Action<RasterOps> Records the chain. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancels between steps and between bands of rows. Exceptions ArgumentNullException build is null. ArgumentException A step would make the size less than 1. ArgumentOutOfRangeException A crop, pad or fill rectangle does not fit the image when the chain runs. LimitExceededException The pixels the chain needs would break MaxTotalBytes. ObjectDisposedException The raster has been disposed. OperationCanceledException cancellationToken was canceled. As<TTo>() Returns a new raster with every frame converted to TTo. See Convert<TFrom, TTo>(ReadOnlySpan<TFrom>, Span<TTo>). public Raster<TTo> As<TTo>() where TTo : unmanaged, IPixelType<TTo> Returns Raster<TTo> The new raster. The caller must dispose it. Type Parameters TTo The pixel type to convert to. Exceptions ObjectDisposedException The raster has been disposed. ColorMask(Rgba8, float) Returns a mask of the first frame: 255 where a pixel lies within tolerance of color, 0 elsewhere, by ImageMagick's -fuzz distance. Use it to select by color, then edit only the selection. public Raster<Gray8> ColorMask(Rgba8 color, float tolerance = 0) Parameters color Rgba8 The color to select, with its alpha. tolerance float The color distance, from 0 (the exact color) to 1 (every color). Returns Raster<Gray8> The mask, the raster's size. The caller must dispose it. Examples // Select by color, then edit only the selection: a magic wand from a point, and every pixel close to a color. using Raster<Gray8> wand = photo.FloodMask(new Point(30, 30), tolerance: 0.12f); using Raster<Gray8> reds = photo.ColorMask(new Rgba8(200, 40, 30, 255), tolerance: 0.2f); photo.Apply(ops => ops .Within(new Mask(wand), o => o.Blur(4)) .Within(new Mask(reds), o => o.Saturation(1.4f)), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException tolerance is outside 0..1. ObjectDisposedException The raster has been disposed. CombineChannels<TPixel>(Raster, Raster, Raster, Raster?) Builds a raster from three or four rasters of the same size, reading each one's gray value (the luminance of a color raster, the alpha of an Alpha8 raster) as red, green, blue and alpha. Without alpha the result is opaque. Frame counts must match, or be 1, which is then used for every frame. The result takes red's metadata and frame metadata, with the sRGB profile. public static Raster<TPixel> CombineChannels<TPixel>(Raster red, Raster green, Raster blue, Raster? alpha = null) where TPixel : unmanaged, IPixelType<TPixel> Parameters red Raster The red channel. green Raster The green channel. blue Raster The blue channel. alpha Raster The alpha channel, or null for opaque. Returns Raster<TPixel> The new raster. The caller must dispose it. Type Parameters TPixel The pixel type of the result. Examples // Pull channels out as gray rasters (Gray8 from 8-bit images), edit one, and build the image again. using Raster red = photo.ExtractChannel(ColorChannel.Red); using Raster green = photo.ExtractChannel(ColorChannel.Green); using Raster blue = photo.ExtractChannel(ColorChannel.Blue); blue.Apply(ops => ops.Blur(2), Ct); using Raster<Rgba8> rebuilt = Raster.CombineChannels<Rgba8>(red, green, blue); Exceptions ArgumentNullException A color channel is null. ArgumentException The rasters differ in size, or in frame count other than 1. Compare(Raster, Raster, CompareOptions?) Compares two images of the same size and returns every cheap metric at once, per channel and overall: mean absolute and mean squared error, RMSE, PSNR, the peak error and how many pixels differ, all on the 0 to 1 scale, with SSIM on request. The images may have different pixel types: an Rgb8 and an Rgba8 copy of one picture compare as identical. Color profiles are not reconciled, so convert both to one with ConvertColor<TTo>(ColorProfile, ColorTransformOptions?) first when they differ. public static CompareResult Compare(Raster a, Raster b, CompareOptions? options = null) Parameters a Raster The first image. b Raster The second image, the same size. options CompareOptions The alpha treatment, fuzz, SSIM, region and frame, or null for Default. Returns CompareResult The differences. Examples // Every cheap metric in one pass, per channel and overall, on the 0 to 1 scale; SSIM on request. CompareResult result = Raster.Compare(expected, actual, new CompareOptions { Ssim = true, Fuzz = 0.02f }); Console.WriteLine($"PSNR {result.Overall.Psnr:F1} dB, SSIM {result.Overall.Ssim:F4}, {result.DifferentPixels} pixels off by more than 2%"); bool sameLook = result.Overall.Psnr >= 40; Exceptions ArgumentNullException a or b is null. ArgumentException The images differ in size. ArgumentOutOfRangeException The frame is missing from an image, or the region leaves the image. ObjectDisposedException An image has been disposed. ConvertColor<TTo>(ColorProfile, ColorTransformOptions?) Returns a new raster of TTo with every frame converted from the encoding this raster is in (GetColorProfile()) to target, and metadata that says so. This is how a CMYK image becomes RGB through its profile, or RGB becomes CMYK for print; As<TTo>() converts numerically instead. public Raster<TTo> ConvertColor<TTo>(ColorProfile target, ColorTransformOptions? options = null) where TTo : unmanaged, IPixelType<TTo> Parameters target ColorProfile The encoding to convert to. options ColorTransformOptions The intent and black point compensation, or null for the defaults. Returns Raster<TTo> The new raster. The caller must dispose it. Type Parameters TTo The pixel type to convert to. Its model need not be the target's: see ColorTransform. Examples // A CMYK image becomes RGB through its profile (or the plain formula if it has none), as a new raster. using Raster<Cmyk8> print = Raster.Load<Cmyk8>(path); using Raster<Rgb8> screen = print.ConvertColor<Rgb8>(ColorProfile.Srgb, new ColorTransformOptions { Intent = RenderingIntent.RelativeColorimetric, BlackPointCompensation = true }); Exceptions ArgumentNullException target is null. ObjectDisposedException The raster has been disposed. UnsupportedFormatException The target is an ICC profile with no tables for converting to it. CountColors(int) Counts the distinct stored colors of a frame, exactly, as ImageMagick's %k does. Each distinct stored value counts, so two float pixels that differ in the last bit are two colors. Types of up to 3 bytes use a 2 MB table; wider ones keep a set of the colors seen, which counts against MaxTotalBytes at its worst case (every pixel distinct). public long CountColors(int frame = 0) Parameters frame int The frame, 0 (the default) for the first. Returns long The number of distinct colors. Examples // Unique colors, the palette of a small image, and quick checks before choosing an output format. long count = photo.CountColors(); IReadOnlyList<Rgba16>? palette = photo.GetColors(256); // null: more than 256 colors bool needsAlpha = !photo.IsOpaque(); bool grayscale = photo.IsGray(tolerance: 1 / 255f); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException frame is not a frame of the image. LimitExceededException The set could break MaxTotalBytes. ObjectDisposedException The raster has been disposed. Create<TPixel>(int, int, EgamiContext?) Creates a raster with one frame, with every byte zero (transparent black for types with alpha). public static Raster<TPixel> Create<TPixel>(int width, int height, EgamiContext? context = null) where TPixel : unmanaged, IPixelType<TPixel> Parameters width int The width in pixels, at least 1. height int The height in pixels, at least 1. context EgamiContext The context to allocate from, or null for Default. Returns Raster<TPixel> The new raster. The caller must dispose it. Type Parameters TPixel The pixel type. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException width or height is less than 1. Create<TPixel>(int, int, TPixel, EgamiContext?) Creates a raster with one frame, filled with one color. public static Raster<TPixel> Create<TPixel>(int width, int height, TPixel fill, EgamiContext? context = null) where TPixel : unmanaged, IPixelType<TPixel> Parameters width int The width in pixels, at least 1. height int The height in pixels, at least 1. fill TPixel The color of every pixel. context EgamiContext The context to allocate from, or null for Default. Returns Raster<TPixel> The new raster. The caller must dispose it. Type Parameters TPixel The pixel type. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException width or height is less than 1. Derive(Action<RasterOps>, CancellationToken) Runs a chain of operations and returns the result as a new raster. See Derive(Action<RasterOps>, CancellationToken). public Raster Derive(Action<RasterOps> build, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) Parameters build Action<RasterOps> Records the chain. cancellationToken CancellationToken Cancels between steps and between bands of rows. Returns Raster The new raster, in the same pixel type. The caller must dispose it. Exceptions ArgumentNullException build is null. ArgumentException A step would make the size less than 1. ArgumentOutOfRangeException A crop, pad or fill rectangle does not fit the image when the chain runs. LimitExceededException The pixels the chain needs would break MaxTotalBytes. ObjectDisposedException The raster has been disposed. OperationCanceledException cancellationToken was canceled. DetectSkew(float) Returns the tilt of the first frame's text lines or other strong horizontal structure, in degrees clockwise, to 0.05°: Deskew(float, Rgba8?, bool, ResampleFilter) turns the image back by it. A gray copy about 1,500 pixels on its long side is binarized with Otsu's threshold and every angle up to maxAngle is scored by how sharply the ink's projection piles up in rows (Postl's projection-profile method). public float DetectSkew(float maxAngle = 15) Parameters maxAngle float The largest tilt looked for, in degrees, more than 0 and at most 45. Returns float The tilt, or 0 when no angle stands out clearly from level (a picture, noise, or an already straight page). Examples // Measure the tilt first, if you want to show it or decide yourself... float tilt = photo.DetectSkew(maxAngle: 10); // ...or straighten in one step, keeping the page size with white corners. using Raster straight = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Deskew(background: Rgba8.White), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException maxAngle is out of range. ObjectDisposedException The raster has been disposed. Difference(Raster, Raster, DifferenceStyle, DifferenceOptions?) Returns a picture of where two images of the same size differ: Highlight marks differing pixels in red over a faded copy of a, as ImageMagick's compare does, and Absolute shows |a − b| per channel. The result has a's pixel type and size. public static Raster Difference(Raster a, Raster b, DifferenceStyle style = DifferenceStyle.Highlight, DifferenceOptions? options = null) Parameters a Raster The first image. b Raster The second image, the same size. style DifferenceStyle What to draw. Defaults to Highlight. options DifferenceOptions The colors, fuzz, factor and frame, or null for Default. Returns Raster The picture, one frame. The caller must dispose it. Examples // ImageMagick compare's red-over-faded picture, and the plain per-channel difference turned up 8 times. using Raster highlight = Raster.Difference(a, b); using Raster gaps = Raster.Difference(a, b, DifferenceStyle.Absolute, new DifferenceOptions { Amplify = 8 }); highlight.Save("highlight.png"); gaps.Save("gaps.png"); Exceptions ArgumentNullException a or b is null. ArgumentException The images differ in size. ArgumentOutOfRangeException style is not defined, or the frame is missing. ObjectDisposedException An image has been disposed. Dispose() Returns the raster's memory to its source. Calling it again does nothing. public void Dispose() Dispose(bool) Releases the frames' memory. protected abstract void Dispose(bool disposing) Parameters disposing bool true when called from Dispose(). DominantColors(int, DominantColorOptions?) Returns the main colors of the first frame with the share of pixels each stands for, largest first: k-means in Oklab on a sample of at most MaxSamples pixels, seeded with Wu's palette so the answer is the same every run, with near-identical clusters merged. Transparent pixels are left out. public IReadOnlyList<WeightedColor> DominantColors(int count = 5, DominantColorOptions? options = null) Parameters count int The most colors wanted, 1 to 128. Defaults to 5. Fewer come back when the image has fewer distinct colors. options DominantColorOptions The sampling, passes and merging, or null for Default. Returns IReadOnlyList<WeightedColor> The colors, largest share first; empty when every pixel is transparent. Examples // The main colors and how much of the picture each covers, e.g. to pick brand colors from a logo or a placeholder color. IReadOnlyList<WeightedColor> colors = logo.DominantColors(5); foreach ((Rgba8 color, double weight) in colors) { Console.WriteLine($"#{color.R:X2}{color.G:X2}{color.B:X2} covers {weight:P0}"); } Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException count is outside 1 to 128. ObjectDisposedException The raster has been disposed. EntropyBounds(float) Returns the rectangle EntropyCrop(float) would keep: the union over the frames of the 16 × 16 tiles whose luminance entropy reaches threshold. public Rect EntropyBounds(float threshold = 0.5) Parameters threshold float The entropy a tile needs, from 0 to 1. Returns Rect The rectangle, or an empty one when no tile reaches the threshold. Examples // Keep the part with detail in it: flat tiles (a plain backdrop) fall away. Rect busy = padded.EntropyBounds(); using Raster<Rgba8> cropped = padded.Derive(ops => ops.EntropyCrop(), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException threshold is outside 0..1. ObjectDisposedException The raster has been disposed. ExtractChannel(ColorChannel) Returns a new gray raster holding one channel of every frame: Gray8 from 8-bit pixel types, Gray16 from 16-bit ones, GrayF32 from half and float ones. A gray raster's red, green and blue are its gray value; a raster without alpha gives an all-white alpha. Resolution and EXIF are kept; the ICC profile is dropped, as one channel of a color image is not a gray image in any profile. public Raster ExtractChannel(ColorChannel channel) Parameters channel ColorChannel The channel. Luminance is 0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B of the stored values. Returns Raster The new raster. The caller must dispose it. Examples // Pull channels out as gray rasters (Gray8 from 8-bit images), edit one, and build the image again. using Raster red = photo.ExtractChannel(ColorChannel.Red); using Raster green = photo.ExtractChannel(ColorChannel.Green); using Raster blue = photo.ExtractChannel(ColorChannel.Blue); blue.Apply(ops => ops.Blur(2), Ct); using Raster<Rgba8> rebuilt = Raster.CombineChannels<Rgba8>(red, green, blue); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException channel is not defined. ObjectDisposedException The raster has been disposed. ExtractChannel<TPixel>(ColorChannel) Returns a new raster of TPixel holding one channel of every frame as its gray value, as ExtractChannel(ColorChannel) does, converted to the type asked for. public Raster<TPixel> ExtractChannel<TPixel>(ColorChannel channel) where TPixel : unmanaged, IPixelType<TPixel> Parameters channel ColorChannel The channel. Returns Raster<TPixel> The new raster. The caller must dispose it. Type Parameters TPixel The pixel type of the result, usually a gray type. Examples // Pull channels out as gray rasters (Gray8 from 8-bit images), edit one, and build the image again. using Raster red = photo.ExtractChannel(ColorChannel.Red); using Raster green = photo.ExtractChannel(ColorChannel.Green); using Raster blue = photo.ExtractChannel(ColorChannel.Blue); blue.Apply(ops => ops.Blur(2), Ct); using Raster<Rgba8> rebuilt = Raster.CombineChannels<Rgba8>(red, green, blue); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException channel is not defined. ObjectDisposedException The raster has been disposed. FindThreshold(ThresholdMethod, ThresholdMode) Returns the level AutoThreshold(ThresholdMethod, ThresholdMode, Rgba8?, Rgba8?, bool) would use, from 0 to 1, found by method in a 256-bin histogram of every frame, as ImageMagick's -auto-threshold finds it; 0.5 for an image of one value. public float FindThreshold(ThresholdMethod method = ThresholdMethod.Otsu, ThresholdMode mode = ThresholdMode.Luminance) Parameters method ThresholdMethod How the level is found. Defaults to Otsu. mode ThresholdMode What is measured; Channels measures red, green and blue together. Defaults to Luminance. Returns float The level. Examples // Threshold a scanned page for OCR: Otsu's level for an evenly lit page, or Bradley's local threshold for uneven light. float level = page.FindThreshold(ThresholdMethod.Otsu); using Raster<Gray8> even = page.Derive(o => o.AutoThreshold(ThresholdMethod.Otsu), Ct); using Raster<Gray8> uneven = page.Derive(o => o.AdaptiveThreshold(limit: 0.15f), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException An enum value is not defined. ObjectDisposedException The raster has been disposed. FloodMask(Point, float, Connectivity) Returns a mask of the first frame's region connected to seed whose colors lie within tolerance of the seed's: the "magic wand". 255 inside the region, 0 elsewhere. public Raster<Gray8> FloodMask(Point seed, float tolerance = 0, Connectivity connectivity = Connectivity.Four) Parameters seed Point Where the region starts. tolerance float The color distance, from 0 (the seed's exact color) to 1 (every color). connectivity Connectivity Whether the region spreads to the four side neighbours or also the four diagonal ones. Returns Raster<Gray8> The mask, the raster's size. The caller must dispose it. Examples // Select by color, then edit only the selection: a magic wand from a point, and every pixel close to a color. using Raster<Gray8> wand = photo.FloodMask(new Point(30, 30), tolerance: 0.12f); using Raster<Gray8> reds = photo.ColorMask(new Rgba8(200, 40, 30, 255), tolerance: 0.2f); photo.Apply(ops => ops .Within(new Mask(wand), o => o.Blur(4)) .Within(new Mask(reds), o => o.Saturation(1.4f)), Ct); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The seed lies outside the raster, tolerance is outside 0..1, or connectivity is not defined. ObjectDisposedException The raster has been disposed. GetColors(int, int) Returns the distinct colors of a frame, as 16-bit colors in ascending order, when there are at most limit. public IReadOnlyList<Rgba16>? GetColors(int limit, int frame = 0) Parameters limit int The most colors wanted; the scan stops once there are more. frame int The frame, 0 (the default) for the first. Returns IReadOnlyList<Rgba16> The colors, or null when there are more than limit. Examples // Unique colors, the palette of a small image, and quick checks before choosing an output format. long count = photo.CountColors(); IReadOnlyList<Rgba16>? palette = photo.GetColors(256); // null: more than 256 colors bool needsAlpha = !photo.IsOpaque(); bool grayscale = photo.IsGray(tolerance: 1 / 255f); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException limit is negative, or frame is not a frame of the image. ObjectDisposedException The raster has been disposed. Grid(IReadOnlyList<Raster>, int, Size?, int, Rgba8, ResampleFilter) Returns a contact sheet, as ImageMagick's montage with -tile and -geometry makes one: the images' first frames in rows of columns cells, each image shrunk to fit its cell if it is larger and centered in it. public static Raster Grid(IReadOnlyList<Raster> images, int columns, Size? cell = null, int spacing = 0, Rgba8 background = default, ResampleFilter filter = ResampleFilter.Bicubic) Parameters images IReadOnlyList<Raster> At least one raster, of any sizes and pixel types. columns int The cells per row, at least 1. cell Size? The cell size, or null (the default) for the largest image's width and height. spacing int The gap between cells, in pixels, 0 or more. background Rgba8 The color of gaps and empty cell space; transparent black by default. filter ResampleFilter The kernel images are shrunk with. Returns Raster The sheet, with the first raster's pixel type, metadata and color profile. The caller must dispose it. Examples // A contact sheet three cells wide; each photo shrinks to fit a 200 × 200 cell and sits in its middle. using Raster sheet = Raster.Grid(photos, columns: 3, cell: new Size(200, 200), spacing: 8, background: Rgba8.White); Exceptions ArgumentNullException images or one of them is null. ArgumentException images is empty. ArgumentOutOfRangeException A count or size is out of range, or the filter is not defined. LimitExceededException The result would break MaxTotalBytes. HaldIdentity(int) Creates the identity Hald CLUT image of level: level³ × level³ pixels holding a (level²)³ table that changes nothing, red fastest, as ImageMagick's hald:8. Grade it in any editor, then load it back with FromHald(Raster). public static Raster<Rgba8> HaldIdentity(int level = 8) Parameters level int The level, from 2 to 16. Defaults to 8 (512 × 512, a 64³ table). Returns Raster<Rgba8> The image; the caller disposes it. Examples // Export the identity Hald image, grade it in any editor, and load the graded image back as a table. using Raster<Rgba8> identity = Raster.HaldIdentity(level: 8); // 512 × 512, a 64³ table identity.Save("hald.png"); using Raster graded = Raster.Load("hald.png"); Lut3D fromHald = Lut3D.FromHald(graded); using Raster<Rgba16> back = fromHald.ToHald(level: 8); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException level is outside 2 to 16. HaldIdentity<TPixel>(int) Creates the identity Hald CLUT image of level in TPixel, such as Rgba16 for 16-bit grading. public static Raster<TPixel> HaldIdentity<TPixel>(int level = 8) where TPixel : unmanaged, IPixelType<TPixel> Parameters level int The level, from 2 to 16. Defaults to 8. Returns Raster<TPixel> The image; the caller disposes it. Type Parameters TPixel The pixel type. Examples // Export the identity Hald image, grade it in any editor, and load the graded image back as a table. using Raster<Rgba8> identity = Raster.HaldIdentity(level: 8); // 512 × 512, a 64³ table identity.Save("hald.png"); using Raster graded = Raster.Load("hald.png"); Lut3D fromHald = Lut3D.FromHald(graded); using Raster<Rgba16> back = fromHald.ToHald(level: 8); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException level is outside 2 to 16. Opening reads the header and the metadata that comes before the image data; ReadRows<TPixel>(Raster<TPixel>) and ReadFrame<TPixel>(Raster<TPixel>) then hand out the image in any pixel type, with Region and MinimumSize applied as in Load(Stream, EgamiContext?, ReaderOptions?). public sealed class RasterDecoder : IDisposable Inheritance object RasterDecoder Implements IDisposable Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // A band of rows at a time: memory is the band plus the format's working set, whatever the image size. using RasterDecoder decoder = RasterDecoder.Open("egret.png"); Console.WriteLine($"{decoder.Info.Width}×{decoder.Info.Height}, {decoder.Info.Access}, holding {decoder.Info.WorkingBytes:N0} bytes"); using Raster<Gray8> band = Raster.Create<Gray8>(decoder.Info.Width, 64); int rows; while ((rows = decoder.ReadRows(band)) > 0) { for (int y = 0; y < rows; y++) { foreach (Gray8 pixel in band.Row(y)) { sum += pixel.L; } } } Remarks A decoder is one caller's object and is not thread-safe. Access says whether the format streams its rows or is decoded into a buffer first, and WorkingBytes how much that holds. api/Egami.Svg.html.title: Namespace Egami.Svg | Egami
api/Egami.Svg.html.summary: Namespace Egami.Svg Classes SvgAttribute An attribute of an SvgElement: its name, namespace, the prefix it was written with, and its value. SvgAttributeCollection An element's attributes, in file order. Setting, adding and removing mark the document's render tree for rebuilding. SvgCanvas A canvas that writes SVG: every drawing call becomes SVG elements, so anything drawn on a Canvas (shapes, strokes, gradients, images, text, clips, layers, recorded pictures) can be saved as a vector file that browsers, Inkscape and Egami.Svg all read. Gradients, patterns, clips, masks, images, glyph outlines and pictures are written once in defs and shared. What SVG cannot express (sweep gradients, noise and composed paints, meshes, layers with filters) is drawn by Egami into an image at FallbackScale and embedded as PNG. The output is SVG 1.1 with CSS mix-blend-mode and isolation for blend modes and layers (and SVG 2's fr for a conical gradient whose start circle has a radius). Disposing the canvas finishes the file and writes it to the stream, which is left open. An image or picture drawn several times is stored once, as it was when first drawn. SvgClip A clip path, in the coordinates of the node it clips: the union of its shapes, each with its own clip-rule. SvgComment An XML comment, kept so a save writes it back. SvgContent One item of an SvgElement's content, in file order: an element, text, a comment or a processing instruction. SvgContentList An element's content in file order: child elements, text, comments and processing instructions. Changes mark the document's render tree for rebuilding. SvgDecodeOptions Options for reading SVG through SvgFormat with Raster.Load and Raster.Probe. SvgDocument An SVG document: an editable element tree read from an .svg or .svgz file, which saves back to SVG and draws through Egami.Drawing's canvas. SvgElement An element of an SVG document's editable tree: its name and namespace, attributes and content, like XDocument's elements. Unknown elements and foreign namespaces (Inkscape's, Illustrator's metadata) are kept, so a save writes them back. SvgException Thrown when an SVG file is not well-formed XML, breaks a safety limit, or, with Strict, has anything a lenient load would skip. SvgFilter A filter, in the coordinates of the node it filters: the filter elements and CSS filter functions of its filter property, run one after the other. SvgFontOptions Where a document's text finds its fonts (question 13): the caller's Collection first, then the fonts installed on the machine unless UseSystemFonts is off, then per-character fallback through the same fonts. A server that renders untrusted files should pass its own collection and turn system fonts off, so output never depends on the machine. SvgFormat SVG and SVGZ as an Egami format: registered with WithFormat(FormatInfo), Raster.Load draws an SVG file at its own size (times Scale) and Raster.Probe gives that size without drawing. The format only reads; nothing outside the file is opened, so images it links are not drawn, and text uses the machine's fonts. For a resolver, your own fonts, a target size or a background, load an SvgDocument and call Rasterize<TPixel>(SvgRenderOptions?). SvgGlyphRenderer Draws the glyphs of an OpenType SVG table (question 20): each glyph's document is read once per font and kept, and the element glyphid is drawn in the font's units, its origin on the baseline. Set it on ColorGlyphRenderer; Rasterize<TPixel>(SvgRenderOptions?) uses it already. SvgGroup A group of nodes drawn in order: a g, svg, a, switch, a use instance or a marker. SvgImage An image: a raster drawn into a rectangle, or another SVG document drawn as a group. SvgLoadOptions How SvgDocument reads a file: what it may fetch, how strict it is, and which limits and diagnostics apply. SvgMask A mask, in the coordinates of the node it masks: content drawn into a region, used by luminance or alpha. SvgNamespaces The XML namespaces SVG files use. SvgNode A node of a document's render tree: the elements resolved for drawing, with styles applied, units in pixels, use expanded, references linked and shapes turned into paths, as resvg's usvg tree. It is immutable, so a document that is not being edited can be drawn on many threads at once. SvgPath A shape: a 2.6 Path with its fill, stroke and markers. SvgProcessingInstruction An XML processing instruction, such as <?xml-stylesheet ...?>, kept so a save writes it back. SvgRenderOptions How Rasterize<TPixel>(SvgRenderOptions?) and Draw(Canvas, RectF?, SvgRenderOptions?) draw a document. SvgResolvers Ready resolvers for Resolver. SvgSaveOptions How Save(Stream, SvgSaveOptions?) writes a document. SvgTextContent Character data in an element: text or a CDATA section, kept apart so a save writes it back the same way. SvgTextRun Text: one run of positioned glyphs in one font with one fill and stroke, drawn with DrawGlyphRun(GlyphRun, Vector2, Paint) so a PDF or SVG canvas keeps real text. A text element becomes a group of these and of the paths of its decorations. SvgWriteOptions How SvgCanvas writes SVG: text, number precision, layout, image format and fallback resolution. Enums SvgImageFormat The format SvgCanvas embeds drawn images in. SvgPaintOrder Which of a shape's fill, stroke and markers is painted first (paint-order). SvgTextMode How SvgCanvas writes text.

api/Egami.YuvRaster.html.summary: Class YuvRaster Namespace Egami Assembly Egami.dll A picture held as separate luma (Y) and chroma (U, V) planes, plus an optional alpha plane, the way video codecs, AVIF, lossy WebP and JPEG store it. This base class is used when the sample type is not known at compile time; YuvRaster<TSample> gives the planes. Convert to and from a Raster with ToRaster(YuvConvertOptions?), CopyTo<TPixel>(Raster<TPixel>, YuvConvertOptions?, CancellationToken) and FromRaster(Raster, ChromaFormat, YuvColor, bool, YuvConvertOptions?). public abstract class YuvRaster : IDisposable Inheritance object YuvRaster Implements IDisposable Derived YuvRaster<TSample> Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples // A 1080p frame as video stores it: full-size luma, chroma at half width and height, BT.709 at limited range. using YuvRaster<byte> frame = YuvRaster.Create(1920, 1080, ChromaFormat.Yuv420, YuvColor.Bt709Limited); // 10-bit HDR planes hold samples 0 to 1023 in ushorts; an alpha plane is optional. using YuvRaster<ushort> hdr = YuvRaster.Create(3840, 2160, ChromaFormat.Yuv420, 10, YuvColor.Bt2020Limited, alpha: true); Console.WriteLine($"Chroma planes are {frame.U!.Width}×{frame.U.Height}"); Remarks A YUV raster is not a Raster: one pixel is spread over planes of different sizes. Operations other than Crop and Resize run on a Raster after conversion. It is not thread-safe for writing, like a raster. Properties BitDepth Gets the bits per sample: 8 for byte samples; 10, 12 or 16 for ushort samples. public int BitDepth { get; } Property Value int ChromaFormat Gets the chroma resolution against luma. public ChromaFormat ChromaFormat { get; } Property Value ChromaFormat Color Gets how the samples turn into RGB: matrix, range and chroma siting. public YuvColor Color { get; } Property Value YuvColor HasAlpha Gets a value indicating whether the raster has an alpha plane. public abstract bool HasAlpha { get; } Property Value bool Height Gets the height of the luma plane in pixels. public int Height { get; } Property Value int Metadata Gets the metadata (EXIF, ICC, XMP and the rest), carried to and from a Raster on conversion. public RasterMetadata Metadata { get; } Property Value RasterMetadata Width Gets the width of the luma plane in pixels. public int Width { get; } Property Value int Methods CopyFromPacked(YuvPackedFormat, ReadOnlySpan<byte>, int, ReadOnlySpan<byte>, int) Copies a frame in an interleaved layout into this raster's planes, with one SIMD pass. The raster must match the layout: 4:2:0 8-bit for NV12 and NV21, 4:2:0 10-bit for P010, 4:2:0 at 10, 12 or 16 bits for P016, 4:2:2 8-bit for YUYV and UYVY. public void CopyFromPacked(YuvPackedFormat format, ReadOnlySpan<byte> data, int stride = 0, ReadOnlySpan<byte> chroma = default, int chromaStride = 0) Parameters format YuvPackedFormat The layout. data ReadOnlySpan<byte> The frame: the luma plane for two-plane layouts, or the only plane for packed 4:2:2. stride int The distance between rows of data, in bytes. 0 means rows are packed. chroma ReadOnlySpan<byte> The interleaved chroma plane of a two-plane layout, or empty when it follows the luma rows in data (at stride × Height). Ignored for YUYV and UYVY. chromaStride int The distance between chroma rows, in bytes. 0 means the luma stride, or the packed chroma row when an odd width makes that longer. Examples // An NV12 frame from Media Foundation or MediaCodec: Y rows, then interleaved U, V rows, both at the same stride. int width = 640, height = 360, stride = 704; byte[] nv12 = new byte[stride * height * 3 / 2]; using YuvRaster<byte> frame = YuvRaster.Create(width, height, ChromaFormat.Yuv420, YuvColor.Bt709Limited); frame.CopyFromPacked(YuvPackedFormat.Nv12, nv12, stride); // A webcam's YUYV, 4:2:2 in one plane, the other way. using YuvRaster<byte> webcam = YuvRaster.Create(width, height, ChromaFormat.Yuv422, YuvColor.Bt601Limited); byte[] yuyv = new byte[width * 2 * height]; webcam.CopyToPacked(YuvPackedFormat.Yuyv, yuyv); Exceptions ArgumentException The raster does not match the layout. ArgumentOutOfRangeException A stride is too small or a span too short. ObjectDisposedException The raster has been disposed. Examples using YuvRaster<byte> frame = YuvRaster.Create(1920, 1080, ChromaFormat.Yuv420, YuvColor.Bt709Limited); // Scale the planes before converting, as video does; crops start on a chroma sample (even x and y at 4:2:0). using YuvRaster<byte> small = frame.Resize(1280, 720, ResampleFilter.Bicubic); using YuvRaster<byte> center = small.Crop(new Rect(320, 180, 640, 360)); // A player scales every frame into the same raster. using YuvRaster<byte> screen = YuvRaster.Create(960, 540, ChromaFormat.Yuv420, YuvColor.Bt709Limited); frame.ResizeTo(screen); // Everything else (rotate, color adjustments, drawing) runs on a Raster after conversion. using Raster<Rgba8> rgb = center.ToRaster<Rgba8>(); rgb.Apply(ops => ops.Rotate(90)); Exceptions ArgumentNullException target is null. ArgumentException The target is this raster, or differs in sample type, chroma format, bit depth or color. ObjectDisposedException Either raster has been disposed. Save(Stream, FormatInfo, WriterOptions?) Encodes the picture in format. JPEG encodes the planes straight, with no color conversion or chroma downsampling, when they are 8-bit BT.601 at full range (4:2:0, 4:2:2 and 4:4:4 keep their sampling, 4:0:0 is gray); other planes are converted to that first. Other formats are saved from ToRaster(YuvConvertOptions?). public void Save(Stream stream, FormatInfo format, WriterOptions? options = null) Parameters stream Stream Where to write, from its current position. It is left open. format FormatInfo The format. options WriterOptions The format's options, or null for its defaults. JPEG's subsampling comes from the planes. Examples // A JPEG's own planes, as decoded: no chroma upsampling and no color conversion. YuvRasterInfo info = YuvRaster.Probe("duck.jpg"); Console.WriteLine($"{info.Info.Width}×{info.Info.Height}, planes: {info.ChromaFormat}"); using YuvRaster planes = YuvRaster.Load("duck.jpg"); // Saving JPEG-colored 8-bit planes skips color conversion and downsampling; other planes are converted first. planes.Save("copy.jpg", new JpegWriterOptions { Quality = 90 }); Exceptions UnsupportedFormatException The format has no writer. ObjectDisposedException The raster has been disposed. ArgumentNullException stream or format is null. Save(Stream, string, WriterOptions?) Encodes the picture in the registered format with this name or file extension. See Save(Stream, FormatInfo, WriterOptions?). public void Save(Stream stream, string formatNameOrExtension, WriterOptions? options = null) Parameters stream Stream Where to write, from its current position. It is left open. formatNameOrExtension string The format's name or one of its extensions, ignoring case. options WriterOptions The format's options, or null for its defaults. Examples // A JPEG's own planes, as decoded: no chroma upsampling and no color conversion. ObjectDisposedException The raster has been disposed. Save(string, WriterOptions?) Encodes the picture to a file, choosing the format from the extension. An existing file is replaced; if encoding fails, the partly written file is deleted. See Save(Stream, FormatInfo, WriterOptions?). public void Save(string path, WriterOptions? options = null) Parameters path string The file path. options WriterOptions The format's options, or null for its defaults. Examples // A JPEG's own planes, as decoded: no chroma upsampling and no color conversion. ObjectDisposedException The raster has been disposed. IOException The file cannot be written. ToRaster(YuvConvertOptions?) Converts to a new raster in the natural pixel type: Rgba8 for 8-bit samples, Rgba16 for more. RGB comes out in the picture's own transfer function; nothing is linearized or tone mapped. public Raster ToRaster(YuvConvertOptions? options = null) Parameters options YuvConvertOptions The chroma filters, or null for Default. Returns Raster The new raster, with a copy of the metadata. The caller must dispose it. Examples using Raster photo = Raster.Load("duck.png"); // RGB to planes and back. RGB comes out in the picture's own transfer (BT.709 video gives BT.709-encoded RGB). using YuvRaster<byte> yuv = YuvRaster.FromRaster(photo, ChromaFormat.Yuv420, YuvColor.Bt709Limited); using Raster rgba = yuv.ToRaster(); // Rgba8 for 8-bit planes, Rgba16 for more using Raster<Rgb8> rgb = yuv.ToRaster<Rgb8>(); // or any pixel type Exceptions ObjectDisposedException The raster has been disposed. ToRaster<TPixel>(YuvConvertOptions?) Converts to a new raster of TPixel. See ToRaster(YuvConvertOptions?). public Raster<TPixel> ToRaster<TPixel>(YuvConvertOptions? options = null) where TPixel : unmanaged, IPixelType<TPixel> Parameters options YuvConvertOptions The chroma filters, or null for Default. Returns Raster<TPixel> The new raster, with a copy of the metadata. The caller must dispose it. Type Parameters TPixel The pixel type. RGB comes out in the picture's own transfer (BT.709 video gives BT.709-encoded RGB). using YuvRaster<byte> yuv = YuvRaster.FromRaster(photo, ChromaFormat.Yuv420, YuvColor.Bt709Limited); using Raster rgba = yuv.ToRaster(); // Rgba8 for 8-bit planes, Rgba16 for more using Raster<Rgb8> rgb = yuv.ToRaster<Rgb8>(); // or any pixel type Exceptions ObjectDisposedException The raster has been disposed. LimitExceededException The new raster breaks the context's MaxTotalBytes. Wrap<TSample>(Memory<TSample>, int, Memory<TSample>, int, Memory<TSample>, int, int, int, ChromaFormat, int, YuvColor, IDisposable?, EgamiContext?) Creates a raster over planes the caller owns, such as a decoder's or the operating system's frame buffers, without copying. When owner is given, disposing the raster disposes it; otherwise the caller keeps the memory alive while the raster is used. Sizes and strides are checked up front; SafetyLimits do not apply to wrapped memory. public static YuvRaster<TSample> Wrap<TSample>(Memory<TSample> y, int yStride, Memory<TSample> u, int uStride, Memory<TSample> v, int vStride, int width, int height, ChromaFormat chromaFormat, int bitDepth, YuvColor color, IDisposable? owner = null, EgamiContext? context = null) where TSample : unmanaged Parameters y Memory<TSample> The luma plane. yStride int The distance between luma rows, in samples. 0 means rows are packed. u Memory<TSample> The U (Cb) plane, or empty for 4:0:0. uStride int The distance between U rows, in samples. 0 means rows are packed. v Memory<TSample> The V (Cr) plane, or empty for 4:0:0. vStride int The distance between V rows, in samples. 0 means rows are packed. width int The luma width in pixels, at least 1. height int The luma height in pixels, at least 1. chromaFormat ChromaFormat The chroma resolution. bitDepth int The bits per sample: 8 for bytes; 10, 12 or 16 for ushort. color YuvColor How the samples turn into RGB. owner IDisposable What to dispose with the raster, or null. context EgamiContext The context for later allocations, or null for Default. Returns YuvRaster<TSample> The raster. Type Parameters TSample byte for 8 bits, ushort for 10, 12 and 16 bits. Examples // A decoder's 10-bit frame, rows padded to 64 samples: wrapped without a copy. Disposing the raster disposes the owner. int width = 50, height = 30, stride = 64, chromaStride = 32; ushort[] y = new ushort[stride * height], u = new ushort[chromaStride * 15], v = new ushort[chromaStride * 15]; using YuvRaster<ushort> wrapped = YuvRaster.Wrap<ushort>( y, stride, u, chromaStride, v, chromaStride, width, height, ChromaFormat.Yuv420, bitDepth: 10, YuvColor.Bt2020Limited, owner: null); Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException A size, stride or bit depth is out of range, or a plane is too short. api/Egami.html.title: Namespace Egami | Egami
api/Egami.html.summary: Namespace Egami Classes CorruptDataException Thrown when data matches a format but breaks its rules, such as a bad checksum, a truncated stream or an invalid table. DiagnosticReporter One call's link to Diagnostics, with the same level filter and per-id cap Egami's own readers and writers use. Get one from StartDiagnostics() at the start of a call (format plug-ins use Diagnostics) and dispose it when the call ends. When the context has no handler it is a shared instance that does nothing, so reporting costs one check. EgamiContext Every setting that is not specific to one call: where memory comes from, how many threads an operation may use, and the safety limits. Contexts are immutable and safe to share. Change one with a with expression. EgamiException The base class of every exception Egami throws for problems with image data or limits. FrameList<TPixel> The frames of a raster, all the same size and pixel type. There is always at least one. Frames added from anywhere are copied, so a frame belongs to one raster only. Frame<TPixel> One frame of a raster: a pixel plane the size of the raster plus per-frame metadata. InkCoverage How much ink an InkRaster prints, from MeasureCoverage(float). InkPlate One plane of an InkRaster: an ink's plate, or the alpha plane. Rows are read and written in place; AsRaster<TPixel>() shows the plane as a gray raster without copying. InkRaster A printed page as plates: one plane per ink of an InkSet (a disabled spot has none) plus one alpha plane, each 8 or 16 bits. A plane holds the ink as it prints over paper, 0 for none to the depth's maximum for full ink: drawing translucently leaves less ink, so the planes are premultiplied by the alpha plane, and a plate is ready to print as it is. A new raster is blank: no ink, alpha 0. InkTiffOptions How an InkRaster is saved as a separated TIFF. LimitExceededException Thrown when a SafetyLimits limit is exceeded. MipChain A chain of ever-halved copies of an image, for making many smaller sizes fast: each resize starts from the smallest level that is still at least twice the target, so a gallery of thumbnail sizes reads each source pixel about once instead of once per size. Level 0 is the source itself; each next level halves the size, rounding up, by averaging 2 × 2 blocks of premultiplied pixels. PixelMemoryLeakEventArgs Describes a pixel memory block that was collected without being disposed. PixelMemoryUsage What a PooledPixelMemorySource has handed out and not yet had back, and opt-in tracking of blocks that were never disposed. Get it from Usage; most callers want PooledPixelMemorySource.Shared.Usage. PixelPlane<TPixel> A width × height grid of pixels, stored row by row. A row is always one contiguous span, but the plane as a whole may be split into several blocks of whole rows. Planes belong to the raster or operation that hands them out, which returns their memory; user code reads and writes them but never frees them. PooledPixelMemorySource The default IPixelMemorySource. Small blocks are arrays rented from a shared pool; larger blocks are unmanaged memory aligned to 64 bytes, which stays off the large object heap and suits SIMD. Planes larger than MaxBlockBytes are split into several blocks of whole rows. ProofOptions How Proof<TPixel>(ProofOptions?) shows the plates on screen. Raster Measuring images: comparison, statistics, histograms, colors and a pixel signature. Nothing here changes a raster. RasterDecoder One open image, decoded a band of rows or a frame at a time. Opening reads the header and the metadata that comes before the image data; ReadRows<TPixel>(Raster<TPixel>) and ReadFrame<TPixel>(Raster<TPixel>) then hand out the image in any pixel type, with Region and MinimumSize applied as in Load(Stream, EgamiContext?, ReaderOptions?). RasterEncoder Creates a RasterEncoder<TPixel>, which writes an image a band of rows or a frame at a time. RasterEncoder<TPixel> An image being written a band of rows or a frame at a time, so a huge image never has to exist whole. The bytes are the ones Save(Stream, FormatInfo, WriterOptions?) writes for the same pixels and options, except where a format must write differently without seeking: top-down BMP and TGA rows, and run-length TGA, which is always top-down. Options that need every pixel before the first byte (automatic palettes, PNG's Reduce, automatic alpha) throw at Create instead of quietly writing something else. RasterList The images of a file that holds several, each its own raster with its own size, pixel type and metadata: a TIFF's pages, an icon's entries. The list owns them: disposing it disposes every raster. Raster<TPixel> An image whose pixels are of type TPixel. Pixel access is by row span. SafetyLimits Limits that protect against hostile or broken files. Readers check sizes from the header before allocating any pixel memory. The defaults let normal photos and screenshots through. Change them with a with expression. SpritePackOptions How Pack(IReadOnlyList<Raster>, SpritePackOptions?) lays sprites out. SpriteSheet A sprite sheet: many images packed into one, with the rectangle of each. Packing uses the MaxRects algorithm with the best short side fit (Jylänki, "A Thousand Ways to Pack the Bin", 2010), the images taken by height, tallest first, and then by input order, so the same inputs always give the same sheet. Sprites are never rotated. UnsupportedFormatException Thrown when no registered format matches the data, or the matching format cannot read or write. YuvConvertOptions The chroma filters for conversions between a YuvRaster and a Raster. YuvPlane<TSample> One plane of a YuvRaster<TSample>: a width × height grid of raw samples, stored row by row. A row is always one contiguous span. Samples are stored low-bit aligned: a 10-bit sample is 0 to 1023 in a ushort. YuvRaster A picture held as separate luma (Y) and chroma (U, V) planes, plus an optional alpha plane, the way video codecs, AVIF, lossy WebP and JPEG store it. This base class is used when the sample type is not known at compile time; YuvRaster<TSample> gives the planes. Convert to and from a Raster with ToRaster(YuvConvertOptions?), CopyTo<TPixel>(Raster<TPixel>, YuvConvertOptions?, CancellationToken) and FromRaster(Raster, ChromaFormat, YuvColor, bool, YuvConvertOptions?). YuvRasterInfo What Probe(Stream, EgamiContext?, ReaderOptions?) reads from a header: the image as Probe(Stream, EgamiContext?, ReaderOptions?) describes it, and the planes Load(Stream, EgamiContext?, ReaderOptions?) would give, if any. YuvRaster<TSample> A picture held as separate Y, U, V and optional alpha planes of TSample samples. See YuvRaster. Structs EgamiDiagnostic One event reported to Diagnostics, and the type of each entry in Warnings. Ids are listed in the diagnostics article and never renamed or reused. Point A position in pixels. X grows to the right and Y downward; the top-left pixel is (0, 0). Rect A rectangle of pixels: the top-left corner and a size. Size A width and height in pixels. Interfaces IPixelMemorySource Supplies the memory behind every PixelPlane<TPixel>. Implement it to control where pixel memory comes from. Implementations must be thread-safe. Enums Alignment Where a smaller image sits across the layout's direction: at the start (left or top), the center or the end. Axis The direction images are laid out in by Append(IReadOnlyList<Raster>, Axis, int, Rgba8, Alignment). ChromaDownsampling How chroma is reduced to the chroma resolution when a raster converts to a subsampled YuvRaster. ChromaUpsampling How chroma is brought up to luma resolution when a YuvRaster converts to RGB. ClearMode Says whether new pixel memory is cleared. DecodeStatus Where a RasterDecoder stands, as Status reports it. DiagnosticLevel How much an EgamiDiagnostic matters. Maps one to one onto the Debug, Information and Warning log levels. InkDepth How many bits each plane of an InkRaster stores per pixel. Delegates RowAction<TPixel> Processes one row of pixels.

articles/cookbook/index.html.title: Cookbook | Egami
articles/cookbook/index.html.summary: Cookbook Task-sized recipes. Each one compiles and runs in Egami's test run. Thumbnails for the web // Decode at the smallest JPEG scale that still covers 400 × 400, turn it upright, fit it, and save at quality 80. using Raster photo = Raster.Load("sideways.jpg", options: new ReaderOptions { MinimumSize = new Size(400, 400) }); photo.Apply(ops => ops.AutoOrient().Fit(400, 400, enlarge: false)); photo.Save("thumb.jpg", new JpegWriterOptions { Quality = 80, StripMetadata = true }); The JPEG decodes at 1/2, 1/4 or 1/8 scale, AutoOrient turns only the small result, and the metadata is left out of the file. Safe handling of untrusted uploads EgamiContext strict = EgamiContext.Default with { Limits = SafetyLimits.Default with { MaxPixels = 25_000_000, MaxTotalBytes = 256L * 1024 * 1024 }, }; try { // Read the header first: cheap, and it rejects what you do not want before any pixel memory is used. RasterInfo info = Raster.Probe(upload, strict); if (info.Width > 8000 || info.Height > 8000) { throw new InvalidDataException("Too large."); } using Raster image = Raster.Load(upload, strict, new ReaderOptions { Recovery = RecoveryMode.Strict }); Console.WriteLine($"{info.Format.Name} {image.Width} × {image.Height}"); } catch (UnsupportedFormatException) { Console.WriteLine("Not an image format we accept."); } catch (LimitExceededException e) { Console.WriteLine($"Over the {e.LimitName} limit."); } catch (CorruptDataException e) { Console.WriteLine($"Damaged at byte {e.Offset}."); } See the security guide for every limit. Log Egami's warnings with ILogger // With Microsoft.Extensions.Logging: one line at startup sends every call's warnings to the app's log, with the id as // a property to filter and count on. Egami itself has no logging dependency. EgamiContext.SetDefault(new EgamiContext { Diagnostics = d => logger.Log(d.Level.ToLogLevel(), "{Source} {Id} at {Offset}: {Message}", d.Source, d.Id, d.Offset, d.Message), }); Set it once at startup; every call that passes no context then reports to the log. The diagnostics page lists every id. Log Egami's warnings with Serilog // With Serilog's static Log: the same one line, with Serilog's level names. EgamiContext context = EgamiContext.Default with { Diagnostics = d => log.Write(d.Level == DiagnosticLevel.Warning ? "Warning" : d.Level == DiagnosticLevel.Info ? "Information" : "Debug", "{Id}: {Message}", d.Id, d.Message), }; Know which file a warning came from // Per file: the handler's closure carries the path, so no correlation id is needed. Contexts are cheap records. foreach (string path in Directory.EnumerateFiles(".", "*.png")) { EgamiContext perFile = EgamiContext.Default with { Diagnostics = d => log.Add($"{path}: {d.Message}") }; using Raster image = Raster.Load(path, perFile); } Reject damaged uploads // Warnings as errors: a handler that throws fails the call with its exception, and nothing the call allocated is leaked. EgamiContext strict = EgamiContext.Default with { Diagnostics = d => throw new InvalidDataException($"{d.Id}: {d.Message}"), }; try { using Raster image = Raster.Load(SampleFiles.Damaged(), strict); } catch (InvalidDataException e) { Console.WriteLine($"Rejected: {e.Message}"); } A handler that throws turns every warning into an error; RecoveryMode.Strict does the same for damage alone, without a handler. Use from ASP.NET Core // In an ASP.NET Core endpoint: `upload` is IFormFile.OpenReadStream(), `response` is HttpResponse.Body. EgamiContext limits = EgamiContext.Default with { Limits = SafetyLimits.Default with { MaxPixels = 40_000_000, MaxTotalBytes = 512L * 1024 * 1024 }, }; using Raster image = await Raster.LoadAsync(upload, limits, new ReaderOptions { MinimumSize = new Size(256, 256) }, Ct); image.Apply(ops => ops.AutoOrient().Cover(256, 256), Ct); await image.SaveAsync(response, JpegFormat.Info, new JpegWriterOptions { Quality = 85, StripMetadata = true }, Ct); Egami has no ASP.NET Core dependency: it reads and writes any Stream. The async calls read the upload into a pooled buffer, counted against MaxTotalBytes, so a slow client never holds a thread. Batch convert a folder // Convert a folder of images to QOI, a few at a time. Each image runs on one thread, so the files run side by side. EgamiContext oneThread = EgamiContext.Default with { MaxParallelism = 1 }; Directory.CreateDirectory("out"); Parallel.ForEach(Directory.GetFiles("in"), new ParallelOptions { MaxDegreeOfParallelism = 4 }, path => { try { using Raster image = Raster.Load(path, oneThread); image.Save(Path.Combine("out", Path.GetFileNameWithoutExtension(path) + ".qoi")); } catch (EgamiException e) { Console.WriteLine($"{path}: {e.Message}"); } }); Convert images to WebP for the web // Photos as lossy WebP, graphics with few colors as lossless: Probe reads only the header to tell them apart. foreach (string path in new[] { "duck.png", "egret.png" }) { using Raster image = Raster.Load(path); bool photo = image.Width * image.Height > 100_000; image.Save(Path.ChangeExtension(path, ".webp"), photo ? new WebpWriterOptions { Quality = 80, Effort = 4 } : new WebpWriterOptions { Lossless = true, Effort = 6 }); } Quality and Effort mean what cwebp's -q and -m mean; lossless keeps every pixel. See the WebP guide for the other options. Turn an animated GIF into WebP // A GIF (or APNG) becomes an animated WebP in one Load and one Save: frames, delays and loop count carry over. Each frame // stores only what changed; lossless frames are exact, MixedFrames keeps whichever kind is smaller per frame. using Raster gif = Raster.Load("pan.gif"); gif.Save("pan.webp", new WebpWriterOptions { Lossless = false, MixedFrames = true }); // Read back, every frame is the composed canvas, as with GIF and APNG. using Raster<Rgba8> webp = Raster.Load<Rgba8>("pan.webp"); foreach (Frame<Rgba8> frame in webp.Frames) { Console.WriteLine($"{frame.Metadata.Delay.TotalMilliseconds} ms, changed {frame.Metadata.Bounds}, blend {frame.Metadata.Blend}"); } Make an animated GIF from frames // Start from one picture and add frames: each Add copies the frame you pass. using Raster<Rgba8> animation = Raster.Load<Rgba8>("duck.png"); animation.Apply(ops => ops.Fit(120, 120)); using Raster<Rgba8> next = animation.Derive(ops => ops.HueRotate(120)); using Raster<Rgba8> last = animation.Derive(ops => ops.HueRotate(240)); animation.Frames.Add(next.Frames[0]); animation.Frames.Add(last.Frames[0]); foreach (Frame<Rgba8> frame in animation.Frames) { frame.Metadata.Delay = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(400); } animation.Metadata.LoopCount = 0; // forever animation.Save("hues.gif"); Show video frames // A player converts every frame into the same raster: after the first frame, nothing is allocated. using YuvRaster<byte> frame = YuvRaster.Create(1280, 720, ChromaFormat.Yuv420, YuvColor.Bt709Limited); using Raster<Bgra8> screen = Raster.Create<Bgra8>(1280, 720); for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) { // ... the decoder writes frame's planes ... frame.CopyTo(screen); } // And the other way, for an encoder: CopyFrom fills existing planes. frame.CopyFrom(screen); Decoder frames in NV12 or P010 copy into the planes first; see planar YUV. Read and write JPEG planes // A JPEG's own planes, as decoded: no chroma upsampling and no color conversion. YuvRasterInfo info = YuvRaster.Probe("duck.jpg"); Console.WriteLine($"{info.Info.Width}×{info.Info.Height}, planes: {info.ChromaFormat}"); using YuvRaster planes = YuvRaster.Load("duck.jpg"); // Saving JPEG-colored 8-bit planes skips color conversion and downsampling; other planes are converted first. planes.Save("copy.jpg", new JpegWriterOptions { Quality = 90 }); Read a CMYK JPEG's inks // A CMYK JPEG loads as RGB by the plain formula, as before; ask for Cmyk8 to get the file's ink amounts instead. using Raster<Cmyk8> inks = Raster.Load<Cmyk8>("duck-cmyk.jpg"); Cmyk8 corner = inks.Row(0)[0]; Console.WriteLine($"Cyan {corner.C}, magenta {corner.M}, yellow {corner.Y}, black {corner.K} (0 = no ink)"); // Resizing filters the four inks, so black stays in the black channel; color adjustments go through RGB instead. inks.Apply(ops => ops.Fit(160, 160)); Save a CMYK JPEG for print // CMYK pixels save as CMYK, inverted behind an Adobe marker as Photoshop writes; YCCK is usually smaller. using Raster<Cmyk8> inks = image.As<Cmyk8>(); inks.Save("duck-cmyk-out.jpg", JpegWriterOptions.Default); inks.Save("duck-ycck.jpg", new JpegWriterOptions { ColorType = JpegColorType.Ycck }); Save a progressive JPEG for the web // Shows coarse first and sharpens as it loads; usually a few percent smaller, and decodes to the same pixels. image.Save("duck-progressive.jpg", new JpegWriterOptions { Progressive = true }); Rotate a JPEG without losing quality // Turns the photo upright by its EXIF orientation without re-encoding: no quality is lost, and the tag is reset. JpegTransform.Apply("sideways.jpg", "upright.jpg", new JpegTransformOptions { Operation = JpegTransformOperation.AutoOrient }); // Rotates, crops and drops the color in one pass; a file can be transformed in place. JpegTransformResult result = JpegTransform.Apply("upright.jpg", "upright.jpg", new JpegTransformOptions { Operation = JpegTransformOperation.Rotate90, Crop = new Rect(0, 0, 200, 120), Grayscale = true, }); Console.WriteLine($"{result.Width} × {result.Height}"); Make a favicon // A favicon: 16, 32 and 48 resized from one raster. A raster that is not square is centred on transparency. logo.Save("favicon.ico", new IcoWriterOptions { Sizes = IcoWriterOptions.FaviconSizes }); // Windows' set: 16 to 256, the 256 entry as PNG and the rest as 32-bit BMP, as Microsoft's guidance asks. logo.Save("app.ico", new IcoWriterOptions { Sizes = IcoWriterOptions.WindowsSizes, Filter = Egami.Operations.ResampleFilter.Lanczos3 }); // Hand-drawn small sizes: each raster is written at its own size; the 48 comes from the largest raster. using Raster<Rgba8> drawn16 = logo.Derive(ops => ops.Fit(16, 16)); Raster.SaveAll([logo, drawn16], "drawn.ico", new IcoWriterOptions { Sizes = [16, 48] }); FaviconSizes writes 16, 32 and 48; every browser and Windows read the file. See the ICO guide. Pick an icon size // Load gives the best entry: the largest, then the deepest. LoadAll gives every entry at its own size. using Raster best = Raster.Load("app.ico"); using RasterList entries = Raster.LoadAll("app.ico"); // MinimumSize picks the smallest entry at least that big, so a 32 × 32 toolbar icon decodes only the 32 × 32 entry. using Raster small = Raster.Load("app.ico", options: new ReaderOptions { MinimumSize = new Size(32, 32) }); List an icon's sizes // Probe reads only the directory: the sizes an icon holds, without decoding a pixel. RasterInfo info = Raster.Probe("app.ico"); Console.WriteLine($"{info.ImageCount} entries; Load gives {info.Width}×{info.Height}"); using Raster best = Raster.Load("app.ico"); foreach (IcoEntry entry in ((IcoDetails)best.Metadata.FormatDetails!).Entries) { Console.WriteLine($"{entry.Width}×{entry.Height}, {entry.BitsPerPixel} bits, {entry.Encoding}"); } Flatten a PSD to PNG and read its profile // Load gives the flattened image Photoshop stores after the layers, in the type that fits the file: Rgb8 here, Rgba16 for // a 16-bit file with transparency, Cmyk8 for CMYK. Save it as anything. using Raster flat = Raster.Load("layered.psd"); flat.Save("layered.png"); // The ICC profile, resolution, EXIF, XMP and IPTC are in the metadata as for every format. using Raster photo = Raster.Load("photo.psd"); ReadOnlyMemory<byte> icc = photo.Metadata.IccProfile; Resolution? dpi = photo.Metadata.Resolution; A file saved without Maximize Compatibility holds only a placeholder; PsdDetails.HasRealComposite says so. See the PSD guide. List a PSD's layers // Layer records come as metadata, bottom to top as the file lists them; their pixels are not loaded. using Raster image = Raster.Load("layered.psd"); foreach (PsdLayer layer in ((PsdDetails)image.Metadata.FormatDetails!).Layers) { if (layer.Kind == PsdLayerKind.GroupEnd) { continue; } string kind = layer.Kind == PsdLayerKind.Layer ? "layer" : "group"; Console.WriteLine($"{new string(' ', 2 * layer.Level)}{layer.Name} ({kind}, {layer.BlendModeKey}, opacity {layer.Opacity:P0}{(layer.IsVisible ? "" : ", hidden")})"); } Load any upload as sRGB // Load straight into sRGB: the same pixels as loading and then calling ConvertColor. using Raster web = Raster.Load(path, options: new ReaderOptions { ConvertColorTo = ColorProfile.Srgb }); Display P3 phone photos, Adobe RGB camera files and CMYK print JPEGs all come out as sRGB, converted through their own profiles while they decode; files with no color information are taken as sRGB and left alone.
