Show a CMYK print file on screen // A CMYK image becomes RGB through its profile (or the plain formula if it has none), as a new raster. using Raster<Cmyk8> print = Raster.Load<Cmyk8>(path); using Raster<Rgb8> screen = print.ConvertColor<Rgb8>(ColorProfile.Srgb, new ColorTransformOptions { Intent = RenderingIntent.RelativeColorimetric, BlackPointCompensation = true }); Show an HDR image on an SDR screen // HDR to SDR tone maps by default (BT.2390, source peak from the file's mDCV/cLLI, else 1,000 cd/m²). using Raster<Rgb8> web = hdr.ConvertColor<Rgb8>(ColorProfile.Srgb); // Or choose the curve and peak; Clip turns tone mapping off. using Raster<Rgb8> soft = hdr.ConvertColor<Rgb8>(ColorProfile.Srgb, new ColorTransformOptions { ToneMapping = ToneMapping.Reinhard, SourcePeakNits = 4000 }); // Linear HDR pixels (1.0 = reference white, 203 cd/m²) can be tone mapped in place. using Raster<RgbaF32> linear = hdr.ConvertColor<RgbaF32>(ColorProfile.LinearSrgb, new ColorTransformOptions { ToneMapping = ToneMapping.Clip }); linear.Apply(ops => ops.ToneMap(ToneMapping.Bt2390, sourcePeakNits: 1000)); Keyword and rate a photo using Raster photo = Raster.Load("sideways.jpg"); // The parsed view of the packet; it is null when the file has none, so start one. XmpData xmp = photo.Metadata.XmpData ??= new XmpData(); xmp.Keywords = [.. xmp.Keywords, "harbour"]; xmp.Rating = 5; // The edit is the packet now: Metadata.Xmp returns it and every format saves it. photo.Save("rated.png"); Lightroom, Bridge and Windows read the keywords and rating from XMP. For news and stock workflows, set the same keywords in IPTC too: using Raster photo = Raster.Load("sideways.jpg"); IptcData iptc = photo.Metadata.Iptc ?? new IptcData(); iptc.Headline = "Harbour at dawn"; iptc.Keywords = [.. iptc.Keywords, "harbour", "Bergen"]; // Any dataset by its key; Add appends to the repeatable ones. iptc.Set(IptcKey.City, "Bergen"); // Text that is not ASCII sets the coded character set (1:90) to UTF-8, so other programs read it right. iptc.Caption = "Fishing boats at Bryggen, Bergen — first light"; foreach (IptcEntry entry in iptc.Entries) { Console.WriteLine($"{entry.Key} {entry.AsString()}"); } // JPEG saves it in its Photoshop resource block (APP13), with the digest Photoshop and Lightroom check. photo.Metadata.Iptc = iptc; photo.Save("captioned.jpg"); Keep the thumbnail upright using Raster photo = Raster.Load("sideways.jpg"); // The thumbnail as stored, if the file has one; ReadThumbnail returns null otherwise. using (Raster<Rgb8>? stored = photo.Metadata.Exif?.ReadThumbnail()) { Console.WriteLine(stored is null ? "No thumbnail" : $"Thumbnail {stored.Width} x {stored.Height}"); } // Turning the image drops the thumbnail, which would show sideways; make a new one from the result. photo.Apply(ops => ops.AutoOrient()); photo.Metadata.Exif?.SetThumbnail(photo); photo.Save("upright.jpg"); Draw into a premultiplied BGRA surface // A Windows or GPU surface is premultiplied BGRA: wrap its memory as PremulBgra8 and draw into it directly. Drawing and // resizing run on the stored values, with no multiply and divide per pixel; conversions still take straight colors. using Raster<PremulBgra8> surface = Raster.Wrap<PremulBgra8>(surfaceMemory, 320, 240, byteStride: 320 * 4); using Raster<Rgba8> logo = Raster.Load<Rgba8>("duck.png"); logo.Apply(ops => ops.Fit(120, 120)); surface.Apply(ops => ops.FillColor(new Rgba8(30, 60, 90, 255)).DrawImage(logo, new Point(20, 20), opacity: 0.8f)); Fill a 16-bit display framebuffer // A 16-bit display framebuffer: wrap it as Bgr565 and draw a photo into it; each level rounds to the nearest of 32 or 64. using Raster<Bgr565> screen = Raster.Wrap<Bgr565>(MemoryMarshal.Cast<ushort, Bgr565>(framebuffer.AsSpan()).ToArray(), 240, 135); using Raster<Rgba8> photo = Raster.Load<Rgba8>("egret.png"); photo.Apply(ops => ops.Cover(240, 135)); screen.Apply(ops => ops.DrawImage(photo, new Point(0, 0))); Bgr565 pixel = screen.Row(60)[120]; Console.WriteLine($"Levels: red {pixel.R} of 31, green {pixel.G} of 63, blue {pixel.B} of 31"); Draw a rounded badge // A rounded badge with an outline and a dot, drawn at twice the size for a sharp result on high-density screens. using Raster<Rgba8> badge = Raster.Create<Rgba8>(240, 80); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = badge.CreateCanvas()) { canvas.Scale(2); RoundRect pill = new(new RectF(2, 2, 116, 36), 18); canvas.FillRoundRect(pill, new Rgba8(46, 160, 67, 255)); canvas.StrokeRoundRect(pill, new Stroke(2), new Rgba8(20, 100, 40, 255)); canvas.FillCircle(new Vector2(22, 20), 7, Rgba8.White); } Drawing at twice the size through Scale(2) keeps every shape's coordinates as designed. See Drawing. Draw chart axes // Axes, ticks and a data line for a chart: hairlines stay one pixel wide whatever the scale. double[] values = [3, 7, 4, 9, 6, 11, 8]; using Raster<Rgba8> chart = Raster.Create(420, 260, Rgba8.White); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = chart.CreateCanvas()) { Rgba8 axis = new(60, 60, 60, 255); canvas.DrawLine(new Vector2(40.5f, 20), new Vector2(40.5f, 230.5f), Stroke.Hairline, axis); canvas.DrawLine(new Vector2(40, 230.5f), new Vector2(400, 230.5f), Stroke.Hairline, axis); for (int i = 0; i < values.Length; i++) { float x = 40.5f + (i * 55); canvas.DrawLine(new Vector2(x, 230), new Vector2(x, 236), Stroke.Hairline, axis); } Vector2[] points = [.. values.Select((v, i) => new Vector2(40 + (i * 55), 230 - (float)(v * 18)))]; canvas.DrawPoints(PointMode.Polygon, points, new Stroke(3) { Join = LineJoin.Round, Cap = LineCap.Round }, new Rgba8(30, 90, 200, 255)); canvas.DrawPoints(PointMode.Points, points, new Stroke(8) { Cap = LineCap.Round }, new Rgba8(30, 90, 200, 255)); } Hairlines on half-pixel coordinates fill exactly one column or row of pixels. Clip a photo to a circle // A round avatar: clip to a circle, draw the photo scaled to fill it, then ring it. using Raster photo = Raster.Load("duck.png"); using Raster<Rgba8> avatar = Raster.Create<Rgba8>(256, 256); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = avatar.CreateCanvas()) { Path circle = Path.Circle(new Vector2(128, 128), 120); canvas.Save(); canvas.ClipPath(circle); int side = Math.Min(photo.Width, photo.Height); RectF square = new((photo.Width - side) / 2, (photo.Height - side) / 2, side, side); canvas.DrawImage(photo, square, new RectF(8, 8, 240, 240)); canvas.Restore(); canvas.StrokePath(circle, new Stroke(6), Rgba8.White); } avatar.Save("avatar.png"); Cut a frame out of a shape // A frame: one round rectangle cut out of another, kept as curves, so a PDF or SVG backend writes it exactly. Path frame = Path.RoundRect(new RoundRect(new RectF(0, 0, 200, 140), 24)) .Difference(Path.RoundRect(new RoundRect(new RectF(20, 20, 160, 100), 12))); // Many shapes in one pass, applied left to right; overlaps and self-intersections removed; an area grown by 4 units. Path dots = Path.Combine([Path.Circle(new Vector2(40, 40), 30), Path.Circle(new Vector2(80, 40), 30), Path.Circle(new Vector2(60, 75), 30)], PathOp.Union); Path clean = Path.Star(new Vector2(50, 50), 45, 20, 5).Simplify(); Path halo = dots.Inflate(4, LineJoin.Round); Boolean operations keep curves, so the frame exports to PDF or SVG exactly. See Path geometry. Draw a dashed route // A dashed route: the pattern travels with the stroke, so a PDF backend writes [8 4] 0 d instead of hundreds of pieces. Path route = new PathBuilder().MoveTo(10, 90).CubicTo(60, 0, 140, 160, 190, 60).ToPath(); Stroke dashed = new(3) { Cap = LineCap.Round, Dash = new DashPattern([8, 4]) }; using Raster<Rgba8> map = Raster.Create(200, 120, Rgba8.White); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = map.CreateCanvas()) { canvas.StrokePath(route, dashed, new Rgba8(200, 60, 30, 255)); } // The outline the stroke fills, as a path: for hit testing, or to export without strokes. Path outline = dashed.ToPath(route, simplify: true); Animate a line drawing itself // Frames of a signature drawing itself: each frame strokes a longer part of the path. Path signature = Path.ParseSvg("M10 60 C30 10 50 110 70 60 S110 10 130 60 S170 110 190 40"); List<Raster<Rgba8>> frames = []; for (int i = 1; i <= 24; i++) { Raster<Rgba8> frame = Raster.Create(200, 100, Rgba8.White); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = frame.CreateCanvas()) { Stroke pen = new(3) { Cap = LineCap.Round, Effect = PathEffect.Trim(0, i / 24f) }; canvas.StrokePath(signature, pen, new Rgba8(20, 40, 120, 255)); } frames.Add(frame); } PathEffect.Trim keeps a fraction of the path's length; stepping it from 0 to 1 gives the frames. Draw an SVG icon // An icon from SVG path data, drawn four times larger, and written back as compact relative data. Path heart = Path.ParseSvg("M12 21.35l-1.45-1.32C5.4 15.36 2 12.28 2 8.5 2 5.42 4.42 3 7.5 3c1.74 0 3.41.81 4.5 2.09" + "C13.09 3.81 14.76 3 16.5 3 19.58 3 22 5.42 22 8.5c0 3.78-3.4 6.86-8.55 11.54L12 21.35z"); string d = heart.Transform(Matrix3x2.CreateScale(4)).ToSvg(new SvgPathFormat { Relative = true, Compact = true }); // Untrusted data: TryParseSvg says whether it is valid; lenient keeps what comes before an error, as browsers draw it. bool valid = Path.TryParseSvg("M0 0 L10 10 L20", out Path? strict); Path drawn = Path.ParseSvg("M0 0 L10 10 L20", lenient: true); try { Path.ParseSvg("M0 0 X"); } catch (SvgPathException e) { Console.WriteLine($"{e.Problem} at character {e.Position}"); } Render an SVG to PNG // An SVG drawn 256 pixels wide and saved as PNG; the height keeps the aspect ratio. SvgDocument document = SvgDocument.Load(input); using Raster<Rgba8> raster = document.Rasterize<Rgba8>(new SvgRenderOptions { Width = 256 }); raster.Save(output); Egami.Svg draws as resvg does where SVG leaves a choice; see SVG. Recolor an SVG icon // Every fill and stroke of a one-color icon set to a brand color, then drawn: edits redraw at once. SvgDocument icon = SvgDocument.Parse(Icon); foreach (SvgElement element in icon.Root.Descendants()) { foreach (string paint in (string[])["fill", "stroke"]) { if (element.Attributes[paint] is string value && value != "none") { element.Attributes[paint] = "#7b2ff7"; } } } using Raster<Rgba8> branded = icon.Rasterize<Rgba8>(new SvgRenderOptions { Width = 64 }); Draw icons from an SVG sprite sheet // Each symbol of a sprite sheet drawn into its own 32-pixel cell of a toolbar strip. SvgDocument sheet = SvgDocument.Parse(Sheet); string[] icons = ["plus", "dot", "plus"]; using Raster<Rgba8> strip = Raster.Create<Rgba8>(32 * icons.Length, 32); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = strip.CreateCanvas()) { for (int i = 0; i < icons.Length; i++) { sheet.Draw(canvas, icons[i], new RectF(32 * i, 0, 32, 32)); } } A symbol's viewBox fits it into each cell; the same calls draw on a PDF page. Label an SVG with your own fonts // A server passes its own fonts and turns the machine's off, so text renders the same everywhere. Egami.Fonts.FontCollection fonts = new(); fonts.AddFile(System.IO.Path.Combine(folder, "NotoSans-Regular.ttf")); SvgLoadOptions options = new() { Fonts = new SvgFontOptions { Collection = fonts, UseSystemFonts = false, DefaultFamily = "Noto Sans" }, }; SvgDocument label = SvgDocument.Parse( "<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' width='120' height='40'><text x='60' y='26' text-anchor='middle'>Label</text></svg>", options); using Raster<Rgba8> raster = label.Rasterize<Rgba8>(new SvgRenderOptions { TextAsPaths = false }); With system fonts off, the label looks the same on every machine. Flow SVG text into a shape // SVG 2 text that wraps: inside a circle (as Inkscape writes flowed text), or in lines 160 units long. SvgDocument card = SvgDocument.Parse(""" <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="400" height="200" font-family="Noto Sans" font-size="14"> <circle id="area" cx="100" cy="100" r="90" fill="#eef"/> <text style="shape-inside: url(#area); shape-padding: 6px; text-align: center"> Text flows into the circle line by line, each line as wide as the circle is at that height. </text> <text x="220" y="40" style="inline-size: 160px">Wrapped at 160 units, as a paragraph fills a column.</text> </svg> """, options); using Raster<Rgba8> raster = card.Rasterize<Rgba8>(); Render an EMF or WMF to PNG // WMF, EMF and EMF+ alike, and the gzip forms WMZ and EMZ. Metafile chart = Metafile.Load(path); Console.WriteLine($"{chart.Kind}, {chart.Size.X} by {chart.Size.Y} points"); // At twice the screen's resolution, over white; text uses the installed fonts. using Raster<Rgba8> image = chart.Rasterize<Rgba8>(new MetafileRenderOptions { Dpi = 192, Background = new RgbaF32(1, 1, 1, 1), }); image.Save(output); Egami.Metafiles plays the records as Windows does (GDI for WMF and EMF, GDI+ for EMF+), in managed code on any OS. Draw a Word or Excel picture onto a page Metafile picture = Metafile.Load(path); // The frame is stretched to the box, as Word stretches a picture to its frame. The same calls draw on a PDF page. using Raster<Rgba8> page = Raster.Create<Rgba8>(400, 300); using RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = page.CreateCanvas(); canvas.Clear(new RgbaF32(1, 1, 1, 1)); picture.Draw(canvas, new RectF(50, 50, 300, 200)); Load metafiles with Raster.Load // Register the format once; Raster.Load then draws metafiles at their own size at 96 DPI. EgamiContext context = EgamiContext.Default.WithFormat(MetafileFormat.Info); using Raster raster = Raster.Load(path, context); RasterInfo info = Raster.Probe(path, context); // the size from the header, nothing drawn // MetafileDecodeOptions sets the resolution; Raster.Load then draws at that DPI. using Raster sharp = Raster.Load(path, context, new MetafileDecodeOptions { Dpi = 300 }); Metafiles that name fonts you do not have // Faces the machine lacks: the built-in table maps Calibri to Carlito, Arial to Liberation Sans and so on; add your own. Metafile picture = Metafile.Load(path); using Raster<Rgba8> image = picture.Rasterize<Rgba8>(new MetafileRenderOptions { FontSubstitutions = new Dictionary<string, string> { ["Segoe UI"] = "Noto Sans" }, Antialias = false, // GDI's own aliased look, for comparing with Windows }); Each glyph still goes where the file put it, so lines keep their length in a substitute face. Paint a dusk sky // A dusk sky: stops in Oklch so the hues turn smoothly, dithered so the wide soft ramp shows no bands, and a sun. using Raster<Rgba8> sky = Raster.Create<Rgba8>(800, 450); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = sky.CreateCanvas()) { canvas.DrawPaint(new LinearGradient( new Vector2(0, 0), new Vector2(0, 450), new GradientStop(0, new Rgba8(20, 30, 90, 255)), new GradientStop(0.6f, new Rgba8(220, 110, 120, 255)), new GradientStop(1, new Rgba8(255, 200, 120, 255))) { Interpolation = GradientInterpolation.Oklch(), Dither = true, }); canvas.FillCircle(new Vector2(560, 380), 160, new RadialGradient(new Vector2(560, 380), 160, new RgbaF32(1, 0.95f, 0.8f, 0.9f), new RgbaF32(1, 0.8f, 0.5f, 0))); } sky.Save("sky.png"); Mixing in Oklch keeps the hues from turning gray between stops, and Dither hides the bands of a wide soft ramp. See Gradients. Draw a card with a shadow // A UI card: a Material-style shadow from its elevation, the card, and a soft inner highlight along its top edge. using Raster<Rgba8> screen = Raster.Create(400, 260, new Rgba8(236, 239, 244, 255)); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = screen.CreateCanvas()) { RoundRect card = new(new RectF(50, 40, 300, 170), 14); canvas.DrawShadow(Path.RoundRect(card), new ShadowOptions { Elevation = 16 }); canvas.FillRoundRect(card, Rgba8.White); canvas.Save(); canvas.ClipRoundRect(card); canvas.FillRect(new RectF(50, 40, 300, 30), new LinearGradient(new Vector2(0, 40), new Vector2(0, 70), new RgbaF32(0.85f, 0.9f, 1, 1), new RgbaF32(1, 1, 1, 1))); canvas.Restore(); } screen.Save("card.png"); Fade a photo's edges // A photo whose edges fade to transparent: an alpha soft mask of a radial gradient, opaque in the middle. using Raster photo = Raster.Load("duck.png"); using Raster<Rgba8> faded = Raster.Create<Rgba8>(photo.Width, photo.Height); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = faded.CreateCanvas()) { Vector2 center = new(photo.Width / 2f, photo.Height / 2f); float radius = MathF.Min(photo.Width, photo.Height) / 2f; SoftMask vignette = new( mask => mask.DrawPaint(new RadialGradient(center, radius, new GradientStop(0.6f, Rgba8.Black), new GradientStop(1, new Rgba8(0, 0, 0, 0)))), SoftMaskKind.Alpha); canvas.SaveLayer(new LayerOptions { Mask = vignette }); canvas.DrawImage(photo, Vector2.Zero); canvas.Restore(); } faded.Save("faded.png"); Fade a group as one // A translucent logo made of overlapping parts: drawn in a layer at 60%, the overlaps do not show through. using Raster<Rgba8> banner = Raster.Create(300, 120, new Rgba8(30, 40, 60, 255)); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = banner.CreateCanvas()) { canvas.SaveLayer(0.6f); canvas.FillCircle(new Vector2(60, 60), 40, new Rgba8(255, 200, 0, 255)); canvas.FillRoundRect(new RoundRect(new RectF(60, 40, 200, 40), 20), new Rgba8(255, 200, 0, 255)); canvas.Restore(); } banner.Save("banner.png"); See Layers. Stretch a button image to any size // One small button image serves every size: corners stay round, the label sits on the stretched center. using Raster<Rgba8> button = Raster.Create<Rgba8>(200, 48); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = button.CreateCanvas()) { canvas.DrawImageNinePatch(skin, new Rect(12, 12, 6, 6), new RectF(0, 0, 200, 48), new SamplingOptions { Filter = ResampleFilter.Bilinear }); } The corners keep their size and the edges and center stretch. An Android .9.png carries its own lattice: see Nine-patches and lattices. Draw a particle field // Pack the sprites once, then draw thousands of them in one call: each with its own place, turn, scale and tint. using SpriteSheet sheet = SpriteSheet.Pack([spark, star], new SpritePackOptions { Padding = 1 }); Random random = new(7); SpriteTransform[] transforms = new SpriteTransform[2000]; RectF[] sources = new RectF[transforms.Length]; RgbaF32[] tints = new RgbaF32[transforms.Length]; for (int i = 0; i < transforms.Length; i++) { Rect frame = sheet.Frames[i % 2]; sources[i] = frame; transforms[i] = SpriteTransform.FromRotationScale( scale: 0.3f + random.NextSingle(), degrees: random.NextSingle() * 360, position: new Vector2(random.NextSingle() * 320, random.NextSingle() * 200), anchor: new Vector2(frame.Width / 2f, frame.Height / 2f)); tints[i] = new RgbaF32(1, 0.5f + (random.NextSingle() / 2), random.NextSingle(), 0.8f); } using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = raster.CreateCanvas()) { // Plus adds the sprites up, as light does. canvas.DrawAtlas(sheet.Image, transforms, sources, tints, BlendMode.Modulate, paint: new SolidPaint(Rgba8.White) { BlendMode = BlendMode.Plus }); } Shade a gradient mesh // A gradient mesh, as an illustration app draws one: a 3×3 grid of colored points, smoothly shaded. Vector2[] grid = new Vector2[16]; RgbaF32[] colors = new RgbaF32[16]; for (int j = 0; j < 4; j++) { for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) { grid[(j * 4) + i] = new Vector2(i * 60, j * 40) + new Vector2(MathF.Sin(j) * 8, MathF.Cos(i) * 6); colors[(j * 4) + i] = new RgbaF32(i / 3f, 0.3f + (j * 0.2f), 1 - (i / 3f), 1); } } int[] indices = [.. Enumerable.Range(0, 9).SelectMany(k => new[] { k + (k / 3), k + (k / 3) + 1, k + (k / 3) + 5, k + (k / 3), k + (k / 3) + 5, k + (k / 3) + 4 })]; using Raster<Rgba8> mesh = Raster.Create(200, 140, Rgba8.White); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = mesh.CreateCanvas()) { canvas.Translate(10, 10); canvas.DrawMesh(new Mesh(MeshMode.Triangles, grid, colors, indices: indices), Rgba8.White); } See Meshes and patches. Reuse a logo at any size // Record any picture code once... PictureRecorder recorder = new(new RectF(0, 0, 40, 40)); DrawLogo(recorder); Picture logo = recorder.Finish(); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = raster.CreateCanvas()) { // ...and replay it anywhere, at any scale, still sharp: replay is vector. canvas.DrawPicture(logo, Matrix3x2.CreateTranslation(10, 10)); canvas.DrawPicture(logo, Matrix3x2.CreateScale(4) * Matrix3x2.CreateTranslation(60, 10)); // A paint with an opacity merges the whole picture as one layer. canvas.DrawPicture(logo, Matrix3x2.CreateTranslation(240, 10), new SolidPaint(Rgba8.White) { Opacity = 0.4f }); // Drawn many times at one scale, a cached image is cheaper than replaying. for (int i = 0; i < 6; i++) { canvas.DrawPicture(logo, Matrix3x2.CreateTranslation(230 + (i * 25), 150), cacheAsImage: true); } } using Raster<Rgba8> icon = logo.ToRaster<Rgba8>(scale: 2); The drawing is recorded once and replayed as vectors, so it is sharp at every size; cacheAsImage trades that for speed when it is drawn many times at one size. Watermark with Multiply // A dark logo that should read as printed on the photo: Multiply darkens by the logo's colors and never adds white. using Raster<Rgba8> logo = Raster.Create(120, 40, new Rgba8(40, 60, 120, 255)); photo.Apply(ops => ops.DrawImage(logo, new Point(photo.Width - 140, photo.Height - 60), BlendMode.Multiply, opacity: 0.6f), Ct); A dark logo drawn with Multiply reads as ink on the photo: light areas of the logo leave the photo unchanged. Tint a photo // Tint toward sepia-orange, keeping the shading: Color takes the tint's hue and saturation and the photo's luminosity. photo.Apply(ops => ops.BlendColor(new Rgba8(220, 150, 80, 255), BlendMode.Color, opacity: 0.5f), Ct); A basic tone panel // A basic tone panel: levels with a midtone lift, a gentle S-curve, and a warm tint in the midtones. The three steps run as // one pass over the pixels. raster.Apply(o => o .Level(black: 0.04f, white: 0.96f, gamma: 1.1f) .SigmoidalContrast(4, midpoint: 0.5f) .Tint(new Rgba8(255, 200, 150, 255), 0.15f), Ct); raster.Save("duck-toned.jpg"); Levels, an S-curve and a tint run as one pass over the pixels. A poster look, and how it reads with color blindness // A two-color poster, then a check of how it reads to someone with deuteranopia. raster.Apply(o => o.Duotone(Rgba8.FromHex("#1b2a49"), Rgba8.FromHex("#f2c14e")).Posterize(4, DitherMode.Ordered), Ct); using Raster<Rgba8> preview = raster.Derive(o => o.SimulateColorBlindness(ColorVisionDeficiency.Deuteranopia), Ct); // High contrast for low vision: gray, lightness inverted so dark becomes light, and more contrast. using Raster<Rgba8> readable = raster.Derive(o => o.HighContrast(grayscale: true, ContrastInvert.Lightness, contrast: 0.3f), Ct); Apply a .cube grade at 70%, and export curves as a .cube // Export a grade for DaVinci Resolve or Premiere, then load a .cube file and apply it at 70%. ColorFilter grade = ColorFilter.Curves(ToneCurve.FromPoints([(0, 0), (0.25f, 0.2f), (0.75f, 0.82f), (1, 1)])) .Then(ColorFilter.Saturation(1.1f)); CubeFile.Write("my-grade.cube", grade.ToLut3D(size: 33), title: "My grade"); Lut3D lut = CubeFile.Read("my-grade.cube"); raster.Apply(o => o.ApplyFilter(ColorFilter.Lerp(ColorFilter.Identity, ColorFilter.FromLut(lut), 0.7f)), Ct); // Tables can also be built from a function, and read at any color. Lut3D warm = Lut3D.FromFunction(c => new Vector3(c.X, c.Y * 0.97f, c.Z * 0.9f), size: 17); Vector3 gray = warm.Evaluate(new Vector3(0.5f), LutInterpolation.Tetrahedral); Grade in any editor through a Hald image // Export the identity Hald image, grade it in any editor, and load the graded image back as a table. using Raster<Rgba8> identity = Raster.HaldIdentity(level: 8); // 512 × 512, a 64³ table identity.Save("hald.png"); using Raster graded = Raster.Load("hald.png"); Lut3D fromHald = Lut3D.FromHald(graded); using Raster<Rgba16> back = fromHald.ToHald(level: 8); Fix a dull scan // Fix a dull scan: stretch it to the full range, clipping the darkest 2% and lightest 1%, then set the midtones. raster.Apply(o => o.Normalize().AutoGamma(), Ct); // Or stretch each channel on its own, which also removes a cast. raster.Apply(o => o.AutoLevel(linked: false), Ct); // Measured steps measure only their scope: here the sky alone is stretched. raster.Apply(o => o.Within(new Rect(0, 0, raster.Width, raster.Height / 3), sky => sky.AutoLevel()), Ct); White-balance a shoot from one reference // Measure once on a reference shot, then apply the same correction to the whole shoot. ColorFilter fix = reference.MeasureAutoLevel().Then(reference.MeasureWhiteBalance()); foreach (Raster<Rgba8> shot in shoot) { shot.Apply(o => o.ApplyFilter(fix), Ct); } // The other measured steps have their Measure helpers too. ColorFilter stretch = reference.MeasureContrastStretch(0.02f, 0.01f); ColorFilter midtones = reference.MeasureAutoGamma(); ColorFilter spread = reference.MeasureEqualize(); Threshold a page for OCR // Threshold a scanned page for OCR: Otsu's level for an evenly lit page, or Bradley's local threshold for uneven light. float level = page.FindThreshold(ThresholdMethod.Otsu); using Raster<Gray8> even = page.Derive(o => o.AutoThreshold(ThresholdMethod.Otsu), Ct); using Raster<Gray8> uneven = page.Derive(o => o.AdaptiveThreshold(limit: 0.15f), Ct); Bring out detail in a foggy landscape // Bring out detail in a flat, foggy landscape: CLAHE on 8 × 8 tiles, then ImageMagick's local contrast. raster.Apply(o => o.Clahe(tilesX: 8, tilesY: 8, clipLimit: 2).LocalContrast(radius: 0.1f, strength: 0.15f), Ct); Blend a row in a custom operation /// <summary>A custom step that screens a horizontal gradient over each row, blending with the Compositor.</summary> public sealed class ScreenGradient : IRasterOperation { public Size OutputSize(Size input) => input; public void Run<TPixel>(OperationInput<TPixel> input) where TPixel : unmanaged, IPixelType<TPixel> { int width = input.Destination.Width; TPixel[] gradient = new TPixel[width]; for (int x = 0; x < width; x++) { gradient[x] = TPixel.FromRgba8(new Rgba8(255, 220, 160, (byte)(255 * x / Math.Max(1, width - 1)))); } input.ForEachBand((start, end) => { for (int y = start; y < end; y++) { input.Source.Row(y).CopyTo(input.Destination.Row(y)); Compositor.Blend<TPixel>(BlendMode.Screen, gradient, input.Destination.Row(y)); } }); } } Compositor.Blend works on any pixel type, so one custom step serves every raster. Blur a face // Blur a face: only pixels inside the rectangle change, and the blur reads the real pixels around it, so there is no seam. photo.Apply(ops => ops .Within(new Rect(200, 120, 160, 120), o => o.Blur(6)) .Within(new Rect(0, 0, photo.Width, 60), o => o.Brightness(0.8f).Saturation(0.5f)), Ct); // a darker band on top The blur reads the real pixels around the rectangle, so its edge has no seam. Add film grain // Film grain: gray Gaussian noise at a third of ImageMagick's default strength; the same seed gives the same grain. photo.Apply(ops => ops.AddNoise(NoiseKind.Gaussian, 0.3f, monochrome: true, seed: 42), Ct); The grain depends only on the seed and the pixel's position, so a batch of frames with the same seed grains alike. Blur the background like a lens // Blur the background like a wide-open lens with a six-blade aperture: bright points become hexagons. LensBlurOptions lens = new() { Blades = 6, Rotation = 15, HighlightGain = 4, HighlightThreshold = 0.8f }; photo.Apply(ops => ops.Within(new Rect(0, 0, photo.Width, photo.Height / 3), o => o.LensBlur(12, lens)), Ct); LensBlur works in linear light, so bright points stay bright discs instead of gray smudges; Within with a mask feathers the edge between the sharp subject and the blurred background. Clean a scan // Clean a scan: specks shrink, edges and text stay. Median(1) is the stronger alternative. scan.Apply(ops => ops.Despeckle(), Ct); For heavy salt-and-pepper noise use Median(1) or Median(2) instead; both keep edges, and both give ImageMagick's pixels. Find edges using Raster edges = photo.Derive(o => o.Edges(), Ct); // Sobel, gray, 0 to 1 using Raster crisp = photo.Derive(o => o.Edges(EdgeOperator.Scharr), Ct); // rotation-steady using Raster colored = photo.Derive(o => o.Edges(EdgeOperator.Sobel, grayscale: false), Ct); // per channel using Raster lines = photo.Derive(o => o.Blur(1).Edges(EdgeOperator.Laplacian3x3), Ct); // second derivative See Edges and morphology for the nine operators. A selection from Canny // Thin white edges on black. A gray raster works as a Mask as it is; an RGBA one needs MaskChannel.Luminance, // because a Mask of a raster with alpha reads its alpha. using Raster<Gray8> edges = Raster.Load<Gray8>("duck.png"); edges.Apply(o => o.CannyEdges(sigma: 1.4f).Dilate(1), Ct); // thin edges, thickened photo.Apply(o => o.Within(new Mask(edges), s => s.FillColor(Rgba8.Red)), Ct); // paint over them Canny's white-on-black map works directly as a Mask; thicken it with Dilate first to catch the pixels beside each edge. Clean a scanned form with Close // Close removes dark specks smaller than the shape (dust and toner dots on the paper) and keeps strokes wider than it; // Open does the opposite, for light pinholes in dark areas. using Raster<Gray8> scan = Raster.Load<Gray8>("scan.tif"); scan.Apply(o => o.Morphology(MorphologyOp.Close, StructuringElement.Disk(1)), Ct); // The outlines of shapes, and the light details smaller than a disk. using Raster outlines = scan.Derive(o => o.Morphology(MorphologyOp.Gradient, StructuringElement.Square(1)), Ct); using Raster details = scan.Derive(o => o.Morphology(MorphologyOp.TopHat, StructuringElement.Disk(5)), Ct); A bevelled logo // A logo on a transparent canvas: alpha is the height, so soften its edges first to give them a slope. logo.Apply(ops => ops .Blur(2.5f) .Lighting(new DistantLight(225, 35), LightingModel.Diffuse(1.4f), new LightingOptions { SurfaceScale = 5, Blend = BlendMode.Multiply }) // shade the slopes .Lighting(new DistantLight(225, 35), LightingModel.Specular(0.8f, 24), new LightingOptions { SurfaceScale = 5, Blend = BlendMode.Screen }), Ct); // and add a highlight logo.Save("bevel.png"); Embossed text // Gray relief: flat paper becomes mid gray, strokes rise toward the light at the top left. using Raster embossed = page.Derive(ops => ops.Emboss(angle: 135, depth: 3, sigma: 1), Ct); // Each color channel on its own, softer and deeper. using Raster colored = page.Derive(ops => ops.Emboss(angle: 45, depth: 6, sigma: 2, grayscale: false), Ct); A variable weight slider // A weight slider: each move draws the sample at the new weight. Faces at a position share the font's memory and are // cached, and glyph masks are cached per position, so dragging back and forth is cheap. Raster<Rgba8> Preview(float weight) { VariationAxis axis = flex.VariationAxes.First(a => a.Tag == new FontTag("wght")); Typeface face = flex.WithVariations(FontVariation.Weight(Math.Clamp(weight, axis.Min, axis.Max))); var font = new Font(face, 28); TextMeasure size = font.MeasureText("Weight"); Raster<Rgba8> preview = Raster.Create((int)MathF.Ceiling(size.Advance) + 16, (int)MathF.Ceiling(size.Height) + 8, Rgba8.White); using RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = preview.CreateCanvas(); canvas.DrawText("Weight", new Vector2(8, 4 + size.Ascent), font, Rgba8.Black); return preview; } Emoji in a caption // A caption mixing words and emoji: the emoji fall back to the color face, cluster by cluster, so a ZWJ sequence or a flag // stays whole; one call shapes and draws every run. string caption = "Launch day \U0001F680 thanks, team \U0001F389"; var fallback = new FontCollection(); fallback.Add(emoji); var options = new Egami.Fonts.Shaping.ShapingOptions { Fallback = new Egami.Fonts.Shaping.FontFallback(fallback.Families) }; using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = image.CreateCanvas()) { canvas.DrawText(caption, new Vector2(8, 32), new Font(text, 20), Rgba8.Black, options); } Color glyphs draw in color on every canvas; on a raster they are cached as images, like other glyphs. A cluster with emoji presentation prefers a color face from the fallback list; text presentation (VS15) prefers an outline face. An Arabic caption // An Arabic caption, right-aligned: the shaper joins the letters and puts the words in right-to-left order, and the measured // advance places the line's right end at the margin. using Raster<Rgba8> photo = Raster.Create(640, 120, new Rgba8(40, 60, 80, 255)); var font = new Font(arabic, 32); string caption = "\u0645\u0631\u062D\u0628\u0627\u0020\u0628\u0627\u0644\u0639\u0627\u0644\u0645"; float width = font.MeasureText(caption).Advance; using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = photo.CreateCanvas()) { canvas.DrawText(caption, new Vector2(photo.Width - 24 - width, 80), font, Rgba8.White); } The shaper picks each letter's joining form and the bidi algorithm orders the words; the origin is still the line's left end, so right alignment subtracts the measured advance. A Hindi label with fallback // A label in Hindi and English with a Latin font: Devanagari clusters (conjuncts, vowel signs, the reph) fall back whole to // the Devanagari face, and the Indic shaper reorders them. var families = new FontCollection(); families.Add(devanagari); var options = new Egami.Fonts.Shaping.ShapingOptions { Language = "hi", Fallback = new Egami.Fonts.Shaping.FontFallback(families.Families), }; using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = image.CreateCanvas()) { canvas.DrawText("Price: \u0915\u0940\u092E\u0924\u0020\u0915\u094D\u0937\u0947\u0924\u094D\u0930", new Vector2(10, 40), new Font(latin, 22), Rgba8.Black, options); } Fallback works on whole grapheme clusters, so a conjunct never splits across two faces. FontFallback.System would find an installed Devanagari face instead, at the cost of output that depends on the machine. Searchable text in a PDF // What a PDF writer needs to keep shaped text searchable: each glyph's cluster points back into the text. A glyph that // stands for several characters (the "ffi" ligature) maps to all of them in ToUnicode; a cluster whose glyphs were // reordered or merged (Indic, Arabic marks) goes in an ActualText span instead. GlyphRun run = new Font(face, 11).Shape("office hours"); var toUnicode = new Dictionary<ushort, string>(); for (int i = 0; i < run.Count; i++) { int start = run.Clusters[i]; int end = i + 1 < run.Count ? run.Clusters[i + 1] : run.Text!.Length; if (end > start) { toUnicode.TryAdd(run.Glyphs[i], run.Text![start..end]); } } A GlyphRun from the shaper carries the text and a cluster per glyph, in visual order; that is all a PDF writer needs for ToUnicode and ActualText. A caption in a box // A caption wrapped into the bottom of a photo, centred, on a translucent band as tall as the lines. RectF box = new(20, 200, 360, 80); ParagraphStyle style = new() { DefaultStyle = new TextStyle { FontFamilies = [family], Size = 15, Color = Rgba8.White }, Align = TextAlign.Center, MaxLines = 3, }; TextLayout layout = Paragraph.Create("Harbour at dawn, seen from the old lighthouse; the fishing boats leave before the ferries.", style).Layout(box.Width); float top = box.Y + box.Height - layout.Height; canvas.FillRect(new RectF(box.X - 8, top - 6, box.Width + 16, layout.Height + 12), new SolidPaint(new Rgba8(0, 0, 0, 140))); canvas.DrawTextLayout(layout, new System.Numerics.Vector2(box.X, top)); The layout's height is known before drawing, so the band behind the text fits the lines exactly; MaxLines stops a long caption from climbing up the photo. A justified article column // A justified column: each paragraph balanced, indented by its first line, with space between paragraphs. ParagraphStyle style = new() { DefaultStyle = new TextStyle { FontFamilies = [family], Size = 13, LineHeight = LineHeight.Multiple(1.4f) }, Align = TextAlign.Justify, LineFill = LineFill.Balanced, }; float y = 10; foreach (string text in paragraphs) { TextLayout layout = Paragraph.Create(text, style).Layout(260); canvas.DrawTextLayout(layout, new System.Numerics.Vector2(20, y)); y += layout.Height + 8; } Balanced filling evens out line lengths, so justified lines stretch less; soft hyphens break long words only where a line needs them. A chat bubble with an emoji // A chat bubble: at most two lines, cut with an ellipsis; the bubble shrinks to the longest line, so short messages get // short bubbles. Emoji come from the second family, character by character. ParagraphStyle style = new() { DefaultStyle = new TextStyle { FontFamilies = [text, emoji], Size = 15, Color = Rgba8.White }, MaxLines = 2, }; TextLayout message = Paragraph.Create("See you at the caf\u00E9 at eight? I will bring the maps, the snacks and the long list of places we still have not seen \U0001F389", style).Layout(240); RoundRect bubble = new(new RectF(12, 12, message.LongestLine + 24, message.Height + 16), 14); canvas.FillRoundRect(bubble, new SolidPaint(new Rgba8(0, 120, 255, 255))); canvas.DrawTextLayout(message, new System.Numerics.Vector2(24, 20)); bool cut = message.DidExceed; // true: offer "show more" LongestLine is the width the lines actually use, which is what a bubble should wrap; DidExceed and HiddenRange say what the ellipsis cut. Japanese vertical text // Japanese set vertically, columns right to left: the width given to Layout is the column height, and DrawText into a // rectangle puts the first column at its right edge. ParagraphStyle style = new() { DefaultStyle = new TextStyle { FontFamilies = [family], Size = 18, Language = "ja" }, WritingMode = WritingMode.VerticalRl, LineBreaking = new LineBreakOptions(Strictness: LineBreakStrictness.Strict), }; TextLayout layout = canvas.DrawText("\u8AF8\u56FD\u9593\u306E\u53CB\u597D\u95A2\u4FC2\u306E\u767A\u5C55\u3092\u4FC3\u9032\u3059\u308B\u3053\u3068\u304C\u809D\u8981\u3067\u3042\u308B\u306E\u3067\u3001\u56FD\u969B\u9023\u5408\u306E\u8AF8\u56FD\u6C11\u306F\u3001\u56FD\u9023\u61B2\u7AE0\u306B\u304A\u3044\u3066\u3001\u57FA\u672C\u7684\u4EBA\u6A29\u3001\u4EBA\u9593\u306E\u5C0A\u53B3\u53CA\u3073\u4FA1\u5024\u4E26\u3073\u306B\u7537\u5973\u306E\u540C\u6A29\u306B\u3064\u3044\u3066\u306E\u4FE1\u5FF5\u3092\u518D\u78BA\u8A8D\u3057", new RectF(10, 10, 220, 300), style); Kana and kanji stand upright and Latin turns sideways, as TextOrientation.Mixed says; hit tests, carets and selections work along the columns. Text flowing across two columns // One article flowed down two columns of a page: LineFlow hands out one line at a time at the width asked for, so the // first column can be narrowed beside a picture and the rest carries on in the second. On Egap's PDF canvas the same // calls write searchable text. ParagraphStyle style = new() { DefaultStyle = new TextStyle { FontFamilies = [family], Size = 10 }, Align = TextAlign.Justify }; LineFlow flow = Paragraph.Create(article, style).CreateFlow(); (float X, float Top, float Bottom)[] columns = [(40, 60, 300), (310, 60, 300)]; foreach ((float x, float top, float bottom) in columns) { float y = top; while (!flow.IsComplete) { float width = x == 40 && y < 160 ? 150 : 245; // beside a picture at the top of column one TextLine line = flow.NextLine(width)!; if (y + line.Height > bottom) { flow.Rewind(line.Start); // that line goes to the next column break; } foreach (LayoutRun run in line.Runs) { if (run.Glyphs is { Count: > 0 } glyphs) { page.DrawGlyphRun(glyphs, new System.Numerics.Vector2(x, y), new SolidPaint(Rgba8.Black)); } } y += line.Height; } } Each line's top is 0, so the caller places it; a line that does not fit goes back with Rewind and starts the next column. A label along a curve // A round badge: one label along the top of a circle and one along the bottom, both reading left to right and centred. // Each glyph sits on the curve at its midpoint, turned to the curve's direction, as SVG's textPath. var badge = new Font(face, 16); Path ring = new PathBuilder().AddOval(new RectF(20, 20, 160, 160)).ToPath(); Path top = new PathBuilder().MoveTo(40, 100).ArcTo(new Vector2(60, 60), 0, false, true, new Vector2(160, 100)).ToPath(); Path bottom = new PathBuilder().MoveTo(40, 100).ArcTo(new Vector2(60, 60), 0, false, false, new Vector2(160, 100)).ToPath(); var centred = new TextOnPathOptions { StartFraction = 0.5f, Anchor = TextAnchor.Center }; using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = image.CreateCanvas()) { canvas.StrokePath(ring, new Stroke(2), new SolidPaint(Rgba8.Black)); canvas.DrawTextOnPath("EGAMI QUALITY", top, badge, Rgba8.Black, centred); // Below, the glyphs hang under the curve: shift the baseline down by the cap height. canvas.DrawTextOnPath("since 2026", bottom, badge, Rgba8.Black, centred with { BaselineShift = -12 }); } A variable font in a PDF // PDF has no variable fonts: embed a static instance at the position the page uses. The subset is an ordinary TrueType // font (glyf and hmtx at that position, no variation tables); its whole-unit advances are the ones to write in /W. Typeface heading = flex.WithVariations(FontVariation.Weight(720), FontVariation.Width(85)); GlyphRun run = new Font(heading, 24).Shape("Annual report"); FontSubset subset = FontSubsetter.Subset(heading, run.Glyphs.ToArray(), new SubsetOptions { FontNamePrefix = "EGAMIA+" }); Typeface embedded = subset.ToTypeface(); var widths = new SortedDictionary<ushort, int>(); foreach (ushort glyph in run.Glyphs) { ushort id = subset.GlyphMap[glyph]; widths[id] = (int)MathF.Round(embedded.GetAdvance(id) * 1000 / embedded.UnitsPerEm); } byte[] fontFile2 = subset.Data.ToArray(); The subset of a variable face is always a static instance; SubsetOptions.Variations gives the position without making a face. A drop shadow for a logo // A logo on a page: a soft shadow under it, then the result flattened onto white for a JPEG. logo.Apply(ops => ops .DropShadow(5, 7, 6, new Rgba8(0, 0, 0, 110)) .Flatten(Rgba8.White), Ct); logo.Save("logo-shadow.jpg"); The canvas grows to hold the shadow; pass Expand = false to keep the size, as inside Within. Pixelate a face // Hide a face: pixelate only the rectangle around it, with the grid starting at its corner so cells line up with it. Rect face = new(100, 40, 72, 64); photo.Apply(ops => ops.Within(face, o => o.Pixelate(12, new Point(face.X, face.Y))), Ct); An oil-paint look // A painted look: a light blur to calm noise, the oil paint, then a touch more saturation and a vignette. using Raster painting = photo.Derive(ops => ops .Blur(0.8f) .OilPaint(radius: 4, levels: 24) .Saturation(1.15f) .Vignette(0.9f, softness: 0.6f), Ct); painting.Save("painting.png"); Edit only the sky // Edit only the sky: a gray mask, white where the edit applies fully, black where it does not, soft in between. photo.Apply(ops => ops .Within(new Mask(sky), o => o.Saturation(1.3f).Contrast(1.1f)) // Or take coverage from a logo's alpha, placed on the photo, and invert the area under it. .Within(new Mask(logo, new Point(20, 20), MaskChannel.Alpha), o => o.Invert()), Ct); A soft mask gives a soft transition; blur the mask raster first to feather a hard selection. Swap red and blue // Swap red and blue: one color matrix, fused with the other color steps into one pass. photo.Apply(ops => ops .ShuffleChannels(ChannelSource.Blue, ChannelSource.Green, ChannelSource.Red, ChannelSource.Alpha) .Brightness(1.05f), Ct); Alpha from a gray image using Raster alpha = photo.Derive(ops => ops.AlphaToGray(), Ct); // see the transparency as gray using Raster cutout = photo.Derive(ops => ops.CopyAlpha(new Mask(matte)), Ct); // a gray image becomes the alpha using Raster onWhite = cutout.Derive(ops => ops.Flatten(Rgba8.White), Ct); // composite onto white, opaque using Raster luma = photo.Derive(ops => ops.LuminanceToAlpha(), Ct); // brightness becomes alpha Remove a green screen // Remove a green screen: within 0.15 of pure green becomes transparent, and alpha ramps back over the next 0.1 for soft edges. photo.Apply(ops => ops.MakeTransparent(new Rgba8(0, 177, 64, 255), tolerance: 0.15f, softness: 0.1f), Ct); Raise the tolerance until the screen is gone, then add softness for clean hair and edges. Select by color, then edit // Select by color, then edit only the selection: a magic wand from a point, and every pixel close to a color. using Raster<Gray8> wand = photo.FloodMask(new Point(30, 30), tolerance: 0.12f); using Raster<Gray8> reds = photo.ColorMask(new Rgba8(200, 40, 30, 255), tolerance: 0.2f); photo.Apply(ops => ops .Within(new Mask(wand), o => o.Blur(4)) .Within(new Mask(reds), o => o.Saturation(1.4f)), Ct); Average a burst of photos // Average a burst of photos to smooth noise; the median removes things that appear in only a few frames. using Raster mean = Raster.Stack([first, second, third], StackMode.Mean); using Raster clean = Raster.Stack([first, second, third], StackMode.Median); Straighten a photographed document // The four corners of a page photographed at an angle, top-left first and clockwise... Vector2[] corners = [new(120, 60), new(560, 40), new(600, 430), new(80, 420)]; // ...go to the corners of an upright 420 × 594 (A4-shaped) canvas. Homography straighten = Homography.FromQuad(corners, new Rect(0, 0, 420, 594)); using Raster page = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Transform(straighten, new TransformOptions { Viewport = new Rect(0, 0, 420, 594) }), Ct); // Homography maps points too, and inverts. Vector2 middle = straighten.Map(new Vector2(340, 240)); bool invertible = straighten.TryInvert(out Homography back); Give the page's four corners in the photo, top-left first and clockwise; the perspective maps them onto an upright canvas. Skew a banner // Lean a banner 12° to the right, filling the uncovered corners with white; the canvas grows to fit. using Raster banner = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Skew(12, 0, new TransformOptions { Background = Rgba8.White }), Ct); // Skew a region in place: a viewport the size of the area keeps it the same size inside Within. using Raster region = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Within(new Rect(100, 100, 200, 120), s => s.Skew(0, 8, new TransformOptions { Viewport = new Rect(0, 0, 200, 120) })), Ct); Rotate a region in place // Turn a 200 × 200 square of the photo by 30° about its own center; the rest of the photo stays as it was. Rect area = new(380, 40, 200, 200); Matrix3x2 turn = Matrix3x2.CreateRotation(MathF.PI / 6, new Vector2(100, 100)); using Raster turned = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Within(area, s => s.Transform(turn, new TransformOptions { Viewport = new Rect(0, 0, 200, 200), Edges = EdgeMode.Clamp })), Ct); A viewport the size of the area keeps the size, so the transform runs inside Within. Correct a wide-angle lens, swirl a region // Correct a wide-angle lens with the PanoTools coefficients a lens database gives (ImageMagick's Barrel), then swirl a // square region in place; size-keeping warps run inside Within. using Raster corrected = photo.Derive(ops => ops .Warp(Warps.Barrel(0.0, -0.018, 0.0)) .Within(new Rect(300, 200, 200, 200), s => s.Warp(Warps.Swirl(90))), Ct); // Size-changing ones: wrap the image into a circle, or bend it into an arc. using Raster disc = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Warp(Warps.Polar(), new SamplingOptions { Background = Rgba8.White }), Ct); using Raster arc = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Warp(Warps.Arc(120)), Ct); // A magnifying glass over the duck's head, blending into the photo over 12 pixels. using Raster loupe = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Warp(Warps.Magnifier(new Rect(380, 60, 160, 160), 2.5f, 12)), Ct); Barrel takes the PanoTools coefficients a lens database such as lensfun gives for the camera and focal length. Ripple with a displacement map // A displacement map the image's size: mid-gray moves nothing, red moves pixels sideways and green up and down. using Raster<Rgba8> map = Raster.Create<Rgba8>(photo.Width, photo.Height); map.ForEachRow((row, y) => { for (int x = 0; x < row.Length; x++) { byte wave = (byte)(128 + (100 * Math.Sin((x + y) / 12.0))); row[x] = new Rgba8(wave, 128, 128, 255); } }); using Raster<Rgba8> rippled = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Displace(map, 16, 0), Ct); Check that a texture tiles seamlessly // Roll the image half way round, so its edges meet in the middle, which shows whether it tiles seamlessly. using Raster rolled = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Offset(photo.Width / 2, photo.Height / 2), Ct); // Fill a 1920 × 1080 wallpaper with copies of the duck's head. using Raster wallpaper = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Tile(1920, 1080, source: new Rect(380, 60, 160, 160)), Ct); Trim a scan // Cut away the white margin, counting near-white (within 10% by ImageMagick's -fuzz distance) as margin too. Rect content = scan.TrimBounds(tolerance: 0.1f); scan.Apply(ops => ops.Trim(tolerance: 0.1f).Fit(400, 400), Ct); Straighten a page // Measure the tilt first, if you want to show it or decide yourself... float tilt = photo.DetectSkew(maxAngle: 10); // ...or straighten in one step, keeping the page size with white corners. using Raster straight = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Deskew(background: Rgba8.White), Ct); A responsive image set from one mip chain // A responsive image set: one chain, then each width from the smallest level at least twice its size. using MipChain chain = MipChain.Build(photo); foreach (int width in (int[])[320, 240, 160, 120, 80]) { using Raster thumbnail = chain.Fit(width, width, ResampleFilter.Lanczos2); thumbnail.Save($"egret-{width}.png"); } A caption on a photo // A caption on a photo: white text with a dark shadow, its baseline 24 pixels above the bottom. using Raster<Rgba8> photo = Raster.Create(640, 360, new Rgba8(90, 120, 160, 255)); var font = new Font(Typeface.FromFile(FontFile), 28); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = photo.CreateCanvas()) { var origin = new Vector2(24, photo.Height - 24); canvas.DrawText("Lofoten, March", origin + new Vector2(2, 2), font, new Rgba8(0, 0, 0, 160)); canvas.DrawText("Lofoten, March", origin, font, Rgba8.White); } A label measured to fit // A label shrunk until it fits a 200-pixel button, then centred on it. const string label = "Download the full report"; var box = new RectF(20, 20, 200, 40); var font = new Font(face, 24); while (font.MeasureText(label).Advance > box.Width - 16 && font.Size > 8) { font = new Font(face, font.Size - 1); } TextMeasure size = font.MeasureText(label); var origin = new Vector2( box.X + ((box.Width - size.Advance) / 2), box.Y + ((box.Height - size.Height) / 2) + size.Ascent); using Raster<Rgba8> image = Raster.Create(240, 80, Rgba8.White); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = image.CreateCanvas()) { canvas.FillRoundRect(new RoundRect(box, 8), new Rgba8(30, 90, 200, 255)); canvas.DrawText(label, origin, font, Rgba8.White); } A font subset for a PDF // Keep only the glyphs a page uses, as a PDF writer embeds them: renumbered from 0, with the map to write the text with. GlyphRun run = new Font(face, 12).Shape("Invoice 2026-10"); FontSubset subset = FontSubsetter.Subset(face, run.Glyphs.ToArray(), new SubsetOptions { FontNamePrefix = "ABCDEF+", KeepCmap = false, }); byte[] fontFile2 = subset.Data.ToArray(); ushort first = subset.GlyphMap[run.Glyphs[0]]; // The face's embedding permissions are reported, never enforced: the writer decides. bool restricted = face.Embedding.HasFlag(FontEmbedding.Restricted); A contact sheet // A contact sheet three cells wide; each photo shrinks to fit a 200 × 200 cell and sits in its middle. using Raster sheet = Raster.Grid(photos, columns: 3, cell: new Size(200, 200), spacing: 8, background: Rgba8.White); A sprite sheet with its JSON // Pack sprites with a 2-pixel gap and 1 pixel of extruded edge, so GPU filtering never bleeds between them. using SpriteSheet sheet = SpriteSheet.Pack([small, tiny, small, tiny], new SpritePackOptions { Padding = 2, Extrude = 1, PowerOfTwo = true }); sheet.Image.Save("sprites.png"); // The rectangles are plain data: writing them for a game engine is one line of System.Text.Json. File.WriteAllText("sprites.json", JsonSerializer.Serialize(sheet.Frames.Select(f => new { f.X, f.Y, w = f.Width, h = f.Height }))); Split a multi-page scan into PNGs using RasterList pages = Raster.LoadAll("scan.tif"); for (int i = 0; i < pages.Count; i++) { pages[i].Save($"page-{i + 1}.png"); } Each page keeps its own size and pixel type; see TIFF. Combine pages into one TIFF using RasterList pages = Raster.LoadAll("scan.tif"); // Several rasters make a multi-page TIFF; one raster saves to any format. Raster.SaveAll(pages, "copy.tif"); Raster.SaveAll([pages[1]], "second.png"); Archive a black-and-white page as a fax // A page where every pixel is black or white saves as a 1-bit CCITT Group 4 fax. page.Save("fax.tif", new TiffWriterOptions { Compression = TiffCompression.CcittGroup4 }); Group 4 is the usual choice for scanned text; it takes 1-bit pages only, so threshold first or set Reduce. Strip metadata // Every writer's options have StripMetadata: the pixels are written, EXIF, XMP, ICC and text are not. image.Save("clean.jpg", new JpegWriterOptions { StripMetadata = true }); Read the size without decoding RasterInfo info = Raster.Probe("sideways.jpg"); bool sideways = info.Orientation is >= Egami.Metadata.ImageOrientation.Transpose; (int width, int height) = sideways ? (info.Height, info.Width) : (info.Width, info.Height); Console.WriteLine($"{info.Format.Name}, shown as {width} × {height}, about {info.EstimatedBytes:N0} bytes to load"); Probe reads only the header, and reports the EXIF orientation, so you know how the image will be shown. Interop with raw buffers // Pixels from somewhere else, such as a camera SDK: 640 × 480 BGRA, rows 2,560 bytes apart. byte[] buffer = new byte[2560 * 480]; // Wrap them without copying, work on them, and save. using (Raster<Bgra8> frame = Raster.Wrap<Bgra8>(buffer, 640, 480, byteStride: 2560)) { frame.Apply(ops => ops.FillColor(Rgba8.Black).Opacity(1)); frame.Save("frame.png"); } // Or copy the pixels out of a raster into your own buffer, row by row. using Raster<Rgba8> image = Raster.Load<Rgba8>("duck.png"); Rgba8[] pixels = new Rgba8[image.Width * image.Height]; for (int y = 0; y < image.Height; y++) { image.Row(y).CopyTo(pixels.AsSpan(y * image.Width, image.Width)); } Native AOT Egami is trimming- and AOT-clean: no reflection, no runtime code generation. Publish as usual: dotnet publish -c Release -r linux-x64 -p:PublishAot=true Egami's own build publishes a small console app this way on every change and checks that it runs with no warnings. Test renders against a baseline // A visual regression check: pass when the render is close to the stored baseline, else save a picture of what moved. CompareResult result = Raster.Compare(baseline, rendered, new CompareOptions { Fuzz = 0.05f }); if (result.DifferentPixels > 0 || result.Overall.Psnr < 45) { using Raster where = Raster.Difference(baseline, rendered, DifferenceStyle.Highlight, new DifferenceOptions { Fuzz = 0.05f }); where.Save("regression.png"); } Find near-duplicate photos // Find near-duplicate photos: hash each once, store the 64-bit keys, and call a pair a duplicate within about 10 bits. ulong a = PerceptualHash.Dct(original), b = PerceptualHash.Dct(copy), c = PerceptualHash.Dct(other); bool duplicate = PerceptualHash.Distance(a, b) <= 10; bool unrelated = PerceptualHash.Distance(a, c) > 10; string key = a.ToString("x16", System.Globalization.CultureInfo.InvariantCulture); Keep the 64-bit hashes in a database column; a lookup within a few bits finds recompressed and resized copies. Check an image is grayscale // A scan that is gray in all but name can be stored as one channel: a third of the size, no visible change. if (gray.IsGray(tolerance: 2 / 255f)) { using Raster<Gray8> oneChannel = gray.As<Gray8>(); oneChannel.Save("scan-gray.png"); } A 16-color poster // A 16-color poster with Atkinson's dither; the pixel type stays as it was. photo.Apply(ops => ops.Quantize(new PaletteOptions { MaxColors = 16, Dither = DitherMode.Atkinson }), Ct); photo.Save("poster.png"); Prepare a photo for a six-color e-ink display // Map onto a fixed palette: here an e-ink display's six inks. Palette inks = Palette.FromColors([Rgba8.Black, Rgba8.White, new(255, 0, 0, 255), new(255, 255, 0, 255), new(0, 0, 255, 255), new(0, 255, 0, 255)]); photo.Apply(ops => ops.Remap(inks, DitherMode.FloydSteinberg), Ct); Brand colors from a logo // The main colors and how much of the picture each covers, e.g. to pick brand colors from a logo or a placeholder color. IReadOnlyList<WeightedColor> colors = logo.DominantColors(5); foreach ((Rgba8 color, double weight) in colors) { Console.WriteLine($"#{color.R:X2}{color.G:X2}{color.B:X2} covers {weight:P0}"); } An indexed image for a PDF // Indices plus palette, for a PDF indexed-color image or a format of your own. using IndexedImage indexed = photo.ToIndexed(new PaletteOptions { MaxColors = 64 }); byte[] lookup = [.. indexed.Palette.Colors.SelectMany(c => new[] { c.R, c.G, c.B })]; byte[] samples = indexed.Indices.ToArray(); Shrink a screen-recording GIF // Shrink a screen recording: merge frames that barely change, drop frames no viewer shows, then resample to 25 fps. recording.Apply(ops => ops.MergeDuplicates(tolerance: 0.01f).DropZeroDelay().Retime(25), Ct); recording.Save("recording.gif"); Speed up an animation 2x // Twice as fast, then backwards: a boomerang clip is the clip followed by its reverse. using Raster fast = clip.Derive(ops => ops.ChangeSpeed(2), Ct); using Raster backwards = fast.Derive(ops => ops.Reverse(), Ct); A looping sticker on an animated background // A looping sticker on an animated background: the sticker keeps its own speed and loops for the background's whole length. background.Apply(ops => ops.DrawAnimation(sticker, new Point(10, 10), new AnimationOverlayOptions { Repeat = 0, Opacity = 0.9f }), Ct); background.Save("with-sticker.gif"); A render pass from OpenEXR as JPEG // One render pass of a multi-layer OpenEXR file, tone mapped for the web. using Raster<RgbaF32> diffuse = Raster.Load<RgbaF32>("render.exr", options: new ExrReaderOptions { Layer = "diffuse" }); diffuse.Apply(ops => ops.ToneMap(ToneMapping.Bt2390)); diffuse.Save("diffuse.jpg", new JpegWriterOptions { Quality = 90 }); ExrReaderOptions.Layer picks a pass by name; ExrDetails lists the parts and layers a file has. ToneMap rolls off what is brighter than white instead of clipping it. See the HDR guide. Show an Ultra HDR photo as HDR // An Ultra HDR photo for an HDR display whose peak is displayHeadroom times SDR white: linear light, 1.0 = SDR white, // here written as a half-float OpenEXR file; an SDR display shows the JPEG as it is. using Raster<RgbaF16> photo = Raster.Load<RgbaF16>("ultrahdr.jpg", options: new ReaderOptions { Hdr = new HdrDecode { Headroom = displayHeadroom } }); photo.Save("photo-hdr.exr"); The gain map is applied for the display's headroom: 1 gives the SDR picture, and the map's own capacity (leave Headroom null) the full HDR rendition. Make an Ultra HDR JPEG from an OpenEXR render // An HDR render as a JPEG every viewer opens, which HDR displays (Android, Chrome, Apple Photos) show brighter. using Raster<RgbaF32> render = Raster.Load<RgbaF32>("render.exr"); render.Save("render-ultrahdr.jpg", new JpegWriterOptions { Quality = 90, GainMap = new GainMapOptions { Scale = 2 } }); The SDR picture is the render tone mapped with BT.2390; the gain map, half the size here, brings the HDR render back. Load a JPEG XL image // JPEG XL loads like any format: lossless, lossy, animated or recompressed from a JPEG, in its natural pixel type. using Raster duck = Raster.Load("duck.jxl"); duck.Save("duck.png"); Lossless and lossy files, animations (as their blended frames), extra channels and recompressed JPEGs all load through Raster.Load; lossy color comes out in the file's own color space. See the formats guide. Get the original JPEG back from a JPEG XL file // A JPEG recompressed into JPEG XL loads as pixels like any other file, and gives its JPEG back byte for byte. using Raster image = Raster.Load("recompressed.jxl"); if (((JxlDetails)image.Metadata.FormatDetails!).HasJpegReconstruction) { JxlImage.ReconstructJpeg("recompressed.jxl", "original.jpg"); } A JPEG recompressed losslessly into JPEG XL (cjxl does this by default for JPEG input) keeps a jbrd box, and JxlImage.ReconstructJpeg writes the original file from it, byte for byte. Loading such a file gives its pixels, as viewers show them. Recompress a JPEG into JPEG XL without loss // A JPEG becomes a JPEG XL file about a fifth smaller with the same pixels, and comes back byte for byte. JxlImage.RecompressJpeg("duck.jpg", "duck.jxl"); JxlImage.ReconstructJpeg("duck.jxl", "duck-again.jpg"); The JPEG's own coefficients become the JPEG XL image, so nothing is decoded again or lost: the file loads to the pixels the JPEG gave, about a fifth smaller (as cjxl makes it, within a few bytes), and JxlImage.ReconstructJpeg writes the original back byte for byte. Baseline and progressive JPEGs with any Huffman tables, restart markers, ICC, Exif and XMP are taken; arithmetic-coded, lossless, hierarchical, 12-bit and CMYK JPEGs, and 4:1:1 sampling, are refused. Save a lossless JPEG XL file // Lossless JPEG XL, about the size cjxl -d 0 makes at the same effort (1 fastest to 7 smallest, 5 by default). using Raster photo = Raster.Load("duck.png"); photo.Save("duck-lossless.jxl", new JxlWriterOptions { Lossless = true, Effort = 7 }); Every pixel comes back exactly, in the raster's own precision: 8 or 16-bit, half or single float, gray or RGB, with alpha when it is not opaque everywhere. The effort follows cjxl's: 1 is its fast path, 7 learns a context tree and tries palettes and color transforms, for files within a few bytes of cjxl's. The ICC profile (or an enumerated sRGB, linear or HDR space), EXIF, XMP and orientation are kept. Save a lossy JPEG XL file // Lossy JPEG XL at cjxl's default: quality 90, which is distance 1.0 (visually lossless). using Raster photo = Raster.Load("duck.png"); photo.Save("duck-lossy.jxl", new JxlWriterOptions { Lossless = false }); // A distance as cjxl -d takes it instead of a quality, and more effort for a smaller file. photo.Save("duck-small.jxl", new JxlWriterOptions { Lossless = false, Distance = 2.5f, Effort = 7 }); Lossy files are VarDCT in XYB, as cjxl writes them for PNG input, and come out within 5% of cjxl's size and Butteraugli score at the same settings (libjxl 0.12.0). Pick either a quality or a distance: Quality is cjxl's -q (90 by default, 100 lossless) and Distance its -d, where 1.0 is visually lossless and each step up gives a smaller file with more visible loss; a distance, when set, wins. Effort 1 to 7 is cjxl's -e: 6 adds the full block-size search and a per-block edge-preserving filter strength, 7 patches for repeated shapes such as text. Progressive and PhotonNoiseIso do what cjxl's -p and --photon_noise_iso do. Large images are coded in 2048-pixel chunks, as cjxl does, so memory stays bounded. A JPEG source is better recompressed than re-encoded: Recompress a JPEG into JPEG XL without loss keeps its pixels exactly and the original file recoverable, where lossy encoding its decoded pixels loses detail a second time. Keep alpha exact in a lossy JPEG XL file // Alpha stays exact in lossy files by default, and fully transparent pixels keep their color. using Raster<Rgba8> logo = Raster.Load<Rgba8>("duck.png"); logo.Save("logo.jxl", new JxlWriterOptions { Lossless = false, Quality = 85 }); // Smaller: alpha coded lossy too, and the color under transparent pixels left to the encoder (as cjxl does). logo.Save("logo-small.jxl", new JxlWriterOptions { Lossless = false, AlphaDistance = 1, KeepTransparentColors = false }); Alpha is an extra channel coded apart from the color, exact by default, so cut-outs keep their edges (below distance 10; from there cjxl and Egami code the whole image at half size). AlphaDistance above 0 codes it lossy as cjxl's --alpha_distance does. Fully transparent pixels keep their color unless KeepTransparentColors is false, which lets the encoder replace it, as libjxl does by default, for a smaller file. Read an HDR JPEG XL file as SDR // An HDR (PQ or HLG) file, tone mapped into sRGB as it loads; the peak comes from the file's intensity_target. using Raster<Rgb8> sdr = Raster.Load<Rgb8>("hdr.jxl", options: new ReaderOptions { ConvertColorTo = Egami.Colors.ColorProfile.Srgb }); sdr.Save("hdr-as-sdr.jpg"); PQ and HLG files keep their curve when they load, with intensity_target as HdrMetadata.MaxContentLightLevel; converting to sRGB tone maps with BT.2390 from that peak. A file with a jhgm gain map loads as its SDR base, and ReaderOptions.Hdr renders it as HDR, as for Ultra HDR photos. Load an AVIF image // AVIF loads like any format, in its natural pixel type: Rgb8 or Rgba8 for 8-bit files, Rgb16 or Rgba16 for 10 and 12 bits. using Raster duck = Raster.Load("duck.avif"); duck.Save("duck.png"); Stills, grids and overlays load through Raster.Load, converted to RGB as libavif converts them, the clean aperture cropped and irot and imir kept as the orientation (AutoOrient applies it). Film grain is added unless AvifReaderOptions.FilmGrain is false. See the formats guide. Get an AVIF file's YUV planes // The AV1 planes themselves, without the conversion to RGB: luma, then chroma at the file's subsampling. using YuvRaster planes = YuvRaster.Load("duck.avif"); ChromaFormat chroma = planes.ChromaFormat; // Yuv420 for most AVIF files YuvRaster.Load gives the decoded AV1 planes at 8, 10 or 12 bits, with the alpha image as a fourth plane, as dav1d decodes them; see Planar YUV. Read an HDR AVIF file as SDR // An HDR (PQ or HLG) AVIF, tone mapped into sRGB as it loads; the peak comes from the file's clli box when it has one. using Raster<Rgb8> sdr = Raster.Load<Rgb8>("hdr.avif", options: new ReaderOptions { ConvertColorTo = Egami.Colors.ColorProfile.Srgb }); sdr.Save("hdr-as-sdr.jpg"); PQ and HLG files keep their curve when they load, with clli and mdcv in RasterMetadata.Hdr; converting to sRGB tone maps with BT.2390. Show an AVIF with a gain map as HDR // An AVIF with a gain map loads as its base image, the map in Metadata.GainMap; ReaderOptions.Hdr renders the HDR // rendition for a display with the given headroom (its peak over SDR white), as linear RgbaF16. using Raster sdr = Raster.Load("gainmap.avif"); bool hasMap = sdr.Metadata.GainMap is not null; using Raster hdr = Raster.Load("gainmap.avif", options: new ReaderOptions { Hdr = new HdrDecode { Headroom = 4 } }); An AVIF tone-mapped image (tmap) loads as its base rendition with the gain map in RasterMetadata.GainMap, and ReaderOptions.Hdr renders the other rendition for a display's headroom, as for Ultra HDR photos; the base may be the SDR or the HDR one. Read an AVIF's thumbnail or depth map // The file's other images: thumbnails, depth maps and auxiliary images, each read on its own. AvifDetails details = (AvifDetails)sdr.Metadata.FormatDetails!; foreach (AvifItem item in details.Items.Where(i => i.IsImage && i.Role is AvifItemRole.Thumbnail or AvifItemRole.Depth or AvifItemRole.GainMap)) { using Raster image = AvifImage.ReadItem("gainmap.avif", item.Id); image.Save($"item-{item.Id}-{item.Role}.png"); } AvifDetails.Items lists every item of the file with what it is to the primary image, and AvifImage.ReadItem decodes any image item on its own, in its natural pixel type. Turn an AVIF image sequence into an animation // An image sequence whose frames are all key frames loads as an animation; save it as an animated WebP. using Raster<Rgba8> frames = Raster.Load<Rgba8>("sequence.avif"); TimeSpan firstDelay = frames.Frames[0].Metadata.Delay; frames.Save("sequence.webp"); A sequence (the avis brand) whose frames are all key frames loads every frame with its delay; one with inter frames loads its first frame with a warning for now. Find a PDF font's glyph by name // A PDF simple font's /Differences array names glyphs: find each by name, and get names back for a ToUnicode guess. ushort aacute = face.TryGetGlyphByName("aacute", out ushort g) ? g : (ushort)0; string? name = face.GetGlyphName(aacute); A simple font's /Differences names glyphs; TryGetGlyphByName finds them in a CFF charset or a TrueType post table. See Font data for PDF. Find a CIDFontType0 glyph by CID // A CIDFontType0 font with /CIDToGIDMap absent reaches glyphs by CID through the CFF charset. CidSystemInfo? collection = cjk.CidSystemInfo; // Adobe-Identity-0 for this font ushort glyph = cjk.TryGetGlyphByCid(1, out ushort byCid) ? byCid : (ushort)0; int cid = cjk.GetCid(glyph); Pick the cmap subtable a PDF font uses // A symbolic TrueType font in PDF looks a code up in (3,0) first, then (1,0); a non-symbolic one uses (3,1). CharacterMap? map = trueType.FindCharacterMap(3, 0) ?? trueType.FindCharacterMap(1, 0) ?? trueType.FindCharacterMap(3, 1); ushort forA = map?.GetGlyph('A') ?? 0; // A Type1C font without /Encoding uses the CFF program's own encoding. CharacterMap? own = face.BuiltInEncoding; // platform 7, encoding 0: the Standard Encoding ushort forB = own?.GetGlyph('B') ?? 0; // Every code the map gives a glyph, in code order, for a PDF writer's /Widths or a ToUnicode table. int mapped = map?.GetMappings().Count() ?? 0; A symbolic TrueType font looks codes up in (3,0), then (1,0); a non-symbolic one in (3,1). A Type1C font without /Encoding uses the CFF program's own encoding, BuiltInEncoding. Decode a PDF's CCITT image // An image XObject with /Filter /CCITTFaxDecode: DecodeParms keys not given keep PDF's defaults. The image's /Height // stands in for a missing Rows, so the decoder stops where the image does. CcittFaxParameters parameters = new() { K = k, EncodedByteAlign = aligned, Columns = columns, Rows = rows > 0 ? rows : height }; byte[] bits = CcittFax.Decode(data, parameters, out int decoded); // The filter's samples: 0 black, 1 white. /Decode [1 0] inverts them, and an /ImageMask paints where a sample is 0. bool invert = decode is [> 0.5, ..]; int rowBytes = (columns + 7) / 8; using Raster<Gray8> image = Raster.Create<Gray8>(width, decoded); for (int y = 0; y < decoded; y++) { Span<Gray8> row = image.Row(y); for (int x = 0; x < Math.Min(width, columns); x++) { bool sample = ((bits[(y * rowBytes) + (x >> 3)] >> (7 - (x & 7))) & 1) != 0; row[x] = new Gray8(sample != invert ? (byte)255 : (byte)0); } } CcittFax.Decode gives what the CCITTFaxDecode filter gives, byte-aligned Group 4 included; the image's /Decode, /ImageMask and color space then apply as after any filter. To load the data straight to Gray8, use CcittFormat; see the CCITT guide. Separations of a CMYK page with spot colours // A CMYK page with two spot colours: a photo converted into the process inks, a Pantone band and a gold rule. InkSet inks = InkSet.FromProfile(ColorProfile.Fogra39) .WithSpot("PANTONE 186 C", InkAppearance.Cmyk(0, 1, 0.81f, 0.04f)) .WithSpot("Gold", InkAppearance.Lab(new LabColor(70, 5, 60))); using InkRaster page = new(inks, 600, 400); using (InkCanvas canvas = new(page)) { canvas.Clear(InkColor.None); canvas.DrawImage(photo, new RectF(40, 40, 360, 240)); canvas.FillRect(new RectF(0, 320, 600, 50), new SolidPaint(InkColor.Spot(inks[4], 1))); canvas.FillRect(new RectF(40, 300, 520, 4), new SolidPaint(InkColor.Spot(inks[5], 1))); } // Every plate as its own gray image (ink shows light), and all of them as one separated TIFF for the RIP. foreach (InkPlate plate in page.Plates) { using Raster<Gray8> gray = plate.AsRaster<Gray8>(); gray.Save($"page-{plate.Name}.png"); } page.Save("page.tif"); InkCanvas draws on plates with any Canvas call; RGB images and colours convert through the ink set's profile. See Printing inks. A spot-colour label with overprint // A label in one spot colour over a CMYK background, overprinted so the press needs no trapping: the background's // plates stay under the spot. Black text overprints too, leaving every other plate alone where it prints. using (InkCanvas canvas = new(page)) { canvas.FillRect(new RectF(0, 0, 300, 120), new SolidPaint(InkColor.Cmyk(0.1f, 0.05f, 0.4f, 0))); canvas.FillPath(Path.RoundRect(new RoundRect(new RectF(20, 20, 260, 80), 12)), new SolidPaint(InkColor.Spot(inks[4], 1)) { Overprint = Overprint.On }); canvas.FillPath(Path.Circle(new Vector2(150, 60), 20), new SolidPaint(InkColor.Cmyk(0, 0, 0, 1)) { Overprint = Overprint.NonZero }); } Overprint.On paints only the inks a colour names; NonZero also leaves the plates of a CMYK colour's zero components alone, as PDF's overprint mode 1. Check total ink coverage before printing // Before sending a page to a press with a 300% total ink limit: where is there too much ink, and how much of the page? InkCoverage coverage = page.MeasureCoverage(limit: 3.0f); if (coverage.MaxTotal > coverage.Limit) { Console.WriteLine($"{coverage.MaxTotal:P0} at {coverage.MaxAt}; {coverage.ShareOver:P1} of the page is over {coverage.Limit:P0}."); } // A soft proof shows how it will look on paper, the paper's own tone included. using Raster<Rgba8> proof = page.Proof<Rgba8>(new ProofOptions { SimulatePaper = true });

articles/diagnostics.html.title: Diagnostics | Egami
articles/diagnostics.html.summary: Diagnostics Egami can tell an app what it recovered from, what it lost on purpose and what it decided on the caller's behalf, through one optional handler on EgamiContext. Egami has no logging dependency: the handler is a plain delegate, so one line sends the events to ILogger, Serilog or the console. // With Microsoft.Extensions.Logging: one line at startup sends every call's warnings to the app's log, with the id as // a property to filter and count on. Egami itself has no logging dependency. EgamiContext.SetDefault(new EgamiContext { Diagnostics = d => logger.Log(d.Level.ToLogLevel(), "{Source} {Id} at {Offset}: {Message}", d.Source, d.Id, d.Offset, d.Message), }); The handler EgamiContext.Diagnostics is an Action<EgamiDiagnostic>, null by default. With no handler, nothing is built and nothing is allocated. Each EgamiDiagnostic carries: Member What it holds Level Warning, Info or Debug, mapping onto the log levels Warning, Information and Debug Source The part of Egami that found it: Png, Tiff, Exif, Limits and so on (the id up to its first dot) Id A stable id such as Png.ChecksumMismatch, to filter and count on without parsing text Message What happened and what Egami did, as a sentence Offset The byte offset in the input, when known Frame The frame or page index, when known Ids are listed below and are never renamed or reused once shipped, like the public API. Levels. EgamiContext.DiagnosticLevel is the lowest level delivered, Warning by default. Events below it are never even formatted. // Info and Debug events are off unless asked for; below the level they are never even formatted. EgamiContext verbose = EgamiContext.Default with { Diagnostics = d => seen.Add(d), DiagnosticLevel = DiagnosticLevel.Debug, }; using Raster image = Raster.Load("duck.jpg", verbose, new ReaderOptions { MinimumSize = new Size(100, 100) }); foreach (EgamiDiagnostic d in seen) { Console.WriteLine($"{d.Level,-7} {d.Id}: {d.Message}"); } Threads. The handler runs inline, on whichever thread found the event, possibly on several decode threads at once, so it must be quick and thread-safe. Egami takes no lock around it. When Warnings arrive. The Warnings a load raises arrive as the call ends, in the order of Metadata.Warnings, on the calling thread; a RasterDecoder session sends them when it is disposed. A reader that waits for more input can take a warning back and read it again, so nothing is sent until it is final. Info and Debug events arrive as they happen. A load that throws sends no Warnings: the exception says what went wrong. Errors. An exception from the handler fails the call with that exception, which turns warnings into errors. Nothing the call allocated is leaked. // Warnings as errors: a handler that throws fails the call with its exception, and nothing the call allocated is leaked. EgamiContext strict = EgamiContext.Default with { Diagnostics = d => throw new InvalidDataException($"{d.Id}: {d.Message}"), }; try { using Raster image = Raster.Load(SampleFiles.Damaged(), strict); } catch (InvalidDataException e) { Console.WriteLine($"Rejected: {e.Message}"); } Repeats. One id is delivered at most 10 times per call, then once more as "The same problem came up N more times". Metadata.Warnings holds the same capped list, so the two always agree. A hostile file cannot flood a log. Per file. Contexts are cheap records, so a context per file, whose handler's closure carries the path, scopes the events to that file. // Per file: the handler's closure carries the path, so no correlation id is needed. Contexts are cheap records. foreach (string path in Directory.EnumerateFiles(".", "*.png")) { EgamiContext perFile = EgamiContext.Default with { Diagnostics = d => log.Add($"{path}: {d.Message}") }; using Raster image = Raster.Load(path, perFile); } Metadata.Warnings Every Warning a load raises is also in RasterMetadata.Warnings, an IReadOnlyList<EgamiDiagnostic>, with or without a handler. Info and Debug events never are. Metadata parsed on first use (XMP, IPTC, ICC) adds its warnings then, and sends them to the handler of the context the raster was loaded with. // Without a handler the same Warnings are in the metadata, each with its id. using Raster image = Raster.Load(SampleFiles.Damaged()); foreach (EgamiDiagnostic warning in image.Metadata.Warnings) { Console.WriteLine($"{warning.Id} at byte {warning.Offset}: {warning.Message}"); } bool checksumsOnly = image.Metadata.Warnings.All(w => w.Id == "Png.ChecksumMismatch"); Reporting from your own code A format plug-in notes a recovery with EgamiInput.Warn(raster, id, message), which lists it in Metadata.Warnings and sends it to the handler as Egami's own readers do; EgamiInput.Diagnostics takes its Info and Debug events. Code with no EgamiInput, such as a video demuxer, starts a DiagnosticReporter for the call with EgamiContext.StartDiagnostics(), which applies the same level filter and cap; disposing it sends the counts of capped ids. Use your own source name in ids (Avi.IndexRebuilt), never one of Egami's. // A decoder outside Egami (a video demuxer, a format plug-in's own entry point) reports through the same handler, with the // same level filter and the same cap of 10 per id per call. Dispose the reporter when the call ends. using (DiagnosticReporter diagnostics = context.StartDiagnostics()) { if (diagnostics.IsEnabled(DiagnosticLevel.Warning)) { diagnostics.Report(DiagnosticLevel.Warning, "Avi.IndexRebuilt", "The index was missing; it was rebuilt from the frames.", offset: 4096); } diagnostics.Report(DiagnosticLevel.Info, "Mjpeg.DhtInserted", "Frames have no Huffman tables; the standard ones were used."); } Logging libraries ILogger takes the mapping in the first example. Serilog's static Log is the same one line: // With Serilog's static Log: the same one line, with Serilog's level names. EgamiContext context = EgamiContext.Default with { Diagnostics = d => log.Write(d.Level == DiagnosticLevel.Warning ? "Warning" : d.Level == DiagnosticLevel.Info ? "Information" : "Debug", "{Id}: {Message}", d.Id, d.Message), }; Memory leaks are reported by PixelMemoryUsage.LeakDetected instead, because they belong to a memory source rather than a call and are found on the finalizer thread after the call has ended; see Memory and threading. they are drawn black Tga.RowsMissing Warning The pixel data ends or is damaged; the rows not decoded are black Tga.RunPastImage Warning An RLE packet goes past the end of the image; the rest of it was ignored Tiff.ByteCountsMissing Warning A page has no usable byte counts; they were worked out Tiff.ExtraSamplesDropped Warning Extra samples that are not alpha were dropped Tiff.Float64Narrowed Warning 64-bit floating-point samples were read as 32-bit Tiff.IfdDamaged Warning An IFD in the chain is damaged; the pages before it were read Tiff.IfdLoop Warning The IFD chain loops; it was read up to there Tiff.IfdOutside Warning The next IFD lies outside the file; the pages before it were read Tiff.InksNotCmyk Warning A page has inks that are not CMYK; only the first was read, as gray Tiff.OffsetsMissing Warning A page has fewer strip or tile offsets than it needs; the rest is black Tiff.PhotometricMissing Warning A page has no PhotometricInterpretation; it was read as RGB or gray Tiff.PredictorIgnored Warning A predictor with a compression it means nothing to was ignored Tiff.RowsPerStripZero Warning RowsPerStrip is 0; the page was read as one strip Tiff.SignedSamples Warning Signed samples were offset so 0 is the middle value Tiff.SubIfdDamaged Warning An EXIF, GPS or other sub-IFD is damaged;
