A canvas raster.CreateCanvas() returns a RasterCanvas<TPixel> that draws on the raster's first frame, in the pixel type's own precision. Calls draw when they are made; Save and Restore bracket changes to the transform and clip. // A canvas draws onto a raster. Calls draw when they are made; dispose the canvas when done. using Raster<Rgba8> raster = Raster.Create(400, 300, Rgba8.White); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = raster.CreateCanvas()) { canvas.FillRect(new RectF(20, 20, 160, 100), new Rgba8(30, 90, 200, 255)); // Save and Restore bracket transform and clip changes. canvas.Save(); canvas.Translate(260, 150); canvas.Rotate(30); canvas.FillRect(new RectF(-50, -30, 100, 60), new Rgba8(200, 60, 30, 200)); canvas.Restore(); canvas.FillCircle(new Vector2(100, 220), 50, Rgba8.Black); } // Blend edges in linear light, which keeps thin lines and translucent colors from darkening. using RasterCanvas<Rgba8> linear = raster.CreateCanvas(new CanvasOptions { ColorSpace = ColorSpace.Linear }); Coordinates are float pixels, y down. Pixel (0, 0) covers the square from (0, 0) to (1, 1), so a RectF with whole-number edges covers whole pixels and a rectangle from 2.5 covers pixel 2 by half. Every pixel gets its exact covered area, rounded to 1/255: abutting shapes leave no seams. CanvasOptions sets where edges blend (ColorSpace.Encoded, the default, or Linear) and the curve Tolerance (0.1 pixel by default). A canvas is for one thread at a time. A large call spreads its rows over EgamiContext.MaxParallelism cores, with the same pixels at any core count. Shapes canvas.FillRect(new RectF(10, 10, 80, 40), Rgba8.Red); canvas.FillRoundRect(new RoundRect(new RectF(100, 10, 80, 40), 12), new Rgba8(0, 128, 0, 255)); // Each corner can have its own radii; radii that would overlap are scaled down together, as CSS does. CornerRadii tab = new(topLeft: 16, topRight: 16, bottomRight: 0, bottomLeft: 0); canvas.FillRoundRect(new RoundRect(new RectF(190, 10, 100, 40), tab), Rgba8.Black); canvas.FillOval(new RectF(10, 60, 120, 60), new Rgba8(255, 200, 0, 255)); canvas.FillCircle(new Vector2(170, 90), 30, new Rgba8(80, 80, 200, 255)); canvas.FillArc(new RectF(210, 60, 60, 60), startDegrees: -90, sweepDegrees: 120, Rgba8.Red); canvas.FillRing(new RoundRect(new RectF(10, 130, 60, 60), 30), new RoundRect(new RectF(25, 145, 30, 30), 15), Rgba8.Black); // The same shapes as paths, to build on or to reuse. Path hexagon = Path.RegularPolygon(new Vector2(120, 160), 30, sides: 6); Path star = Path.Star(new Vector2(200, 160), outerRadius: 30, innerRadius: 12, points: 5); canvas.FillPath(hexagon, new Rgba8(0, 150, 150, 255)); canvas.FillPath(star, new Rgba8(220, 160, 0, 255)); Each shape has a Fill and a Stroke call. RoundRect takes CornerRadii, one x and y radius per corner; its Kind (RoundRectKind) says when it is really a rectangle or an ellipse. FillRing fills between two round rectangles. Paths A Path holds contours of lines, quadratic and cubic curves, built with a PathBuilder, and never changes once built. Arcs, ovals and round corners become cubic curves as they are added. PathVerb names each command and Points holds their points, for code that reads paths back. // A path is built once and never changes, so it can be drawn many times and from many threads. Path heart = new PathBuilder() .MoveTo(150, 60) .CubicTo(150, 30, 100, 20, 90, 60) .CubicTo(80, 100, 130, 130, 150, 160) .CubicTo(170, 130, 220, 100, 210, 60) .CubicTo(200, 20, 150, 30, 150, 60) .Close() .ToPath(); canvas.FillPath(heart, Rgba8.Red); // SVG's arc command, and the even-odd rule: an inner contour becomes a hole. Path frame = new PathBuilder() .AddRect(new RectF(10, 10, 60, 60)) .AddCircle(new Vector2(40, 40), 20) .MoveTo(10, 120) .ArcTo(radii: new Vector2(30, 20), rotationDegrees: 0, largeArc: false, clockwise: true, end: new Vector2(70, 120)) .Close() .ToPath(FillRule.EvenOdd); canvas.FillPath(frame, Rgba8.Black); bool hit = heart.Contains(new Vector2(150, 100)); // hit testing on the curves themselves RectF box = heart.TightBounds; // curves measured at their extremes FillRule decides what is inside: NonZero (the default) or EvenOdd. Shapes are added clockwise; a PathDirection.CounterClockwise contour inside a clockwise one makes a hole under NonZero too. Contains uses the winding number on the curves themselves, and counts a point on the outline as inside. Transform takes a Matrix3x2, or a Homography for perspective. Strokes Stroke is the pen: Width, Cap (LineCap.Butt, Round, Square), Join (LineJoin.Miter, Round, Bevel) and MiterLimit (4). The pen is applied in local coordinates, so a non-uniform scale gives an elliptical pen. // The pen is data: width, caps, joins and miter limit. Width 1, butt caps and miter joins by default. Stroke thick = new(12) { Cap = LineCap.Round, Join = LineJoin.Round }; canvas.DrawLine(new Vector2(20, 20), new Vector2(280, 20), thick, new Rgba8(30, 90, 200, 255)); Path zigzag = Path.Polygon([new(20, 120), new(80, 60), new(140, 120), new(200, 60), new(260, 120)], close: false); canvas.StrokePath(zigzag, new Stroke(8) { Join = LineJoin.Miter, MiterLimit = 4 }, Rgba8.Black); // A hairline is one device pixel wide whatever the transform. canvas.StrokeCircle(new Vector2(150, 160), 30, Stroke.Hairline, Rgba8.Red); Width 0 is a hairline: one device pixel across its major axis at any scale, as in Skia. A stroke thinner than a pixel draws as a hairline, fainter by its width. Overlaps within one stroke never double the color. DrawPoints takes a PointMode: dots, pairs of points as lines, or one polyline. Paints A color converts to a SolidPaint wherever a Paint is expected. The paint also carries a BlendMode, an Opacity and Antialias. // A color converts to a SolidPaint. A paint also carries a blend mode, an opacity and whether edges are antialiased. canvas.FillRect(new RectF(0, 0, 200, 100), Rgba8.White); SolidPaint glaze = new(new RgbaF32(0.9f, 0.2f, 0.1f, 1)) { BlendMode = BlendMode.Multiply, Opacity = 0.6f }; canvas.FillCircle(new Vector2(60, 50), 40, glaze); // Pixel art: no antialiasing, so every pixel is fully drawn or not at all. canvas.FillCircle(new Vector2(150, 50), 30, new SolidPaint(Rgba8.Black) { Antialias = false }); Gradients LinearGradient, RadialGradient, ConicalGradient (between two circles, as the HTML canvas, Skia and PDF define it) and SweepGradient take GradientStops from 0 to 1. Tile says what lies past the ends (Clamp, Repeat, Mirror, Decal), and with Clamp, ExtendStart and ExtendEnd can leave one side empty, as a PDF shading's Extend does. Stops mix in encoded sRGB by default, or in linear light, Oklab or Oklch with a HueMethod (GradientInterpolation, whose InterpolationSpace names the space), as CSS Color 4 defines them, and premultiplied so a fade to a transparent color never darkens. Every paint has a LocalMatrix, which turns a radial gradient into an ellipse. On 8-bit targets a gradient reads 1024 colors made once per paint; Dither adds a 4×4 ordered pattern that hides banding on large soft ramps. using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = raster.CreateCanvas()) { // Two colors along a line; past the ends the end colors repeat (TileMode.Clamp). canvas.FillRect(new RectF(0, 0, 200, 100), new LinearGradient(new Vector2(0, 0), new Vector2(200, 0), new RgbaF32(0.1f, 0.3f, 0.9f, 1), new RgbaF32(1, 0.8f, 0.2f, 1))); // Several stops, mixed in Oklab for even midpoints, repeating every 40 pixels. canvas.FillRect(new RectF(200, 0, 200, 100), new LinearGradient( new Vector2(200, 0), new Vector2(240, 0), new GradientStop(0, new Rgba8(230, 40, 60, 255)), new GradientStop(0.5f, new Rgba8(250, 210, 60, 255)), new GradientStop(1, new Rgba8(230, 40, 60, 255))) { Tile = TileMode.Repeat, Interpolation = GradientInterpolation.Oklab, }); // A radial gradient stretched into an ellipse by its local matrix, and a sweep around a center. canvas.FillOval(new RectF(10, 110, 180, 80), new RadialGradient(Vector2.Zero, 1, new RgbaF32(1, 1, 1, 1), new RgbaF32(0, 0.4f, 0.2f, 1)) { LocalMatrix = Matrix3x2.CreateScale(90, 40) * Matrix3x2.CreateTranslation(100, 150), }); canvas.FillCircle(new Vector2(300, 150), 45, new SweepGradient( new Vector2(300, 150), new GradientStop(0, new Rgba8(255, 0, 0, 255)), new GradientStop(0.5f, new Rgba8(0, 0, 255, 255)), new GradientStop(1, new Rgba8(255, 0, 0, 255)))); } Images, noise and your own paints ImagePaint fills with an image under its local matrix, tiled per axis, sampled by Egami's filters and from a MipChain level when shrunk. NoisePaint.Fractal and NoisePaint.Turbulence (its NoisePaintKind) are SVG's feTurbulence (matching SkiaSharp's noise shaders), and NoisePaint.Simplex is smoother and tiles exactly. BlendPaint combines two paints with a blend mode, WithColorMatrix runs a color matrix on a paint (a ColorMatrixPaint), and a CustomPaint record fills rows of premultiplied colors from C#. // Fill a shape with a photo tiled as a pattern, half size, turned 15 degrees. using Raster photo = Raster.Load("duck.png"); using Raster<Rgba8> raster = Raster.Create(400, 300, Rgba8.White); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = raster.CreateCanvas()) { ImagePaint pattern = new(photo, TileMode.Mirror, TileMode.Mirror) { LocalMatrix = Matrix3x2.CreateScale(0.5f) * Matrix3x2.CreateRotation(MathF.PI / 12), }; canvas.FillPath(Path.Star(new Vector2(200, 150), 140, 60, 5), pattern); } using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = raster.CreateCanvas()) { // SVG's feTurbulence fractal noise, stitched so a 128-pixel tile repeats without a seam, made gray by a color matrix. Paint stone = NoisePaint.Fractal(0.03f, 0.03f, octaves: 5, seed: 7, tileSize: new Size(128, 128)) .WithColorMatrix(new ColorMatrix([0.3f, 0.6f, 0.1f, 0, 0, 0.3f, 0.6f, 0.1f, 0, 0, 0.3f, 0.6f, 0.1f, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1])); canvas.DrawPaint(stone); // Smooth simplex noise as a soft overlay. canvas.DrawPaint(NoisePaint.Simplex(0.01f, octaves: 3) with { BlendMode = BlendMode.Overlay, Opacity = 0.5f }); } LinearGradient sky = new(new Vector2(0, 0), new Vector2(0, 100), new RgbaF32(0.2f, 0.4f, 0.9f, 1), new RgbaF32(0.9f, 0.6f, 0.4f, 1)); NoisePaint clouds = NoisePaint.Fractal(0.02f, 0.05f, 4, seed: 3); // Noise multiplied onto the gradient, then the whole paint turned to sepia. Paint paint = new BlendPaint(sky, clouds, BlendMode.SoftLight).WithColorMatrix(ColorMatrix.Sepia(0.6f)); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = raster.CreateCanvas()) { canvas.DrawPaint(paint); } // Concentric rings from C#: a record class whose Shade fills one row of premultiplied colors. It runs on several threads at // once, so it keeps no state. public sealed record class Rings(float Spacing) : CustomPaint { public override void Shade(int y, int x, Span<PremulRgbaF32> row, in Matrix3x2 inverse) { for (int i = 0; i < row.Length; i++) { Vector2 p = Vector2.Transform(new Vector2(x + i + 0.5f, y + 0.5f), inverse); float v = 0.5f + (0.5f * MathF.Cos(p.Length() * MathF.Tau / Spacing)); row[i] = new PremulRgbaF32(v, v * 0.6f, 0.2f, 1); } } } A colour can also be given as printing inks: new SolidPaint(InkColor), a GradientStop with an InkColor, and Mesh.WithInks and Patch.WithInks for vertex and corner colours. An ink canvas prints the inks; every other canvas, SVG included, draws the colour's appearance in sRGB. Paint.Overprint (an Overprint) says which plates a paint prints on an ink canvas, as PDF's overprint does; RGB canvases ignore it. The colour management guide covers inks. // A spot colour, overprinting what is below. An ink canvas prints its plate; this RGB canvas draws its appearance. var logo = Colors.InkColor.Spot("PANTONE 186 C", 1, Colors.InkAppearance.Cmyk(0, 1, 0.81f, 0.04f)); canvas.FillRect(new RectF(10, 10, 80, 40), new SolidPaint(logo) { Overprint = Overprint.On }); Layers SaveLayer sends later drawing into a layer that the matching Restore merges with an opacity, a blend mode, a filter (any chain of Egami's operations that keeps the size) and a soft mask: what PDF calls a transparency group. Two overlapping shapes in a half-opacity layer fade as one. The layer covers only its bounds inside the clip, grown by the filter's reach (RasterOps.Reach, an OperationReach), so a blur near the clip's edge still sees what was drawn just outside it. Backdrop runs a chain on what lies behind the layer first, for frosted glass, and Isolated = false starts the layer from the backdrop. using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = raster.CreateCanvas()) { // Group opacity: the overlapping circles fade as one shape, with no darker overlap. canvas.SaveLayer(0.5f); canvas.FillCircle(new Vector2(80, 100), 60, new Rgba8(200, 30, 30, 255)); canvas.FillCircle(new Vector2(140, 100), 60, new Rgba8(200, 30, 30, 255)); canvas.Restore(); // A group blended with Multiply and blurred as a whole; the layer grows by the blur's reach, so nothing is cut. canvas.SaveLayer(new LayerOptions { BlendMode = BlendMode.Multiply, Filter = ops => ops.Blur(4) }); canvas.FillRect(new RectF(180, 40, 90, 120), new Rgba8(40, 120, 220, 255)); canvas.FillCircle(new Vector2(225, 100), 30, Rgba8.White); canvas.Restore(); } A SoftMask is drawn on its own canvas; its luminosity over a backdrop color, or its alpha, through an optional transfer curve, multiplies the layer, as a PDF soft mask does. using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = raster.CreateCanvas()) { // A luminosity mask, as a PDF soft mask: white shows the photo, black hides it, a gradient fades it out to the right. RectF area = new(0, 0, photo.Width, photo.Height); SoftMask fade = new(mask => mask.FillRect(area, new LinearGradient(new Vector2(area.Width * 0.6f, 0), new Vector2(area.Width, 0), new RgbaF32(1, 1, 1, 1), new RgbaF32(0, 0, 0, 1)))); canvas.SaveLayer(new LayerOptions { Mask = fade }); canvas.DrawImage(photo, Vector2.Zero); canvas.Restore(); } Common layer effects In Egami each layer effect is a LayerOptions.Filter or Backdrop chain, so any Egami operation works on a layer. Effect Egami Gaussian or box blur effect Filter = o => o.Blur(sigma) or o.BoxBlur(radius) Drop shadow Filter = o => o.DropShadow(dx, dy, sigma, color, new DropShadowOptions { Expand = false }) Outer glow Filter = o => o.Glow(sigma, color, spread) Inner glow Filter = o => o.Glow(sigma, color, spread, inner: true) Inner shadow Filter = o => o.InnerShadow(dx, dy, sigma, color) Color matrix, brightness, contrast, saturation, grayscale, sepia, hue Filter = o => o.ColorMatrix(...) and the tone steps Opacity LayerOptions.Opacity Blend mode LayerOptions.BlendMode Backdrop blur and other backdrop effects Backdrop = o => o.Blur(sigma) and any other chain Blurs and shadows Paint.Blur takes a MaskBlur: the shape's coverage blurred by a sigma in device pixels before the paint is applied, keeping the inside and outside as its BlurStyle says, as Skia's blur mask filter. Axis-aligned rectangles with the normal style are blurred exactly, from the error function. DrawShadow casts a Material-style shadow from a shape's elevation and a light, after Skia's shadow utilities; a group's drop shadow is a layer filter. using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = raster.CreateCanvas()) { // A soft-edged card (exact, from the error function) and a neon outline: the stroke's outer blur only, then the stroke. canvas.FillRoundRect(new RoundRect(new RectF(20, 20, 110, 80), 12), new SolidPaint(new Rgba8(30, 30, 30, 255)) { Blur = new MaskBlur(6) }); Path ring = Path.Circle(new Vector2(220, 60), 40); canvas.StrokePath(ring, new Stroke(4), new SolidPaint(new Rgba8(255, 40, 200, 255)) { Blur = new MaskBlur(8, BlurStyle.Outer) }); canvas.StrokePath(ring, new Stroke(4), new Rgba8(255, 200, 250, 255)); } using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = raster.CreateCanvas()) { // A card floating 12 pixels up: its ambient and spot shadows, then the card itself. RoundRect card = new(new RectF(60, 40, 180, 110), 10); canvas.DrawShadow(Path.RoundRect(card), new ShadowOptions { Elevation = 12 }); canvas.FillRoundRect(card, Rgba8.White); // A whole group's drop shadow: a layer with a drop shadow filter that keeps the layer's size. canvas.SaveLayer(new LayerOptions { Filter = ops => ops.DropShadow(3, 4, 3, new Rgba8(0, 0, 0, 90), new DropShadowOptions { Expand = false }) }); canvas.FillCircle(new Vector2(110, 95), 20, new Rgba8(230, 80, 40, 255)); canvas.FillRect(new RectF(140, 80, 60, 30), new Rgba8(40, 120, 220, 255)); canvas.Restore(); } Clips ClipRect, ClipRoundRect and ClipPath take a ClipOp: Intersect keeps the inside, Difference the outside. Clips are antialiased unless asked not to be. A clip that is a pixel-aligned rectangle costs nothing; any other clip is a coverage mask of one byte per pixel of its bounds, and drawing through it costs about 1.2 times drawing without. // Clips are antialiased and last until the matching Restore. canvas.Save(); canvas.ClipPath(Path.Circle(new Vector2(100, 100), 80)); canvas.ClipRect(new RectF(60, 60, 80, 80), ClipOp.Difference); // a square hole canvas.DrawPaint(new Rgba8(30, 90, 200, 255)); // fills the whole clip canvas.Restore(); // Only whole pixels inside the clip are drawn after a pixel-aligned rectangle clip, at no extra cost. canvas.ClipRect(new RectF(0, 0, 100, 200)); canvas.FillCircle(new Vector2(100, 190), 40, Rgba8.Black); Images DrawImage draws all or part of an image into a rectangle, under the transform and clip, sampled with Egami's SamplingOptions. At its own size on whole pixels it blends exactly as DrawImage in an operation chain does. using Raster photo = Raster.Load("duck.png"); using Raster<Rgba8> page = Raster.Create(800, 600, Rgba8.White); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = page.CreateCanvas()) { // At its own size: whole-pixel placement blends exactly as DrawImage does. canvas.DrawImage(photo, new Vector2(10, 10)); // Scaled into a rectangle and turned, sampled with any of Egami's filters. canvas.Save(); canvas.Rotate(-8, new Vector2(500, 300)); canvas.DrawImage(photo, new RectF(350, 150, 300, 300 * photo.Height / photo.Width), new SamplingOptions { Filter = ResampleFilter.Lanczos3 }); canvas.Restore(); // A part of the image, at half opacity. canvas.DrawImage(photo, source: new RectF(0, 0, 100, 100), destination: new RectF(10, 450, 140, 140), paint: new SolidPaint(Rgba8.Black) { Opacity = 0.5f }); } Nine-patches and lattices DrawImageNinePatch stretches an image to a rectangle while its corners keep their size: the edges stretch one way and the center both ways, as Skia's drawImageNine. DrawImageLattice generalizes it: a Lattice's x and y divisions cut the image into columns and rows that alternate fixed and stretchable, and each cell can draw its part of the image, nothing, or a fixed color (LatticeCellKind). Fixed parts shrink in proportion when the destination is too small for them. NinePatch.FromAndroid reads an Android .9.png: the one-pixel border's black markers become the lattice, and the right and bottom markers the content padding. using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = raster.CreateCanvas()) { // An Android .9.png: its one-pixel border marks what stretches. The corners stay sharp at any size. (Raster inner, Lattice lattice, Rect? padding) = NinePatch.FromAndroid(file); canvas.DrawImageLattice(inner, lattice, new RectF(10, 10, 180, 48)); inner.Dispose(); // A nine-patch from a plain image: the 8-pixel corners keep their size, the edges and center stretch. canvas.DrawImageNinePatch(frame, new Rect(8, 8, 8, 8), new RectF(10, 70, 120, 40)); // A lattice can leave cells out or fill them with a color: here the center becomes a flat panel. LatticeCellKind[] kinds = [.. Enumerable.Repeat(LatticeCellKind.Default, 9)]; kinds[4] = LatticeCellKind.FixedColor; RgbaF32[] colors = new RgbaF32[9]; colors[4] = new RgbaF32(0.95f, 0.95f, 0.9f, 1); canvas.DrawImageLattice(frame, new Lattice([8, 16], [8, 16]) { CellKinds = kinds, CellColors = colors }, new RectF(150, 70, 140, 40)); } The raster backend draws the cells as one textured mesh, so neighboring cells meet without seams at any scale or position. Sprite atlases DrawAtlas draws many sprites from one image in one call, as Skia's drawAtlas: each sprite is a source rectangle placed by a SpriteTransform (a rotation and uniform scale, then a move, as Skia's RSXform), and may be tinted by a color combined with it by a blend mode. Each sprite blends with what lies below on its own, so additive particles add up. It pairs with SpriteSheet.Pack; the sheet's texels are prepared once for the whole call. // Pack the sprites once, then draw thousands of them in one call: each with its own place, turn, scale and tint. using SpriteSheet sheet = SpriteSheet.Pack([spark, star], new SpritePackOptions { Padding = 1 }); Random random = new(7); SpriteTransform[] transforms = new SpriteTransform[2000]; RectF[] sources = new RectF[transforms.Length]; RgbaF32[] tints = new RgbaF32[transforms.Length]; for (int i = 0; i < transforms.Length; i++) { Rect frame = sheet.Frames[i % 2]; sources[i] = frame; transforms[i] = SpriteTransform.FromRotationScale( scale: 0.3f + random.NextSingle(), degrees: random.NextSingle() * 360, position: new Vector2(random.NextSingle() * 320, random.NextSingle() * 200), anchor: new Vector2(frame.Width / 2f, frame.Height / 2f)); tints[i] = new RgbaF32(1, 0.5f + (random.NextSingle() / 2), random.NextSingle(), 0.8f); } using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = raster.CreateCanvas()) { // Plus adds the sprites up, as light does. canvas.DrawAtlas(sheet.Image, transforms, sources, tints, BlendMode.Modulate, paint: new SolidPaint(Rgba8.White) { BlendMode = BlendMode.Plus }); } Meshes and patches A Mesh is triangles (MeshMode: a list, a strip or a fan, from the vertices or from indices) with an optional color, texture coordinate or value at each vertex. DrawMesh fills the triangles' union once, antialiased on its outer edges only, so a mesh has no cracks between its triangles, which PDF requires of its mesh shadings; where triangles overlap, the later one shows. Vertex colors interpolate in the canvas's color space, premultiplied (Gouraud shading); with texture coordinates, the paint is mapped onto each triangle; and the two combine by a blend mode, the vertex color as the destination. As in Skia, a solid paint's color gives way to the vertex colors and only its alpha applies. using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = raster.CreateCanvas()) { // Gouraud shading: a color at each corner, blended across each triangle without cracks between them. Vector2[] quad = [new(10, 10), new(140, 20), new(130, 140), new(20, 120)]; RgbaF32[] colors = [new(1, 0.2f, 0.2f, 1), new(1, 0.9f, 0.2f, 1), new(0.2f, 0.6f, 1, 1), new(0.6f, 0.2f, 0.9f, 1)]; canvas.DrawMesh(new Mesh(MeshMode.Fan, quad, colors), Rgba8.White); // A textured mesh: each vertex says which point of the paint lands on it, here bending a photo into a trapezoid. Vector2[] trapezoid = [new(170, 20), new(280, 30), new(290, 140), new(160, 130)]; Vector2[] corners = [new(0, 0), new(64, 0), new(64, 64), new(0, 64)]; canvas.DrawMesh(new Mesh(MeshMode.Fan, trapezoid, texCoords: corners), new ImagePaint(photo)); } A Patch is a curved four-sided surface: a Coons patch from four cubic edges (Patch.Coons, 12 points, PDF shading type 6 and Skia's drawPatch) or a tensor-product patch from a 4×4 net (Patch.Tensor, PDF type 7), with colors, values or texture coordinates at its corners. DrawPatch cuts it into triangles under the current transform until they stray less than a quarter of a device pixel from the surface, and where it folds over itself the larger parameters cover the smaller, as PDF specifies. // A Coons patch: four cubic edges, clockwise from the top-left corner, and a color at each corner. Vector2[] edges = [ new(20, 20), new(80, 0), new(150, 40), new(220, 20), // top, left to right new(200, 80), new(240, 140), new(220, 180), // right, down new(150, 160), new(80, 200), new(20, 180), // bottom, right to left new(40, 120), new(0, 60), // left, up ]; Patch patch = Patch.Coons(edges, [new RgbaF32(1, 0, 0, 1), new RgbaF32(1, 1, 0, 1), new RgbaF32(0, 0, 1, 1), new RgbaF32(0, 1, 0, 1)]); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = raster.CreateCanvas()) { canvas.DrawPatch(patch); // PDF's function-based shadings give each corner a value instead, mapped through a gradient's stops. Patch shaded = Patch.Tensor(patch.ToTensorNet().Span, cornerValues: [0, 0.3f, 1, 0.6f]); canvas.Translate(10, 10); canvas.Scale(0.3f); canvas.DrawPatch(shaded, valueStops: [new GradientStop(0, Rgba8.Black), new GradientStop(1, Rgba8.White)]); } Values are PDF's way of shading through a function: each vertex or corner carries one number t, interpolated, then mapped to a color through gradient stops, so a renderer of PDF shadings types 4 to 7 hands Egami its meshes and patches directly and the colors stay smooth inside each triangle. Recorded drawings A PictureRecorder is a canvas that records instead of drawing; Finish returns an immutable Picture. DrawPicture replays it on any canvas under a matrix, through the public calls, so it stays sharp at any scale and a vector backend receives it as vectors. A paint with an opacity or a blend mode merges the whole drawing as one layer; cacheAsImage draws an image of it rendered at the current scale and kept with the drawing, for a drawing repeated many times at one scale. ToRaster renders it, and Playback replays it without the state DrawPicture adds. A drawing replays on many threads and canvases at once. // Record any picture code once... PictureRecorder recorder = new(new RectF(0, 0, 40, 40)); DrawLogo(recorder); Picture logo = recorder.Finish(); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = raster.CreateCanvas()) { // ...and replay it anywhere, at any scale, still sharp: replay is vector. canvas.DrawPicture(logo, Matrix3x2.CreateTranslation(10, 10)); canvas.DrawPicture(logo, Matrix3x2.CreateScale(4) * Matrix3x2.CreateTranslation(60, 10)); // A paint with an opacity merges the whole picture as one layer. canvas.DrawPicture(logo, Matrix3x2.CreateTranslation(240, 10), new SolidPaint(Rgba8.White) { Opacity = 0.4f }); // Drawn many times at one scale, a cached image is cheaper than replaying. for (int i = 0; i < 6; i++) { canvas.DrawPicture(logo, Matrix3x2.CreateTranslation(230 + (i * 25), 150), cacheAsImage: true); } } using Raster<Rgba8> icon = logo.ToRaster<Rgba8>(scale: 2); Drawing patterns A PicturePaint fills shapes with a drawing repeated by tile modes: the tiling patterns of PDF and SVG, and Skia's picture shader. The raster backend renders one tile at the scale it is drawn at and keeps it with the drawing, so a zoomed pattern stays sharp. // A tile drawn once as vectors fills any shape, repeated, and stays sharp when the canvas is zoomed. PictureRecorder tile = new(new RectF(0, 0, 20, 20)); tile.FillCircle(new Vector2(10, 10), 4, new Rgba8(220, 60, 60, 255)); tile.StrokeRect(new RectF(0.5f, 0.5f, 19, 19), new Stroke(1), new Rgba8(230, 230, 230, 255)); PicturePaint dots = new(tile.Finish(), TileMode.Repeat, TileMode.Repeat) { LocalMatrix = Matrix3x2.CreateRotation(MathF.PI / 8) }; using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = raster.CreateCanvas()) { canvas.FillRoundRect(new RoundRect(new RectF(10, 10, 280, 180), 24), dots); } Documents A canvas also carries what a document backend needs and pixels never show. DrawImage takes an EncodedImage, a file's bytes probed but not decoded, so a PDF page can embed a JPEG as it is while a raster canvas draws the decoded pixels. DrawImageMask paints through an image used as a mask, as PDF's stencil masks: its alpha, or for an image without alpha its gray level, is the coverage. LayerOptions.Knockout makes a layer a knockout group: each call inside it composites with what the layer started as and replaces earlier calls where it covers. DrawAnnotation marks a link to a URL, a named destination or a link to one (Annotation, as Skia's drawAnnotation), and BeginMarkedContent and EndMarkedContent bracket drawing with a MarkedContent tag for tagged PDF, with a structure node id, replacement text and alternate text. Backends get OnDrawEncodedImage, OnDrawAnnotation, OnBeginMarkedContent and OnEndMarkedContent; by default the image is decoded and the others do nothing. // A JPEG kept as its bytes: a PDF backend embeds them as they are; a raster canvas draws the decoded pixels. EncodedImage jpeg = EncodedImage.Load("photo.jpg"); canvas.DrawImage(jpeg, new RectF(20, 20, 128, 96)); // A 1-bit scan as a stencil: its white pixels paint in ink, its black ones leave the page as it is. using Raster<Gray8> scan = Raster.Create(32, 16, new Gray8(255)); canvas.DrawImageMask(scan, new RectF(160, 20, 64, 32), new Rgba8(20, 40, 120, 255), new SamplingOptions { Filter = ResampleFilter.Nearest }); // A knockout group: each shape composites with what the group started as, so overlapping translucent shapes do not darken. canvas.SaveLayer(new LayerOptions { Knockout = true }); canvas.FillCircle(new Vector2(180, 100), 20, new RgbaF32(1, 0, 0, 0.5f)); canvas.FillCircle(new Vector2(200, 100), 20, new RgbaF32(0, 0, 1, 0.5f)); canvas.Restore(); // A layout engine marks links, destinations and structure while it draws; pixels show none of it. canvas.BeginMarkedContent(new MarkedContent("P") { NodeId = 12 }); canvas.DrawAnnotation(new RectF(20, 130, 120, 16), Annotation.Url("https://example.com")); canvas.DrawAnnotation(new RectF(20, 150, 0, 0), Annotation.NamedDestination("chapter-2")); canvas.EndMarkedContent(); Saving drawings Picture.Save writes Egami's own documented binary format, .egdr, and Picture.Load reads it back as untrusted input, under the context's safety limits. Images are kept as PNG, text as its outlines. A drawing that holds C# code (a CustomPaint, or a layer's filter or soft mask) cannot be saved: Save throws and names the call. // Keep a picture in Egami's own documented format, and load it later; a loaded file is untrusted, so the context's // safety limits apply. using (FileStream file = File.Create("logo.egdr")) { logo.Save(file); } Picture loaded; using (FileStream file = File.OpenRead("logo.egdr")) { loaded = Picture.Load(file); } Path geometry Paths can be combined, outlined, dashed, measured, reshaped by effects, and read from and written as SVG path data. Every result is a new Path that keeps lines, quadratics and cubics where the input had them, so a vector backend writes it exactly. Boolean operations Op combines two areas with a PathOp: Union, Intersect, Difference, Xor or ReverseDifference (with shortcuts for the first four). Path.Combine takes any number of paths in one pass, applied left to right. Simplify returns the same area without overlaps or self-intersections. // A frame: one round rectangle cut out of another, kept as curves, so a PDF or SVG backend writes it exactly. Path frame = Path.RoundRect(new RoundRect(new RectF(0, 0, 200, 140), 24)) .Difference(Path.RoundRect(new RoundRect(new RectF(20, 20, 160, 100), 12))); // Many shapes in one pass, applied left to right; overlaps and self-intersections removed; an area grown by 4 units. Path dots = Path.Combine([Path.Circle(new Vector2(40, 40), 30), Path.Circle(new Vector2(80, 40), 30), Path.Circle(new Vector2(60, 75), 30)], PathOp.Union); Path clean = Path.Star(new Vector2(50, 50), 45, 20, 5).Simplify(); Path halo = dots.Inflate(4, LineJoin.Round); Each input keeps its fill rule; open contours count as closed. Results use NonZero, with outer contours clockwise on screen and holes counterclockwise, and no contours cross. Crossings are found on the curves themselves and cut exactly. The tolerance (0.05 units by default) is how close points must be to count as the same: ends and crossings within a tenth of it merge, and edges that run within it of each other merge, so nearly coincident outlines leave no slivers. Pass a smaller tolerance for geometry that will be drawn larger. Inflate grows an area by a distance, or shrinks it for a negative one, with a LineJoin at the corners. Outlines and dashes Stroke.ToPath returns the outline a pen draws, as a path to fill: filled at the given scale it gives exactly the stroke's pixels, and simplify: true removes its overlaps for export or hit testing. Stroke.Dash takes a DashPattern of absolute on and off lengths and a phase, as PDF, SVG and Skia define them; Scaled turns lengths given in widths into units. // A dashed route: the pattern travels with the stroke, so a PDF backend writes [8 4] 0 d instead of hundreds of pieces. Path route = new PathBuilder().MoveTo(10, 90).CubicTo(60, 0, 140, 160, 190, 60).ToPath(); Stroke dashed = new(3) { Cap = LineCap.Round, Dash = new DashPattern([8, 4]) }; using Raster<Rgba8> map = Raster.Create(200, 120, Rgba8.White); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = map.CreateCanvas()) { canvas.StrokePath(route, dashed, new Rgba8(200, 60, 30, 255)); } // The outline the stroke fills, as a path: for hit testing, or to export without strokes. Path outline = dashed.ToPath(route, simplify: true); A backend receives the pattern as data, so PDF can write d and SVG stroke-dasharray; the raster backend cuts the path into dashes along its curves before outlining it. Measuring PathMeasure lists each contour as a ContourMeasure: its Length, and the position, tangent and placing matrix at any distance. GetSegment returns a piece of the contour that keeps its curves; AddSegment chains pieces into one contour. Lengths are integrated, not taken from a flattened outline, and are exact to about 1e-4 units. // Measure a path: its length, and a point and direction at any distance, curves included. Path route = new PathBuilder().MoveTo(10, 90).CubicTo(60, 0, 140, 160, 190, 60).ToPath(); PathMeasure measure = new(route); ContourMeasure contour = measure.Contours[0]; Vector2 halfway = contour.GetPosition(contour.Length / 2); Vector2 heading = contour.GetTangent(contour.Length / 2); // An arrowhead placed at the end, turned along the path, and the middle third as a path of its own (still a cubic). Path arrow = Path.Polygon([new(-6, -4), new(0, 0), new(-6, 4)]).Transform(contour.GetMatrix(contour.Length)); Path middle = contour.GetSegment(contour.Length / 3, 2 * contour.Length / 3); Path effects A PathEffect turns one path into another: Dash, Corner (rounded corners), Trim, Jitter, Stamp (a shape repeated along the path, placed by a StampStyle), Hatch and HatchPath (lines or shapes on a lattice inside an area). Then and Plus combine them. path.Apply(effect) applies one; Stroke.Effect has the canvas apply it before dashing and stroking. // A hand-drawn chart line: jittered the same way on every run, then its corners rounded. Path data = Path.Polygon([new(10, 80), new(50, 30), new(90, 60), new(130, 20), new(170, 50)], close: false); PathEffect sketchy = PathEffect.Jitter(segmentLength: 6, deviation: 1.5f, seed: 7).Then(PathEffect.Corner(3)); using Raster<Rgba8> chart = Raster.Create(180, 100, Rgba8.White); using (RasterCanvas<Rgba8> canvas = chart.CreateCanvas()) { canvas.StrokePath(data, new Stroke(2) { Effect = sketchy }, new Rgba8(40, 40, 40, 255)); // Dots along the line, and hatching inside a circle. canvas.FillPath(data.Apply(PathEffect.Stamp(Path.Circle(Vector2.Zero, 2), advance: 12, style: StampStyle.Translate)), Rgba8.Black); canvas.FillPath(Path.Circle(new Vector2(150, 75), 20).Apply(PathEffect.Hatch(Matrix3x2.CreateScale(1, 5) * Matrix3x2.CreateRotation(0.6f), width: 1)), Rgba8.Black); } // A line that draws itself: trim it to a growing fraction of its length, frame by frame. Path frame30 = data.Apply(PathEffect.Trim(0, 0.3f)); Jitter hashes its seed with the contour and the point, so a path jitters the same way on every thread and machine. SVG path data Path.ParseSvg reads the d attribute grammar of SVG 1.1 and 2; TryParseSvg returns false instead of throwing SvgPathException, and lenient: true keeps every complete command before the first error. ToSvg writes path data, absolute or relative, compact or spaced, to a precision (SvgPathFormat). // An icon from SVG path data, drawn four times larger, and written back as compact relative data. Path heart = Path.ParseSvg("M12 21.35l-1.45-1.32C5.4 15.36 2 12.28 2 8.5 2 5.42 4.42 3 7.5 3c1.74 0 3.41.81 4.5 2.09" + "C13.09 3.81 14.76 3 16.5 3 19.58 3 22 5.42 22 8.5c0 3.78-3.4 6.86-8.55 11.54L12 21.35z"); string d = heart.Transform(Matrix3x2.CreateScale(4)).ToSvg(new SvgPathFormat { Relative = true, Compact = true }); // Untrusted data: TryParseSvg says whether it is valid; lenient keeps what comes before an error, as browsers draw it. bool valid = Path.TryParseSvg("M0 0 L10 10 L20", out Path? strict); Path drawn = Path.ParseSvg("M0 0 L10 10 L20", lenient: true); try { Path.ParseSvg("M0 0 X"); } catch (SvgPathException e) { Console.WriteLine($"{e.Problem} at character {e.Position}"); } In an operation chain Draw adds a step that draws on each frame with a canvas over the step's pixels (DrawingExtensions). // Draw as a step in an operation chain: inside Within the canvas covers the area, with its origin at the area's corner. raster.Apply(ops => ops .Draw(canvas => canvas.FillRect(new RectF(0, 0, 300, 200), new Rgba8(240, 240, 255, 255))) .Within(new Rect(100, 50, 100, 100), area => area.Draw(canvas => canvas.FillCircle(new Vector2(50, 50), 40, Rgba8.Red))), Ct); // On an animation the step runs once per frame, and can be told which. raster.Apply(ops => ops.Draw((canvas, frame) => canvas.FillCircle(new Vector2(20 + (frame * 4), 20), 10, Rgba8.Black)), Ct); Printing inks InkCanvas draws into an InkRaster's plates instead of RGB pixels. It shares the raster canvas's rasterizer, clips and layers, so shapes, strokes and text cover the same pixels; where the RGB canvas blends colours, it sets each plate. Ink paints print their inks by name, and RGB colours, gradients and images convert into the process inks as InkCanvasOptions says (the RGB encoding, intent and black point compensation). InkCanvas.Clear(InkColor.None) leaves blank paper. // Plates for CMYK and a spot; an RGB photo converts through FOGRA39, the logo prints on its own plate. Egami.Colors.InkSet inks = Egami.Colors.InkSet.FromProfile(Egami.Colors.ColorProfile.Fogra39) .WithSpot("PANTONE 186 C", Egami.Colors.InkAppearance.Cmyk(0, 1, 0.81f, 0.04f)); using InkRaster page = new(inks, 300, 200); using (InkCanvas canvas = new(page)) { canvas.Clear(Egami.Colors.InkColor.None); // paper canvas.FillRect(new RectF(0, 0, 300, 120), new Rgba8(80, 140, 200, 255)); // RGB: converted to CMYK canvas.FillCircle(new Vector2(150, 100), 40, new SolidPaint(Egami.Colors.InkColor.Spot(inks[4], 1))); } Other backends Canvas is abstract. Each public call is checked, tracked (transform, clip bounds, save stack) and then ends in one protected hook, so a backend sees shapes and pens as data: a PDF page can write a rectangle as re and a pen as w, J, j and M. Hooks a backend leaves alone have defaults: rectangles, round rectangles and ovals become paths. A backend that cannot express a call (a blend mode its format lacks, a CustomPaint, a filtered layer) can draw it into pixels with RasterizeFallback, which returns a FallbackImage. Layers reach a backend through OnSaveLayer and OnRestoreLayer; a PDF page would write a transparency group with its opacity, blend mode and soft mask. OnDrawMesh and OnDrawPatch let a PDF page write shading types 4 to 7, OnDrawPicture a form XObject drawn once and referenced each time, and OnDrawImageLattice and OnDrawAtlas images per cell or sprite; by default meshes go through the raster fallback, patches become meshes, and the others become images and meshes. // A backend overrides hooks; the base class has already checked the arguments and tracks the transform and clip bounds. // This one writes SVG elements, keeping rectangles as rectangles and strokes as stroke settings. public sealed class SvgCanvas(float width, float height) : Canvas(width, height) { private readonly System.Text.StringBuilder _body = new(); public string Document => $"<svg xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\" width=\"{Width}\" height=\"{Height}\">{_body}</svg>"; protected override void OnDrawRect(RectF rect, Stroke? stroke, Paint paint) => _body.Append(FormattableString.Invariant($"<rect x=\"{rect.X}\" y=\"{rect.Y}\" width=\"{rect.Width}\" height=\"{rect.Height}\" {Style(stroke, paint)}/>")); protected override void OnDrawPath(Path path, Stroke? stroke, Paint paint) { System.Text.StringBuilder d = new(); int p = 0; foreach (PathVerb verb in path.Verbs) { int count = verb switch { PathVerb.Quad => 2, PathVerb.Cubic => 3, PathVerb.Close => 0, _ => 1 }; d.Append(verb switch { PathVerb.Move => "M", PathVerb.Line => "L", PathVerb.Quad => "Q", PathVerb.Cubic => "C", _ => "Z" }); foreach (Vector2 point in path.Points.Slice(p, count)) { d.Append(FormattableString.Invariant($"{point.X},{point.Y} ")); } p += count; } _body.Append(System.Globalization.CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, $"<path d=\"{d}\" {Style(stroke, paint)}/>"); } protected override void OnClipPath(Path path, ClipOp op, bool antialias) { // Clips would become <clipPath> elements; this sketch leaves them out. } protected override void OnDrawImage(Raster image, RectF source, RectF destination, SamplingOptions sampling, Paint? paint) { // An image would be embedded as a PNG data URI. } private string Style(Stroke? stroke, Paint paint) { Rgba8 c = paint is SolidPaint solid ? solid.Color.ToRgba8() : Rgba8.Black; string color = $"#{c.R:x2}{c.G:x2}{c.B:x2}"; string transform = Matrix.IsIdentity ? "" : FormattableString.Invariant($" transform=\"matrix({Matrix.M11} {Matrix.M12} {Matrix.M21} {Matrix.M22} {Matrix.M31} {Matrix.M32})\""); return stroke is null ? $"fill=\"{color}\"{transform}" : FormattableString.Invariant($"fill=\"none\" stroke=\"{color}\" stroke-width=\"{stroke.Width}\" stroke-linecap=\"{stroke.Cap.ToString().ToLowerInvariant()}\"{transform}"); } } Accuracy and speed Fills are within a mean level of SkiaSharp's and closer than SkiaSharp's to the exact covered area. Boolean operations, outlines, dashes, effects and SVG parsing give paths within a mean level of SkiaSharp's, and measured lengths agree within 1e-3. The figures are in the 2.6.1 and 2.6.2 release notes.

articles/guides/edges-and-morphology.htm.title: Edges and morphology | Egami
articles/guides/edges-and-morphology.htm.summary: Edges and morphology Edge operators measure how fast the image changes at each pixel; Canny's detector turns that into thin edge lines; and morphology grows, shrinks and cleans up shapes by taking the maximum or minimum over a neighbourhood. All of them keep the image's size, so they work inside Within scopes. Operation Does Edges(op, grayscale) The gradient magnitude of a fixed kernel, 0 to 1; gray by default, or per channel CannyEdges(sigma, low, high) Thin white edges on black, as ImageMagick's -canny Morphology(op, shape, iterations) Dilate, erode, open, close, gradient, top hat or bottom hat over a StructuringElement Dilate(radius), Erode(radius) The maximum or minimum over a square; Dilate(rx, ry) and Erode(rx, ry) over a rectangle Find edges using Raster edges = photo.Derive(o => o.Edges(), Ct); // Sobel, gray, 0 to 1 using Raster crisp = photo.Derive(o => o.Edges(EdgeOperator.Scharr), Ct); // rotation-steady using Raster colored = photo.Derive(o => o.Edges(EdgeOperator.Sobel, grayscale: false), Ct); // per channel using Raster lines = photo.Derive(o => o.Blur(1).Edges(EdgeOperator.Laplacian3x3), Ct); // second derivative EdgeOperator picks the kernels. Every operator is scaled so a full black-to-white step gives 1, so their results can be compared and thresholded alike. Operator Kernels Notes Sobel (default) 3 × 3 pair, weights 1, 2, 1 The usual choice Scharr 3 × 3 pair, weights 3, 10, 3 Its strength depends least on the edge's direction Prewitt 3 × 3 pair, weights 1, 1, 1 RobertsCross 2 × 2 diagonal differences Sharpest and noisiest; the pixel and the one below right Kirsch, Robinson Eight 3 × 3 compass kernels The strongest of the eight directions Laplacian3x3, Laplacian5x5 One kernel, absolute value Second derivative: edges come out as double lines LaplacianOfGaussian 5 × 5, absolute value A Laplacian smoothed against noise Gradient pairs write sqrt(gx² + gy²); the compass operators keep the largest of their eight responses. The edges are measured on premultiplied values, so transparent areas count as black, and alpha is kept. With grayscale: true (the default) the pixels are first reduced to Rec. 709 luma and the magnitude is written as gray; with false red, green and blue each get their own. Past the border the edge pixel repeats. A selection from Canny // Thin white edges on black. A gray raster works as a Mask as it is; an RGBA one needs MaskChannel.Luminance, // because a Mask of a raster with alpha reads its alpha. using Raster<Gray8> edges = Raster.Load<Gray8>("duck.png"); edges.Apply(o => o.CannyEdges(sigma: 1.4f).Dilate(1), Ct); // thin edges, thickened photo.Apply(o => o.Within(new Mask(edges), s => s.FillColor(Rgba8.Red)), Ct); // paint over them CannyEdges runs the four steps of Canny's detector: a Gaussian blur of the luma with standard deviation sigma, the gradient from Canny's own 2 × 2 first differences, non-maximum suppression (a pixel is kept only if neither neighbour across its edge is stronger), and hysteresis: pixels at least high times the image's strongest gradient start edges, and edges follow 8-connected pixels down to low times it. The output is white edges, one pixel wide, on black, with alpha kept. The parameters mean what ImageMagick's -canny 0x{sigma}+{low × 100}%+{high × 100}% means, and the edge maps match it pixel for pixel except where ImageMagick stops a trace early: it keeps its trace stack in one image row, so a trace deeper than the image is wide ends part way. Egami follows every connected pixel, so it finds the same edges plus the rest of those traces. A gray edge map is a Mask as it is. A color raster used as a Mask is read by its alpha, so for an RGBA edge map pass MaskChannel.Luminance: new Mask(edges, Channel: MaskChannel.Luminance). Clean a scanned form with Close // Close removes dark specks smaller than the shape (dust and toner dots on the paper) and keeps strokes wider than it; // Open does the opposite, for light pinholes in dark areas. using Raster<Gray8> scan = Raster.Load<Gray8>("scan.tif"); scan.Apply(o => o.Morphology(MorphologyOp.Close, StructuringElement.Disk(1)), Ct); // The outlines of shapes, and the light details smaller than a disk. using Raster outlines = scan.Derive(o => o.Morphology(MorphologyOp.Gradient, StructuringElement.Square(1)), Ct); using Raster details = scan.Derive(o => o.Morphology(MorphologyOp.TopHat, StructuringElement.Disk(5)), Ct); Morphology is flat: dilation takes each channel's maximum over the shape, erosion the minimum, on the stored values, so 8 and 16-bit results are exact. The rest combine them: MorphologyOp Is Use Dilate Maximum Grow light areas, close dark gaps Erode Minimum Shrink light areas, remove light specks Open Erode, then dilate Remove light details smaller than the shape; never brightens Close Dilate, then erode Remove dark details smaller than the shape; never darkens Gradient Dilate minus erode Outlines as wide as the shape TopHat Image minus its open The light details the open removed BottomHat Its close minus the image The dark details the close removed iterations repeats each dilation and erosion: Open with 2 erodes twice, then dilates twice, as ImageMagick's Open:2. Alpha is dilated and eroded with the color, so a logo's shape grows and shrinks with it; Gradient, TopHat and BottomHat keep alpha, since a difference of alpha would make an opaque image transparent. Past the border the edge pixel repeats, as ImageMagick does. Shapes StructuringElement disk = StructuringElement.Disk(4); // x² + y² ≤ 16, ImageMagick's Disk:4 StructuringElement diamond = StructuringElement.Diamond(3); // |x| + |y| ≤ 3 StructuringElement plus = StructuringElement.Cross(2); // ImageMagick's Plus:2 StructuringElement corner = StructuringElement.FromMask( new[,] { { true, true, true }, { true, false, false }, { true, false, false }, }, new Point(0, 0)); // [y, x] cells; the origin sits on the pixel using Raster rounded = photo.Derive(o => o.Morphology(MorphologyOp.Open, disk, iterations: 2), Ct); The factories make ImageMagick's kernels of the same name, so -morphology Dilate Disk:4 and Morphology(MorphologyOp.Dilate, StructuringElement.Disk(4)) give identical pixels. Cross(r) is ImageMagick's Plus:r. Shape Cells Square(r) The (2r + 1) square Rectangle(rx, ry) The (2rx + 1) × (2ry + 1) rectangle, Skia's dilate and erode radii Disk(r) x² + y² ≤ r² Diamond(r) |x| + |y| ≤ r Cross(r) The row and column through the origin, 2r + 1 long FromMask(cells, origin) Any set of cells, [y, x], with the origin on the pixel being computed Erosion reads the cells as offsets from the pixel and dilation reads them mirrored, as ImageMagick does, so Open and Close work as expected for lopsided shapes too. Squares and rectangles cost the same per pixel whatever their size (van Herk and Gil-Werman's running maximum down the columns); other shapes cost in proportion to their height. using Raster grown = photo.Derive(o => o.Dilate(3), Ct); // light areas grow 3 px: a 7 × 7 square using Raster shrunk = photo.Derive(o => o.Erode(3), Ct); // light areas shrink 3 px using Raster wide = photo.Derive(o => o.Dilate(6, 1), Ct); // 13 × 3, as Skia's dilate radii

articles/guides/effects.html.title: Effects | Egami
articles/guides/effects.html.summary: Effects The editor's effects menu: a vignette, glows and bloom, pixelate, oil paint, Kuwahara, spread, drop and inner shadows. Every effect keeps the image's size, except DropShadow, which by default grows the canvas to hold the shadow. Operation Does Vignette(radius, softness, color, center) Darkens or tints outside an ellipse fitted to the image, with a soft edge: ImageMagick's -vignette shape Glow(sigma, color, spread, inner) An outer glow behind the alpha shape, or an inner glow inside it, as an editor's layer style Bloom(threshold, sigma, intensity) Bright areas blurred and screened back in linear light: the photographic glow Pixelate(cellSize, origin) Each cell becomes its premultiplied average OilPaint(radius, levels) Each pixel becomes a pixel of the most common intensity in its square: ImageMagick's -paint Kuwahara(radius, sigma) Each pixel takes its value from the least varied of four squares: ImageMagick's -kuwahara Spread(radius, seed) Each pixel takes a random neighbour's value within the radius: ImageMagick's -spread DropShadow(dx, dy, sigma, color, options) Skia's DropShadow: the alpha moved, blurred and colored, with the image on top InnerShadow(dx, dy, sigma, color) A shadow inside the alpha shape, cast by everything outside it, as an editor's layer style Vignette, glow and bloom // Darken the corners: the edge of the ellipse passes through the corners and fades over half the radius. using Raster dark = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Vignette(), Ct); // A tighter, softer, warm-white vignette, off-center toward the subject. using Raster light = photo.Derive( ops => ops.Vignette(0.6f, softness: 0.8f, color: new Rgba8(255, 245, 230, 255), center: new System.Numerics.Vector2(photo.Width * 0.4f, photo.Height * 0.5f)), Ct); radius is a fraction of the half-diagonal: 1 puts the edge of the ellipse through the corners. The ellipse has the image's proportions and its center is the image's middle unless center moves it. softness is the share of the radius the edge fades over. The fade is the profile of a blurred edge, computed per pixel from the distance to the ellipse, so it costs the same at any softness. While the ellipse stays inside the image the result is within 5 levels of ImageMagick's -vignette (which blurs a drawn ellipse, so it bends where the ellipse leaves the image). The color is mixed source-over on premultiplied values; its alpha is the vignette's strength. // A soft yellow glow around the badge, behind it; spread hardens it before it fades. using Raster outer = logo.Derive(ops => ops.Glow(8, new Rgba8(255, 210, 0, 230), spread: 0.3f), Ct); // A white glow coming in from the badge's edges, inside it only. using Raster inner = logo.Derive(ops => ops.Glow(5, Rgba8.White, inner: true), Ct); Glow is built from Egami's own steps and gives exactly what the same chain gives by hand: a layer that is the color with the image's alpha (or 1 − alpha for an inner glow), blurred with BlurMethod.Fast, its alpha multiplied by 1 / (1 − spread) and by the color's alpha; then the image is drawn over the layer, or the layer drawn over the image with BlendMode.SourceAtop so it stays inside the shape. An opaque image has no edge to glow from: glow a logo or a cut-out. // Highlights above 80% bleed light into their surroundings, added in linear light as a lens does. photo.Apply(ops => ops.Bloom(threshold: 0.8f, sigma: 12, intensity: 1.5f), Ct); Bloom is a chain too: each channel's part above threshold (stored values), stretched to 0..1 and scaled by intensity, blurred in linear light with BlurMethod.Fast, and screened onto the image in linear light, so light adds as it does in a lens. Pixelate, oil paint, Kuwahara and spread // 12-pixel cells, each the average of what it covers. using Raster blocks = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Pixelate(12), Ct); Cells start at origin and repeat both ways; cells cut by the image's edges average what they hold. The average is taken on premultiplied values, so transparent pixels do not darken a cell; for Rgba8 and Bgra8 it is computed in whole numbers and rounded once, so it is exact. using Raster painted = photo.Derive(ops => ops.OilPaint(radius: 4, levels: 20), Ct); using Raster magick = photo.Derive(ops => ops.OilPaint(3, levels: 256), Ct); // ImageMagick's -paint 3, pixel for pixel OilPaint follows ImageMagick's -paint: a (2r + 1) square window, intensity in 256 bins (fewer with levels), and the output is a whole pixel of the most common bin, picked by ImageMagick's scan order. With 256 levels the result equals ImageMagick's pixel for pixel at 8 bits; the default 20 levels make broader strokes. The histogram slides along each row. // Flattens texture into patches while keeping edges; a small blur first, as ImageMagick's -kuwahara 4x1. using Raster smooth = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Kuwahara(4, sigma: 1), Ct); Kuwahara follows ImageMagick's -kuwahara radius x sigma: an optional Gaussian blur with ImageMagick's kernel (σ, out to the radius), then of the four (r + 1) squares with the pixel at a corner, the one whose luma varies least gives the pixel its value, sampled at its middle. Summed-area tables make the cost independent of the radius. Results are within a few levels of ImageMagick's, where near-equal variances may pick another square. // Frosted glass: every pixel takes a neighbour's value up to 3 pixels away; the same seed gives the same result. using Raster frosted = photo.Derive(ops => ops.Spread(3, seed: 42), Ct); Spread moves no pixel further than the radius. The offsets come from a hash of the seed and the position (SplitMix64), so a seed gives the same pixels on any machine, at any thread count and inside a scope. Drop shadows // Skia's DropShadow: 6 px right and down, blurred with sigma 8, black at 55%; the canvas grows to hold the shadow. using Raster shadowed = logo.Derive(ops => ops.DropShadow(6, 6, 8, new Rgba8(0, 0, 0, 140)), Ct); // Keep the size, or keep only the shadow (as Skia's DropShadowOnly and ImageMagick's -shadow). using Raster same = logo.Derive(ops => ops.DropShadow(4, 4, 3, Rgba8.Black, new DropShadowOptions { Expand = false }), Ct); using Raster shadow = logo.Derive(ops => ops.DropShadow(0, 10, 12, Rgba8.Black, new DropShadowOptions { ShadowOnly = true, SigmaY = 6 }), Ct); The parameters mean what Skia's do: the offset moves the shadow, sigma is the Gaussian's standard deviation (σx, with SigmaY for a different σy), and the color's alpha is the shadow's opacity. Fractional offsets move the shadow by fractions. Expand (the default) grows the canvas by 3σ plus the offset on the sides the shadow reaches past the image, so the shadow is never cut off; the image moves right and down by what was added on the left and top. ImageMagick's -shadow adds round(2σ) on every side instead, which cuts about 2% of a shadow's edge. A growing step cannot run inside Within; with Expand = false the size stays and it can. Method is BlurMethod.Fast by default, whose cost does not grow with sigma; BlurMethod.Exact uses the Gaussian kernel and is within a level of the same chain built from Pad, Offset, ColorMatrix, Convolve and DrawImage. Inner shadows // A shadow inside the badge, cast from up and left, as a pressed button looks. using Raster pressed = logo.Derive(ops => ops.InnerShadow(2, 3, 3, new Rgba8(0, 0, 0, 140)), Ct); InnerShadow is the chain written by hand: the color with 1 − alpha, moved by the offset rounded to whole pixels with the uncovered strips counted as outside, blurred fast, faded by the color's alpha and drawn source-atop. With glows and drop shadows it covers an editor's layer styles, and on a canvas layer it is a LayerOptions.Filter. Cookbook A drop shadow for a logo // A logo on a page: a soft shadow under it, then the result flattened onto white for a JPEG. logo.Apply(ops => ops .DropShadow(5, 7, 6, new Rgba8(0, 0, 0, 110)) .Flatten(Rgba8.White), Ct); logo.Save("logo-shadow.jpg"); Blur a face // Hide a face: pixelate only the rectangle around it, with the grid starting at its corner so cells line up with it. Rect face = new(100, 40, 72, 64); photo.Apply(ops => ops.Within(face, o => o.Pixelate(12, new Point(face.X, face.Y))), Ct); Inside Within, cells stay on the grid that origin sets, and each cell averages all of its pixels, including those outside the rectangle, so the result inside equals pixelating the whole image there. Start the grid at the rectangle's corner so whole cells fill it. An oil-paint look // A painted look: a light blur to calm noise, the oil paint, then a touch more saturation and a vignette. using Raster painting = photo.Derive(ops => ops .Blur(0.8f) .OilPaint(radius: 4, levels: 24) .Saturation(1.15f) .Vignette(0.9f, softness: 0.6f), Ct); painting.Save("painting.png");

articles/guides/egdr-format.html.title: The .egdr format | Egami
articles/guides/egdr-format.html.summary: The .egdr format An Egami drawing file holds a recorded Picture: the calls a PictureRecorder kept, and the images, paths and nested drawings they use. Picture.Save writes it and Picture.Load reads it; this page is the format's specification, version 1.1, for anyone writing a reader or writer of their own. See Drawing for the API. Layout All numbers are little-endian. u8, u16 and u32 are unsigned integers of 1, 2 and 4 bytes, i32 a signed 4-byte integer, f32 an IEEE 754 single, and bool a u8 that is 0 or 1. A file is a 12-byte header followed by chunks: Bytes Field Value 0 to 7 Signature 89 45 47 44 52 0D 0A 1A (\x89EGDR\r\n\x1A, after PNG's: it catches text-mode transfers and stops type) 8 to 9 Major version u16, 1. A reader rejects a major version it does not know. 10 to 11 Minor version u16, 1. A reader accepts any minor version of its major version. Each chunk is a 4-byte ASCII type, a u32 payload length, and the payload. A reader skips the payload of a chunk type it does not know, which is how later minor versions add to the format. The chunk types of version 1.1: Type Payload Defines IMAG A PNG file The next image, numbered from 0 PATH A path, below The next path, numbered from 0 DRAW A drawing, below The next drawing, numbered from 0 ENCI An encoded image file (a JPEG, a PNG, any format Egami reads), its bytes as they were given The next encoded image, numbered from 0 INKS Ink entries, below (since 1.1) Nothing: it annotates the DRAW chunk right after it DEND Empty The end. The file's drawing is the last DRAW chunk before it. A chunk refers to images, paths and drawings by number, and only to ones defined by earlier chunks, so a file is read in one pass and cannot hold a cycle. A writer writes each image, path and drawing once, however often it is used. Bytes after DEND are ignored. Paths Field Type Fill rule u8: 0 nonzero, 1 even-odd Verb count u32 Verbs u8 each: 0 move, 1 line, 2 quadratic, 3 cubic, 4 close Point count u32, the sum of the verbs' points: 1 for a move or a line, 2 for a quadratic, 3 for a cubic, 0 for a close Points f32 x and y each, finite A line, quadratic or cubic must follow a move, or another segment, in its contour: after a close, a new contour starts with a move. Drawings Field Type Bounds Rectangle Call count u32 Calls One after another, each an opcode u8 and its operands The payload must end exactly after the last call. A rectangle is four f32: x, y, width and height. A matrix is six f32: M11, M12, M21, M22, M31, M32, as .NET's Matrix3x2, which maps a row vector (x, y, 1). A color is four f32: red, green, blue and straight alpha, encoded (sRGB) values from 0 to 1. A point is two f32. A string is a u32 byte count and that many bytes of UTF-8. A round rectangle is a rectangle and the x and y radii of its corners: top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left. An enum is a u8 with the value Egami's enum of that name has. Every number must be finite. Opcode Call Operands 1 Save None 2 Restore (also ends a layer) None 3 SaveLayer Opacity f32, BlendMode, a flags u8 (1 isolated, 2 knockout), has-bounds bool, bounds rectangle if it has them 4 SetMatrix Matrix 5 ClipRect Rectangle, ClipOp, antialias bool 6 ClipRoundRect Round rectangle, ClipOp, antialias bool 7 ClipPath Path number u32, ClipOp, antialias bool 8 DrawPaint Paint 9 DrawRect Rectangle, has-stroke bool, stroke if it has one, paint 10 DrawRoundRect Round rectangle, has-stroke bool, stroke, paint 11 DrawOval Rectangle, has-stroke bool, stroke, paint 12 DrawPath Path number u32, has-stroke bool, stroke, paint 13 DrawPoints PointMode, count u32, points, stroke, paint 14 DrawImage Image number u32, source rectangle (inside the image), destination rectangle, sampling, has-paint bool, paint 15 DrawLattice Image number, lattice, destination rectangle, sampling, has-paint bool, paint 16 DrawAtlas Image number, count u32, that many sprite transforms (four f32: ScaleCos, ScaleSin, Tx, Ty), that many source rectangles, has-colors bool, that many colors if it has them, BlendMode, sampling, has-paint bool, paint 17 DrawMesh Mesh, paint, BlendMode, stops 18 DrawPatch Patch, paint, BlendMode, stops 19 DrawPicture Picture number u32, matrix, has-paint bool, paint, cache-as-image bool 20 DrawEncodedImage Encoded image number u32, source rectangle (inside the image), destination rectangle, sampling, has-paint bool, paint 21 DrawAnnotation Area rectangle, AnnotationKind, the URL or name as a string 22 BeginMarkedContent Tag as a string, a flags u8 (1 node id, 2 actual text, 4 alternate text), then the node id i32 and the two strings for the flags set 23 EndMarkedContent None; every BeginMarkedContent in a drawing has its EndMarkedContent in the same drawing 24 DrawImageMask Image number u32, destination rectangle, sampling, paint Coordinates are those the recorder's hooks received: local coordinates under the matrix last set. Replaying a drawing sets each recorded matrix after the matrix the drawing is replayed under. Text is written as DrawPath of its outlines, filled, since a file holds no fonts. A stroke is width f32 (0 for a hairline), LineCap, LineJoin, miter limit f32, has-dash bool, and for a dash an interval count u32, the intervals as f32 and the phase f32. Path effects never reach a file: the canvas applies them before the hook. Sampling is ResampleFilter, ColorSpace, EdgeMode and the background color as four u8 (red, green, blue, alpha). Stops are a count u32, then each stop's offset f32 (0 to 1) and color. A lattice is the x division count u32 and the divisions as i32, the same for y, has-bounds bool and the bounds as four i32 (x, y, width, height), has-kinds bool and one LatticeCellKind per cell, has-colors bool and one color per cell. There are (x divisions + 1) · (y divisions + 1) cells, row by row. A mesh is MeshMode, the vertex count u32, the positions, a flags u8 (1 colors, 2 texture coordinates, 4 values, 8 indices), then for each flag set in that order: a color per vertex, a point per vertex, an f32 per vertex, and an index count u32 with that many i32 indices, each below the vertex count. Colors and values are not both present, and a mesh with values has at least one stop. A patch is PatchKind (0 Coons, 1 tensor), its 12 or 16 points, a flags u8 (1 colors, 2 texture coordinates, 4 values), then four corner colors, four corner points and four corner f32 values for the flags set, in that order. Paints A paint is its kind u8, the fields every paint has, then its own: Field Type BlendMode u8 Opacity f32, 0 to 1 Flags u8: 1 antialias, 2 dither, 4 has a mask blur Local matrix Matrix Mask blur Sigma f32 and BlurStyle, when flag 4 is set Kind Paint Own fields 1 SolidPaint Color 2 LinearGradient Start point, end point, gradient fields 3 RadialGradient Center point, radius f32, gradient fields 4 ConicalGradient Start point, start radius f32, end point, end radius f32, gradient fields 5 SweepGradient Center point, start angle f32, end angle f32, gradient fields 6 ImagePaint Image number u32, TileMode x, TileMode y, sampling 7 NoisePaint NoisePaintKind, base frequency x and y f32, octaves i32, seed i32, has-tile bool, tile width and height i32 8 BlendPaint Destination paint, source paint, BlendMode 9 ColorMatrixPaint Source paint, the 20 matrix values f32, row by row 10 PicturePaint Picture number u32, TileMode x, TileMode y, tile rectangle The gradient fields are the stops (at least one), TileMode, a flags u8 (1 extend start, 2 extend end, 4 premultiplied), InterpolationSpace and HueMethod. A simplex noise uses its x frequency. A CustomPaint runs C# and has no kind: saving a drawing that uses one throws, and so does saving a layer with a filter, a backdrop or a soft mask, naming the call. Inks A drawing made with ink colours (InkColor), overprint or layers with a ColorSpace keeps them in an INKS chunk written just before its DRAW chunk, which holds every colour as its sRGB appearance. A 1.0 reader skips INKS and draws the appearances; an ink canvas reading 1.1 prints the inks. The payload is an entry count u32, then each entry: the byte offset u32 in the next DRAW chunk's payload that it is about, its kind u8, a data length u32 and the data. Each offset appears once and must be the start of what its kind names: Kind At Data 1 A color: a SolidPaint's, a stop's, a mesh vertex's or a patch corner's An ink colour 2 A paint's kind u8 Overprint u8: 1 on, 2 nonzero (absent means off) 3 A SaveLayer opcode The layer's colour space as an ICC profile An ink colour is a flags u8 (1 for a process CMYK colour, whose four inks are Cyan, Magenta, Yellow and Black in that order), an ink count u32, and per ink: its name as a string, ColorantKind u8 (0 process, 1 spot, 2 technical), an appearance u8 (0 none, 1 CMYK, 2 sRGB, 3 Lab D50) with four f32 when there is one (RGB and Lab leave the fourth 0), and its tint f32. A mesh's or patch's vertices have inks all or none. Reading untrusted files Egami's reader checks every count against the bytes left before it allocates, puts every value through the constructors that check it, reads images with the PNG reader under the context's SafetyLimits, counts what it decodes toward MaxTotalBytes, and limits drawings to 64 levels of nesting and 50 million calls with nested drawings expanded, so a small file cannot ask for an exponential replay. Any failure is an EgamiException. The reader has a fuzz target, egdr.

articles/guides/extending.html.title: Custom operations and formats | Egami
articles/guides/extending.html.summary: Custom operations and formats Everything here uses only Egami's public API; Egami's own test suite has an outside project that does each of these things. Operations An operation implements IRasterOperation: it says what size it makes and fills the destination rows. /// <summary>Swaps red and blue, in parallel bands of rows.</summary> public sealed class SwapRedBlue : IRasterOperation { public Size OutputSize(Size input) => input; public void Run<TPixel>(OperationInput<TPixel> input) where TPixel : unmanaged, IPixelType<TPixel> { input.ForEachBand((start, end) => { for (int y = start; y < end; y++) { Span<TPixel> source = input.Source.Row(y); Span<TPixel> destination = input.Destination.Row(y); for (int x = 0; x < source.Length; x++) { Vector4 v = source[x].ToScaled(); destination[x] = TPixel.FromScaled(new Vector4(v.Z, v.Y, v.X, v.W)); } } }); } } image.Apply(ops => ops.Fit(100, 100).Add(new SwapRedBlue()), TestContext.Current.CancellationToken); OutputSize is asked while the chain is planned, before any pixel changes. Throw there for arguments that cannot work. When the size stays the same, Source and Destination may be the same plane (IsInPlace); read a row before you write it. ForEachBand runs bands of rows on up to EgamiContext.MaxParallelism threads and checks the cancellation token between bands. A step that changes the size updates the EXIF dimensions and drops the thumbnail, as the built-in resizes do. TPixel.Layout tells you the pixel type, so you can take a fast path for the types you know and fall back to ToScaled and FromScaled for the rest. Check Layout.Alpha before you assume straight alpha. To run a chain on part of a larger picture, such as a tile or a canvas layer, pad the part by how far the chain reads: RasterOps.Reach returns that as an OperationReach, or null when a step reads the whole image (a resize, a turn, a custom operation). // How far a chain reads around each pixel: run it on a part of a picture padded by this much, and the part comes out as it // would in the whole picture. OperationReach? reach = RasterOps.Reach(ops => ops.Blur(3).Glow(4, Rgba8.White)); if (reach is OperationReach r) { Console.WriteLine($"pad by {r.X} × {r.Y}"); } // A resize reads the whole image: its reach is unknown. Assert.Null(RasterOps.Reach(ops => ops.Resize(100, 100))); Formats A format is a FormatInfo: a name, extensions, a signature check, a reader and a writer. /// <summary>A minimal format: "RAW8", width and height as big-endian numbers, then RGBA rows.</summary> public static class Raw8Format { public static FormatInfo Info { get; } = new() { Name = "RAW8", Extensions = ["raw8"], SignatureLength = 4, Matches = header => header.StartsWith("RAW8"u8), Reader = new Reader(), Writer = new Writer(), }; private sealed class Reader : IFormatReader { public RasterInfo ReadInfo(EgamiInput input, ReaderOptions options) { (int width, int height) = Header(input); return new RasterInfo { Format = Info, Width = width, Height = height, Layout = Rgba8.Layout, FrameCount = 1, EstimatedBytes = 4L * width * height }; } public Raster<TPixel> Read<TPixel>(EgamiInput input, ReaderOptions options) where TPixel : unmanaged, IPixelType<TPixel> { (int width, int height) = Header(input); // CreateRaster checks the size against the safety limits before allocating. Raster<TPixel> raster = input.CreateRaster<TPixel>(width, height); using IMemoryOwner<byte> row = input.RentScratch(width * 4); for (int y = 0; y < height; y++) { input.ReadExactly(row.Memory.Span[..(width * 4)]); PixelConvert.Convert<Rgba8, TPixel>(MemoryMarshal.Cast<byte, Rgba8>(row.Memory.Span[..(width * 4)]), raster.Row(y)); } return raster; } public Raster Read(EgamiInput input, ReaderOptions options) => Read<Rgba8>(input, options); private static (int Width, int Height) Header(EgamiInput input) { input.Skip(4); return ((int)input.ReadUInt32BigEndian(), (int)input.ReadUInt32BigEndian()); } } private sealed class Writer : IFormatWriter { public void Write<TPixel>(Raster<TPixel> raster, Stream output, WriterOptions options) where TPixel : unmanaged, IPixelType<TPixel> { Span<byte> header = stackalloc byte[12]; "RAW8"u8.CopyTo(header); BinaryPrimitives.WriteUInt32BigEndian(header[4..], (uint)raster.Width); BinaryPrimitives.WriteUInt32BigEndian(header[8..], (uint)raster.Height); output.Write(header); Rgba8[] row = new Rgba8[raster.Width]; for (int y = 0; y < raster.Height; y++) { PixelConvert.Convert<TPixel, Rgba8>(raster.Row(y), row); output.Write(MemoryMarshal.AsBytes(row.AsSpan())); } } } } // Register it in a context... EgamiContext context = EgamiContext.Default.WithFormat(Raw8Format.Info); using (FileStream output = File.Create("duck.raw8")) { image.Save(output, Raw8Format.Info); } using Raster back = Raster.Load("duck.raw8", context); // ...or, once at startup before any other Egami call, make it part of the default context: // EgamiContext.SetDefault(new EgamiContext().WithFormat(Raw8Format.Info)); Readers read only through EgamiInput, which keeps them inside the safety limits: Member Use Peek, Read, ReadExactly, Skip, ReadByte, ReadUInt16/32… Read the data; a short read throws CorruptDataException CreateRaster<TPixel>(width, height) The raster you decode into, size-checked before any allocation AddFrame(raster) Another frame for animated formats, counted against MaxFrames and the memory budget RentScratch(bytes) Working memory counted against the same budget CheckMemory, CheckFrameCount, CheckMetadataBytes Check a number from the header before acting on it Warn(raster, id, text) Note something a lenient read recovered from, with a stable id such as Pcx.PaletteMissing Corrupt(offset, problem) The exception to throw for data that breaks the format's rules Respect ReaderOptions.Recovery: in Lenient mode keep what decoded and warn; in Strict mode throw. The writer gets the raster and a stream; options come as your own WriterOptions subclass. Streaming Two optional interfaces let a format stream. A reader that also implements IRowFormatReader returns a RowReader<TNatural> from Open: the open image hands out rows as RasterDecoder asks for them (top-down, never going back within a frame) and moves through frames with NextFrame. The decoder applies Region, MinimumSize and the pixel conversion after it. A writer that also implements IRowFormatWriter returns a RowEncoder<TPixel> from Start, which takes rows (or frames, for an animation) one at a time; Save, SaveAsync, RasterEncoder and Transcode then all write through it. When streaming, EncodeStart.Whole is null: an option that needs every pixel before the first byte should call EncodeStart.Refuse. /// <summary>The same RAW8 format, streaming: rows go in and out one at a time, so RasterDecoder, RasterEncoder and Transcode stream it.</summary> public static class StreamingRaw8Format { public static FormatInfo Info { get; } = Raw8Format.Info with { Reader = new Reader(), Writer = new Writer() }; private sealed class Reader : IFormatReader, IRowFormatReader { private static readonly IFormatReader Whole = Raw8Format.Info.Reader!; public RasterInfo ReadInfo(EgamiInput input, ReaderOptions options) => Whole.ReadInfo(input, options) with { Access = RasterAccess.Streamed }; public Raster<TPixel> Read<TPixel>(EgamiInput input, ReaderOptions options) where TPixel : unmanaged, IPixelType<TPixel> => Whole.Read<TPixel>(input, options); public Raster Read(EgamiInput input, ReaderOptions options) => Whole.Read(input, options); // The open image reads each row when it is asked for; the decoder crops, reduces and converts after it. public RowReader Open(EgamiInput input, ReaderOptions options) { input.Skip(4); int width = (int)input.ReadUInt32BigEndian(); return new Rows(input, width, (int)input.ReadUInt32BigEndian()); } } private sealed class Rows(EgamiInput input, int width, int height) : RowReader<Rgba8> { private readonly Rgba8[] _row = new Rgba8[width]; private int _next; private bool _started; public override int Width => width; public override int Height => height; public override Metadata.RasterMetadata Metadata { get; } = new(); public override Metadata.FrameMetadata? NextFrame() { if (_started) { return null; } _started = true; return new Metadata.FrameMetadata(); } public override void ReadRow<TPixel>(int y, int x, Span<TPixel> destination) { for (; _next <= y; _next++) { input.ReadExactly(MemoryMarshal.AsBytes(_row.AsSpan())); } PixelConvert.Convert<Rgba8, TPixel>(_row.AsSpan(x, destination.Length), destination); } } private sealed class Writer : IFormatWriter, IRowFormatWriter { public void Write<TPixel>(Raster<TPixel> raster, Stream output, WriterOptions options) where TPixel : unmanaged, IPixelType<TPixel> => Raw8Format.Info.Writer!.Write(raster, output, options); // Save, SaveAsync, RasterEncoder and Transcode all write through the encoder. public RowEncoder<TPixel> Start<TPixel>(Stream output, EncodeStart<TPixel> start) where TPixel : unmanaged, IPixelType<TPixel> => new Encoder<TPixel>(output, start.Width, start.Height); } private sealed class Encoder<TPixel> : RowEncoder<TPixel> where TPixel : unmanaged, IPixelType<TPixel> { private readonly Stream _output; private readonly Rgba8[] _row; public Encoder(Stream output, int width, int height) { _output = output; _row = new Rgba8[width]; Span<byte> header = stackalloc byte[12]; "RAW8"u8.CopyTo(header); BinaryPrimitives.WriteUInt32BigEndian(header[4..], (uint)width); BinaryPrimitives.WriteUInt32BigEndian(header[8..], (uint)height); output.Write(header); } public override void WriteRow(ReadOnlySpan<TPixel> row) { PixelConvert.Convert<TPixel, Rgba8>(row, _row); _output.Write(MemoryMarshal.AsBytes(_row.AsSpan())); } public override void Complete() { } } } A format without them still works everywhere: the decoder reads the whole image with Read and serves rows from it, and the encoder gathers the image and calls Write at the end. Pixel types A pixel type is an unmanaged struct implementing IPixelType<TSelf>. Its Layout says how it is stored: a layout Egami knows (Rgba with Unorm8, say) lets Egami take its fast paths; anything else uses PixelChannelOrder.Other, and Egami converts it only through its own ToScaled and FromScaled. Wrapping memory Raster.Wrap puts a raster over memory you own, without copying: a Memory<TPixel> with a stride in pixels, or a Memory<byte> with a stride in bytes, such as a video frame whose rows are padded. Pass an IDisposable owner to have the raster release the memory when it is disposed. Rows and planes For a one-off pass over pixels, ForEachRow runs a lambda on each row in parallel; no operation class needed. using Raster<Rgba8> image = Raster.Create<Rgba8>(256, 64); // A horizontal gradient; rows run in parallel, each row is a Span over the pixels. image.ForEachRow((row, y) => { for (int x = 0; x < row.Length; x++) { row[x] = new Rgba8((byte)x, (byte)(y * 4), 128, 255); } }); Each frame's pixels are a PixelPlane<TPixel>: rows of Span<TPixel>, and the whole frame as one span when it is stored in one block.
